## Read-only data audit (observed, 2026-09-23)

The attached reproducible DuckDB scan read all relevant compressed files. It observed 200,859 ICU stays. Applying age ≥18 (`>89` mapped to 90), first unit visit, `unitstaytype='admit'`, and ICU duration >24 h gave 107,153. Of these, 28,719 had any periodic systemic MAP; 19,402 had at least 202 valid bins in the inclusive diagnostic window; 18,721 also had a pre-landmark creatinine; and 17,136 had a later creatinine. After requiring an admission creatinine within -6 to +6 h and excluding a creatinine rise meeting the study rule during 0–24 h, 11,161 remained with 1,860 subsequent events across 162 hospitals (16.7%). This is the bounded pre-analysis count; the executable must recompute using the exact half-open window and report the additional day-1 dialysis sensitivity exclusion rather than treating these counts as final results.

Among the 17,136 lab-complete stays before prevalent-AKI exclusion, valid periodic-MAP bins had median 271 (IQR 245–285), median inter-bin gap 5 minutes at every reported quantile, and 90th-percentile gap 5 minutes except an observed maximum of 15. Duplicate patient-offset rows were negligible (one excess row). There were 17,297 out-of-range bins (<20 or >180 mmHg), proving artifact filtering is material. Nadir median was 56 mmHg (IQR 49–62); equivalent observed hours below 65 had median 1.5 (IQR 0.17–5.0). Creatinine was overwhelmingly labeled mg/dL (817,776 rows in the dominant interface spelling plus case variants). Post-landmark test count median was 5 (IQR 3–6); first post-landmark test median offset was 2,114 minutes and last was 7,686 minutes. Seventy-two hospitals had ≥50 pre-exclusion complete stays and 74 had at least ten provisional events and ten non-events.

Vasopressor-name/unit heterogeneity was confirmed. In the 17,136 pre-exclusion complete stays, 5,781 (33.7%) had a qualifying infusion entry during day 1; distinct entry offsets had median 11 (IQR 4–22). This supports presence/timing adjustment but not a standardized dose claim. In `apacheApsVar`, 171,177 rows represented 171,177 stays; missing/-1 rates included 1.85% for `meanbp`, 21.67% for `creatinine`, 50.89% for `urine`, 60.90% for albumin, and 77.17% for pH/PaO2/PCO2/FiO2. Missing indicators or training-set multiple imputation are mandatory. `vitalAperiodic` had 9,666,403 first-day rows in 187,279 stays, but values ranged 0–286, confirming both broader coverage and artifact risk.

Coverage sensitivity before prevalent-AKI exclusion yielded 20,352 complete stays at ≥50% bins, 19,043 at ≥60%, 17,136 at ~70%, 14,500 at ≥80%, and 10,798 at ≥90%. The primary exact rule is 202 of 288 expected half-open five-minute bins (70.1%); report deviations between the diagnostic inclusive count and final half-open count.

## Population and temporal rules

Index one stay per person: first chronological `unitvisitnumber=1`, `unitstaytype='admit'`; if malformed ties occur, smallest `patientunitstayid`. Adults ≥18, alive/in ICU at minute 1,440, with at least 202/288 valid invasive-MAP bins, an admission creatinine in [-360,+360] minutes, at least one creatinine in (-360,1440], and at least one in (1440,10080]. Exclude day-1 `dialysis=1` in the phenotype-validity analysis; report main results with and without this exclusion because its timing within day 1 is unavailable. Do not infer chronic dialysis absence from missingness.

Exposure window is ICU minutes [0,1440); landmark is 1,440. Outcome window is (1440,10080], administratively censored at unit discharge. A stay has prevalent/evolving exposure-window AKI and is excluded if any creatinine through the landmark rises ≥0.3 mg/dL from the admission value or reaches ≥1.5 times admission. This cannot exclude community-acquired AKI when admission creatinine is already elevated; state that limitation.

Subsequent creatinine-defined AKI is either (a) a rise ≥0.3 mg/dL from the last valid pre-landmark creatinine by minute 4,320 (48 hours after landmark), or (b) any creatinine through minute 10,080 ≥1.5 times admission creatinine. The executable should also implement the general all-pairs 48-hour rule as a sensitivity. Urine-output AKI, renal-replacement initiation, etiology, and biomarker-confirmed injury are not claimed.

## Exposure construction and artifact rules

Deduplicate same-stay/same-offset rows by median. Discard MAP <20 or >180 mmHg; flag but do not automatically discard physiologically abrupt adjacent changes. Do not interpolate primary values. Define coverage as valid bins/288 and normalize duration to observed bins:

- Nadir: minimum valid `systemicmean`.
- Primary burden: (24 × n(MAP<65)/n(valid)), equivalent observed hours under 65.
- Secondary depth-duration: mean deficit (Σ max(65-MAP,0)/n(valid)), mmHg.
- Temporal descriptors: longest consecutive run (gaps exactly five minutes), episode count, four six-hour burden values, and 24 hourly burdens/masks.

Repeat at thresholds 55, 60, and 70; coverage 50/60/80/90%; excluding isolated one-bin lows; winsorizing at 0.5/99.5%; restricting to median and 90th-percentile gaps of five minutes; and using irregular noninvasive MAP as a separate modality analysis with no carry-forward beyond 60 minutes. A burden result that appears only under one artifact rule is inconclusive.

## Transparent prespecified baseline and estimand

Create a deterministic hospital-held-out 70/15/15 train/validation/test split using SHA-256(`"eicu-map-aki-20260923:"+hospitalid`), with all stays from a hospital in one partition. Before outcomes are modeled, verify each partition has ≥20 hospitals and ≥100 events; if not, rotate a documented salt once and freeze it. No patient or hospital crosses partitions. Model choices and thresholds use train/validation only; test is opened once.

Fit penalized logistic regression:

- B0 (nadir baseline): restricted cubic spline of MAP nadir (knots from training only) plus age, sex, ethnicity, admission source, unit type, admission weight, admission creatinine, creatinine-test counts/timing available by landmark, MAP coverage/gap metrics, and missing indicators; add the non-BP/non-creatinine `apacheApsVar` variables as the prespecified measured-severity block.
- B1 (burden model): B0 plus a restricted cubic spline of primary burden. No automatic feature search.
- B2 (treatment-rival): B1 plus any vasopressor, number of distinct infusion offsets, first/last offset, number of hourly bins with entries, and agent classes. Attenuation from B1 to B2 is reported; B2 is not interpreted as a direct effect because treatment can be mediator, response to severity, or collider.

The primary association estimand is the test-population standardized risk difference and risk ratio comparing each person’s fitted risk at the training-set 75th versus 25th burden percentile within their 5-mmHg nadir stratum, restricted to common support, holding measured covariates fixed. Also report the burden spline and hospital-cluster-robust odds-ratio contrasts. This is an associational estimand.

Evaluate test log loss (primary predictive metric), Brier score, AUROC, AUPRC, calibration intercept/slope, calibration curves, and net benefit over plausible alert probabilities (descriptive only). Compare B1 versus B0 using paired hospital-cluster bootstrap (1,000 resamples) for Δlog loss and all metrics; bootstrap the full preprocessing/refit. Report pooled and equal-hospital-weighted results. A within-hospital fixed-effect sensitivity among hospitals with both outcomes addresses site case mix; it is separate from new-hospital transport.

## Scientifically substantive temporal alternative

Fit a penalized functional logistic model on the same split and outcome. Inputs are the 24 hourly fractions of valid bins below 65, hourly nadirs, hourly coverage masks, and hourly vasopressor-entry masks plus B0 static covariates. Represent the hypotension coefficient over hour with six cubic B-spline basis functions and a second-difference roughness penalty selected on validation log loss; include longest-run length and a prespecified hypotension×vasopressor-entry functional interaction. Call this T1. It is newly fitted to predict subsequent AKI.

B1 knows total burden and nadir but loses order, fragmentation, recovery, and treatment co-occurrence. T1 can reveal whether equal total burden concentrated late, early, or in long runs has different transportable information. Compare T1 with B1 on held-out log loss/calibration and with three falsifying ablations: permute hourly order within stay while retaining total burden/nadir; remove missingness channels; remove vasopressor channels. Stable temporal weights require cluster-bootstrap intervals and consistent sign in validation and test; they are not mechanistic renal-perfusion effects.

A small temporal convolutional network over 288 five-minute MAP/mask bins was considered. It could learn nonlinear episode morphology, but adds less directly interpretable information than T1 for this question and increases overfitting/site-shortcut risk at ~11,000 stays. Revisit only if T1 materially improves held-out log loss, residual diagnostics show unresolved within-hour morphology, and at least 1,500 events remain after final exclusions. Proposed envelope then: one A100, 4 CPUs, 32 GiB, ≤2 hours, five seeds. Selected B0–T1 work is CPU-suitable: 8–16 CPUs, 32–64 GiB, approximately 1–3 hours including 1,000 hospital bootstraps; this estimate is unverified, while the full audit scan measured ~52 seconds on the ordinary environment.

## Testing-density and timing rivals

First model the probability of any post-landmark creatinine among all otherwise eligible 24-hour survivors. Report whether burden/nadir predict ascertainment. Repeat the outcome analysis with inverse-probability-of-observation weights estimated out-of-fold by hospital, stabilized and truncated at 1st/99th percentiles. Repeat among patients with a creatinine in the fixed (1440,4320] window, and among those with ≥2 post-landmark tests. Include post-test count only in descriptive sensitivity, never as a baseline predictor of an outcome it helps define.

Repeat complete construction at 12-hour and 36-hour landmarks, with matching exposure and subsequent windows, without selecting the favorable landmark. Exclude outcome tests in the first 60 minutes after landmark as a lag sensitivity. Report death/discharge before an adequate outcome opportunity; do not label an untested stay a non-event.

## Falsification and interpretation

Support requires both: (1) B1’s held-out standardized 75th-versus-25th burden risk difference is >0 with a hospital-bootstrap 95% interval excluding 0 after B0 adjustment, and (2) B1 improves held-out log loss over B0 with its 95% interval excluding 0, without major calibration deterioration. It must retain direction under ≥60/80% coverage, fixed 48-hour ascertainment, and within-hospital analyses. T1 is separately supported only if it improves held-out log loss over B1 and nonconstant temporal structure survives order/missingness/vasopressor ablations.

Adverse evidence is an upper 95% bound ≤1 absolute percentage point for the standardized burden risk difference together with no held-out log-loss gain, or a reversed association stable across hospitals. That would refute a clinically meaningful incremental burden signal under this measurement design, not prove hypotension harmless.

Inconclusive evidence includes intervals spanning both 0 and +1 percentage point, strong hospital heterogeneity, failure under held-out hospitals, effect disappearance under coverage/testing/timing controls, or unstable T1 weights. Revise toward a measurement-validation study if measurement controls dominate; defer if event/common-support counts become inadequate. Do not repeatedly alter thresholds after test inspection.

A supportive result establishes only a transportable adjusted association and incremental prognostic information. It does not show that hypotension caused AKI, that vasopressors caused or prevented injury, that MAP 65 is optimal, or that raising MAP reduces risk. Those claims need richer pre-ICU renal baselines, hourly urine output and RRT timing, fluid/cardiac-output/nephrotoxin information, clinical adjudication of AKI cause, and ultimately a prospective intervention study. An adverse result does not validate nadir as causal. Clinical experts must adjudicate artifact bounds, dialysis/CKD exclusions, vasopressor mapping, and actionability.

## Demonstration adaptations and dispositions

- **Delphi natural-history paper:** inspected full article methods/text. It learns ordered, continuously timed disease tokens with a modified GPT-2 and compares against simpler incidence baselines. Adaptation insight: order needs an explicit same-question baseline and held-out evaluation. Missing dependency: eICU has five-minute summaries, not raw waveforms or the paper’s population-scale disease trajectories/Danish registry. Disposition: do not reproduce; defer a transformer, choose T1 as the smallest interpretable order-preserving test.
- **ALADYNOULLI Bayesian paper:** inspected article optimization/model passages. It uses Gaussian-process latent trajectories and genetic effects to learn shared longitudinal signatures. Adaptation insight: smooth temporal coefficients and held-out trajectory evaluation can be useful without reproducing genetics. Missing dependency: no germline genetics and no scientific need for cross-disease latent signatures here. Disposition: adapt smoothness regularization in T1; reject latent-signature reproduction because it does not sharpen burden versus nadir.
- **Oncoformer cancer demonstration:** only the publisher supplement and metadata are available; the main article/complete STAR Methods were not inspected. The supplement shows lab-only/image-only/full ablations and missingness/cohort-invariance ideas. Missing dependency: chest X-rays and complete methods. Disposition: adapt explicit missingness-channel and modality-ablation logic; do not claim or attempt multimodal reproduction.

[K1] Public inspected source: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC11018652/fullTextXML\n\nSchuurmans J, et al. *Hypotension during intensive care stay and mortality and morbidity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.* Intensive Care Medicine. 2024;50:516–525. doi:10.1007/s00134-023-07304-4.

[K2] Public inspected source: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC4056430/fullTextXML\n\nPoukkanen M, et al.; FINNAKI Study Group. *Hemodynamic variables and progression of acute kidney injury in critically ill patients with severe sepsis: data from the prospective observational FINNAKI study.* Critical Care. 2013;17:R295. doi:10.1186/cc13161.

[K3] Public inspected source: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC4057151/fullTextXML\n\nKellum JA, Lameire N; KDIGO AKI Guideline Work Group. *Diagnosis, evaluation, and management of acute kidney injury: a KDIGO summary (Part 1).* Critical Care. 2013;17:204. doi:10.1186/cc11454.

Missing indicators or training-set multiple imputation are mandatory. `vitalAperiodic` had 9,666,403 first-day rows in 187,279 stays, but values ranged 0–286, confirming both broader coverage and artifact risk.

Coverage sensitivity before prevalent-AKI exclusion yielded 20,352 complete stays at ≥50% bins, 19,043 at ≥60%, 17,136 at ~70%, 14,500 at ≥80%, and 10,798 at ≥90%. The primary exact rule is 202 of 288 expected half-open five-minute bins (70.1%); report deviations between the diagnostic inclusive count and final half-open count.

## Population and temporal rules

Index one stay per person: first chronological `unitvisitnumber=1`, `unitstaytype='admit'`; if malformed ties occur, smallest `patientunitstayid`. Adults ≥18, alive/in ICU at minute 1,440, with at least 202/288 valid invasive-MAP bins, an admission creatinine in [-360,+360] minutes, at least one creatinine in (-360,1440], and at least one in (1440,10080]. Exclude day-1 `dialysis=1` in the phenotype-validity analysis; report main results with and without this exclusion because its timing within day 1 is unavailable. Do not infer chronic dialysis absence from missingness.

Exposure window is ICU minutes [0,1440); landmark is 1,440. Outcome window is (1440,10080], administratively censored at unit discharge. A stay has prevalent/evolving exposure-window AKI and is excluded if any creatinine through the landmark rises ≥0.3 mg/dL from the admission value or reaches ≥1.5 times admission. This cannot exclude community-acquired AKI when admission creatinine is already elevated; state that limitation.

Subsequent creatinine-defined AKI is either (a) a rise ≥0.3 mg/dL from the last valid pre-landmark creatinine by minute 4,320 (48 hours after landmark), or (b) any creatinine through minute 10,080 ≥1.5 times admission creatinine. The executable should also implement the general all-pairs 48-hour rule as a sensitivity. Urine-output AKI, renal-replacement initiation, etiology, and biomarker-confirmed injury are not claimed.

## Exposure construction and artifact rules

Deduplicate same-stay/same-offset rows by median. Discard MAP <20 or >180 mmHg; flag but do not automatically discard physiologically abrupt adjacent changes. Do not interpolate primary values. Define coverage as valid bins/288 and normalize duration to observed bins:

- Nadir: minimum valid `systemicmean`.
- Primary burden: (24 × n(MAP<65)/n(valid)), equivalent observed hours under 65.
- Secondary depth-duration: mean deficit (Σ max(65-MAP,0)/n(valid)), mmHg.
- Temporal descriptors: longest consecutive run (gaps exactly five minutes), episode count, four six-hour burden values, and 24 hourly burdens/masks.

Repeat at thresholds 55, 60, and 70; coverage 50/60/80/90%; excluding isolated one-bin lows; winsorizing at 0.5/99.5%; restricting to median and 90th-percentile gaps of five minutes; and using irregular noninvasive MAP as a separate modality analysis with no carry-forward beyond 60 minutes. A burden result that appears only under one artifact rule is inconclusive.

## Transparent prespecified baseline and estimand

Create a deterministic hospital-held-out 70/15/15 train/validation/test split using SHA-256(`"eicu-map-aki-20260923:"+hospitalid`), with all stays from a hospital in one partition. Before outcomes are modeled, verify each partition has ≥20 hospitals and ≥100 events; if not, rotate a documented salt once and freeze it. No patient or hospital crosses partitions. Model choices and thresholds use train/validation only; test is opened once.

Fit penalized logistic regression:

- B0 (nadir baseline): restricted cubic spline of MAP nadir (knots from training only) plus age, sex, ethnicity, admission source, unit type, admission weight, admission creatinine, creatinine-test counts/timing available by landmark, MAP coverage/gap metrics, and missing indicators; add the non-BP/non-creatinine `apacheApsVar` variables as the prespecified measured-severity block.
- B1 (burden model): B0 plus a restricted cubic spline of primary burden. No automatic feature search.
- B2 (treatment-rival): B1 plus any vasopressor, number of distinct infusion offsets, first/last offset, number of hourly bins with entries, and agent classes. Attenuation from B1 to B2 is reported; B2 is not interpreted as a direct effect because treatment can be mediator, response to severity, or collider.

The primary association estimand is the test-population standardized risk difference and risk ratio comparing each person’s fitted risk at the training-set 75th versus 25th burden percentile within their 5-mmHg nadir stratum, restricted to common support, holding measured covariates fixed. Also report the burden spline and hospital-cluster-robust odds-ratio contrasts. This is an associational estimand.

Evaluate test log loss (primary predictive metric), Brier score, AUROC, AUPRC, calibration intercept/slope, calibration curves, and net benefit over plausible alert probabilities (descriptive only). Compare B1 versus B0 using paired hospital-cluster bootstrap (1,000 resamples) for Δlog loss and all metrics; bootstrap the full preprocessing/refit. Report pooled and equal-hospital-weighted results. A within-hospital fixed-effect sensitivity among hospitals with both outcomes addresses site case mix; it is separate from new-hospital transport.

## Scientifically substantive temporal alternative

Fit a penalized functional logistic model on the same split and outcome. Inputs are the 24 hourly fractions of valid bins below 65, hourly nadirs, hourly coverage masks, and hourly vasopressor-entry masks plus B0 static covariates. Represent the hypotension coefficient over hour with six cubic B-spline basis functions and a second-difference roughness penalty selected on validation log loss; include longest-run length and a prespecified hypotension×vasopressor-entry functional interaction. Call this T1. It is newly fitted to predict subsequent AKI.

B1 knows total burden and nadir but loses order, fragmentation, recovery, and treatment co-occurrence. T1 can reveal whether equal total burden concentrated late, early, or in long runs has different transportable information. Compare T1 with B1 on held-out log loss/calibration and with three falsifying ablations: permute hourly order within stay while retaining total burden/nadir; remove missingness channels; remove vasopressor channels. Stable temporal weights require cluster-bootstrap intervals and consistent sign in validation and test; they are not mechanistic renal-perfusion effects.

A small temporal convolutional network over 288 five-minute MAP/mask bins was considered. It could learn nonlinear episode morphology, but adds less directly interpretable information than T1 for this question and increases overfitting/site-shortcut risk at ~11,000 stays. Revisit only if T1 materially improves held-out log loss, residual diagnostics show unresolved within-hour morphology, and at least 1,500 events remain after final exclusions. Proposed envelope then: one A100, 4 CPUs, 32 GiB, ≤2 hours, five seeds. Selected B0–T1 work is CPU-suitable: 8–16 CPUs, 32–64 GiB, approximately 1–3 hours including 1,000 hospital bootstraps; this estimate is unverified, while the full audit scan measured ~52 seconds on the ordinary environment.

## Testing-density and timing rivals

First model the probability of any post-landmark creatinine among all otherwise eligible 24-hour survivors. Report whether burden/nadir predict ascertainment. Repeat the outcome analysis with inverse-probability-of-observation weights estimated out-of-fold by hospital, stabilized and truncated at 1st/99th percentiles. Repeat among patients with a creatinine in the fixed (1440,4320] window, and among those with ≥2 post-landmark tests. Include post-test count only in descriptive sensitivity, never as a baseline predictor of an outcome it helps define.

Repeat complete construction at 12-hour and 36-hour landmarks, with matching exposure and subsequent windows, without selecting the favorable landmark. Exclude outcome tests in the first 60 minutes after landmark as a lag sensitivity. Report death/discharge before an adequate outcome opportunity; do not label an untested stay a non-event.

## Falsification and interpretation

Support requires both: (1) B1’s held-out standardized 75th-versus-25th burden risk difference is >0 with a hospital-bootstrap 95% interval excluding 0 after B0 adjustment, and (2) B1 improves held-out log loss over B0 with its 95% interval excluding 0, without major calibration deterioration. It must retain direction under ≥60/80% coverage, fixed 48-hour ascertainment, and within-hospital analyses. T1 is separately supported only if it improves held-out log loss over B1 and nonconstant temporal structure survives order/missingness/vasopressor ablations.

Adverse evidence is an upper 95% bound ≤1 absolute percentage point for the standardized burden risk difference together with no held-out log-loss gain, or a reversed association stable across hospitals. That would refute a clinically meaningful incremental burden signal under this measurement design, not prove hypotension harmless.

Inconclusive evidence includes intervals spanning both 0 and +1 percentage point, strong hospital heterogeneity, failure under held-out hospitals, effect disappearance under coverage/testing/timing controls, or unstable T1 weights. Revise toward a measurement-validation study if measurement controls dominate; defer if event/common-support counts become inadequate. Do not repeatedly alter thresholds after test inspection.

A supportive result establishes only a transportable adjusted association and incremental prognostic information. It does not show that hypotension caused AKI, that vasopressors caused or prevented injury, that MAP 65 is optimal, or that raising MAP reduces risk. Those claims need richer pre-ICU renal baselines, hourly urine output and RRT timing, fluid/cardiac-output/nephrotoxin information, clinical adjudication of AKI cause, and ultimately a prospective intervention study. An adverse result does not validate nadir as causal. Clinical experts must adjudicate artifact bounds, dialysis/CKD exclusions, vasopressor mapping, and actionability.

## Demonstration adaptations and dispositions

- **Delphi natural-history paper:** inspected full article methods/text. It learns ordered, continuously timed disease tokens with a modified GPT-2 and compares against simpler incidence baselines. Adaptation insight: order needs an explicit same-question baseline and held-out evaluation. Missing dependency: eICU has five-minute summaries, not raw waveforms or the paper’s population-scale disease trajectories/Danish registry. Disposition: do not reproduce; defer a transformer, choose T1 as the smallest interpretable order-preserving test.
- **ALADYNOULLI Bayesian paper:** inspected article optimization/model passages. It uses Gaussian-process latent trajectories and genetic effects to learn shared longitudinal signatures. Adaptation insight: smooth temporal coefficients and held-out trajectory evaluation can be useful without reproducing genetics. Missing dependency: no germline genetics and no scientific need for cross-disease latent signatures here. Disposition: adapt smoothness regularization in T1; reject latent-signature reproduction because it does not sharpen burden versus nadir.
- **Oncoformer cancer demonstration:** only the publisher supplement and metadata are available; the main article/complete STAR Methods were not inspected. The supplement shows lab-only/image-only/full ablations and missingness/cohort-invariance ideas. Missing dependency: chest X-rays and complete methods. Disposition: adapt explicit missingness-channel and modality-ablation logic; do not claim or attempt multimodal reproduction.

## Key bibliography

[K1] Schuurmans J, et al. *Hypotension during intensive care stay and mortality and morbidity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.* Intensive Care Medicine. 2024;50:516–525. doi:10.1007/s00134-023-07304-4.

[K2] Poukkanen M, et al.; FINNAKI Study Group. *Hemodynamic variables and progression of acute kidney injury in critically ill patients with severe sepsis: data from the prospective observational FINNAKI study.* Critical Care. 2013;17:R295. doi:10.1186/cc13161.

[K3] Kellum JA, Lameire N; KDIGO AKI Guideline Work Group. *Diagnosis, evaluation, and management of acute kidney injury: a KDIGO summary (Part 1).* Critical Care. 2013;17:204. doi:10.1186/cc11454.

# Recovery order after circulatory stabilization and 72-hour organ-support re-escalation

## Objective and scientific boundary

Run the complete, frozen MIMIC-IV v3.1 investigation described here. Newly construct the cohort, estimate the adjusted kidney-first versus respiratory-first 72-hour risk difference, fit and evaluate B0–B2 and the prespecified longitudinal model, quantify uncertainty, test the severity and observation-process rivals, and report an evidence-linked interpretation.

The strongest available evidence says that longitudinal organ-dysfunction patterns stratify sepsis prognosis beyond an admission snapshot [K1], renal improvement is prognostically relevant but does not erase risk [K2], and residual circulatory support can alter risk around ventilator liberation [K3]. It does not establish the hypothesis below.

Primary falsifiable hypothesis: among adult first ICU stays with concurrent vasopressor-treated circulatory failure, invasive ventilation, and acute kidney dysfunction, followed by 12 hours free of vasopressor infusion, kidney-versus-respiratory recovery order during the next 24 hours adds clinically useful prediction of respiratory, circulatory, or renal support re-escalation during the subsequent 72 hours beyond complete same-landmark severity and observation intensity. The primary two-sided contrast is kidney-first minus respiratory-first among stays in which both organs recover by the landmark.

This is descriptive and prognostic. Do not claim causality, biological mechanism, treatment benefit, a monitoring threshold, or transportability.

## Population and fixed temporal boundaries

The unit is the first ICU stay per `[internal identifier]`. Include patients aged at least 18 at ICU admission, where age is `anchor_age + year(admittime) - anchor_year`.

1. Find a qualifying joint-support episode during ICU hours 0–72: temporal overlap of a running selected vasopressor infusion, invasive ventilation, and KDIGO stage at least 1 by creatinine or urine output, or RRT. Baseline creatinine is the minimum serum creatinine from hospital admission through ICU hour 6; if none exists, use the first ICU-window value and flag the weaker baseline. Implement KDIGO thresholds. Urine-output staging requires weight and at least 18 observed hours in the relevant 24-hour window.
2. Define circulatory stabilization `s` as the first time after the last qualifying overlap at which all selected vasopressor intervals have ended and no selected vasopressor is recorded during the next 12 hours. The confirming future 12 hours may establish `s`, but must not enter predictors.
3. The recovery-observation window is `[s,s+24h)`; `t0=s+24h`. Exclude from the primary analysis and report separately stays with support re-escalation during this ascertainment window.
4. At `t0`, require survival, presence in the same ICU stay, no vasopressor or RRT, no invasive ventilation, and both kidney and respiratory recovery.
5. Follow from `t0` through `t0+72h`, censoring at ICU discharge. In-ICU death without prior re-escalation is a competing event. Discharge alive is a competing event in cause-specific sensitivity analyses and a non-event in the primary discrete 24-hour person-period model.

Respiratory recovery is the end of the last invasive-ventilation procedure interval in `[s,t0)`, with no new invasive ventilation through `t0`. This is a procedure-interval proxy, not direct extubation.

Kidney recovery is the first 6-hour boundary after which creatinine is below 1.5 times baseline, rolling urine output is at least 0.5 mL/kg/h where observed, no RRT is active, and all conditions persist through `t0`. If creatinine or adequate urine/weight observation cannot establish recovery, classify it as unknown, never as non-recovery.

Classify kidney-first if kidney recovery precedes respiratory recovery by at least 6 hours, respiratory-first if the reverse is at least 6 hours, and synchronous if the absolute difference is below 6 hours. The primary model compares kidney-first with respiratory-first only. Preserve synchronous cases descriptively and in secondary models. Also report the secondary full-cohort landmark groups: both recovered, kidney-only, respiratory-only, neither, and indeterminate coverage. Do not substitute those groups for the primary estimand.

## Outcomes

The primary outcome is first support re-escalation within 72 hours:

- a new invasive-ventilation interval (item 225792) after at least 6 hours free;
- a new selected vasopressor infusion after the 24-hour recovery-observation window;
- a new RRT interval (225441, 225802, 225803, 225805, 225809, or 225955) after no RRT at `t0`.

Report each component. Treat death without prior support as competing. Repeat at 48 and 96 hours. Exclude comfort-measures or treatment-limitation cases only if you implement and validate a prespecified diagnosis/note adjudication algorithm; otherwise report this as unavailable clinical adjudication.

## Covariates, rivals, and models

At `t0`, B1 must add to B0 all of: age, sex, admission type and care unit, ICU time, Charlson indicators, baseline-creatinine quality, current creatinine and baseline ratio, 6/12/24-hour urine output and coverage, respiratory-support status, last-6-hour worst SpO2, FiO2 and respiratory rate, last PEEP and ventilator mode, current/last-6-hour MAP, heart rate, temperature, GCS components, lactate, bilirubin, platelets, sodium, potassium, bicarbonate, BUN, hemoglobin, WBC, cumulative fluid input/output, weight, diuretic dose, prior RRT, invasive-ventilation duration, vasopressor duration and peak/count, and each organ's worst KDIGO/respiratory state during recovery ascertainment. Add missingness indicators; learn median imputation on training data only.

B2 must add measurement counts and time since last measurement for creatinine, urine output, SpO2, FiO2, respiratory rate, MAP, blood gas, and lactate; distinct chart hours; and fractions of expected urine/chart bins observed.

Fit:

- B0: order group, age, sex, time, and care unit in a discrete-time complementary-log-log model.
- B1: B0 plus current severity and treatment variables.
- B2, the primary baseline: B1 plus observation intensity.
- B2+order as the direct incremental-order comparison if B2 is represented without order in prediction comparisons; coefficient/risk tables must make the parameterization unambiguous.
- cause-specific Cox sensitivities for re-escalation, death, and discharge.

Use restricted cubic splines for continuous covariates, variance-inflation and positivity diagnostics, standardized 72-hour risks, and kidney-first minus respiratory-first risk difference with 1,000 subject-level bootstrap replicates. Use cluster-robust standard errors by subject. Complete cases are a sensitivity only.

For the observation-process rival, model apparent recovery order with charting/store lag (`storetime-charttime`) and counts. Repeat the primary contrast in the dense-observation stratum: at least two creatinine results, at least 18 hours of urine coverage, and respiratory charting in at least 12 distinct hours. Report whether adjustment/restriction attenuates or reverses the order contrast and whether the negative control carries the signal.

Fit a masked time-aware GRU, or a temporal convolutional network only if the GRU dependency genuinely fails, to 6-hour bins from qualifying overlap through `t0`. Inputs are the same raw organ, treatment, and observation-intensity variables plus masks and time since last observation. Targets are discrete 24-hour hazards for first re-escalation, death, and discharge. Freeze architecture and hyperparameters before test evaluation and use training only for early stopping. On identical patients and splits, compare B2, B2+order, and the temporal model using 72-hour AUPRC/AUROC, integrated Brier score, log loss, calibration intercept/slope, and component risks. Include mask-free/mask-only and order/temporal ablations sufficient to determine whether temporal order rather than missingness alone accounts for gain.

Split patients temporally by `anchor_year`: earliest 70% train, next 15% validation, latest 15% test, allocating whole tied years nearest these proportions. Fit all preprocessing on train. Open test once after design freeze. Apply Benjamini–Hochberg within the secondary family; also report exploratory unadjusted confidence intervals.

## Exact private input binding

Read only `/data/mimic-iv-3.1.zip` (bound source SHA-256 `0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09`). Use these archive members and columns:

- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/icustays.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],[internal identifier],intime,outtime,first_careunit,last_careunit`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/admissions.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],admittime,dischtime,deathtime,admission_type,hospital_expire_flag`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/patients.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],gender,anchor_age,anchor_year,dod`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/inputevents.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],starttime,endtime,storetime,itemid,rate,rateuom,amount,amountuom,patientweight,statusdescription`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/procedureevents.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],starttime,endtime,storetime,itemid,statusdescription`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/outputevents.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],charttime,storetime,itemid,value,valueuom`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/labevents.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],itemid,charttime,storetime,valuenum,valueuom`; join on `[internal identifier]` and constrain time to the ICU stay.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/chartevents.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],charttime,storetime,itemid,value,valuenum,valueuom,warning`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/d_items.csv.gz`: `itemid,label,linksto,category,unitname`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/d_labitems.csv.gz`: `itemid,label,fluid,category`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/diagnoses_icd.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],seq_num,icd_code,icd_version`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/d_icd_diagnoses.csv.gz`: `icd_code,icd_version,long_title`.

Join ICU event tables by `[internal identifier]`, admissions by `[internal identifier]`, patients by `[internal identifier]`, and diagnosis dictionaries by `icd_code,icd_version`. Discharge diagnoses may define comorbidity only; they may not define onset or eligibility.

Selected vasopressors: epinephrine 221289/229617, dopamine 221662, phenylephrine 221749/229630/229631/229632, norepinephrine 221906, and vasopressin 222315. Exclude `statusdescription='Rewritten'`; require positive rate or amount. Angiotensin II 229709/229764 is sensitivity only. Diuretics are furosemide 221794/228340 and bumetanide 229639.

Procedure items: invasive ventilation 225792; RRT 225441/225802/225803/225805/225809/225955. Require non-Rewritten intervals and temporal overlap.

Primary urine items: 226557/226558/226559/226560/226561/226564/226565/226567/226627/226631/226713. Exclude mixed GU-irrigant items 226566 and 227489 from primary analysis; include only in sensitivity.

Labs: creatinine 50912/52546; lactate 50813/52442/53154; bicarbonate 50882; total bilirubin 50885/53089; potassium 50971/52610; sodium 50983/52623; BUN 51006/52647; hemoglobin 50811/51222/51640; platelets 51265/53189; WBC 51301/51755/51756.

Chart items: heart rate 220045; MAP 220052/220181; respiratory rate 220210; SpO2 220277; GCS eye/verbal/motor 220739/223900/223901; temperature C 223762; FiO2 223835; PEEP 220339; ventilator mode 223849/229314; oxygen device 226732; weight 224639/226512.

Produce `item_dictionary.csv` by exact, case-insensitive source dictionary lookup and include `role,itemid,dictionary,label,linksto,category,unit`. Do not broaden item sets by substring.

## Required output contract

Write all files below to `/workspace`. They contain private derived data and must not be published.

1. `analysis.py`: executable source used for extraction/modeling. It must support `python /workspace/analysis.py --self-test` and run deterministic synthetic tests of interval overlap, stabilization with 12-hour look-ahead, kidney recovery persistence/unknown handling, order classification, outcomes after `t0`, and feature/outcome leakage.
2. `analysis_manifest.json`: `schema="recovery-order-manifest-v1"`, source SHA-256, exact member-to-required-column map, the analysis.py SHA-256, split years and patient counts, frozen model configuration, random seeds, fit timestamps, and SHA-256 hashes of every other required output.
3. `cohort_audit.csv`: one row per otherwise eligible landmark candidate, with at least `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],anchor_year,split,landmark_group,order_group,recovery_unknown,stabilization_failed,feature_max_offset_hours,outcome_first_offset_hours,primary_event_72h,event_type_72h`. Offsets are relative to `t0`; no predictor offset may exceed zero and no outcome offset may be negative.
4. `test_predictions.csv`: one row per kidney-first or respiratory-first held-out test patient, with `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],order_group,event_time_hours,event_type,risk_b2_24,risk_b2_48,risk_b2_72,risk_b2_order_24,risk_b2_order_48,risk_b2_order_72,risk_b2_calibrated_72,risk_b2_order_calibrated_72,risk_gru_24,risk_gru_48,risk_gru_72,risk_if_kidney_first_72,risk_if_respiratory_first_72`. All risks must be finite in [0,1], and each model's 24/48/72 risks must be nondecreasing. The calibrated 72-hour risks must use calibration parameters fitted on validation data only and recorded in the manifest. `event_type` is one of `reescalation,death,discharge,none`; `event_time_hours` is blank only for none.
5. `bootstrap_risk_differences.csv`: exactly 1,000 rows with `replicate,risk_difference`, generated by subject-level resampling and corresponding to the primary standardized kidney-first minus respiratory-first contrast.
6. `results.json`: schema `recovery-order-results-v1`. Include:
   - `status` (`complete` or `incomplete`) and `incomplete_reasons`;
   - cohort flow and per-order event counts;
   - `primary`: `contrast="kidney-first minus respiratory-first"`, `risk_difference`, `ci95=[lower,upper]`, B2 and B2+order integrated Brier scores, validation-fitted calibration-corrected 72-hour log losses, and calibration slopes;
   - component and 48/96-hour sensitivity risk differences with confidence intervals;
   - observation-rival results including dense-stratum risk difference/CI and charting-negative-control estimate/CI;
   - B0–B2 coefficient/risk tables and cause-specific sensitivity summaries;
   - `gru`: fitted model type, checkpoint/config hashes, learning-curve summary, Brier/log-loss/calibration/discrimination metrics, and mask/order ablations;
   - diagnostics: recovery-unknown fraction, group outcome-event counts, calibration stability, positivity, convergence, and sensitivity-direction agreement;
   - `classification`: `supportive`, `adverse`, or `inconclusive`;
   - `claims`: structured claim IDs from the interpretation rules below, each linked to result field paths.
7. `conclusion.md`: human-readable conclusion, primary estimate and uncertainty, cohort/measurement limitations, model comparison, classification, and explicit claim boundaries. Every numerical statement must cite a `results.json` field path.

The verifier recomputes event counts, standardized risk difference, integrated Brier scores, bootstrap percentile interval, and leakage checks from the submitted audit/prediction/bootstrap files; checks hashes, source/member/column and item-dictionary fidelity; runs self-tests; and checks whether structured conclusions follow from computed results. It does not establish clinical truth.

## Falsification and interpretation rules

First mark the result inconclusive if the primary CI spans both -0.05 and +0.05, either order group has fewer than 100 primary outcome events, recovery is unknown in more than 30% of otherwise eligible stays, calibration is unstable, required fits/outputs fail, or sensitivity estimates disagree materially.

A supportive result requires all of: primary adjusted CI excludes zero; absolute adjusted risk difference is at least 0.05; component and 48/96-hour estimates are directionally stable; B2+order improves held-out integrated Brier score by at least 0.005 or has lower held-out 72-hour log loss after validation-fitted calibration correction; B2/B2+order are adequately calibrated; and the association does not reverse after B2 observation-intensity adjustment or dense-observation restriction. The only positive clinical claim allowed is `incremental_prognostic_information_selected_cohort`. Also state `no_mechanism`, `no_treatment_benefit`, and `no_transportability`.

An adverse result is supported when not inconclusive and either the CI lies wholly within [-0.05,+0.05], held-out Brier improvement is below 0.005 with a calibrated current-state baseline, or the association reverses/vanishes under observation restriction while the charting negative-control CI excludes zero. Allowed claims are `favors_current_state_observation_explanation`, `against_using_order_for_monitoring`, and `does_not_refute_all_trajectory_value`.

An inconclusive result permits only `measurement_validation_or_more_data_needed` and `neither_confirmation_nor_refutation`. If criteria conflict or do not cleanly support either directional interpretation, use inconclusive and explain why. A precise result in either direction can be supportive because the hypothesis is two-sided.

Never assert `biological_mechanism`, `causal_effect`, `treatment_benefit`, `monitoring_threshold`, or `external_transportability`. Goals of care, extubation intent/failure, prophylactic/procedural support, and urine-versus-irrigation validity require clinical adjudication. Mechanism, treatment benefit, transportability, and a monitoring threshold require chart review, external validation, or a prospective study.

## Key references

[K1] Xu Z, Mao C, Su C, et al. “Sepsis subphenotyping based on organ dysfunction trajectory.” *Critical Care* 26, 197 (2022). https://doi.org/10.1186/s13054-022-04071-4

[K2] Peters E, Antonelli M, Wittebole X, et al. “A worldwide multicentre evaluation of the influence of deterioration or improvement of acute kidney injury on clinical outcome in critically ill patients with and without sepsis at ICU admission.” *Critical Care* 22, 188 (2018). https://doi.org/10.1186/s13054-018-2112-z

[K3] Zarrabian B, Wunsch H, Stelfox HT, Iwashyna TJ, Gershengorn HB. “Liberation from Invasive Mechanical Ventilation with Continued Receipt of Vasopressor Infusions.” *American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine* 205:1053–1063 (2022). https://doi.org/10.1164/rccm.202108-2004OC

The frozen receipt mappings are in `/task/key-references.json` when mounted by the task harness. K1 and K2 were inspected from full-text XML excerpts; K3 was inspected from an indexed abstract only.

# Recovery order after circulatory stabilization and 72-hour organ-support re-escalation

Status: complete experiment proposal; no outcome analysis has been run. Parent: `candidate-04131591b134016dfa0de0c4`.

## Clinical opening and exact claim

The strongest existing evidence supports a bounded statement: longitudinal organ-dysfunction patterns stratify sepsis prognosis beyond an admission snapshot [K1]; renal improvement is prognostically relevant but does not erase risk [K2]; and residual circulatory support can alter the risk associated with ventilator liberation [K3]. These observations do **not** establish that kidney-versus-respiratory recovery order after circulation has stabilized is independently informative.

**Primary falsifiable hypothesis.** Among adult first ICU stays with a clinically meaningful episode of concurrent vasopressor-treated circulatory failure, invasive ventilation, and acute kidney dysfunction, followed by 12 hours without vasopressor infusion, the ordering of kidney and respiratory recovery observed during the next 24 hours predicts new respiratory, circulatory, or renal support in the subsequent 72 hours beyond a complete same-landmark severity snapshot and observation intensity. Prespecified contrast: kidney-first versus respiratory-first among stays in which both recover by the landmark. The direction is intentionally two-sided; the experiment estimates which ordering, if either, is higher risk.

This is a descriptive/prognostic, not causal or mechanistic, hypothesis. “Kidney-first” may mark persistent pulmonary injury; “respiratory-first” may mark residual renal/fluid vulnerability. The strongest rivals are (i) current severity/treatment burden and (ii) clinician observation/treatment intensity, which can create apparent recovery times.

**Clinical importance.** If order adds calibrated short-horizon information when both organs look recovered at the landmark, it can justify different post-stabilization monitoring or step-down caution. If it does not, clinicians and risk systems should prefer current state and charting context rather than infer “recovery debt” from sequence.

## Population, time zero, and no-leakage windows

Unit is the first ICU stay per `[internal identifier]` in MIMIC-IV v3.1. Include age >=18 at ICU admission. Follow-up need not be complete: eligibility requires survival and continued ICU presence only through the landmark, after which ICU discharge is a competing event. Require:

1. **Qualifying joint-support episode:** within ICU hours 0–72, overlap of (a) any running vasopressor infusion, (b) invasive ventilation procedure interval, and (c) acute kidney dysfunction: KDIGO stage >=1 by creatinine or urine output, or RRT. Baseline creatinine is the minimum serum creatinine from hospital admission through 6 h after ICU admission; if unavailable, use the first ICU-window value and flag this weaker baseline. Kidney staging follows KDIGO thresholds; urine output requires available weight and >=18 observed hours in a 24-h window. This cohort enriches for genuine multiorgan recovery; it is not claimed to be all sepsis.
2. **Circulatory stabilization time `s`:** first time after the last overlap at which all qualifying vasopressor infusion intervals have ended and no vasopressor is recorded for the next 12 h. `s` is known only after that 12-h confirmation.
3. **Recovery-observation window:** `[s, s+24h)`. Define fixed landmark `t0=s+24h`. Exclude support re-escalation during this window from the primary analysis; it means stabilization failed before phenotype ascertainment and is reported separately.
4. At `t0`, patient is alive, still in the same ICU stay, without vasopressor or RRT, not invasively ventilated, and both organs meet recovery definitions. This restriction makes the primary order comparison hold the same binary organ-support state at the landmark.
5. **Follow-up:** `[t0,t0+72h]`, censored at ICU discharge. In-ICU death without prior re-escalation is a competing event, not counted as successful non-event. Discharge alive is also competing for cause-specific sensitivity and is the non-event state in the primary 24-h person-period model.

Respiratory recovery time is the end of the last invasive-ventilation interval in `[s,t0)`, with no new invasive ventilation through `t0`; extubation itself is not directly recorded, so this is a procedure-interval proxy. Kidney recovery time is the first 6-h boundary after which creatinine is <1.5x baseline, rolling urine output is >=0.5 mL/kg/h where observed, no RRT is active, and these conditions persist to `t0`. If creatinine or adequate urine/weight observation cannot establish recovery, kidney recovery is unknown—not failure. Primary order is kidney-first if kidney recovery precedes respiratory recovery by >=6 h, respiratory-first for the reverse, and synchronous if absolute difference <6 h. Primary model uses kidney-first versus respiratory-first; synchronous is retained descriptively and in secondary models.

Secondary full-cohort state groups at `t0`: both recovered, kidney-only recovered, respiratory-only recovered, neither recovered, and indeterminate coverage. They must not be interpreted as the primary order estimand.

## Outcomes and falsification

Primary outcome is first **support re-escalation** within 72 h:

- new invasive ventilation interval (item 225792) after >=6 h free;
- new vasopressor infusion (prespecified inputevents items below) after the 24-h recovery-observation period;
- new RRT procedure interval (225441, 225802, 225803, 225805, 225809, 225955) after no RRT at `t0`.

Report components separately. Death without prior support is a competing event. Sensitivities: 48-h and 96-h horizons; exclude comfort-measures/limitation cases only if a prespecified diagnosis/note adjudication algorithm can be validated—otherwise report this as missing clinical adjudication, not an automated exclusion.

**Supportive:** the adjusted kidney-first versus respiratory-first risk difference has a 95% CI excluding 0 and absolute magnitude >=5 percentage points, is directionally stable across component outcomes and sensitivities, improves held-out integrated Brier score by >=0.005 or calibration-slope-corrected log loss over the complete current-state baseline, and survives observation-intensity adjustment/stratification.

**Adverse/falsifying:** CI excludes effects larger than ±5 points, or held-out performance improvement is <0.005 with calibrated current-state baseline, or the association reverses/vanishes after observation-intensity restriction while a charting-intensity negative control carries the signal. This refutes clinically useful independent ordering information, not all value of trajectories.

**Inconclusive:** CI spans both ±5 points, either order group has <100 outcome events, recovery times are unknown for >30% of otherwise eligible stays, calibration is unstable, or sensitivity estimates disagree materially. Revise measurement or seek another dataset; do not call a null.

## Variables, rivals, and analysis

At `t0`, baseline model covariates are age, sex, admission type/care unit, ICU time, Charlson comorbidity indicators, baseline creatinine-quality flag, current creatinine and ratio to baseline, 6/12/24-h urine output and coverage, current respiratory support status, last 6-h worst SpO2, FiO2 and respiratory rate, last PEEP/ventilator mode, current/last-6-h MAP, heart rate, temperature, GCS components, lactate, bilirubin, platelets, sodium, potassium, bicarbonate, BUN, hemoglobin, WBC, cumulative fluid input/output, weight, diuretic dose, prior RRT, invasive-ventilation duration, vasopressor duration and peak/count, and each organ's worst KDIGO/respiratory state in the recovery window. Include missingness indicators; median imputation is learned in training only. This deliberately “overmatches” current severity before adding order.

Observation-intensity rival variables are per-window counts and time since last measurement for creatinine, urine output, SpO2, FiO2, respiratory rate, MAP, blood gas, and lactate; distinct chart hours; and fraction of expected urine/chart bins observed. Primary comparisons are sequential:

- B0: prespecified order groups plus age/sex/time/care unit in a discrete-time complementary-log-log model.
- B1: B0 + all current severity/treatment covariates.
- B2 (primary): B1 + observation-intensity variables.
- Negative-control artifact check: charting/store lag (`storetime-charttime`) and counts predict apparent recovery order; rerun in dense-observation stratum (creatinine at least twice, urine coverage >=18 h, respiratory charting in >=12 distinct hours). A dominant intensity signal or order attenuation supports the measurement rival.
- Cause-specific Cox models for re-escalation, death, and discharge are sensitivity analyses. Use cluster-robust SE by subject (one stay makes this conservative), restricted cubic splines for continuous covariates, and variance-inflation/positivity checks. Report standardized 72-h risks and kidney-first minus respiratory-first risk difference with 1,000 subject bootstrap CIs.

No p-value-only claim. Complete-case analysis is sensitivity. Missing current values use training-fold imputation; missing recovery evidence creates “indeterminate,” never “not recovered.”

## Substantive longitudinal alternative

Fit a masked time-aware GRU (alternative acceptable: temporal convolutional network) to 6-h bins from the qualifying overlap through `t0`, using the same raw organ, treatment, and observation-intensity inputs plus masks and time-since-last-measurement. Target is discrete 24-h hazards for first re-escalation/death/discharge. It can reveal nonlinear duration, relapse, and cross-organ lag patterns that the single order label and landmark snapshot discard. Freeze architecture/hyperparameters before test evaluation; use training only for early stopping. Compare B2 versus B2+order and GRU on identical splits using 72-h AUPRC/AUROC, integrated Brier score, log loss, calibration intercept/slope, and component risks; bootstrap paired differences. The learned model is scientifically selected only if calibration is adequate and improvement is clinically material (Brier >=0.005) with stable ablation evidence that temporal order—not missingness masks alone—accounts for gain. Otherwise defer it and retain the transparent baseline.

## Split and multiplicity

Patient-level temporal split by deidentified anchor year: earliest 70% train, next 15% validation, latest 15% test; if anchor-year ties prevent target proportions, allocate whole years nearest those proportions. Fit preprocessing only on train. Test set is opened once after design freeze. Primary contrast/outcome/horizon is single. Component outcomes, state groups, thresholds, learned model, and 48/96-h horizons are secondary; use Benjamini–Hochberg within the secondary family and report unadjusted CIs as exploratory.

## Exact MIMIC binding

Read-only source: `[private path]`, SHA-256 `0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09`.

- `icu/icustays` member `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/icustays.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier], [internal identifier], [internal identifier], intime, outtime, first_careunit, last_careunit`.
- `hosp/admissions`: `[internal identifier], [internal identifier], admittime, dischtime, deathtime, admission_type, hospital_expire_flag`; `hosp/patients`: `[internal identifier], gender, anchor_age, anchor_year, dod`. Join `[internal identifier]`; age at admission = `anchor_age + year(admittime)-anchor_year`.
- `icu/inputevents`: join `[internal identifier]`; intervals `starttime,endtime`, event `itemid`, `rate,rateuom,amount,patientweight,statusdescription`. Vasopressors verified in local `d_items`: epinephrine 221289/229617; dopamine 221662; phenylephrine 221749/229630/229631/229632; norepinephrine 221906; vasopressin 222315. Exclude `statusdescription='Rewritten'`; require positive rate or amount. Angiotensin II 229709/229764 is sensitivity because units/formulation differ. Diuretics: furosemide 221794/228340, bumetanide 229639.
- `icu/procedureevents`: `[internal identifier],starttime,endtime,itemid,statusdescription`. Invasive ventilation 225792. RRT 225441, 225802, 225803, 225805, 225809, 225955. Require non-Rewritten and interval overlap.
- `icu/outputevents`: `[internal identifier],charttime,itemid,value,valueuom`. Primary urine IDs verified by exact local labels: 226557, 226558, 226559, 226560, 226561, 226564, 226565, 226567, 226627, 226631, 226713. Exclude 226566 and 227489 because their labels mix urine with GU irrigant; include only in sensitivity.
- `hosp/labevents`: join `[internal identifier]` and restrict `charttime` within ICU; `itemid,charttime,storetime,valuenum,valueuom`. Serum creatinine 50912 and 52546. Other verified blood items: lactate 50813/52442/53154; bicarbonate 50882; bilirubin total 50885/53089; potassium 50971/52610; sodium 50983/52623; BUN 51006/52647; hemoglobin 50811/51222/51640; platelets 51265/53189; WBC 51301/51755/51756. Dictionary is `hosp/d_labitems`.
- `icu/chartevents`: `[internal identifier],charttime,storetime,itemid,value,valuenum,valueuom,warning`. Verified IDs: HR 220045; invasive/noninvasive MAP 220052/220181; RR 220210; SpO2 220277; GCS eye/verbal/motor 220739/223900/223901; temperature C 223762; FiO2 223835; PEEP 220339; ventilator modes 223849/229314; O2 device 226732; weights 224639/226512. Dictionary is `icu/d_items`.
- Comorbidity only: `hosp/diagnoses_icd([internal identifier],[internal identifier],seq_num,icd_code,icd_version)` joined to `hosp/d_icd_diagnoses(icd_code,icd_version,long_title)`; codes are discharge diagnoses and cannot define onset or enter temporal eligibility.

The table JSON schemas and actual gzip headers were inspected and agree. Item sets must be reproduced by an exact, case-insensitive `d_items`/ `d_labitems` lookup with `linksto`, label, unit, and category assertions; fail readiness on mismatch rather than broad substring expansion.

## Feasibility, resources, deliverables, and limits

A completed bounded scan of the four smaller ICU members (`work/feasibility-counts.json`, job `job-c5c3502621a095e8326c9f31`, 104 s) found 94,458 ICU stays; 28,483 with a selected vasopressor, 31,969 with invasive ventilation, 4,472 with RRT, and 90,182 with selected urine output. There were 21,222 stays with both vasopressor and invasive-ventilation records, 20,790 also with urine output, and 2,414 also with RRT. These are non-temporal support counts, not the qualifying analytic N or hypothesis result. A first probe that also streamed the 2.59-GB compressed labevents member hit the 600-s cap; creatinine item availability is dictionary/header-verified, while its cohort count remains a solver readiness output. Full solver deliverables:

1. frozen `item_dictionary.csv`, cohort flow with exclusion counts, overlap/recovery/event counts and missingness by split/order;
2. leakage tests proving no exposure/covariate timestamp exceeds `t0` and no outcome precedes it;
3. B0–B2 coefficient/risk tables, standardized risks/CIs, calibration/discrimination, component and competing-risk analyses;
4. observation-intensity negative controls/dense-stratum analysis;
5. GRU checkpoint/config, learning curves, masked-versus-no-mask/order-ablation results and paired test metrics;
6. machine-readable `results.json` linking every conclusion to computed cells, plus supportive/adverse/inconclusive interpretation.

Estimated full workload (unverified): extraction 2–4 h on 16 CPUs/128 GiB; baseline/bootstrap 1–2 h on 16 CPUs; GRU 1–3 h on one A100/32 GiB, total under the 8-h solver envelope. CPU is sufficient for the baseline; one allocated GPU is justified only for repeated longitudinal fits. Discovery counts used 4 CPUs/32 GiB and no GPU.

Clinical adjudication remains essential for goals-of-care limitations, extubation intent/failure, whether support was prophylactic/procedural, and whether urine records contain irrigation. MIMIC alone cannot establish mechanism, treatment benefit, transportability, or a monitoring threshold. Those require chart review, external validation (e.g. eICU with harmonized definitions), and ultimately a prospective study.

## Interpretation contract

Supportive results establish incremental prognostic information in this selected MIMIC cohort, not a biological recovery mechanism or benefit from intervention. Adverse results favor the same-time severity/observation explanation and argue against using order for monitoring. Inconclusive results motivate measurement validation or more data, not confirmation or refutation.

## Key references

[K2] Peters E, et al. *A worldwide multicentre evaluation of the influence of deterioration or improvement of acute kidney injury on clinical outcome in critically ill patients with and without sepsis at ICU admission.* Crit Care. 2018;22:188. doi:10.1186/s13054-018-2112-z. Full-text XML sections inspected.

[K3] Zarrabian B, et al. *Liberation from Invasive Mechanical Ventilation with Continued Receipt of Vasopressor Infusions.* Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2022;205:1053–1063. doi:10.1164/rccm.202108-2004OC. Indexed abstract only inspected.

# Surveillance-gated day-60 HCC marker decoupling after resection

Status: substantive child design; bounded source audits are observed, but no biomarker state or outcome model has been fitted. The question is narrowed from predicting a composite “recurrence-management event” to testing whether recurrence-report information is separable from the processes that generate imaging and treatment records.

## Scientific opening, claim boundary, and advance

The strongest evidence-supported claim is that a 4–6-week postoperative AFP response is prognostic in a selected high-AFP resection cohort [K1]. It is not evidence that persistent AFP is residual tumor. Persistent AFP without detected recurrence has been documented after apparently curative resection [K3]. A further threat is treatment meaning: post-hepatectomy TACE can be assigned as adjuvant management in patients treated as recurrence-free, and a current randomized protocol explicitly contrasts adjuvant TACE with intensive follow-up [K2]. Thus a post-landmark treatment code is not a recurrence diagnosis.

The unresolved claim is whether a day-60 AFP/PIVKA-II trajectory component that has decoupled from liver-injury recovery carries information about a subsequent untreated surveillance image, rather than merely predicting who is tested, imaged, or treated. The leading explanation is persistent tumor-associated signal. The strongest rival is a combination of postoperative hepatocyte injury/regeneration, assay or calendar drift, PIVKA-II perturbation by vitamin-K-related treatment, prior/adjuvant treatment selection, and informative surveillance.

Resolving this boundary is clinically consequential. A marker signal specific to independently ascertained recurrence could motivate a prospective imaging-prioritization study. A signal that mainly predicts testing or treatment would warn against using this EHR composite for occult-disease inference. This child advances the parent by removing treatment-only events from the recurrence-report outcome, representing surveillance and treatment as explicit competing observation processes, and requiring a first-untreated-image contrast before any tumor interpretation.

## Hypothesis and exact scientific deliverable

At a fixed day-60 landmark after first definitive HCC resection, a marker-persistence state learned from AFP and optional PIVKA-II will be distinguishable from a surgery-linked injury state only if it:

1. predicts an affirmative versus explicitly nonpositive first liver CT/MRI report obtained before any post-landmark HCC-directed treatment;
2. is more strongly associated with that report content than with the probability/timing of imaging or treatment itself;
3. remains stable across calendar eras, exact assay labels/specimen types, no-prior-treatment restrictions, and removal of PIVKA-II observations exposed to recorded vitamin-K/warfarin/antibiotic proxies; and
4. improves held-out report-content calibration and discrimination over the same-split static day-60 baseline.

The deliverable is newly fitted baseline and joint longitudinal models on one frozen cohort and split, producing: cohort and transition flows; assay/medication audits; first-transition cumulative incidences; content-model metrics; estimated injury and marker states/loadings; observation-intensity coefficients; state-identifiability checks; and conclusions mechanically mapped to supportive, adverse, or inconclusive criteria. Readiness is not completion.

The day-60 clinical question is preserved, but the biological-recurrence claim is gated. If first untreated surveillance reports or adjudicated positive/negative reports fail the thresholds below, the only valid deliverable is an ascertainment/measurement result; no recurrence-prediction model may be interpreted.

## Observed decision-changing audit

These are feasibility observations, not hypothesis results.

The parent’s broad audit found 6,880 landmark patients after early-treatment exclusion, but only 244 had recorded cross-sectional surveillance imaging in days 61–365, 672 had treatment, and 693 had either component. A new stricter audit required adult same-encounter HCC/resection in 2012–2023, numeric AFP before surgery and in days 0–14 and 15–60, an acute injury measurement, and no directed treatment in days -180:-1 or 0:60. After correcting a duplicate-procedure-row bug, 215 patients remained: 16 had liver CT/MRI, 46 had treatment, 36 had treatment before any recorded scan or no scan, and only nine had a scan before treatment (five lexical proxy-positive and four nonpositive). Pathology restriction and clinical adjudication were not applied in this bounded audit, so these are not final cohort counts.

The same audit found marked calendar distribution shifts for recorded AFP and PIVKA-II and many medication rows matching vitamin K or antibiotic terms; these are not proof of assay drift or PIVKA confounding, but they make pooled absolute thresholds indefensible. The failed nine-patient probe caused by treating same-episode procedure rows as repeat therapy is retained as an implementation warning: repeat resection must be in a different encounter and at least seven days after index.

This evidence warrants narrowing. A day-61–365 “no recurrence” label is not computable from record absence, and treatment cannot be pooled with affirmative imaging. The first untreated image is the only defensible computable disease-content contrast, and even it requires report-rule validation and expert review.

The baseline requires only one acute and one recovery measurement. PIVKA-II is optional, never a membership requirement.

Predictors use day -90 through +60. One prediction is made at day 60. The marked observation window is day 61 through day 365, administrative end, or last observed dated record. Record absence is censoring, not a negative outcome.

## Outcomes and estimands

The first post-landmark transition is one of:

- **S: untreated surveillance report** — first dated liver/upper-abdominal CT or MRI report before any HCC-directed post-landmark procedure/systemic-treatment proxy;
- **T: treatment before qualifying imaging** — first TACE/embolization, ablation, repeat resection, transplant, or systemic-treatment proxy before S; this is a management transition, not recurrence;
- **C: censoring/no transition** — last recorded contact or administrative day 365.

Within S, the computable report-content mark is prespecified as affirmative recurrence/residual/new HCC/progression/metastasis, explicit nonpositive language, uncertain, or unclassified. The primary binary content contrast includes only affirmative versus explicit nonpositive reports after negation/temporality rules are frozen; uncertain/unclassified reports are reported and excluded. A report is “untreated” only relative to recorded HCC treatment; prior unrecorded outside treatment cannot be excluded.

Estimands:

1. content association: adjusted odds/hazard contrast for day-60 marker versus injury states on affirmative versus explicit nonpositive first untreated report;
2. ascertainment association: state-specific cause-specific hazards/cumulative incidences for S and T;
3. discrimination gain of the longitudinal alternative over the baseline for report content, conditional on passing the report gate;
4. differential association with generic non-HCC imaging/encounter contact as a negative-control ascertainment outcome.

No causal treatment effect is estimated. Treatment-intent text is summarized as explicit recurrence, explicit adjuvant, both, or ambiguous; ambiguous events stay ambiguous.

## Methods on the same split

### Simple baseline

Fit two linked but conventional models:

1. elastic-net cause-specific Cox models from day 60 for S and T, with C as censoring and cumulative-incidence reporting;
2. Firth logistic regression among S for affirmative versus explicit nonpositive content.

Inputs are age, sex, calendar year, service, pathology lexical proxies, preoperative AFP rank within year, latest day-15:60 AFP/preoperative log ratio, latest optional PIVKA-II ratio, acute peak and day-15:60 latest ALT/AST/bilirubin/INR/albumin/platelet ratios, recorded vitamin-K/warfarin/antibiotic flags, and pre-landmark encounter/lab/imaging counts and missingness. This preserves interpretability but loses irregular timing, recovery shape, cross-marker covariance, and dependence between measurement and observation.

### Substantive longitudinal alternative

Fit a constrained continuous-time joint marked point-process model:

- injury state (I_i(t)), initialized by surgery and allowed patient-specific recovery, loading on ALT/AST/bilirubin/INR and inversely on albumin/platelets;

# Surveillance-gated day-60 HCC marker decoupling after resection

Status: substantive child design; bounded source audits are observed, but no biomarker state or outcome model has been fitted. The question is narrowed from predicting a composite “recurrence-management event” to testing whether recurrence-report information is separable from the processes that generate imaging and treatment records.

## Scientific opening, claim boundary, and advance

The strongest evidence-supported claim is that a 4–6-week postoperative AFP response is prognostic in a selected high-AFP resection cohort [K1]. It is not evidence that persistent AFP is residual tumor. Persistent AFP without detected recurrence has been documented after apparently curative resection [K3]. A further threat is treatment meaning: post-hepatectomy TACE can be assigned as adjuvant management in patients treated as recurrence-free, and a current randomized protocol explicitly contrasts adjuvant TACE with intensive follow-up [K2]. Thus a post-landmark treatment code is not a recurrence diagnosis.

The unresolved claim is whether a day-60 AFP/PIVKA-II trajectory component that has decoupled from liver-injury recovery carries information about a subsequent untreated surveillance image, rather than merely predicting who is tested, imaged, or treated. The leading explanation is persistent tumor-associated signal. The strongest rival is a combination of postoperative hepatocyte injury/regeneration, assay or calendar drift, PIVKA-II perturbation by vitamin-K-related treatment, prior/adjuvant treatment selection, and informative surveillance.

Resolving this boundary is clinically consequential. A marker signal specific to independently ascertained recurrence could motivate a prospective imaging-prioritization study. A signal that mainly predicts testing or treatment would warn against using this EHR composite for occult-disease inference. This child advances the parent by removing treatment-only events from the recurrence-report outcome, representing surveillance and treatment as explicit competing observation processes, and requiring a first-untreated-image contrast before any tumor interpretation.

## Hypothesis and exact scientific deliverable

At a fixed day-60 landmark after first definitive HCC resection, a marker-persistence state learned from AFP and optional PIVKA-II will be distinguishable from a surgery-linked injury state only if it:

1. predicts an affirmative versus explicitly nonpositive first liver CT/MRI report obtained before any post-landmark HCC-directed treatment;
2. is more strongly associated with that report content than with the probability/timing of imaging or treatment itself;
3. remains stable across calendar eras, exact assay labels/specimen types, no-prior-treatment restrictions, and removal of PIVKA-II observations exposed to recorded vitamin-K/warfarin/antibiotic proxies; and
4. improves held-out report-content calibration and discrimination over the same-split static day-60 baseline.

The deliverable is newly fitted baseline and joint longitudinal models on one frozen cohort and split, producing: cohort and transition flows; assay/medication audits; first-transition cumulative incidences; content-model metrics; estimated injury and marker states/loadings; observation-intensity coefficients; state-identifiability checks; and conclusions mechanically mapped to supportive, adverse, or inconclusive criteria. Readiness is not completion.

The day-60 clinical question is preserved, but the biological-recurrence claim is gated. If first untreated surveillance reports or adjudicated positive/negative reports fail the thresholds below, the only valid deliverable is an ascertainment/measurement result; no recurrence-prediction model may be interpreted.

## Observed decision-changing audit

These are feasibility observations, not hypothesis results.

The parent’s broad audit found 6,880 landmark patients after early-treatment exclusion, but only 244 had recorded cross-sectional surveillance imaging in days 61–365, 672 had treatment, and 693 had either component. A new stricter audit required adult same-encounter HCC/resection in 2012–2023, numeric AFP before surgery and in days 0–14 and 15–60, an acute injury measurement, and no directed treatment in days -180:-1 or 0:60. After correcting a duplicate-procedure-row bug, 215 patients remained: 16 had liver CT/MRI, 46 had treatment, 36 had treatment before any recorded scan or no scan, and only nine had a scan before treatment (five lexical proxy-positive and four nonpositive). Pathology restriction and clinical adjudication were not applied in this bounded audit, so these are not final cohort counts.

The same audit found marked calendar distribution shifts for recorded AFP and PIVKA-II and many medication rows matching vitamin K or antibiotic terms; these are not proof of assay drift or PIVKA confounding, but they make pooled absolute thresholds indefensible. The failed nine-patient probe caused by treating same-episode procedure rows as repeat therapy is retained as an implementation warning: repeat resection must be in a different encounter and at least seven days after index.

# Pre-illness creatinine–cystatin C discordance, grip strength, and hospitalized AKI

## Task and scientific status

Conduct the frozen UK Biobank experiment below. This is an open-ended research task: no association result is supplied and no favorable result is required. Newly compute the cohort, estimates, uncertainty, model comparisons, control-outcome tests, sensitivities, and a result-linked interpretation. A correct adverse or inconclusive result earns the same credit as a correct supportive result.

The strongest inspected evidence is bounded. Large eGFRcys−eGFRcr differences are common in UK Biobank and have multiple non-GFR predictors [K1]. Discordance is associated with frailty and broad adverse outcomes in SPRINT [K2]. During prolonged critical illness, muscle loss can make creatinine eGFR substantially overestimate measured GFR [K3]. None establishes incident AKI prediction in ambulatory adults, a low-grip interaction, a muscle mechanism at baseline, or benefit from cystatin-C-guided care.

The unresolved hypothesis is: among participants with baseline race-free 2021 CKD-EPI eGFRcr at least 60 mL/min/1.73m² and no prior inpatient N17 code, a 15-unit lower delta = eGFRcys−eGFRcr predicts higher 10-year cumulative incidence of first hospitalized coded AKI after adjustment for eGFRcr and prespecified confounders, with a larger risk contrast at lower sex-specific grip strength.

The leading explanation is renal vulnerability missed by creatinine in people with low muscle reserve. The strongest rival is that discordance reflects inflammation, adiposity, smoking, diabetes, frailty, or generalized hospitalization/coding opportunity. This study tests prognostic separation, not mechanism or treatment effect.

## Supplied read-only inputs

Use UKB snapshot `d836bc0ca31c844b0462e1a293673818bfed046b8b0173bf360958169e8958a1`. The four ordinary CSVs are mounted read-only and join one-to-one on `eid`; overlapping identifiers must agree. Do not copy private row-level data into submitted reports.

| Table | Runtime path | Required fields |

Also estimate the low-minus-high-grip difference in the delta risk contrast, the cause-specific hazard ratio, and the delta×grip interaction, all with 95% confidence intervals. Never include eGFRcr, eGFRcys, and their algebraic difference in one model.
