Repeat the standardized discordance contrast for K35 and S72 as secondary outcomes, not adjustment variables. Report counts and joint uncertainty. Fit the scientifically substantive alternative using the same inputs: a competing-risk gradient-boosted survival model on one frozen participant-level 70/15/15 train/validation/test split stratified by AKI, death, and sex. Compare held-out calibration slope/intercept, integrated Brier score, time-dependent AUC, and decision curves against the Cox baseline. Separately compare the fully specified Cox model with its no-delta/no-grip baseline so any claimed incremental clinical utility is tied to the proposed information. Inspect stability of nonlinear delta×grip regions across bootstrap or frozen split repetitions. Retain the learned alternative only for reproducible nonlinearity or clinically relevant calibrated net benefit, never merely a small AUC increase. It cannot establish mechanism. Lock thresholds before fitting and compute classifications from estimates, never from whether the hypothesis is preferred.

Supportive results justify prospective prognostic enrichment and a future testing study, not causal benefit, measured GFR, a muscle mechanism, or treatment benefit. # Working proposal: pre-illness creatinine–cystatin C discordance, grip strength, and hospitalized AKI

Status: working design; the full hypothesis has not been tested. Aggregate feasibility and follow-up diagnostics are not inferential results.

## Scientific opening and falsifiable hypothesis

The strongest currently inspected evidence supports three bounded claims: large eGFRcys−eGFRcr differences are common in UK Biobank and have many non-GFR predictors [K1]; the difference is associated with frailty and broad adverse outcomes in SPRINT [K2]; and acute muscle loss can make creatinine eGFR substantially overestimate measured GFR during prolonged critical illness [K3]. None establishes that pre-illness discordance predicts incident AKI in generally ambulatory adults, that low grip modifies that association, or that cystatin-C testing prevents harm.

Primary hypothesis: among UK Biobank participants with baseline 2021 CKD-EPI eGFRcr >=60 mL/min/1.73m2 and no prior inpatient N17 code, a 15-unit lower eGFRcys−eGFRcr predicts a higher 10-year cumulative incidence of first hospitalized coded AKI after adjustment for eGFRcr and prespecified confounders. The discordance risk contrast is larger at lower sex-specific grip strength.

Leading explanation: discordance identifies renal vulnerability missed by creatinine in people with low muscle reserve. Strongest rival: discordance chiefly reflects inflammation, adiposity, smoking, diabetes, frailty, or generalized hospitalization/coding opportunity. This study tests prognostic separation, not a biological mechanism or treatment effect.

## Exact population, time, and data bindings

Use UKB snapshot d836bc0ca31c844b0462e1a293673818bfed046b8b0173bf360958169e8958a1. All sources are read-only ordinary CSV files, joined one-to-one on eid.

- population table, [private path], sex 31-0.0, age 21022-0.0.
- assessment table, [private path]; grip 46-0.0 and 47-0.0; waist 48-0.0; BMI 21001-0.0; ethnicity 21000-0.0; smoking 20116-0.0; diabetes 2443-0.0; BP 4079-0.0/.1 and 4080-0.0/.1.
- biological_samples table, [private path]), cystatin C 30720-0.0 (mg/L), CRP 30710-0.0, urine albumin 30500-0.0, urine creatinine 30510-0.0, glucose 30740-0.0, HbA1c 30750-0.0.
- health_outcomes table, [private path]; death dates 40000-0.0 and 40000-1.0.
- schema files: datasets/ukb/table-38565c9e35e7cb6c.json, table-901ef6c7ddce2d51.json, table-c6b666d905f3b02f.json, and table-3cfae45e0905b0e3.json.

Use baseline instance 0, plausible positive assays, maximum available hand grip, 2012 CKD-EPI eGFRcys and race-free 2021 CKD-EPI eGFRcr. Exclude prevalent/index-day N17 and validated kidney failure, dialysis, or transplant codes. Begin follow-up after a 30-day washout; primary event is the earliest normalized ICD-10 code beginning N17. Death competes.

A 10-year risk is estimable only if an authoritative inpatient linkage end date or a prespecified common supported horizon covers each participant. The local catalog explicitly says no source release/extraction timestamp is available. The aggregate audit found observed inpatient dates through 2022-10-31, but observed maxima alone cannot prove linkage completeness. Provider dates are nation- and release-specific; field 191-0.0 is only an early loss-to-follow-up flag for a small subset, not universal last contact. Follow to first event, death, 10 years, loss-to-follow-up where applicable, or this common end; require baseline on/before 2012-05-31 for the standardized 10-year risk.

## Estimand and analyses

Primary estimand: standardized cumulative-incidence difference and ratio at 10 years comparing delta=eGFRcys−eGFRcr of −15 versus 0 at eGFRcr 90, separately at sex-specific 25th and 75th grip percentiles. Report the cause-specific HR and delta×grip interaction with 95% confidence intervals. Never include eGFRcr, eGFRcys, and their algebraic difference in one model.

Baseline: cause-specific Cox model with splines, sequentially adding delta, grip, and delta×grip to eGFRcr plus age, sex, ethnicity, smoking, diabetes, BMI/waist, blood pressure, CRP, albuminuria, glycemia, assessment year, and center when verified. Use Aalen–Johansen/g-formula standardization, death as competing event, Fine–Gray sensitivity, bootstrap uncertainty, proportional-hazards checks, first-year exclusion, alternate discordance thresholds, and complete-case sensitivity after covariate-only imputation.

Ascertainment/frailty rival tests, treated as secondary outcomes rather than adjustment variables:

1. Repeat the standardized discordance contrast for first inpatient acute appendicitis (K35*) as a plausibly kidney-unrelated acute coded event; exclude prevalent/index-day K35.
2. Repeat it for first hip fracture (S72*) as a frailty-sensitive outcome; exclude prevalent/index-day S72. A similar association with both controls, especially without AKI specificity, weakens the renal-vulnerability interpretation; null controls strengthen specificity but cannot prove mechanism.
3. Report event counts and confidence intervals. Specificity is supportive only when AKI's lower confidence bound is >0 and each control estimate is smaller with an interval including 0. It is adverse when either control has lower bound >0 and a point estimate at least as large as AKI. It is inconclusive when control intervals cannot exclude an AKI-sized effect. Do not interpret imprecise null controls as reassuring.

Learned alternative: fit a same-input competing-risk gradient-boosted survival model on a frozen 70/15/15 participant split stratified by AKI, death, and sex. Compare held-out calibration slope/intercept, integrated Brier score, time-AUC, and decision curves with the Cox baseline; inspect stability of nonlinear delta×grip regions across bootstrap/split repetitions. The alternative is retained only if it reveals reproducible nonlinear interaction or clinically relevant calibrated net benefit, not a small AUC increase. It cannot establish mechanism. Disease-sequence learning is deferred unless prior event order materially confounds this estimand; latent trajectories lack repeated biomarker support; raw-image multimodal reproduction is unavailable and a lab-only variant does not add a distinct test.

Planning envelope: <=16 CPUs, <=128 GiB, <=8 hours; optional one A100 for repeated boosted fits. Prior full data scan was measured at about seven minutes on eight CPUs; model time is unverified. No GPU is scientifically required.

## Falsification and interpretation

Lock thresholds before fitting. Primary support requires the lower 95% confidence bound for the adjusted 10-year risk difference (delta −15 versus 0) to exceed 0. Clinical usefulness additionally requires its lower bound to exceed 0.5 percentage points and held-out calibration/decision utility to improve. An adverse result is an upper bound <=0; adverse for utility is an upper bound <0.5 points with no incremental utility. Intervals crossing these thresholds, unstable date pairing/splits, inadequate negative-control precision, or an unverifiable 10-year censor date are inconclusive. Apply the same directional rule to the low-versus-high grip contrast.

Required newly computed deliverables: attrition and missingness; code/date-pair audit; defensible follow-up endpoint decision; event counts; eGFR distributions; baseline coefficients and standardized risks; interaction and uncertainty; negative-control estimates; held-out performance/calibration/decision metrics; sensitivity analyses; and a machine-readable conclusion linked to outputs.

Supportive results justify prospective prognostic enrichment and testing research, not causal benefit, measured GFR, or a muscle mechanism. Adverse results argue against this stratification claim but not against cystatin C assay accuracy. Inconclusive results require deferral or a study with linkage metadata. Clinical adjudication/additional data are required for KDIGO AKI/stage, measured GFR, indications for testing, treatment response, and external transportability.

## Executed feasibility evidence, not hypothesis results

A managed full aggregate scan of all 502,370 outcome rows verified 259 code/date pairs, 84 unpaired or invalid cells, death fields 40000-0.0 and 40000-1.0, observed inpatient dates through 2022-10-31, and participant counts of 25,618 ever N17, 4,956 ever K35, and 7,041 ever S72. These counts establish field integrity and control-event support only; no exposure association was estimated.

## Key inspected works

[K1] Chen DC et al. Cystatin C- and Creatinine-based Estimated GFR Differences: Prevalence and Predictors in the UK Biobank. Kidney Medicine. 2024;6:100796. doi:10.1016/j.xkme.2024.100796. Inspected full-text XML, especially abstract, Introduction, Methods/Outcomes.

[K2] Potok OA et al. The Difference Between Cystatin C- and Creatinine-Based Estimated GFR and Associations With Frailty and Adverse Outcomes: A Cohort Analysis of SPRINT. American Journal of Kidney Diseases. 2020;76:765–774. doi:10.1053/j.ajkd.2020.05.017. Inspected PMC full-text passages on methods, hospitalizations, frailty, results, and limitations.

[K3] Haines RW et al. Comparison of Cystatin C and Creatinine in the Assessment of Measured Kidney Function during Critical Illness. Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology. 2023;18:997–1005. doi:10.2215/CJN.0000000000000203. Inspected PMC full-text passages on iohexol, muscle mass, estimates, and limitations.

Demonstration dispositions: a Delphi-style sequence model is deferred unless prior disease order changes this estimand; an ALADYNOULLI-style latent trajectory lacks repeated biomarker support; Oncoformer cannot be reproduced without images, and its lab-only adaptation does not answer a distinct uncertainty here.

If export linkage is absent, set status to unverified, do not fit or report 10-year models as valid, mark cox-results.json and learned-results.json not_run_release_unverified, and make every scientific conclusion inconclusive. This is a completed prerequisite audit, not a completed estimation study.

Automatic evaluation can check document presence and hash consistency but cannot establish provider authenticity or export linkage. Even a mechanically complete verified branch must state that linkage requires expert review.

## Cox/Aalen–Johansen baseline

When the release gate permits fitting, estimate cause-specific Cox hazards for N17 and death. Include eGFRcr, delta, sex-standardized grip, delta×grip, age, sex, raw categorical ethnicity/smoking/diabetes/center, assessment year, BMI, waist, averaged systolic and diastolic BP, CRP, glucose, HbA1c, and albuminuria only if units are verified. Use restricted cubic splines for continuous main effects with knots fixed at cohort 5th, 35th, 65th, and 95th percentiles. Never enter eGFRcr, eGFRcys, and their difference together. Impute covariates only, inside training/bootstrap samples; never impute exposures, outcomes, or dates. Include a complete-case sensitivity.

Aalen–Johansen curves are unadjusted descriptions. Obtain adjusted cumulative incidence by g-computation over the empirical covariate distribution using both cause-specific hazards. At eGFRcr=90, report standardized 10-year cumulative-incidence differences and ratios for delta −15 versus 0 separately at sex-specific 25th and 75th grip percentiles. Report cause-specific HRs, delta×grip interaction, participant-bootstrap 95% intervals, proportional-hazards diagnostics, first-year exclusion, alternative discordance definitions, Fine–Gray sensitivity, and primary-position N17 sensitivity.

Keep the primary AKI cohort unchanged. For direct specificity contrasts, create a secondary common-risk subset additionally free of K35 and S72 on or before day 30. Fit identical covariates, censoring, death competition, and contrasts for N17, K35, and S72 and standardize all to that same subset. Let theta_j be log standardized 10-year risk ratio for delta −15 versus 0 and D_j=theta_AKI−theta_j for j=K35,S72. Obtain joint participant-bootstrap intervals and repeat for the low-minus-high-grip modification contrast. Do not compare raw risk differences across outcomes.

## Learned alternative

On the same baseline inputs and common-risk subset, fit ten one-year intervals with a two-layer shared representation of 64 and 32 ReLU units, dropout 0.1, and task-specific yearly hazard heads for N17, K35, S72, and death. A nonfatal task remains at risk until its event, death, verified loss, or administrative end; one nonfatal event does not censor another task.

Use participant-level 70/15/15 train/validation/test splits stratified by sex and observed N17/death, seeds 20260923, 20260924, and 20260925. Tune only learning rate and L2 penalty on validation loss with early stopping. From cause-specific hazards compute the same intervention CIFs and D contrasts. On held-out data report calibration-in-the-large and slope at 10 years, IPCW integrated Brier score, time-dependent AUC, AKI decision curves, delta×grip surfaces, and a shared-head ablation constraining delta/grip effects across outcomes.

This alternative tests whether nonlinear delta–grip structure is shared across acute-admission/frailty outcomes or reproducibly AKI-specific. Retain it for interpretation only if calibration is acceptable, task-specific modeling improves held-out Brier score or net benefit, and D direction and interaction surface are stable across all three seeds. Otherwise mark it deferred and retain Cox/AJ inference. A small AUC gain alone is insufficient.

Planning envelope: at most 16 CPUs, 128 GiB, and 8 hours; one allocated A100 may be used for the learned model, with CPU fallback. The prior seven-minute outcome scan is measured; learned-model runtime is unverified.

## Outputs in /workspace

Write executable analysis code as analysis.py and create:

1. run-manifest.json: analysis ID, timestamps, exact source hashes, analysis.py hash, package versions, seeds, and read-only bindings.
2. censoring-provenance.json: release evidence and verified or unverified status.
3. codebook.json: normalization, exact prefix lists, 259 all-position pairs, 80 primary-position pairs, and clinician-review status.
4. field-audit.json: required-column presence, key uniqueness, pair validity, assay/date ranges, and unit checks.
5. cohort-flow.csv and missingness.csv: sequential counts for every inclusion/exclusion, imputation, common-risk restriction, and 10-year eligibility.
6. events.json: N17, K35, S72, and death counts overall and by age band and sex, overlaps, and control precision.
7. cox-results.json: fit status, coefficients, knots, PH tests, standardized CIF/RD/RR contrasts, interactions, joint bootstrap covariance/intervals, and all sensitivities.
8. learned-results.json: fit status, split hashes, architecture, hyperparameters, convergence, held-out metrics, ablation, intervention contrasts, and three-seed stability.
9. conclusion.json: labels and JSON-pointer-like evidence paths for primary_hypothesis, clinical_utility, renal_specificity_vs_K35, renal_specificity_vs_S72, measurement_sensitivity, effect_modification, and censoring_status.
10. report.md: claims linked to output cells and uncertainty, including supportive, adverse, and inconclusive interpretations.

### Minimum machine-readable contract

The verifier accepts additional fields but requires these paths and types:

- `run-manifest.json`: `analysis_sha256`, integer `seeds`, and `source_sha256` mapping the four target names `population.csv`, `assessment.csv`, `biological-samples.csv`, and `health-outcomes.csv` to their task hashes.
- `censoring-provenance.json`: `status` (`verified` or `unverified`), `document_path`, `document_sha256`, `source_uri`, `version`, `retrieved_at`, `linked_to_export`, `linkage_rationale`, `nation_completeness`, `common_end`, and `expert_review_status`. A verified status requires a readable document whose bytes match `document_sha256`, `linked_to_export=true`, the three frozen nation dates, common end `2022-05-31`, and nonempty linkage rationale; this remains subject to provider/expert adjudication.
- `codebook.json`: `normalization="uppercase_remove_punctuation"`, `outcome_prefixes`, `kidney_exclusion_prefixes`, `all_position_pairs=259`, `primary_position_pairs=80`, `egfr_equations`, and `clinician_review_status`.
- `field-audit.json`: `required_columns` as table-to-column-to-boolean mappings, `eid_unique` booleans, `row_counts` (502370 for each one-to-one source), `all_position_pairs`, `primary_position_pairs`, `invalid_or_unpaired_cells`, `unit_checks`, and `date_ranges`.
- `cohort-flow.csv`: columns `step,count` and named stages `source_rows`, `age_40_80`, `valid_sex_index_markers_grip`, `egfrcr_ge_60`, `no_prestart_n17_or_kidney_failure`, `analytic_cohort`, and `common_risk_subset`; `missingness.csv`: columns `variable,n_missing,n_total`. Counts must be nonnegative and internally possible.
- `events.json`: nonnegative integer counts under `overall` for `N17`, `K35`, `S72`, and `death`, plus `by_age_sex`, `overlaps`, and `control_precision`. N17, K35, and S72 must be nonzero for a completed source/cohort audit; zero-event endpoints require an explicit task revision because the frozen comparisons are not estimable.
- `cox-results.json`: `fit_status`. A completed fit additionally requires `coefficients`, `spline_knots`, `ph_tests`, `contrasts`, `joint_bootstrap`, and `sensitivities` containing `complete_case`, `first_year_exclusion`, `alternative_discordance`, `fine_gray`, and `primary_position_n17`. Every interval used for a conclusion must have finite numeric `estimate`, `lower`, and `upper` with `lower <= estimate <= upper`; risk-difference and D intervals are decimal-scale, not percentages. Also record `outcome_source_sha256`, `analysis_sha256`, and at least 200 completed participant-bootstrap replicates so fitted artifacts are provenance-bound. Put machine-used intervals in `decision_intervals` under names referenced by conclusion entries.
- `learned-results.json`: `fit_status`. A completed fit additionally requires `outcome_source_sha256` and `analysis_sha256` matching the submitted bindings and script, plus architecture `hidden_units=[64,32]`, `dropout=0.1`, ten yearly intervals, the three fixed seeds, split hashes, hyperparameters/convergence, held-out calibration/Brier/AUC/decision metrics, ablation, intervention contrasts, and stability.
- `conclusion.json`: each required conclusion is an object with `label`, `evidence_paths`, and `claim`. Allowed scientific labels are `supportive`, `adverse`, and `inconclusive`; `censoring_status.label` is `verified` or `unverified`. Evidence paths for automatically classified claims must point to named entries in `cox-results.json.decision_intervals`.

`analysis.py` must expose `normalize_icd(value)` and `compute_egfr(age, sex, creatinine_umol_l, cystatin_mg_l)` so bounded synthetic checks can test core preparation. It must be the actual script used for the submitted outputs, not a post hoc placeholder. The verifier's synthetic checks and artifact consistency checks are limited and do not reproduce the full study.

Use supportive/adverse/inconclusive labels, never confirmation language. For each AKI RD contrast, supportive requires lower 95% bound >0; adverse requires upper bound <=0; otherwise it is inconclusive. Clinical utility is supportive only when lower bound >0.005 and calibrated decision utility improves; it is adverse when upper bound <0.005 and no incremental utility exists; otherwise inconclusive. Renal specificity is supportive only when the corresponding D lower bound >0, adverse when its upper bound <=0, otherwise inconclusive. Wide intervals are inconclusive. Controls cannot rescue adverse AKI evidence. Measurement attenuation has no frozen numeric threshold and must be reported as a bounded sensitivity requiring expert interpretation, not automated mechanistic proof.

The report must explain patterns: smaller/null K35 with smaller positive S72 favors renal-plus-shared-frailty; similar AKI and K35 favors generalized admission/coding opportunity; similar AKI and S72 with smaller K35 favors shared frailty/reserve; attenuation for primary-position N17 favors coding artifact. These patterns bound interpretation and do not prove a mechanism.

## Evaluation boundary

The verifier checks hashes, field/code pairing, cohort invariants, equations recorded in the codebook, release-gate enforcement, presence of actual fitting artifacts, uncertainty, metric completeness, and consistency between numerical intervals and conclusion labels. It rejects favorable-answer shortcuts, stale hashes, malformed outputs, claims unsupported by their own intervals, and mechanistic or treatment claims.

It cannot validate the renal exclusion set, adjudicate KDIGO AKI/stage, establish release linkage, infer measured GFR or muscle mechanism, prove cystatin-C-guided benefit, or establish external transportability. Those require clinician/provider review, missing encounter/laboratory evidence, or another study.

## Key inspected works

[K1] Chen DC et al. “Cystatin C- and Creatinine-based Estimated GFR Differences: Prevalence and Predictors in the UK Biobank.” Kidney Medicine 2024;6:100796. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xkme.2024.100796

[K2] Potok OA et al. “The Difference Between Cystatin C- and Creatinine-Based Estimated GFR and Associations With Frailty and Adverse Outcomes: A Cohort Analysis of SPRINT.” American Journal of Kidney Diseases 2020;76:765–774. https://doi.org/10.1053/j.ajkd.2020.05.017

[K3] Haines RW et al. “Comparison of Cystatin C and Creatinine in the Assessment of Measured Kidney Function during Critical Illness.” Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology 2023;18:997–1005. https://doi.org/10.2215/CJN.0000000000000203

# Pre-illness creatinine–cystatin C discordance, grip strength, and hospitalized AKI: specificity and measurement stress test

Status: prospective study design; no exposure–outcome association has been fitted. This child preserves the parent’s primary population, 10-year estimand, and hypothesis, but makes the censoring gate, control roles, cross-outcome comparisons, measurement sensitivity, learned alternative, and solver outputs deterministic.

## Supported evidence, unresolved claim, and clinical advance

The strongest inspected evidence supports three bounded claims. Large eGFRcys−eGFRcr differences are common in UK Biobank and have multiple non-GFR predictors [K1]. Discordance is associated with frailty and broad adverse outcomes in SPRINT [K2]. During prolonged critical illness, muscle loss can make creatinine eGFR substantially overestimate measured GFR [K3]. These findings do not establish incident AKI prediction in ambulatory adults, a low-grip interaction, a muscle mechanism at baseline, or benefit from cystatin-C-guided care.

Unchanged primary hypothesis: among UK Biobank participants with baseline race-free 2021 CKD-EPI eGFRcr >=60 mL/min/1.73m2 and no prior inpatient N17 code, a 15-unit lower 2012 CKD-EPI eGFRcys minus eGFRcr predicts a higher 10-year cumulative incidence of first hospitalized coded AKI after adjustment for eGFRcr and prespecified covariates; the contrast is larger at lower sex-specific grip strength.

The leading interpretation is prognostic renal vulnerability obscured by creatinine in people with low muscle reserve. Rivals are: (R1) cystatin-C and creatinine non-GFR determinants, including inflammation, adiposity, smoking, diabetes, and muscle mass; (R2) generalized frailty; (R3) acute-admission or coding opportunity; and (R4) N17 measurement error or secondary-position coding during another illness. Resolution could justify prospective enrichment or a future cystatin-C-guided trial. It cannot establish true GFR, mechanism, or treatment benefit.

## Exact data binding

Use UKB snapshot `d836bc0ca31c844b0462e1a293673818bfed046b8b0173bf360958169e8958a1`. All sources are read-only CSV files, joined one-to-one on `eid`.

- `population`, `[private path]`, schema `datasets/ukb/table-38565c9e35e7cb6c.json`: `eid`, sex `31-0.0`, age at recruitment `21022-0.0`, and possible loss-to-follow-up date `191-0.0`.
- `assessment`, `[private path]`, schema `datasets/ukb/table-901ef6c7ddce2d51.json`: index date `53-0.0`, center `54-0.0`, grip `46-0.0` and `47-0.0`, waist `48-0.0`, BMI `21001-0.0`, ethnicity `21000-0.0`, smoking `20116-0.0`, diabetes `2443-0.0`, systolic BP `4080-0.0/.1`, and diastolic BP `4079-0.0/.1`.
- `biological_samples`, `[private path]`, schema `datasets/ukb/table-c6b666d905f3b02f.json`: creatinine `30700-0.0` (µmol/L), cystatin C `30720-0.0` (mg/L), CRP `30710-0.0`, urine albumin `30500-0.0`, urine creatinine `30510-0.0`, glucose `30740-0.0`, and HbA1c `30750-0.0`.
- `health_outcomes`, `[private path]`, schema `datasets/ukb/table-3cfae45e0905b0e3.json`: all-position ICD-10 `41270-0.0…258` paired by array index with first inpatient diagnosis date `41280-0.0…258`; primary-position sensitivity pair `41202-0.0…79` with `41262-0.0…79`; death dates `40000-0.0` and `40000-1.0`. The schema contains all named columns. These are first-recorded code dates, not encounter-level admission records.

The catalog records no source release/extraction timestamp and lacks most field coding dictionaries. Normalize ICD strings by uppercasing and removing punctuation only. Preserve unknown categorical codes as an explicit level; do not globally treat negative codes as missing. Average valid paired BP replicates, use maximum valid hand grip, and require positive creatinine and cystatin C. Compute urine albumin/creatinine ratio only after unit metadata is frozen; otherwise omit it and report that missing dependency rather than guess units.

## Population and temporal boundary

Use baseline instance 0; age 40–80; valid sex, index date, both kidney markers, and at least one grip value; eGFRcr >=60. Follow-up starts at index plus 30 days. Exclude any N17 code dated on or before follow-up start. Also exclude pre-start ICD-10 prefixes `N18.5`, `N18.6`, `Z49`, `Z94.0`, `Z99.2`, or `T86.1` as an operational kidney-failure/replacement set; a renal clinician must approve this set before clinical interpretation. Do not infer dialysis procedures without a separately adjudicated OPCS-4 list.

Primary outcome is earliest post-start all-position `N17*` date. Death is competing. Primary-position `N17*` from 41202/41262 is a prespecified measurement-specificity sensitivity, not a replacement outcome.

Administrative-censoring gate: before model fitting, freeze a provider/release document whose provenance can be linked to this export and that states inpatient completeness dates. If it validates England 2022-10-31, Scotland 2022-08-31, and Wales 2022-05-31, use the common end 2022-05-31 and require index <=2012-05-31 for 10-year risk. The observed inpatient maximum of 2022-10-31 and public reports of those dates are consistency checks only. If release matching is absent, `censoring_status=unverified`; no 10-year estimate may be labeled valid, and the scientific result is inconclusive. Field 191 may censor earlier only after its date semantics are verified.

## Cox/Aalen–Johansen baseline

Primary adjusted model: cause-specific Cox hazards for N17 and death. Use eGFRcr, delta=eGFRcys−eGFRcr, sex-standardized grip, delta×grip, age, sex, raw categorical ethnicity/smoking/diabetes/center, assessment year, BMI, waist, averaged BP, CRP, glycemia, and albuminuria when units are verified. Use restricted cubic splines with knots fixed at the 5th, 35th, 65th, and 95th cohort percentiles for continuous main effects. Never enter eGFRcr, eGFRcys, and their algebraic difference together. Impute covariates only, within training/bootstrap samples; do not impute exposure, outcome, or dates. Report complete-case sensitivity.

Aalen–Johansen curves are unadjusted descriptions. Adjusted cumulative incidence comes from g-computation over the empirical covariate distribution using both fitted cause-specific hazards. The unchanged estimand is the standardized 10-year cumulative-incidence difference and ratio for delta −15 versus 0 at eGFRcr 90, separately at the sex-specific 25th and 75th grip percentiles. Report cause-specific HRs, the delta×grip interaction, 95% bootstrap intervals, proportional-hazards diagnostics, first-year exclusion, alternative discordance definitions, Fine–Gray sensitivity, and the primary-position N17 sensitivity.

## Control-outcome logic

Appendicitis and hip fracture are complementary but not interchangeable controls.

- First inpatient `K35*` is a negative-control outcome for a broad acute-admission/coding-opportunity association. It is imperfect: its age/sex pattern differs from AKI and it does not measure longitudinal admission frequency, lab surveillance, or nephrotoxic exposure.
- First inpatient `S72*` is a frailty-sensitive rival outcome, not a negative control. Low grip and generalized vulnerability can genuinely predict hip fracture, so requiring a null S72 association would contradict the purpose of the control.
- The available first-diagnosis arrays lack encounter identifiers and repeated admissions. Therefore neither control can falsify differential renal testing or coding within a hospitalization. That interpretation requires episode-level HES/admission records or adjudication and is unavailable here.

Keep the primary AKI cohort unchanged. For direct specificity contrasts, create a secondary common-risk subset that additionally has no K35 or S72 date on/before day 30. Fit the same covariates, censoring rule, death competitor, and 10-year contrasts for all three outcomes. Standardize all outcomes to this same subset. Because baseline incidences differ, do not compare raw risk differences across outcomes. Let theta_j be the log standardized 10-year risk ratio for delta −15 versus 0 and D_j=theta_AKI−theta_j for j=K35,S72; obtain joint participant-bootstrap intervals. Repeat for the low-minus-high-grip modification contrast.

Interpretation is two-dimensional:

- Primary prognostic support: AKI risk-difference lower 95% bound >0. Clinical usefulness additionally requires lower bound >0.5 percentage points.
- Renal specificity supported relative to a control only if the corresponding D lower bound >0; adverse relative to that control if D upper bound <=0; otherwise inconclusive. A wide control interval is inconclusive, not reassuring.
- AKI positive, K35 null/smaller, and S72 positive but smaller favors a renal-plus-shared-frailty interpretation.
- AKI and K35 effects of similar size favor generalized acute-admission/coding opportunity.
- AKI and S72 effects of similar size, with K35 smaller, favor shared frailty/physiological reserve.
- Primary-position N17 materially attenuated toward the controls favors outcome-coding artifact.
- AKI upper 95% risk-difference bound <=0 is adverse for the primary hypothesis regardless of controls. Controls never rescue a null AKI result.

These rules bound interpretation; they do not prove a muscle or renal mechanism.

## Scientifically substantive learned alternative

Fit a multi-task discrete-time survival model on the same baseline inputs and the same common-risk subset. Construct ten one-year intervals. A two-layer shared neural representation (64 and 32 ReLU units, dropout 0.1) feeds task-specific yearly hazard heads for N17, K35, S72, and death. Nonfatal heads remain at risk until their own event, death, loss, or administrative end; one nonfatal control does not censor another. Use participant-level 70/15/15 train/validation/test splitting, stratified by sex and observed N17/death status, fixed seed 20260923; tune only learning rate and L2 penalty on validation loss, with early stopping. Repeat seeds 20260923, 20260924, and 20260925 as a stability analysis.

From predicted cause-specific hazards, compute each endpoint’s cumulative incidence under the same delta/grip interventions and empirical standardization as the Cox model. Compare held-out calibration-in-the-large and slope at 10 years, IPCW integrated Brier score, time-dependent AUC, and AKI decision curves. Report the cross-outcome D contrasts and delta×grip surface across seeds. A shared-head ablation that constrains delta/grip effects across outcomes tests whether task-specific structure materially improves held-out loss and specificity contrasts.

This alternative answers a scientific question the Cox baseline loses: whether nonlinear delta–grip risk structure is shared across frailty/acute-admission outcomes or is reproducibly AKI-specific. It is not selected for the primary claim merely for a small AUC gain. Retain it only if calibration is acceptable, the task-specific model improves held-out Brier score or net benefit, and the direction of D and the interaction surface is stable across all three seeds. Otherwise defer it and retain Cox/AJ inference. A latent true-GFR mechanistic model is not identifiable from two baseline filtration markers without measured GFR or validated repeat measurement error and is explicitly rejected.

Planning envelope: preprocessing and Cox/AJ on <=16 CPUs and <=128 GiB; multi-task fitting on one allocated A100 (or CPU fallback) with <=16 CPUs, <=128 GiB, <=8 hours. The earlier full outcome scan was measured at about seven minutes on eight CPUs. Learned-model time is unverified; GPU capacity is available but not scientifically required.

## Falsification and exact solver deliverables

The primary result is supportive only if its lower 95% bound exceeds 0; clinically useful only if it also exceeds 0.5 percentage points and calibrated decision utility improves. It is adverse if its upper bound is <=0, and adverse for utility if its upper bound is <0.5 points with no incremental utility. Crossing intervals, unstable models, inadequate control precision, invalid code/date pairing, or unverified censoring are inconclusive.

Required new outputs:

1. `run-manifest.json`: source SHA-256 values, script hash, package versions, seeds, and read-only bindings.
2. `censoring-provenance.json`: provider document URI/path, byte hash, version/retrieval time, release-match rationale, nation-specific dates, chosen common end, and `verified|unverified`. Unverified status must force an inconclusive conclusion.
3. `codebook.json`: exact normalization, N17/K35/S72 and kidney-exclusion prefix lists, all-position and primary-position array ranges, and clinician-review status.
4. `field-audit.json`: all required columns, pair counts, invalid/unpaired cells, assay/date ranges, and explicit unit checks.
5. `cohort-flow.csv` and `missingness.csv`: sequential counts for every inclusion, exclusion, imputation, common-risk restriction, and 10-year eligibility.
6. `events.json`: outcome and competing-death counts overall and by age band/sex, with overlap counts and effective control precision.
7. `cox-results.json`: coefficients, knots, PH tests, standardized CIF/RD/RR contrasts, interactions, joint bootstrap covariance/intervals, and sensitivities.
8. `learned-results.json`: split hashes, architecture/hyperparameters, convergence, calibration/Brier/AUC/decision metrics, ablation, intervention contrasts, and three-seed stability.
9. `conclusion.json`: separate `primary_hypothesis`, `clinical_utility`, `renal_specificity_vs_K35`, `renal_specificity_vs_S72`, `measurement_sensitivity`, and `censoring_status` labels, each with pointers to computed cells.
10. `report.md`: claims linked to outputs and uncertainty, including adverse and inconclusive interpretations.

An automatic verifier can check source hashes, field pairing, equations, cohort logic, censoring gate enforcement, model outputs, uncertainty, and consistency of conclusion labels with numerical rules. It cannot establish release matching from an unversioned current webpage, validate the clinical code set, adjudicate KDIGO AKI/stage, infer measured GFR or muscle mechanism, prove testing benefit, or establish external transportability.

## Bounded feasibility evidence

The parent’s aggregate audit observed 502,370 outcome rows, all 259 all-position ICD/date pairs, 84 invalid or unpaired cells, inpatient dates through 2022-10-31, and all-time counts of 25,618 N17, 4,956 K35, and 7,041 S72. The current schema audit additionally verifies all 80 primary-position 41202/41262 pairs and all named baseline fields. A separate bounded audit has been submitted to measure cohort-specific event support without fitting any exposure association; until it completes, only the parent’s all-time counts are observed. These are feasibility checks, not hypothesis results.

## Key inspected works

[K1] Chen DC et al. *Cystatin C- and Creatinine-based Estimated GFR Differences: Prevalence and Predictors in the UK Biobank.* Kidney Medicine. 2024;6:100796. doi:10.1016/j.xkme.2024.100796. Full-text XML inspected.

[K2] Potok OA et al. *The Difference Between Cystatin C- and Creatinine-Based Estimated GFR and Associations With Frailty and Adverse Outcomes: A Cohort Analysis of SPRINT.* American Journal of Kidney Diseases. 2020;76:765–774. doi:10.1053/j.ajkd.2020.05.017. PMC full text inspected.

[K3] Haines RW et al. *Comparison of Cystatin C and Creatinine in the Assessment of Measured Kidney Function during Critical Illness.* Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology. 2023;18:997–1005. doi:10.2215/CJN.0000000000000203. PMC full text inspected.

# Day-60 HCC marker-versus-injury ascertainment after resection

## Objective and evidence boundary

Conduct the frozen route-B investigation of informative measurement and management after first observed HCC resection. You must newly extract the cohort and fit a transparent baseline and a scientifically matched longitudinal alternative on the same patients, outcomes, covariates, and frozen patient split. Produce the required computational evidence and classify the result as `supportive`, `adverse`, or `inconclusive` using the rules below. Confirmation is not rewarded; a correctly computed adverse or inconclusive result is equally valid.

The strongest prior evidence supports only this claim: in 549 selected resected HCC patients with preoperative AFP >400 ng/mL, incomplete AFP response at 4–6 weeks was associated with worse recurrence-free and overall survival [K1]. It does not establish residual tumor. Persistent postoperative AFP without detected recurrence has been reported [K3], and postoperative TACE can have adjuvant or lesion-detection roles rather than denote recurrence [K2].

The unresolved biological route-A claim is whether a day-60 AFP/PIVKA-II component, separated from injury, predicts subsequently detected untreated tumor. It is not estimable in this snapshot and must not be fitted: a frozen source audit found only 18 first untreated reports in the broad marker cohort (8 lexical affirmative, 3 explicitly nonpositive, 1 uncertain, 6 unclassified; one report each in validation and locked test), far below the adjudicated-content gate.

The selected, falsifiable route-B hypothesis is that among first observed HCC resections without recorded HCC-directed therapy through day 60, availability and apparent prognostic association of day-60 marker trajectories are materially shaped by informative measurement and management. Specifically, remeasurement, first imaging, and treatment-intent transitions depend on prior contact, marker/injury history, and latent injury state, and complete-case marker associations attenuate or change after jointly modeling observation intensity.

This is a complete route-B investigation, not a prediction-only benchmark or prerequisite audit. The scientific deliverable is a newly computed cohort flow and data audit; newly fitted matched baseline and longitudinal models; uncertainty, diagnostics, sensitivities, and negative controls; and a conclusion traceable to computed outputs. It estimates ascertainment. It does not estimate recurrence, treatment effect, biological tumor state, or benefit from surveillance.

## Read-only data bindings

All files are ordinary UTF-8 CSVs from HCC snapshot `3f97e661e1884c34c1e2cdbf74ba0cf6d6c8995853e85f1857c3d72b82ccf521`; there are no archive members. Treat `/data` as read-only and keep derived data in `/workspace`.

| Table | Runtime path | Required source columns | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `encounters` | `/data/encounters.csv` | `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `年龄`, `性别`, `就诊时间`, `入院时间`, `出院时间`, `就诊科室` | Encounter spine, demographics, contact clock. Encounter date is admission, else visit, else discharge. |

| `diagnoses` | `/data/diagnoses.csv` | `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `诊断名称`, `诊断类型` | Same-encounter HCC support and recurrence-intent text; inherits encounter date because it has no native time. |

# Day-60 HCC marker-versus-injury ascertainment after resection

Status: reference-complete crossover child. A bounded source audit resolved the parents’ decisive feasibility objection. The disease-content route is retained as a frozen gate but is not authorized for fitting: even a deliberately broad, procedure-only “untreated” upper-bound cohort produced 18 first liver CT/MRI reports before later treatment. The executable deliverable is therefore the ascertainment/measurement study (route B). No biomarker or outcome model has been fitted.

## Scientific opening, claim boundary, and advance

The strongest supported claim is that AFP response at the 4–6-week postoperative visit is prognostic for recurrence and survival in a selected cohort of 549 resected HCC patients with preoperative AFP >400 ng/mL [K1]. This does not show that persistent AFP is residual tumor. A documented patient had persistent postoperative AFP with repeated imaging showing no recurrence over two years [K3]. Postoperative treatment is also not a recurrence label: a current randomized protocol assigns high-risk, apparently curatively resected patients to adjuvant TACE versus intensive follow-up, and notes that TACE’s angiographic component may itself detect occult lesions [K2].

The unresolved biological claim is whether an AFP/PIVKA-II component at day 60, separated from postoperative liver injury, carries information about subsequently detected untreated tumor. Its leading interpretation is persistent tumor-associated signal. Its strongest rival is a compound process: injury/regeneration changes AFP, assay/calendar and vitamin-K-related effects alter measurements, clinicians selectively remeasure or image concerning patients, treatment is selected before imaging, and outside surveillance is missing.

The available snapshot cannot adequately test the biological claim. The substantive advance is instead to quantify the observation mechanism that makes that claim non-identifiable here: whether marker and injury trajectories, their missingness, and prior clinical contact predict who is remeasured, imaged, or treated and how treatment intent changes the apparent endpoint. This can prevent an EHR-derived “recurrence” score from confusing tumor biology with care selection and specifies the prospective evidence needed to reopen the clinical question.

## Hypotheses and selected deliverable

Biological hypothesis retained but not currently estimable (route A): among patients with a first observed HCC resection and no HCC-directed therapy through day 60, a day-60 marker-persistence state (M_i(60)), separated from an injury-recovery state (I_i(60)), predicts an affirmative versus explicitly nonpositive first liver CT/MRI report obtained before later treatment, more strongly than it predicts imaging or treatment occurrence.

Selected ascertainment hypothesis (route B): among first observed HCC resections without recorded HCC-directed therapy through day 60, the availability and apparent prognostic association of day-60 tumor-marker trajectories are materially shaped by informative measurement and management. Specifically, models that jointly represent marker/injury values and observation intensity will show that remeasurement, first imaging, and treatment-intent transitions depend on prior contact, marker/injury measurement history, and latent injury state; complete-case marker associations will attenuate or change after this process is modeled.

The route-B scientific deliverable is newly fitted, same-split baseline and longitudinal models that produce: a frozen cohort flow; assay/specimen/calendar and missingness audit; marker-versus-injury measurement-state frequencies through day 60; post-landmark marker/injury remeasurement intensities; first S/T/D/C transition incidences with T intent marks; baseline and joint-model coefficients, calibration and uncertainty; latent-state/loadings and identifiability diagnostics; complete-case versus observation-aware contrasts; negative controls; and a conclusion mapped to supportive, adverse, or inconclusive criteria. It estimates ascertainment, not recurrence, treatment effect, or biological tumor state.

## Decisive bounded audit

The new aggregate-only audit read the HCC source snapshot directly. It defined an adult’s earliest dated liver resection in 2012–2023 in the same encounter as a non-uncertain HCC diagnosis, excluded transplant/donor/biopsy/puncture/cyst/recurrent-procedure wording, required surgery within 30 days of the encounter date, and deduplicated all index-encounter procedure rows.

Lexical feasibility labels were 8 affirmative, 3 explicitly nonpositive, 1 uncertain, and 6 unclassified; validation and locked-test each contained only one report. The pathology-supported broad cohort had 13 first untreated scans; excluding prior procedure treatment left 17; the parent-like cohort had 15.

These are upper bounds because the audit ignored medication-defined HCC therapy. It did not clinically adjudicate pathology, scan purpose, report content, treatment intent, or outside care. A marker-persistence state (M_i(t)), allowed to clear, plateau, or rise, loads on AFP and optional PIVKA-II/AFP-L3; AFP may load on both. Observation submodels include exact label/specimen, calendar-era offsets, censoring, missingness masks, and vitamin-K/warfarin/antibiotic flags. Shared random effects link (M_i(60)), (I_i(60)), measurement intensities, prior contact, and baseline covariates to L-M/L-I and S/marked-T intensities.

The alternative can reveal whether an apparent marker component predicts values, the act of measurement, surveillance, or treatment selection; the baseline loses this distinction. It cannot make either latent state biologically “tumor.” Compare constrained/unconstrained two-factor fits, leave-one-marker-out and AFP-only fits, three seeds, posterior predictive checks, factor-swap checks, and simulated recovery of known states. A multivariate functional-PCA plus the same transition models is the CPU fallback if the joint model is non-identifiable. A generic transformer is deferred because flexible prediction does not resolve the observation-process rival.

## Gates, evaluation, and falsification

Route A remains frozen and may be reopened only by a new source or prospective collection meeting all of: ≥300 first untreated S reports; ≥100 blinded-review affirmative and ≥100 explicit-negative reports; ≥20 of each in locked test; PPV and NPV ≥0.85 after adjudication; and adequate paired day-60 marker/injury support. No resampling, report-text rescue, treatment-as-recurrence substitution, or test-set pooling can satisfy this gate.

Route B proceeds only after the full procedure-plus-medication cohort extraction confirms ≥500 eligible patients, ≥150 S-or-T transitions overall, ≥30 transitions in train/validation/test, and ≥100 participants per nonempty day-60 measurement-state category used for inference. The joint state model additionally requires ≥500 participants with at least two distinct pre-landmark observation dates and simulation recovery correlation ≥0.8 without factor swapping. If it fails, the baseline measurement audit remains the deliverable and latent-state claims are inconclusive.

Evaluate weekly observation-rate calibration, time-dependent Brier score and calibration for S/T, multinomial log loss/calibration, held-out likelihood, state/loadings and seed stability, and paired participant bootstrap 95% intervals. Primary scientific contrasts are: complete-case versus observation-aware marker coefficients; marker-state versus injury-state associations with L-M/L-I, S, and each T intent mark; and change in calibration after adding observation intensity. Sensitivities include pathology-supported, no-prior-treatment, calendar era, AFP-only, PIVKA medication-restricted, strict versus expanded imaging, and generic nonhepatic imaging/contact negative controls. Report weight tails and effective sample size; inverse-probability weighting is a sensitivity, not a cure for absent outcomes.

Support for the route-B hypothesis requires stable state separation plus materially different observation/transition hazards by measurement history or latent injury state, and attenuation or sign change of the complete-case marker association after joint observation modeling, with paired 95% intervals excluding no change and consistent direction across calendar/no-prior-treatment sensitivities. This supports an informative-ascertainment warning, not tumor biology.

Adverse evidence is stable near-null observation-intensity effects, unchanged calibrated marker associations after observation modeling, and no association with generic contact or treatment-selection states. This weakens the proposed ascertainment explanation but still cannot support the biological hypothesis because route A failed.

Inconclusive evidence includes failed route-B support gates, nonpositivity/effective sample size <50%, unstable/factor-swapped states, incompatible assay eras, intent-rule PPV/NPV <0.85, unavailable clinical review, or intervals spanning meaningful attenuation and amplification. Such a result means this snapshot cannot quantify either biological decoupling or ascertainment reliably.

Computationally checkable claims are source/schema hashes, joins, dates, cohort flow, procedure-episode deduplication, measurement-state and S/T/D/C construction, split isolation, model fits, diagnostics, metrics, uncertainty, and whether the reported conclusion follows the thresholds. Curative intent, true recurrence, outside care, assay equivalence, treatment intent, latent-state biology, and benefit from earlier imaging require hepatobiliary/radiology review, assay metadata, linked external records, or a prospective scheduled-imaging study. An automatic verifier must not certify them.

## Resources and alternatives retained

Measured extraction: 4 CPUs/64 GiB requested, 125.9 seconds for the bounded multi-gigabyte audit. Planned route-B extraction, label audits, baseline, bootstrap, and functional-PCA fallback: 8–16 CPUs, 64 GiB, 1–2 hours. Planned three-seed joint model: one allocated A100, 8 CPUs, 64 GiB, 2–4 hours, unmeasured. Total fits within the configured 8-hour, 16-CPU/8-GPU/256-GiB solver envelope. GPU is a throughput choice, not scientific merit.

Alternatives not selected:

- Route A untreated-report content: scientifically preferred but deferred by the observed 18-report upper bound; revisit with scheduled CT/MRI or linked external imaging plus adjudication.
- Composite recurrence-management outcome: rejected because adjuvant/diagnostic treatment and record absence are not recurrence.
- Interval-censored biological onset: rejected without serial credible negative scans.
- IPW alone: retained as sensitivity; it cannot repair structural absence or positivity failure.
- Generic transformer: revisit only after adequate adjudicated content and evidence of residual nonlinear sequence information.

## Compact bibliography

[K1] Liang L, Wang MD, Zhang YM, et al. Association of Postoperative Biomarker Response with Recurrence and Survival in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma and High Alpha-Fetoprotein Expressions (>400 ng/ml). *Journal of Hepatocellular Carcinoma*. 2021;8:103–118. doi:10.2147/JHC.S289840.

[K2] Huang CM, Chen SC, Yan YH, et al. Efficacy and safety of adjuvant transarterial chemoembolization in high-risk HCC after curative hepatectomy: a phase III RCT protocol. *iLIVER*. 2026;5(2):100236. doi:10.1016/j.iliver.2026.100236. Protocol; no results.

[K3] Di Carlo I, Mannino M, Toro A, et al. Persistent increase in alpha-fetoprotein level in a patient without underlying liver disease who underwent curative resection of hepatocellular carcinoma: a case report and review of the literature. *World Journal of Surgical Oncology*. 2012;10:79. doi:10.1186/1477-7819-10-79.
