They omit `hospitalid`, hospital attributes, the algorithm label, source-stratum label, and derived model predictions. Reviewers see source names because clinical interpretation requires them, but not which source triggered the algorithm.

Prespecified source signatures are: historical interval only; interval plus invasive airway; explicit RT off; ventilator-to-noninvasive/room-air device transition; treatment-only corroboration; multiple concordant sources; and negative windows with (a) abrupt cessation of previously regular invasive settings, (b) airway/device change not meeting v1, (c) weaning/reintubation text only, or (d) no liberation sentinel. Hospital volume and respiratory-documentation density terciles are crossed with these signatures.

### Phase I: rule development, excluded from performance estimation

Two ICU clinicians independently review 240 windows: 120 A=1 and 120 A=0, balanced over hospital-volume/documentation terciles and source signatures, with no more than one window per person. They classify IMV at L, provisional liberation time as an interval, 48-hour reinstitution, D/X/tracheostomy, and sustained liberation as **definite**, **probable**, **definitely absent**, or **indeterminate because eICU evidence is insufficient**. A third clinician resolves disagreements after recording initial labels.

The team may revise v0 once using only Phase I. It must publish the changed rule, disagreement taxonomy, and expected direction of each change. Phase-I packets never enter final accuracy estimates. Then freeze v1, the full sampling frame, random seed, inclusion probabilities, packet generator, manual, and source strata.

### Phase II: independent hospital-stratified validation

For every hospital with at least 50 index episodes:

- Review a stratified probability sample of (min(40,N_{h,+})) A=1 windows, allocating at least five where available to each represented source signature and retaining exact inclusion probabilities.
- Review every A=0 window if their total is at most 1,200 (the inherited provisional audit suggests about 553). If there are more than 1,200, review a fixed 1,200-window stratified probability sample with at least 24 per hospital where available, one random base component plus sentinel-enriched components, and retain Horvitz-Thompson weights. This cap is fixed before labels are seen.
- One ICU clinician reviews every packet. A blinded 30% random replicate, every probable/indeterminate packet, and every packet with logically discordant transition labels receives a second independent review; a third clinician arbitrates after initial labels are locked.
- Report raw and weighted counts, effective sample size, packet exclusions, review time, pairwise agreement, prevalence-adjusted agreement, and kappa for each component. No hospital identifiers appear in reviewer materials or public outputs.

For hospital (h), let weighted counts (D_{ah},N_{ah},U_{ah}) denote definite/probable event, definitely absent, and indeterminate reference states within algorithm stratum (A=a). “Probable” is included with definite only in the central estimate and moved to U in the conservative analysis. Design-weighted central sensitivity, PPV, specificity, and NPV are reported. Without pretending U is resolved, partial-identification intervals include:

- (PPV_h in [D_{1h}/T_{1h},(D_{1h}+U_{1h})/T_{1h}]);
- (Se_h in [D_{1h}/(D_{1h}+D_{0h}+U_{0h}), (D_{1h}+U_{1h})/(D_{1h}+U_{1h}+D_{0h})]);
- analogous specificity bounds obtained by interchanging definite event/absence and A strata.

Use survey-weighted hospital/person-cluster bootstrap with simultaneous 95% intervals. Also report event-time agreement within 6 and 12 hours and hospital-specific median signed timing error.

The transparent measurement baseline M0 is these design-weighted confusion tables and worst-case bounds. The scientifically substantive alternative M1 is a clinician-anchored hierarchical Bayesian observation model: source indicators and their interactions generate the observed algorithm/source pattern conditional on latent S; hospital random effects are estimated separately for sensitivity and false-positive probability; adjudicated windows anchor the latent state; sampling weights enter a pseudo-likelihood; and weakly informative priors are fixed before Phase II. M1 can reveal whether apparent misses track a source mix or an irreducible hospital effect that M0 aggregates away. It is admissible only if posterior predictive checks reproduce weighted source-by-hospital confusion tables and its conclusions lie within M0 partial-identification bounds; it cannot “rescue” a failed M0 gate.

For each validation bootstrap/posterior draw and true event prevalence (p) over the observed adjudication-supported range, compute the observed event probability expected under identical recovery but hospital-specific ascertainment:
(q_h(p)=Se_h p+(1-Sp_h)(1-p)).
Define (Delta_{asc}) as the maximum over p of the hospital P90-P10 of (q_h(p)). This translates sensitivity/specificity differences into the same absolute-risk scale as the recovery estimand.

### Gate fixed before recovery modeling

No hospital recovery random effect, P90-P10 recovery contrast, hospital ranking, or Model B/L fit may be computed or viewed until all of the following pass on Phase II alone:

1. sustained-liberation central PPV and sensitivity and landmark-IMV PPV are each at least 0.85, with pooled simultaneous lower 95% bounds at least 0.80; the indexed-window design does not claim landmark-IMV sensitivity;
2. every retained hospital has conservative lower 95% bounds at least 0.70 for both PPV and sensitivity, and at least 20 reviewed A=1 windows plus either an A=0 census or weighted A=0 effective sample size at least 20;
3. the simultaneous 95% upper bound for (Delta_{asc}) is at most 5 absolute percentage points under both M0 bounds and admissible M1;
4. no source signature has a sensitivity difference whose simultaneous upper bound exceeds 10 points after hospital adjustment; no one source produces more than 90% of endpoints in more than 25% of retained hospitals;
5. indeterminate reference status is at most 10% overall and 20% in every retained hospital; median signed timing error is within ±6 hours in every hospital and the hospital P90-P10 timing-bias spread is at most 12 hours;
6. kappa is at least 0.70 for sustained liberation and reinstitution; at least 30 hospitals retain at least 50 index cases and 20 adjudication-compatible endpoints.

Failure of any item ends the hospital-recovery branch. Report a measurement-only result, including whether failure arose from low PPV, low sensitivity, differential source ascertainment, timing, imprecision, or insufficient hospitals. Do not relax thresholds, inspect recovery contrasts, replace the outcome with `actualventdays`, merge sites, or drop adverse hospitals after seeing labels. If M0 passes but M1 fails calibration, proceed only with M0-based correction; if M0 fails, M1 cannot override it.

## Common recovery inputs, split, and measurement correction

After a pass, both recovery models use identical fixed demographics/admission/APACHE/EOL variables and four six-hour bins from t0 to L containing respiratory settings, oxygenation/ventilation, vital signs, selected labs, sedative/opioid/pressor exposure, measurement counts, missingness masks, time since last observation, and chart-entry delay. The transparent model receives prespecified first/last/min/max, slope, area-outside-range, and observation-count summaries; the learned model receives the same binned tensor and masks. Neither receives post-L physiology, `actualventdays`, outcome-period discharge destination, hospital volume, or an outcome-derived feature.

Assign five folds by deterministic hash of `uniquepid`, stratified so every hospital contributes to each fold. Fit units, plausibility/winsorization limits, imputation, feature selection, hyperparameters, and the measurement calibration on training data or the separately adjudicated validation set only. No patient's repeated stays cross folds. Keep the same folds for both models.

The frozen adjudication model supplies hospital/source-specific emission probabilities for reconstructed P/S/R labels. Primary Model B and L fits use either a joint latent-state likelihood or at least 200 multiple imputations of true transitions from those emissions; combine model and sampling uncertainty and nest the hospital/person bootstrap outside imputation. The naive v1 label analysis is a labeled sensitivity only. Recovery support must hold over the entire admissible M0 partial-identification region, not merely M1 posterior means.

## Model B: transparent competing-risk multistate baseline

Preserve the hierarchical semi-Markov piecewise-exponential model for V→P, P→S, P→R, R→P, and V/P/R→D or X, plus tracheostomy, with six-hour intervals for days 1–3 and daily intervals thereafter. Use prespecified restricted cubic splines for continuous baseline summaries, diagnosis group and unit type, and partially pooled hospital random intercepts for each transition. Integrate over the adjudication-calibrated emission model. Standardize 14-day state occupation by g-computation over the pooled baseline distribution. Report coefficients, shrinkage, P90-P10 contrasts, and nested bootstrap/imputation intervals.

Model B is interpretable and keeps competing paths explicit, but loses within-day order, nonlinear covariation, and observation dynamics beyond summaries.

## Model L: structured learned longitudinal alternative

Preserve the two-layer, 64-hidden-unit GRU with dropout 0.2 over the four six-hour bins. It outputs:

1. a physiologic recovery state, supervised by next-bin respiratory burden (FiO2, PEEP, pressure/volume, SpO2/PaO2, vasopressor, neurologic summaries); and
2. an observation state, supervised by next-bin label availability, counts, and entry delays.

Both states and fixed covariates feed the same calibrated semi-Markov transitions as Model B. A gradient-reversal penalty suppresses hospital prediction from the physiologic state conditional on case mix; the observation state may encode workflow. Hospital effects appear only in transition heads, not patient embeddings. Tune on training folds lexicographically: multistate likelihood/calibration first, then leakage, never desired heterogeneity. Reject Model L if hospital macro-AUROC from the physiologic state exceeds 0.65, state calibration materially worsens, or the observation model contradicts adjudicated source errors. Ablate observation state, recovery state, adversary, and missingness/count inputs.

Model L can test whether nonlinear temporal ordering and explicit observation dynamics account for variation that Model B attributes to hospital context. It does not discover a biological mechanism. The recovery hypothesis requires both admissible models; a technically failed L permits a valid baseline analysis but not the two-model persistence claim.

## Evaluation, falsification, and interpretation

Held-out evaluation includes integrated Brier score, transition likelihood, state calibration at days 3/7/14, 48-hour R discrimination/calibration, standardized S/D/X/R/tracheostomy/ventilated risks, P90-P10 and hospital random-effect uncertainty, fold stability, and subgroup results by age, sex, broad race/ethnicity, surgical/medical status, and baseline severity. Sensitivities include strict dual-source episodes, source-balanced reweighting, timing perturbations drawn from adjudicated intervals, 72-hour and seven-day sustain, exclusion of pre-L EOL records, and profiling the full admissible measurement bounds. Use 1,000 nested cluster bootstraps sampling hospitals then people.

- **Supportive:** the measurement gate passes; both corrected admissible models show P90-P10 S-risk at least 10 points with lower 95% bound above 5 over all admissible measurement parameters; fold and primary-sensitivity ordering Spearman is at least 0.70; source-balanced/strict dual-source directions persist; and no D/X/R/tracheostomy tradeoff explains the apparent advantage. This supports persistent adjusted hospital-context heterogeneity in eICU-documented sustained liberation, not causation or quality. If Model L reduces Model B hospital variance by at least 25% while residual support remains, nonlinear pre-landmark trajectory/observation information explains part of the descriptive variation.
- **Adverse/falsifying:** the measurement gate fails; or after a pass either admissible model has contrast below 5 points/interval including zero, unstable ordering, reversal under measurement bounds/source balancing/timing, a compensating rise in D/X/R, or failed learned-model leakage/calibration. Conclude that eICU does not support a stable recovery difference; differential ascertainment, case mix, competing outcomes, or model instability is the stronger explanation.
- **Inconclusive:** measurement bounds span both admissible and inadmissible comparability, fewer than 30 hospitals remain, corrected intervals span both <5 and ≥10 points, models materially disagree without a resolved diagnostic, or reviewer uncertainty is too high. Report precisely what additional adjudication or source data could narrow the result; do not call an imprecise null falsification.
- **Measurement-only:** low or differential sensitivity/PPV, source dependence, or timing error blocks recovery modeling. This is a substantive result about nonportable eICU ventilation ascertainment.

Even a supportive association cannot identify weaning, sedation, mobility, staffing, or other practices as causes. Causal or quality conclusions require reliable time-varying practice measures, readiness/SBT data, goals-of-care and clinician judgment, positivity and causal assumptions, ICU expert review, and preferably prospective or quasi-experimental replication with source-chart validation. Public rankings are prohibited.

## Outputs, readiness, and verifier boundaries

Required pre-gate outputs are `cohort_flow.json`, `phenotype_v0.yaml`, `phase1_sampling_frame.parquet`, `phase1_labels.csv`, `phenotype_v1.yaml`, `phase2_sampling_frame.parquet`, `packet_manifest.csv`, `adjudication_labels.csv`, `reviewer_agreement.json`, `weighted_confusion_by_hospital_source.csv`, `partial_identification_bounds.csv`, `ascertainment_contrast_draws.parquet`, `measurement_gate.json`, and an immutable `gate_pass.token` written only by threshold-checking code.

Recovery scripts require `gate_pass.token` and matching hashes; otherwise they terminate before loading hospital outcomes. Post-pass outputs are `split_assignments.csv`, `state_transitions.parquet`, measurement-model and recovery-model manifests/checkpoints, `state_metrics.json`, `hospital_standardized_risks.csv`, `hospital_contrasts.json`, `sensitivity_results.csv`, `ablation_results.csv`, bootstrap/imputation draws, and a claim-to-output report.

The automatic verifier can check paths/hashes, joins, hospital-relative clocks, sampling inclusion probabilities and weights, blinding fields, packet uniqueness, confusion/bound formulas, gate enforcement, split grouping, leakage, state exclusivity, transition logic, competing-risk arithmetic, uncertainty calculations, and whether conclusions match computed supportive/adverse/inconclusive criteria. It cannot determine whether clinicians adjudicated correctly, convert available-eICU evidence into true source-chart sensitivity, establish a causal practice effect, certify quality, or generalize beyond the snapshot.

## Resources and alternatives

Measured inherited discovery work: full respiratoryCare/respiratoryCharting/treatment audit about 8.5 CPU-minutes with 4 CPUs/16 GiB; focused schema scans took seconds. Provisional counts were 5,201 landmark stays in 37 hospitals, 4,648 candidate ends, and 381 later starts within 48 hours; these are feasibility counts, not results.

Human review is the limiting resource: Phase I requires 480 primary reviews plus arbitration; Phase II is expected to require roughly 1,500–2,700 primary/replicate reviews depending on the frozen frame. The solver must report observed median review time and stop as inconclusive if expert adjudication cannot be obtained. CPU proposal: packet construction and M0/M1 measurement analysis on 8–16 CPUs/32–64 GiB for 1–3 hours; Model B plus nested bootstrap on 16 CPUs/64 GiB for 2–4 hours. Model L uses one allocated A100-80GB, 8 CPUs/64 GiB, approximately 1–3 hours per fold, with checkpoints, within the configured 8-hour, 16-CPU, 8-GPU planning envelope. GPU runtime is unverified; no GPU pilot was needed for the measurement repair. Ordinary shell CUDA absence is irrelevant.

Alternatives retained: a design-weighted M0 is primary because it makes unresolved-event assumptions visible; M1 is retained because it can separate source mix from residual hospital detection effects, but cannot override M0 bounds. Reviewing detected events only was rejected because it estimates PPV, not sensitivity. Random negative-window review without sentinel enrichment was rejected as inefficient; enrichment without a random component was rejected as nonrepresentative. Capture-recapture without clinician anchors was deferred because source dependence makes it weakly identified. A cause-specific Cox model, `actualventdays` regression, extubation-only classifier, and end-to-end transformer remain deferred for the parent's reasons. Revisit true clinical sensitivity only with source respiratory-therapy/procedure records or a linked prospective cohort.

## Exactly three inspected key works

[K1] Burns KEA, Rizvi L, Cook DJ, et al.; Canadian Critical Care Trials Group. “Ventilator Weaning and Discontinuation Practices for Critically Ill Patients.” *JAMA*. 2021;325:1173–1184. doi:10.1001/jama.2021.2384. Abstract inspected.

[K2] Pham T, Heunks L, Bellani G, et al.; WEAN SAFE Investigators. “Weaning from mechanical ventilation in intensive care units across 50 countries (WEAN SAFE): a multicentre, prospective, observational cohort study.” *Lancet Respir Med*. 2023;11:465–476. doi:10.1016/S2213-2600(22)00449-0. Abstract inspected.

[K3] Hüser M, Lyu X, Faltys M, et al. “RMS: a ML-based system for ICU respiratory monitoring and resource planning.” *npj Digital Medicine*. 2025;8:775. doi:10.1038/s41746-025-02081-4. Full-text XML inspected.

# Preoperative HCC MVI trajectories in explicitly graded pathology cases

## Objective and scientific boundary

Conduct a complete, reproducible internal temporal-validation study of whether longitudinal routine-care measurements before first recorded HCC resection improve prediction of pathology-recorded microvascular invasion (MVI) over matched latest snapshots.

The unresolved hypothesis is:

> Among adults with same-encounter pathology-confirmed HCC, one nonconflicting explicit M0/M1/M2 grade, no recorded procedure-defined treatment on days -180:-1, and strict numeric laboratories on at least two preoperative days, transparent day -90:-1 trajectory summaries improve temporally held-out M1/M2-versus-M0 prediction over the latest snapshot. An order-specific claim additionally requires an ordinal sequence model to beat matched transparent value summaries and an unordered learned set model, and order destruction must attenuate its gain.

This is a recorded-grade prediction estimand. Do not reinterpret it as prediction for all resections, a causal effect, tumor biology, pathology adequacy, treatment benefit, or clinical utility. A favorable result is not required. Correct adverse or inconclusive conclusions are equally valid.

Existing evidence supports only these narrower statements. A static AFP/tumor-size/margin score achieved useful discrimination in external Chinese cohorts and MVI requires pathology [K1]. M0/M1/M2 have explicit histopathologic definitions and M2 was associated with prognosis in a selected resection series with specified sampling [K2]. Selectively missing reference standards can bias complete-case accuracy estimates, while weighting depends on unverifiable missingness assumptions [K3]. None establishes that trajectories improve MVI prediction here.

The new scientific deliverable is newly fitted selection and outcome models, locked predictions, uncertainty estimates, falsification analyses, and conclusions linked to computed outputs. The included evidence is the frozen study design and bibliography, not a fitted model or answer.

## Runtime and submission interface

The eight private CSVs are mounted read-only under `/data`. Write all derived data, checkpoints, and final outputs below `/workspace`. Do not modify source files or emit direct identifiers, exact dates, or source free text in outputs.

Provide an executable `/solution/solve.sh`. It must run the complete analysis from the mounted files and create `/workspace/results` with every required output below. It may invoke code stored under `/solution`. Do not use canned results from the proposal's prior aggregate audit as substitutes for reconstruction.

The full workload may use at most 16 CPUs, 262144 MiB memory, one allocated A100 for the learned sequence models, and eight hours. Inside an allocated GPU runtime use `cuda:0`; support a documented CPU fallback. Estimated rather than measured costs are 1-2 hours for feature construction and transparent models, 3-6 hours for five-seed learned models on one A100, and 1-2 hours for bootstrap/sensitivities. The prior selection audit took 102.6 seconds on 4 CPUs/32 GiB, but that is not a runtime guarantee.

## Exact data bindings

Snapshot: `3f97e661e1884c34c1e2cdbf74ba0cf6d6c8995853e85f1857c3d72b82ccf521`. All are ordinary CSV files, not archive members. Join encounter tables on (`患者主索引`, `就诊号`) and link longitudinal patient history on `患者主索引`.

| Runtime path | Table and required columns | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `/data/pathology.csv` | pathology: `患者主索引, 就诊号, 病理, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 机器型号`; no native time | HCC denominator, explicit grade outcome, generic/conflict audit only |
| `/data/procedures.csv` | procedures: `患者主索引, 就诊号, 手术, 开始时间, 结束时间, 手术来源` | index resection and procedure-defined prior-treatment exclusion |
| `/data/encounters.csv` | encounters: keys plus `年龄, 性别, 就诊时间, 入院时间, 出院时间, 就诊科室` | demographics, service, clock audit; never export direct identifiers |
| `/data/diagnoses.csv` | diagnoses: keys plus `诊断名称, 诊断类型`; no native time | denominator audit only |
| `/data/labs.csv` | labs: keys plus `检验, 定性结果, 定量结果, 标本类型, 检验时间` | exact-label numeric sequences and availability; units/platform/reference ranges unavailable |
| `/data/examinations.csv` | examinations: keys plus `检查, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 开始时间, 机器型号, 检查号` | eligible pre-cutoff tumor-report features; reports only, no images |
| `/data/medications.csv` | medications: keys plus `用药, 单次用药计量, 单次用药计量单位, 频次, 开始时间, 结束时间, 用药方式, 药品类型` | systemic-treatment sensitivity; indication unavailable |
| `/data/clinical_documents.csv` | clinical_documents: keys plus complaint/history/admission/course/discharge/procedure text; no row time | blinded adjudication sampling only, never model features |

Mortality, recurrence, outside treatment or intent, lab units/platforms/reference ranges, pathology issue time, specimen/block identity, block count, sampling protocol, and images are unavailable. Vitals, transfers, and front-page tables have no useful payload.

## Frozen population, clocks, target, and split

1. Define the index as the earliest recorded qualifying liver-resection start for each patient. A qualifying procedure name contains liver and resection, and excludes transplant/donor, biopsy/puncture, drainage, abscess/cyst, and isolated cholecystectomy. Collapse exact duplicate procedure rows. Report ties or ambiguous starts; exclude the prespecified >1-day qualifying-start spans and 13 encounter-clock anomalies in the required sensitivity.
2. Require age at least 18 and a same-encounter pathology row whose `检查所见` or `检查诊断` explicitly supports HCC.
3. Extract grades only following `MVI提示风险分级:` (allow the Chinese colon and harmless spacing/bullet variants) in HCC pathology rows. The outcome-model cohort requires exactly one unique nonconflicting M0/M1/M2 grade. Pathology is never a predictor.
4. Exclude missing procedure time, an earlier recorded qualifying resection, and recorded embolization/intervention, ablation/radiofrequency/microwave, infusion/chemotherapy/radiotherapy, or targeted systemic treatment on calendar days -180:-1. “No recorded prior treatment” is institution-record limited.
5. The prediction cutoff is the start of calendar day -1. Predictor events are calendar days -90:-1 relative to index; surgery-day and later information is prohibited. Require strict numeric labs on at least two distinct days. Do not convert inequalities. Collapse exact duplicate labs. For a same-label/time duplicate, use the median only when every value is strict numeric; otherwise mark it ambiguous.
6. Keep exact lab labels separate because units/platform/reference ranges are absent. Fit training-era label/year robust scaling and freeze it.
7. Primary outcome: pathology-recorded M1/M2 versus M0. Ordered grade is secondary; M2 versus M0/M1 is exploratory.
8. Split by index year: 2014-2018 train, 2019 validation, 2020-2021 locked test. Use 2022-2023 only for reporting and 2024-2025 only as drift stress. Five-fold patient-level cross-fitting occurs within training; no patient may cross sets. Freeze all dictionaries, transformations, penalties, hyperparameters, thresholds, and selection rules before opening locked test results.
9. Reconstruct and reconcile the audited primary-period serial cohort: train n=2,210 with 935 events; validation n=992 with 463 events; locked test n=1,365 with 510 events. A mismatch is not to be hidden; document and resolve it before claiming completion.

## Full-denominator selection analysis

Rebuild the flow from all first qualifying resections through linked pathology, pathology-confirmed HCC, explicit/nonconflicting grade, and serial-lab eligibility overall and by year/split. Report generic-MVI, no-MVI-text, grade conflict, and missing-link states.

Within all pathology-HCC resections, report standardized differences and grade availability by age, sex, service, year, any/serial numeric labs, preoperative exam, lexical tumor-report availability, and size-like-report availability. Fit in 2014-2018:

- a transparent logistic grade-availability model; and
- a nonlinear histogram gradient-boosting alternative on the same listed variables.

Evaluate both without refitting in 2019 and 2020-2021, including discrimination, calibration, overlap, stabilized-weight distribution, clipping fraction, and effective sample size. Report unweighted outcome analysis as primary. An observed-covariate stabilized-IPW outcome sensitivity is secondary and assumption-dependent.

Weighting is interpretable only if validation/test predicted probabilities remain within 0.10-0.95, unclipped effective sample size is at least 70% of selected N, fewer than 5% of weights are clipped at prespecified 1st/99th percentiles, weighted and unweighted conclusions agree, and expert review supports a plausibly ignorable recording process. The frozen audit found these gates unmet; new computation must not silently override that fact. Report split-specific worst-case M1/M2 prevalence bounds, but never present them as bounds on AUROC, calibration, or net benefit.

## Matched outcome-model ladder

All models use the same 4,567 primary-period patients, static variables, report rules, event window, and outcome. Use five fixed seeds for learned models and report every seed.

- **S-value:** penalized logistic regression with age, sex, year, service; latest strict value and missingness for every exact label observed in at least 100 training patients; prespecified AFP, PIVKA-II, platelets, albumin, bilirubin, ALT, AST, INR/PT, GGT, ALP, WBC, hemoglobin, creatinine; and latest eligible report-derived tumor size, multiplicity, irregular margin/capsule, and modality. Use splines for prespecified continuous terms and elastic net for other labels. Also report the reduced AFP/size/margin benchmark [K1].
- **S-full:** S-value plus days since each latest value and total distinct measurement days.
- **V:** transparent value trajectory using S-value's vocabulary and inputs. Add per-label first/latest/min/max/median/range, IQR or MAD/SD, latest-minus-first, rank-block medians, Theil-Sen slope over observation rank, ordinal min/max positions, direction changes, and availability. Add AFP-PIVKA-II, ALT-AST, albumin-bilirubin, INR-platelets, GGT-ALP, and WBC-platelets interactions.
- **F:** V plus per-label count, distinct days, span, recency, median/max gap, calendar day of first/latest/min/max, Theil-Sen slope per day, -90:-31/-30:-8/-7:-1 medians and changes, shared-day co-change for the six pairs, and total event/day/panel and early/middle/late intensity.
- **D-bag:** permutation-invariant Deep Sets over exact-label/scaled-value tokens plus S-value static/report inputs, with no date, gap, position, panel, or count tokens.
- **T-value:** permutation-invariant within-day pooling followed by an ordinal day transformer (at most 4 layers, width 128, 8 heads) plus S-value inputs. It receives day order but no absolute date, gap, panel size, or observation count.
- **T-shuffle:** same architecture as T-value, trained on deterministic patient-level day-order permutations and evaluated with 20 locked permutations.
- **T-full:** T-value plus day-to-index, interday gap, panel composition/size, and intensity, with S-full inputs.
- **Controls:** timing-only and value-day reassignment models/experiments are mandatory.

Cap raw tokens at 512 before within-day pooling using a train-frozen deterministic day-stratified rule. Report truncation by split and outcome. D-bag tests nonlinear unordered value information; T-value tests residual ordinal information; F/T-full may expose care-process timing. None identifies a mechanism.

Multivariate GP/state-space factors remain deferred pending stable transparent gain and simulation recovery. Gradient boosting on F is secondary and cannot replace the matched ladder. Radiomics is infeasible because images are absent.

## Evaluation and uncertainty

For each required model, report on validation and locked test: AUROC, AUPRC, log loss, Brier score, calibration intercept/slope/in-the-large, and decision net benefit at 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, and 0.50. Select the operating threshold on validation for 80% sensitivity, then report locked-test sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV. Report calibration by sex, age <65/at least 65, tumor size at most 5/>5 cm, service, year, and ascertainment era only when each evaluated cell has at least 20 events.

Use 2,000 paired patient bootstrap replicates for locked-test model differences, preserving patient rows. For reproducibility, for each comparison initialize NumPy `default_rng(seed)`, draw locked-test row indices with replacement at the original test size, reject and redraw any sample lacking either outcome class, and stop after exactly 2,000 valid replicates. Use the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. Declare the seed. Include point estimates and percentile 95% intervals for these exact comparison names:

- `V_vs_S_value`;
- `F_vs_S_full`;
- `T_value_vs_V` and `T_value_vs_D_bag`;
- `T_value_vs_T_shuffle`;
- `T_value_vs_T_value_order_destroyed` and `T_value_order_destroyed_vs_V`;
- `T_full_vs_F` and `T_full_vs_T_value`;
- `T_full_vs_timing_only` and `T_full_vs_value_day_reassignment`.

For every comparison provide rows for `auroc` and `brier_reduction`. The candidate is left of `_vs_`. AUROC point/replicates are candidate minus reference. Brier-reduction point/replicates are reference Brier minus candidate Brier. The `V_vs_S_full` rows are required only for the no-material-inferiority support gate; their AUROC lower bound must exceed -0.01 and their Brier-reduction point must exceed -0.005.

A transparent V support claim requires all of: locked-test AUROC gain over S-value at least 0.02 and Brier reduction at least 0.01, both paired intervals excluding zero; no material inferiority to S-full (AUROC-difference lower bound greater than -0.01 and Brier increase below 0.005); calibration slope 0.8-1.2; net-benefit gain at at least two adjacent thresholds without material harm elsewhere; and no direction reversal from validation to test. Apply the same gates to F versus S-full for complete transparent longitudinal support.

An order-specific support claim requires T-value AUROC gain at least 0.02 and Brier reduction at least 0.01 versus V with intervals excluding zero; improvement in both metrics versus D-bag; superiority to T-shuffle; loss of at least 50% of its Brier gain over V with material AUROC attenuation after frozen-model order destruction; calibration/net-benefit gates; and no era reversal. T-full alone can never support a value/order claim.

## Mandatory falsifications and sensitivities

Run and label: day -7 cutoff; latest-day-only; report-free; conservative rejection of grade/pathology/postoperative report language; exclusion of >1-day qualifying-start spans and the 13 encounter-clock anomalies; any-prior-recorded-treatment exclusion; labs-only, reports-only, and demographics-plus-observation-only controls; same-day panel collapse; exact-label restriction; leave-one-year-out fits; outcome permutation; automated feature-time leakage tests; timing-only; value-day reassignment; trained day shuffle; and frozen-model order destruction.

Prepare privacy-preserving stratified manifests for blinded pathology review of graded, generic-ungraded, no-MVI-text, conflicting, and no-linked-pathology encounters across 2014-2015, 2016-2020, and 2021, and for radiology parser review. Do not claim these reviews occurred unless reviewer outputs are actually supplied. Without expert review, specimen/index correspondence, sampling adequacy, grade omission mechanism, and report parser validity remain unresolved.

## Interpretation rules

Supportive results establish only internal temporally held-out prediction among explicitly graded cases. If V or F passes but T-value fails, conclude that interpretable trajectories help while rejecting an order-specific learned claim. If D-bag matches T-value, unordered nonlinear interactions suffice. If only F or T-full improves, care timing/process predicts; biological attribution is prohibited.

Adverse evidence includes precise exclusion of V/F gains, matching by snapshots/D-bag/T-shuffle, no attenuation after order destruction, gain confined to F/T-full, learned-model miscalibration, era/subgroup reversal, or dependence on the 2014-2015/2021 template discontinuities. State which claim is contradicted; do not claim equivalence from an imprecise null.

Inconclusive evidence includes broad intervals, poor calibration, severe truncation, dependency/seed instability, failed adjudication, or gain confined to day -1 or flagged reports. An imprecise null does not refute biology or the hypothesis generally. Report uncertainty and the next required evidence.

No computed result can establish causality, tumor biology, all-resection transport, external validity, pathology sampling adequacy, treatment benefit, or actual clinical utility. These require clinical adjudication, missing specimen/sampling evidence, external validation, or another study.

## Required outputs and mechanical contract

Create all files below `/workspace/results`. JSON must be valid UTF-8 JSON without NaN/Infinity. CSVs must have headers and finite numeric fields where applicable.

### `analysis_manifest.json`

Include: `schema="hcc-mvi-analysis-v1"`, `status="complete"`, snapshot ID, source SHA-256 mapping, exact population/window/split definitions, direct-identifier suppression statement, code version/hash, package versions, random seeds, device/runtime resources, trained model list, feature dictionary hashes, test-open timestamp relative to frozen tuning, and an `adjudication` object saying what was/was not reviewed. The trained model list must include `S_value,S_full,V,F,D_bag,T_value,T_shuffle,T_full,timing_only,value_day_reassignment`.

### `cohort_flow.csv`

Columns: `split,year,stage,n,events`. Include stages `first_qualifying_resection,pathology_linked,pathology_hcc,explicit_nonconflicting_grade,serial_numeric_labs` overall and by year/split. The primary serial rows must reconcile to the frozen counts above.

### `selection_diagnostics.json`

Include grade-availability models and their validation/test AUROC, Brier, calibration, probability ranges; standardized differences; weight quantiles, clipping fraction, unclipped/clipped ESS; prevalence bounds by split; and explicit booleans for each weighting gate. Label transport as `not_identified` unless the missing evidence and expert-review requirements are genuinely supplied.

### `predictions.csv`

One row per primary-period patient with a nonreversible `patient_key` and columns:
`patient_key,split,year,outcome,grade,sex,age,tumor_size_cm,service,ascertainment_era,S_value,S_full,V,F,D_bag,T_value,T_shuffle,T_full,timing_only,value_day_reassignment,T_value_order_destroyed`.
Probabilities must be finite in [0,1]. No direct source key may appear. Rows and outcomes must be identical across models.

### `metrics.csv`

Columns: `model,split,n,events,auroc,auprc,log_loss,brier,calibration_intercept,calibration_slope,calibration_in_the_large,net_benefit_020,net_benefit_030,net_benefit_040,net_benefit_050,threshold_80sens,sensitivity,specificity,ppv,npv`. Include every model on validation and locked test. The verifier recomputes core metrics from predictions.

### `bootstrap_comparisons.csv`

Columns: `comparison,metric,direction,replicates,point,ci_low,ci_high,seed`. Use `direction="candidate_minus_reference"` for AUROC and `direction="reference_minus_candidate"` for Brier reduction. Include all fixed comparisons and exactly 2,000 replicates; reported points and intervals must derive from the submitted predictions.

### `falsifications.csv`

Columns: `analysis,status,n,metric,effect,ci_low,ci_high,artifact_path,interpretation`. Include every mandatory falsification/sensitivity. `status` is `completed`, `failed`, or `requires_expert_review`; failures must be explained and make affected claims inconclusive.

### `claims.json`

Use `schema="hcc-mvi-claims-v1"` and a nonempty `claims` array. Every claim has:
`id,claim_type,status,text,population_scope,evidence_files,rule,uncertainty,requires_expert_review`.
Allowed `claim_type`: `transparent_value,transparent_full,order_specific,selection_transport,clinical_interpretation,limitation`. Allowed `status`: `supportive,adverse,inconclusive,descriptive`.

Each evidence file must be one of the required outputs and each inferential claim must cite the exact comparison rows/rules. All claims must retain the phrase “among explicitly graded cases” in their population scope. `selection_transport` cannot be supportive from these data alone. Claims of causality, biology, all-resection transport, sampling adequacy, treatment benefit, or clinical utility must be marked `requires_expert_review=true` and framed as not established. Correct numbers paired with unsupported conclusions fail verification.

## Readiness limitation

Packaging readiness checks only imports, exact mounted headers, file hashes when practical, and tiny synthetic metric/interpretation logic. It does not run the study, fit the models, validate the pathology parser, establish verifier completeness, or determine scientific truth.

## Bibliography

[K1] Xu J, Zhang Y-L, Yang M, et al. “Preoperative Prediction of Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Chinese Retrospective Multicenter Study Based on Global Meta-Analysis.” *Cancer Medicine*. 2026. https://doi.org/10.1002/cam4.71749

[K2] Li Z, Xu L, Liu X, et al. “Comparisons of clinical patterns, short- and long-term prognostic outcomes in patients stratified by the severity of microvascular invasion after curative resection for hepatocellular carcinoma.” *World Journal of Surgical Oncology*. 2026;24:132. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12957-026-04229-2

[K3] Naaktgeboren CA, de Groot JAH, Rutjes AWS, et al. “Anticipating missing reference standard data when planning diagnostic accuracy studies.” *BMJ*. 2016;352:i402. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.i402

# Preoperative HCC MVI trajectories in an explicitly graded pathology target

Status: substantive ascertainment child of candidate-c5d8f8dec6cef68a3cf42134. A new aggregate full-denominator audit was executed; no MVI outcome model was fitted. The clinical question, prediction cutoff, outcome, day −90:−1 feature window, temporal split, data bindings, and matched baseline/learned trajectory alternatives are preserved. The scientific repair is an explicit recorded-grade target population and a prohibition on transporting model performance to ungraded resections without additional pathology evidence.

## Question, supported evidence, unresolved claim, and advance

The clinical question remains whether longitudinal routine-care measurements available before first recorded HCC resection improve prediction of pathology-recorded M1/M2 microvascular invasion (MVI) over matched latest snapshots. A reproducible increment could inform surgical approach/margin discussions, neoadjuvant-study eligibility, and counseling; it cannot establish treatment benefit.

The strongest evidence-supported claims are narrower than the hypothesis. A static AFP/tumor-size/margin score achieved C-statistics near 0.81 in two Chinese validation cohorts, and MVI requires pathology [K1]. M0/M1/M2 have explicit histopathologic definitions, with M2 associated with recurrence and mortality in a selected retrospective resection series [K2]. Missing or selectively observed reference-standard outcomes can bias complete-case accuracy estimates; weighting and imputation depend on assumptions about outcome missingness that can be unverifiable [K3].

The unresolved hypothesis is:

> Among adults with same-encounter pathology-confirmed HCC, one nonconflicting explicit M0/M1/M2 grade, no recorded procedure-defined treatment on days −180:−1, and strict numeric laboratories on at least two preoperative days, transparent day −90:−1 trajectory summaries will improve temporally held-out M1/M2-versus-M0 prediction over the latest snapshot. Any stronger learned-order claim additionally requires an ordinal sequence model to beat matched transparent value summaries and an unordered learned set model, and requires order destruction to attenuate its gain.

This is a recorded-grade estimand, not prediction for every resection candidate. The substantive advance over the parent is to audit the full eligible resection denominator and separate three populations: all first qualifying resections, same-encounter pathology-confirmed HCC resections, and explicitly graded HCC resections. The audit shows explicit grade recording is strongly template-era dependent, so weighting cannot identify transport to ungraded patients. The trajectory hypothesis remains unresolved.

## Executed full-denominator ascertainment audit

The read-only snapshot was scanned in 102.6 seconds on 4 CPUs/32 GiB; no row-level records or free text were emitted. The script and aggregate outputs are attached.

For 2014–2021, the broad denominator contains 12,574 adults at their earliest recorded dated qualifying liver resection with no recorded procedure-defined treatment on days −180:−1. Of these, 11,725 have same-encounter pathology, 11,405 have pathology text explicitly supporting HCC, and 849 have no linked pathology despite an HCC diagnosis row. Diagnosis has no timestamp and is audit-only.

Within the 11,405 pathology-HCC target:

- 9,084 (79.65%) have exactly one nonconflicting explicit M0/M1/M2 grade;
- 30 have conflicting explicit grades;
- 177 have generic MVI language or the grade heading without an extractable grade;
- 2,114 have HCC pathology but no explicit MVI-grade or generic-MVI text;
- 3,644 observed grades are M1/M2 (40.11% among graded cases);
- without assumptions, target-population M1/M2 prevalence is bounded only by 31.95%–52.30%; these prevalence bounds do not bound AUROC, calibration, or net benefit.

Grade availability among pathology-HCC resections changed sharply by year: 0.20% in 2014, 49.60% in 2015, 96.07% in 2016, 98.06% in 2017, 97.35% in 2018, 96.97% in 2019, 97.09% in 2020, and 50.30% in 2021. It was 78.04% in the 2014–2018 train era, 96.97% in 2019 validation, and 73.81% in the 2020–2021 test era. This is adverse evidence against stable ascertainment and unrestricted temporal transport.

Age and sex differences in grade availability were small in the aggregate, but service ranged from 78.20% to 86.73% among services with adequate counts. Availability was 80.73% with versus 78.58% without serial numeric labs, 80.85% with versus 70.63% without a lexical preoperative tumor report, and 80.57% with versus 65.10% without a size-like report. These are descriptive selection diagnostics, not causal explanations and not evidence that the missing outcome is conditionally random.

The reconstruction exactly reconciles the parent's all-year strict graded denominator (10,171) and serial cohort (5,204). The frozen primary periods contain 4,567 serial patients: 2,210/935 M1/M2 in 2014–2018, 992/463 in 2019, and 1,365/510 in 2020–2021. The remaining all-year serial records are report-only later-era data, including the 2024–2025 stress set; they cannot rescue primary failure.

A transparent grade-availability logistic model and a nonlinear histogram gradient-boosting alternative used year, age, sex, service, numeric-lab availability, serial-lab availability, preoperative-exam availability, lexical tumor-report availability, and size-like-report availability. Both were fit in 2014–2018 and evaluated without refitting in 2019 and 2020–2021. Neither transported (logistic AUROC 0.502/0.483; learned alternative 0.437/0.471), and the learned alternative was grossly miscalibrated after the template shift. A full-period observed-covariate propensity diagnostic produced a maximum stabilized weight of 63.0 and effective sample size 5,857 of 9,084 before clipping (8,307 after 1st/99th-percentile clipping). This is adverse to relying on IPW, not proof of no selection.

## Identification decision and selection repair

Primary inference is restricted to patients whose qualifying first resection encounter has pathology-confirmed HCC and exactly one explicit nonconflicting M0/M1/M2 grade. All claims must say “among explicitly graded cases.” This is a target-population restriction, not a claim that grading is random or representative.

The following are mandatory alongside every model result:

1. The full-denominator flow from qualifying resection through pathology link, pathology-HCC, explicit/nonconflicting grade, and serial-lab eligibility, overall and by year/split.
2. Standardized differences and grade-availability rates by age, sex, service, year, any/serial labs, preoperative exam, tumor-report availability, and size-like-report availability.
3. The transparent logistic and nonlinear selection diagnostics on the frozen temporal split, calibration, probability overlap, stabilized-weight distribution, clipping fraction, and effective sample size.
4. Unweighted primary outcome-model metrics and a secondary stabilized-IPW analysis standardized only over observed covariates among pathology-HCC resections. The weighted analysis is labeled assumption-dependent; it cannot upgrade the target.
5. Worst-case M1/M2 prevalence bounds by split. Extreme all-ungraded-M0 and all-ungraded-M1/M2 assignments may be shown as outcome-prevalence scenarios only, not as identified model-performance estimates.
6. Year-specific outcome-model metrics when support permits, with particular attention to 2014–2015 and 2021 template discontinuities. A 2016–2020 high-ascertainment sensitivity is secondary and cannot replace the locked 2020–2021 test.

Weighting becomes interpretable only if selection probabilities have overlap (validation/test minimum predicted probability ≥0.10, maximum ≤0.95; unclipped effective sample size ≥70% of selected N; <5% weights clipped at prespecified 1st/99th percentiles), weighted and unweighted conclusions agree, and expert review supports a plausibly ignorable recording process conditional on modeled variables. The executed max weight of 63 and temporal model failure mean these gates are not met now. Even if later met, unmeasured template, specimen, and sampling factors remain a limitation.

Expansion to all pathology-HCC resections requires blinded hepatopathology adjudication of a stratified sample of graded, generic-ungraded, no-MVI-text, conflicting, and no-linked-pathology encounters across 2014–2015, 2016–2020, and 2021. Review must determine whether absent grade means true M0, omitted template field, nonresection specimen, inadequate sampling, or failed linkage and must verify specimen/index correspondence. The current source lacks pathology issue time, specimen/block identity, block count, and sampling protocol; these cannot be repaired automatically.

## Frozen population, clocks, outcome, and split

Index remains the earliest recorded qualifying liver-resection start per patient. A qualifying procedure name contains liver and resection and excludes transplant/donor, biopsy/puncture, drainage, abscess/cyst, and isolated cholecystectomy. Exact duplicate procedure rows are collapsed. The pathology-HCC target requires pathology in the same (患者主索引, 就诊号) encounter and HCC wording in 检查所见 or 检查诊断. The analysis cohort additionally requires exactly one unique grade following “MVI提示风险分级:” across HCC pathology rows.

Include age ≥18. Exclude missing procedure time, conflicting/no explicit grade from outcome-model fitting, an earlier recorded qualifying resection, and recorded embolization/intervention, ablation/radiofrequency/microwave, infusion/chemotherapy/radiotherapy, or targeted systemic treatment on days −180:−1. “No recorded prior treatment” is institutional-record limited.

Prediction cutoff remains start of calendar day −1. Inputs have event days −90:−1; surgery-day and later events are prohibited. Strict numeric labs on at least two distinct days are required for the outcome-model cohort. Exact duplicate labs are collapsed; same-label/time duplicates use the median only if all are strict numeric, otherwise they are ambiguous. Inequalities are not converted. Exact labels are not pooled because units/platform/reference ranges are absent. Training-era label/year robust scaling is frozen.

Primary outcome remains pathology-recorded M1/M2 versus M0; ordered grade is secondary and M2 versus M0/M1 exploratory. Pathology is outcome/selection audit data only and is never a feature. Split remains 2014–2018 train, 2019 validation, and 2020–2021 locked test; 2022–2023 is report-only and 2024–2025 drift stress only. Five-fold patient-level cross-fitting occurs within train; no patient crosses sets. All outcome models use the same 4,567 primary-period patients, event window, static inputs, and eligible report rules.

## Matched baseline and substantive learned alternatives

All dictionaries, transformations, penalties, hyperparameters, thresholds, and selection rules are learned in train and frozen through validation before test. Learned models use five fixed seeds.

S-value is penalized logistic regression on age, sex, year, service, the latest strict value and missing indicator for each exact label observed in at least 100 training patients, prespecified AFP, PIVKA-II, platelets, albumin, bilirubin, ALT, AST, INR/PT, GGT, ALP, WBC, hemoglobin, creatinine, and latest eligible report-derived size, multiplicity, irregular margin/capsule, and modality. S-full adds days since each latest value and total distinct measurement days. Prespecified continuous terms use splines; other labels use elastic net. Report the reduced AFP/size/margin benchmark [K1].

V is the transparent value-trajectory alternative on S-value's inputs and vocabulary. Per label add first/latest/minimum/maximum/median/range/IQR or MAD/SD, latest-minus-first, rank-block medians, Theil–Sen slope over observation rank, ordinal min/max positions, direction changes, and availability. Prespecified cross-marker interactions are AFP–PIVKA-II, ALT–AST, albumin–bilirubin, INR–platelets, GGT–ALP, and WBC–platelets.

F is the transparent full trajectory/timing alternative. It adds V plus per-label count, distinct days, span, recency, median/max gap, calendar day of first/latest/min/max, Theil–Sen slope per day, −90:−31/−30:−8/−7:−1 medians and changes, shared-day co-change summaries for the six pairs, and total event/day/panel and early/middle/late intensity. F can reveal interpretable trends, extrema, variability, synchronization, timing, and observation intensity that a snapshot loses, but timing gain may represent workflow rather than tumor biology.

D-bag is a permutation-invariant Deep Sets model over all exact-label/scaled-value tokens plus S-value static/report inputs, without date, gap, position, panel, or count tokens. It tests nonlinear cross-marker information without chronology.

T-value uses permutation-invariant within-day pooling followed by an ordinal day transformer (≤4 layers, width ≤128, ≤8 heads) plus S-value inputs. It sees day order but no absolute date, gap, panel size, or observation count. T-shuffle uses the same architecture with deterministic patient-level day-order permutations and 20 locked evaluation permutations. T-full adds day-to-index, interday gap, panel composition/size, and intensity plus S-full inputs. Timing-only and value–day reassignment controls are mandatory. Cap at 512 raw tokens before within-day pooling using a train-frozen deterministic day-stratified rule; report truncation by split/outcome.

The substantive learned models can reveal nonlinear unordered interactions, residual ordinal dependence, and timing/process dependence that V/F may lose. They do not identify mechanism. Multivariate GP/state-space latent factors remain deferred because sparse exact-label repetition and absent units make latent factors fragile; revisit only after stable transparent gain plus simulation recovery. Gradient boosting on F is secondary, not a substitute for the matched ladder. Images are unavailable, so radiomics is infeasible.

## Outcome-model estimands, metrics, and falsification

Report paired AUROC, AUPRC, log loss, Brier, calibration intercept/slope/in-the-large, and decision net benefit at risks 0.20/0.30/0.40/0.50 on identical locked-test patients with 2,000 paired patient bootstraps. Report sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV at a validation-selected 80% sensitivity and calibration by sex, age <65/≥65, tumor size ≤5/>5 cm, service, year, and ascertainment era when ≥20 events/cell.

Fixed comparisons are V−S-value; F−S-full; T-value−V and T-value−D-bag; T-value−T-shuffle plus frozen-model order destruction; and T-full−F/T-value plus timing-only and value–day reassignment controls.

Transparent value-trajectory support requires locked-test V versus S-value AUROC improvement ≥0.02 and Brier reduction ≥0.01, both paired intervals excluding zero, no material inferiority to S-full (lower AUROC bound >−0.01 and Brier increase <0.005), calibration slope 0.8–1.2, net-benefit gain at at least two adjacent thresholds without material harm elsewhere, and no direction reversal between 2019 and 2020–2021. F versus S-full uses the same gates for complete transparent longitudinal support.

A learned order-specific claim requires T-value to improve AUROC ≥0.02 and Brier ≥0.01 versus V with intervals excluding zero; improve both versus D-bag; beat T-shuffle; lose at least 50% of its Brier gain over V with material AUROC attenuation after order destruction; pass calibration/net-benefit gates; and avoid era reversal. T-full alone cannot satisfy a value/order claim.

Mandatory falsifications/sensitivities are day −7 cutoff, latest-day-only, report-free run, conservative rejection of grade/pathology/postoperative report language, exclusion of >1-day qualifying-start spans and 13 encounter-clock anomalies, any-prior-recorded-treatment exclusion, labs-only/report-only/demographics-and-observation-only controls, same-day panel collapse, exact-label restriction, leave-one-year-out fits, outcome permutation, automated feature-time leakage tests, and the parent’s blinded pathology/radiology reviews.

Supportive results establish only internal temporally held-out prediction among explicitly graded cases. If V or F supports but T-value fails, interpretable trajectories help and learned-order value is rejected. If D-bag matches T-value, unordered nonlinear interactions suffice. If only F/T-full improves, care timing/process predicts and tumor-biological interpretation is prohibited.

Adverse results include precise exclusion of V/F gains, V or D-bag/T-shuffle matching T-value, no attenuation after order destruction, gain confined to F/T-full, learned-model miscalibration, era/subgroup reversal, or dependence on 2014–2015/2021 template discontinuities. The executed ascertainment audit is already adverse to all-resection transport.

Inconclusive results include broad intervals, poor calibration, severe truncation, dependency/seed instability, failed adjudication, or gain confined to day −1/flagged reports. An imprecise null does not refute a biological relationship. No result here establishes causality, tumor biology, external transport, sampling adequacy, or treatment benefit.

## Exact read-only bindings

Snapshot: 3f97e661e1884c34c1e2cdbf74ba0cf6d6c8995853e85f1857c3d72b82ccf521. Join encounter tables on (患者主索引, 就诊号); link longitudinal history on 患者主索引. All are ordinary CSV files; sources remain read-only and derived files stay in the workspace.

- pathology table, `[private path]`: 患者主索引, 就诊号, 病理, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 机器型号. No native time. Outcome, pathology-HCC denominator, generic-MVI/conflict audit only.
- procedures, `[private path]`: 患者主索引, 就诊号, 手术, 开始时间, 结束时间, 手术来源. Index, prior resection, and procedure-defined treatment exclusion.
- encounters, `[private path]`: encounter keys, 年龄, 性别, 就诊时间, 入院时间, 出院时间, 就诊科室. Demographics/service/clock audit; direct identifiers prohibited.
- diagnoses, `[private path]`: encounter keys, 诊断名称, 诊断类型. HCC denominator audit only; no timestamp.
- labs, `[private path]`: encounter keys, 检验, 定性结果, 定量结果, 标本类型, 检验时间. Exact-label preoperative sequences and availability; no unit/platform/reference-range column.
- examinations, `[private path]`: encounter keys, 检查, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 开始时间, 机器型号, 检查号. Pre-cutoff tumor-report/size availability and allowed report features; no images.
- medications, `[private path]`: encounter keys, 用药, dose/unit/frequency, 开始时间, 结束时间, 用药方式, 药品类型. Systemic-treatment sensitivity only; indication unavailable.
- clinical_documents, `[private path]`: encounter keys plus complaint/history/admission/course/discharge/procedure text. Blinded adjudication only; no row timestamp.

Mortality, recurrence, outside treatment/intent, lab units/platforms, pathology issue time, specimen/block identity, sampling protocol, and images are unavailable. Vitals, transfers, and front-page tables have no useful payload. All four configured datasets remain directly accessible and read-only; only HCC is analyzed.

## Solver deliverables, compute, and verification

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted outcome and selection models plus locked aggregate outputs—not confirmation of the hypothesis. Completion requires:

- reproducible full-denominator and model-cohort flow; year/split ascertainment tables; parser conflict/generic-MVI manifests; schema/header/hash checks;
- transparent and learned grade-availability fits, calibration/overlap/weight diagnostics, standardized differences, prevalence bounds, and adjudication sampling manifests;
- S-value, S-full, V, F, D-bag, T-value, T-shuffle, T-full, timing-only, and value–day control fits; seed/truncation/tuning records; locked predictions;
- paired metrics, calibration, decision curves, subgroup/year/era outputs, falsifications, unweighted primary and assumption-labeled weighted sensitivity;
- `claims.json` linking every conclusion to computed files and a rule, explicitly tagging “recorded-grade,” “assumption-dependent transport sensitivity,” or “requires clinical adjudication.”

Measured ascertainment audit cost is 102.6 seconds on 4 CPUs/32 GiB. Estimated outcome feature/S/V/F work is 1–2 hours on 8–16 CPUs/≤64 GiB. Five-seed D/T fitting is an unverified 3–6 hours on one allocated A100 80 GiB plus 8 CPUs/64 GiB; bootstrap and selection sensitivities are 1–2 hours on 16 CPUs. This fits the 16-CPU/262-GiB/8-hour solver envelope. GPU jobs must request one allocated device and use cuda:0; no GPU is needed for selection diagnostics.

The verifier can check hashes, headers, joins, clocks, exclusions, cohort reconciliation, parser states, split isolation, selection-model computation, weight/ESS rules, model inputs, matched comparisons, metrics, bootstrap intervals, and whether claims follow the prespecified supportive/adverse/inconclusive rules. It must reject correct computations paired with claims of all-resection transport, causality, biology, sampling adequacy, or treatment benefit. It cannot establish specimen correspondence, pathology adequacy, missingness ignorability, or clinical utility; those require expert review, missing evidence, external validation, or another study.

## Exactly three key references

[K3] Naaktgeboren CA, de Groot JAH, Rutjes AWS, et al. Anticipating missing reference standard data when planning diagnostic accuracy studies. BMJ. 2016;352:i402. doi:10.1136/bmj.i402.

# Residual instability before ICU-to-ward transfer

## Objective and evidence boundary

Run the complete frozen MIMIC-IV experiment testing whether recent measured-value direction adds residual, temporally transportable 48-hour deterioration information when endpoint state and direction disagree. Newly fit all required models and report uncertainty-linked conclusions. No outcome model or hypothesis result is supplied.

The strongest currently supported claim is feasibility: the frozen cohort is reconstructible, spans usable approximate eras, and has adequate pre-outcome measurement support. The unresolved hypothesis is that, conditional on endpoint-state risk C at ICU-to-ward transfer t0, worsening G raises and improvement lowers 48-hour ICU-return/death risk, with the largest risk and fixed-quota ranking changes in reassuring/worsening and concerning/improving discordant states. A value-specific transported result would support only residual measured-value information and useful re-ranking. It cannot establish physiology, mechanism, safe transfer, preventability, or benefit from monitoring, delayed transfer, or ICU retention.

The experiment is open-ended. Supportive, adverse, endpoint-sufficiency, simple-adequacy, and inconclusive results are all valid outcomes when supported by computed estimates and uncertainty. Do not optimize for confirmation.

## Frozen population, time origin, and outcomes

Construct one row per hospitalization's first eligible adult ICU-to-one-of-the-frozen-17-general-ward transfers after ICU length of stay of at least 24 hours. Use t0 = icu/icustays.outtime and require the exact successor hosp/transfers.intime = t0 on nonmissing [internal identifier] and [internal identifier]. Preserve the step-down sensitivity. The frozen 17 exact destination values are: Medicine; Neurology; Med/Surg; Medicine/Cardiology; Cardiology; Oncology; Hematology/Oncology; Transplant; Vascular; Med/Surg/GYN; Surgery/Trauma; Med/Surg/Trauma; Surgery; Cardiac Surgery; Medical/Surgical (Gynecology); Surgery/Pancreatic/Biliary/Bariatric; Thoracic Surgery. The exact audit target is 49,157 transfers and 2,607 raw adverse composites; any mismatch must stop interpretation and be explained, not silently redefine the cohort.

Predictors use only [t0-24h,t0). Chart rows require charttime < t0 and storetime < t0. Input/procedure rows require interval overlap with the window and storetime < t0. No post-t0 measurement, treatment, service, destination change, or note may enter a predictor.

The raw three-state 48-hour outcome is:

- adverse: same-admission later ICU transfer intime or admissions.deathtime in (t0,t0+48h];
- live discharge: the frozen valid-live-discharge rule;
- no event: neither above.

Retain the adjudicated six-hour first-transition extension W to ICU return R, death D, valid live discharge L, or no observed valid transition W, the administrative-discordance flag, 33 unresolved records, and all inherited endpoint sensitivities. Discharge notes are adjudication evidence only; they never enter predictors or automatic labels.

## Frozen pooled and temporal protocols

## Result meanings

Supportive bounded evidence requires inherited pooled and transport gates, positive D1 Brier-gain intervals in pooled test and both late eras, positive I interval in the prespecified direction, at least one supported pooled discordant cell with at least 5 additional observed R+D events per 1,000 reviewed at a fixed quota and no overall loss, concordant adjudicated R+D direction, and value evidence not reproduced by process-only/permutations. Conclude only residual measured-value information and useful re-ranking.

Adverse evidence includes an opposite interaction interval, D1 worsening Brier/IBS, a loss of at least 5 events per 1,000, endpoint-sensitivity reversal, or disappearance of value evidence while process-only reproduces it. This rejects the specified discordance prioritization claim, not all longitudinal physiology.

Endpoint sufficiency requires pooled and both late-era D1 95% upper bounds below a 0.002 Brier gain, upper bounds below 2 extra captures per 1,000 at every quota, and exclusion of the prespecified material interaction. Prefer E0/S0.

Simple adequacy is secondary: D1 is supportive while L2-D upper bounds exclude an additional 0.002 Brier gain and 2 events per 1,000 in both late eras. Prefer D1.

Otherwise report inconclusive when uncertainty spans material benefit and harm, coverage/support fails, seeds are unstable, calibration fails, endpoint sensitivities disagree, or named cells are unsupported. An imprecise null is not falsification.

All substantive categories require verified censoring and assay/code semantics, support and matching passes, >=90% bootstrap convergence, and adequate held-out calibration/stability. A failed hard gate forces `inconclusive`.

- `adverse_broad_coding_frailty`: D is precisely null/reversed after baseline history, broad nonrenal emission or multiple families are associated comparably to N17, NMF locates the apparent N17 pattern on a shared high-burden component, or principal-position D reverses incompatibly.
- `adverse_chronic_or_shared_renal`: theta18>0 with D<=0, or both renal contrasts are similar with adequate precision.
- `adverse_both_profile_claims`: both endpoint upper 95% bounds <=0 with adequate precision.
- `inconclusive`: any hard gate fails; comparison/principal N18 estimates are too sparse or imprecise; methods disagree without adjudication; ties change direction; or intervals cannot distinguish patterns. An imprecise null is not refutation.

Do not change profiles, windows, code families, NMF rank rules, outcomes, or thresholds after seeing results. If more than one adverse pattern applies, report all applicable patterns and select the most direct primary interpretation with justification.

Even a supportive result cannot establish KDIGO AKI, biochemical CKD onset, complete contact/testing opportunity, true GFR, renal reserve, mechanism, transportability, or benefit from marker-guided care. # Fixed-combined-eGFR marker profiles and recorded renal transition with baseline-only observation-process repair

Status: prospective substantive child of candidate-d231a1dcdc20105c0b885f95. No marker-profile/outcome association has been fitted. The age-40–69 population, fixed-combined-eGFR P− versus P0 contrast, day-30 origin, competing N17/N18 first transitions, profile support, matching, censoring, adjudication, uncertainty and three inspected works are preserved. The scientific repair is to remove every post-baseline code-emission state from adjustment. All observation-process adjustment is frozen at index; post-index nonrenal emissions are outcomes or descriptive diagnostics only.

## Supported evidence, unresolved claim, and advance

The strongest evidence currently supports only three bounded claims. Large eGFRcys-minus-eGFRcr differences are common in UK Biobank and have kidney and non-GFR predictors [K1]. Such differences carry frailty and broad adverse-outcome information in SPRINT, and a combined equation may lose some prognostic information [K2]. Administrative AKI coding can have incomplete and subgroup-dependent recognition relative to serum-creatinine KDIGO AKI [K3]. The parent’s outcome-only audit additionally observed different coding contexts for recorded N17-first and N18-first (12.0% versus 1.39% same-day principal-family confirmation and median prior-year nonrenal first-code counts 3 versus 0). That observation neither establishes a profile association nor identifies its cause.

Unresolved hypothesis: among supported UKB adults aged 40–69 in the common day-30 N17/N18-free state, the profile P− (2021 combined eGFR G=90; eGFRcys−eGFRcr=−15), versus P0 (G=90; delta=0), has a larger adjusted 10-year relative-risk contrast for first recorded inpatient N17 than for first recorded inpatient N18, and this N17 selectivity is not merely a manifestation of pre-index coding/frailty burden or a similarly broad association with subsequent nonrenal code emission.

Let theta17=log RR10(N17_first; P−/P0), theta18=log RR10(N18_first; P−/P0), and D=theta17−theta18. D remains the primary estimand. The child improves discrimination between two explanations without conditioning on an exposure-, prodrome-, or outcome-affected process:

- renal-selective profile information predicts N17 more than N18 even after measured pre-index history, without a comparably strong broad nonrenal-code pattern;
- broad morbidity/observation explains the apparent selectivity if the profile tracks pre-index code-history structure and subsequent nonrenal first-code emission as strongly as N17.

This is a descriptive standardized joint-marker profile contrast. “Robust to measured baseline history” is not “deconfounded,” and no result identifies an intervention, true GFR, renal reserve, biological AKI/CKD, treatment effect, or mechanism.

## Exact UKB data binding and availability

Use read-only snapshot d836bc0ca31c844b0462e1a293673818bfed046b8b0173bf360958169e8958a1. All sources are ordinary CSVs joined one-to-one on eid; no archive member is involved.

- population: [private path]; datasets/ukb/table-38565c9e35e7cb6c.json; eid, sex 31-0.0, age 21022-0.0, linkage-loss field 191-0.0 (do not use until semantics are verified).
- assessment: [private path]; datasets/ukb/table-901ef6c7ddce2d51.json; index 53-0.0, centre 54-0.0, grips 46-0.0/47-0.0, waist 48-0.0, BMI 21001-0.0, ethnicity 21000-0.0, smoking 20116-0.0, diabetes 2443-0.0, SBP 4080-0.0/.1, DBP 4079-0.0/.1.
- biological_samples: [private path]; datasets/ukb/table-c6b666d905f3b02f.json; creatinine 30700-0.0, cystatin C 30720-0.0, CRP 30710-0.0, urine albumin 30500-0.0, urine creatinine 30510-0.0, glucose 30740-0.0, HbA1c 30750-0.0.
- health_outcomes: [private path]; datasets/ukb/table-3cfae45e0905b0e3.json; all-position codes 41270-0.0…258 paired by array index with first inpatient diagnosis dates 41280-0.0…258; principal codes 41202-0.0…79 paired with 41262-0.0…79; death 40000-0.0/1.0; lifetime HESIN row count 41259-0.0 descriptive only.

The full catalog and direct headers confirm these fields: 259 all-position and 80 principal code/date pairs. The parent audit found 84 all-position and 35 principal codes without paired dates and no dates without codes; exclude unpaired entries from date-dependent features and report them. Normalize codes uppercase and alphanumeric.

Critical measurement limit: 41270/41280 and 41202/41262 are first recorded code appearances, not all diagnoses, admissions, tests, or contacts. There are no record-level HESIN/HESIN_DIAG rows, admission identifiers/dates, provider/nation, outpatient kidney trajectories, or validated healthcare-contact process. Field 41259 includes post-outcome care and is prohibited from every adjustment/representation. Available fields can distinguish a renal profile association from *measured baseline first-code history and broad subsequent first-code emission*, but cannot separate biological N17 from unmeasured contact, testing, or coding propensity.

## Population, clocks, profiles, outcomes, censoring

Preserve the parent exactly: baseline instance 0; age 40–69; valid sex/index; positive creatinine/cystatin C; at least one grip; race-free 2021 eGFRcr >=60. Verify assay and urine units. Risk starts S=index+30 days. Exclude N17 on/before S and pre-S N18.5/N18.6/Z49/Z94.0/Z99.2/T86.1; the common state also excludes all N18* on/before S. A renal clinician must approve this operational set.

Generate participant-age/sex-specific raw P− and P0 profiles by inverting the inherited equations. Preserve the frozen windows: P− is 85<=G<=95 and −18<=delta<=−12; P0 is 85<=G<=95 and −3<=delta<=3. Require >=100 observations for each window in every sex × five-year-age stratum, both target points inside each observed stratum convex hull, and the inherited local raw-assay nearest-neighbour audit. The frozen 1:1 match is without replacement, exact on sex, five-year age band and assessment year, with |G_i−G_j|<=1.5 and a 0.2 pooled-SD propensity-logit caliper; its propensity model uses inherited nonprofile covariates, centre, continuous age and G. Reject matched inference if either group loses >50%, there are <1,000 pairs, or any prespecified covariate/G |SMD|>0.10. Repeat matching inside each participant bootstrap.

The baseline-only audit had all 24 profile/stratum hull checks pass, worst standardized raw-assay nearest-neighbour distance 0.0431, and 10,893 pairs with 54.9%/90.9% retention and max |SMD| 0.0352. Rerun unchanged after diagnosis restriction and corrected calendar eligibility before outcome modeling; failure is inconclusive, never permission to move G/delta or relax gates.

Through 10 years assign mutually exclusive N17-first, N18-first, same-day N17/N18 tie, death-first, death/renal same-day tie, or event-free/censored. Preserve both tie categories and inherited assignment/exclusion sensitivities.

Ten-year eligibility is S+10 calendar years <= verified administrative end C, not index+10 years. Use a participant-applicable C only if export-linked provider documentation validates it; otherwise censoring_status=unverified and every 10-year clinical inference is inconclusive. Observed maxima (diagnoses 2022-10-31; death 2022-12-19) cannot prove completeness. Do not treat missing 191 as continued observation.

## Frozen pre-index observation profile

All features are calculated strictly before index, not before each outcome. The primary lookback is [index−5 calendar years, index); sensitivity windows are [index−2 years,index) and [index−10,index−5). Report left-history availability because the export begins yielding first appearances around 1995.

Transparent baseline-history block, from valid non-N17/N18 41270/41280 pairs:

1. log1p total distinct code first appearances in the five-year window;
2. log1p counts in [index−5,index−2) and [index−2,index);
3. number of represented ICD-10 chapters;
4. days since the most recent nonrenal first appearance, with “none” explicit;
5. proportion of all-position code/date pairs exactly matched by normalized code and date to a principal 41202/41262 pair, with “none” explicit;
6. assessment calendar year.

Model counts/recency with prespecified restricted splines. This is a baseline morbidity/coding summary, not admission intensity. Missing history may mean no recorded first appearance or unavailable history and is not proof of health.

No post-index or peri-event code count, state, principal confirmation, 41259 total, or future outcome is an adjustment variable. Prior-365-day and event-day counts remain labeled descriptive diagnostics. A post-index HMM may be reported only as an explicitly different mediation/prodrome sensitivity with no “adjusted/deconfounded” language; it is not required and cannot support the primary claim.

Before fitting renal outcomes, quantify the association of P− versus P0 with the *pre-index* scalar-history features and NMF scores using the frozen matched windows and standardized differences. This is a temporal negative-control-style comparison: an index assay profile cannot cause codes first recorded before index, so a strong broad association flags selection, stable frailty/morbidity, or persistent observation differences. It is not a true causal negative control because the biological marker profile may predate its measurement and genuinely relate to prior illness. Report it regardless of direction and never use a favorable balance result to claim absence of unmeasured observation bias.

## Transparent primary analysis and falsification comparisons

Fit inherited cause-specific Cox transition models and standardized CIFs for all-position N17/N18/death/ties with splined G, delta, prespecified G×delta, inherited covariates, and the frozen pre-index observation block. Report theta17, theta18 and D with joint participant-bootstrap uncertainty (>=500 successful replicates; <90% convergence is inconclusive). The unchanged matched Aalen–Johansen corroboration adds the pre-index block to propensity balance and preserves exact strata, |G|<=1.5 pair caliper, propensity caliper, retention, pair-count and SMD gates.

Repeat endpoint definition using principal-position N17/N18 as a directional ascertainment analysis. Estimate profile-by-endpoint principal-confirmation probabilities among all-position events using only baseline variables. Sparse principal N18 prevents treating this as co-primary.

Prespecified post-index comparison outcomes use the same risk origin/horizon but are never covariates:

- annual count/rate of new non-N17/N18 all-position code first appearances, analyzed by overdispersed recurrent-count regression with death and verified follow-up offset;
- any newly first-recorded acute respiratory infection code J09–J18;
- any newly first-recorded injury/poisoning code S00–T14;
- remote negative-control-style families H60–H95 (ear/mastoid) and L00–L99 (skin).

For each family, report all-cohort “any new code” and family-free-at-S first-family-code risk; the latter uses its own explicitly reported risk subset and cannot replace the renal estimand. Report the number of eligible unseen codes at S because first-appearance counts mechanically deplete as history accumulates; do not call the resulting rate healthcare utilization. These are falsification/comparison outcomes, not guaranteed null controls: frailty may genuinely affect infection/injury and cystatin C may have nonrenal correlates. Their role is to detect a broad, non-N17-selective pattern. Freeze families before viewing any profile association; no replacement after results.

Define thetaB for broad nonrenal emission and thetaNC,j for each family. Bootstrap Qj=theta17−thetaNC,j on a compatible log-risk scale. Negative controls support specificity only if their estimates are precise enough; “not significant” is not evidence of absence.

## Substantive learned alternative: baseline-history phenotypes

The scalar block loses diagnosis composition, recency-by-chapter structure, and principal/all-position mix. Learn an outcome-blind nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) from pre-index history only.
