Select rank by validation Poisson reconstruction deviance plus stability (matched-component cosine >=0.80 across seeds), not renal prediction. Apply frozen loadings to validation/test and bootstrap refits; name components only after listing highest-loading codes, and never label them admissions or mechanisms.

Use the learned component scores, rather than post-baseline states, in the identical cause-specific/discrete-time competing-risk model. Compare: inherited clinical covariates; transparent scalar-history block; NMF history; and scalar+NMF. Hold the P−/P0 estimand, population, horizon and endpoint definitions fixed. Evaluate held-out calibration-in-the-large/slope, endpoint/multiclass IPCW Brier, time-dependent AUC, and exact theta17/theta18/D across seeds. Scientific value comes from whether composition/recency reveals a shared morbidity/coding axis that the scalar count hides, not a small AUC gain.

As a multi-outcome stress test, use frozen NMF scores with the broad comparison outcomes. A component that predicts N17, injury/infection, remote-code families and total nonrenal emission similarly favors a shared history/observation interpretation; an N17 association orthogonal to broad components is compatible with, but does not prove, renal selectivity.

A sequence transformer is deferred because each code has only a first-appearance date and NMF directly targets the unresolved baseline composition/recency question. All interpretations require verified censoring, units/code semantics, exact-risk-set support, convergence, calibrated held-out predictions and justified uncertainty.

Thus a gain over the latest snapshot could be generated by more opportunities to observe an abnormal value or by workup intensity, not value evolution.

The strongest supported claim is only that the dataset contains a large explicitly graded resection cohort, selective grade recording is template-era dependent, and routine-care measurement processes can be informative. The unresolved claim tested here is:

> Among explicitly graded, untreated, pathology-HCC first resections in the high-ascertainment 2016–2020 era with at least two strict numeric preoperative lab days, does a model receiving exactly two laboratory days and at most one value per exact label/day improve 2020 prediction of M1/M2 over an otherwise matched latest-day snapshot, after accounting for static severity/tumor-burden inputs and observation intensity?

A positive result supports incremental historical-value prediction under a fixed information budget. It does not establish tumor biology, biological change, causal mechanism, external transport, or treatment benefit. Those stronger claims require scheduled serial assays, validated imaging/pathology, and external prospective study.

Thus most “serial” patients have only two calendar days but many panel rows; unrestricted extrema, token sets, and learned sequences are strongly exposed to panel size and duplication.

No exact laboratory label had at least 20 patients with a strict numeric measurement in both a fixed early window (day −90:−31) and late window (day −30:−1). Within a retained day and exact label, collapse strict numeric duplicates by median; then retain at most one value per label/day. Add earlier value, latest-minus-earlier, and paired-label availability. Do not provide date, gap, row count, or panel multiplicity to V2. Fit 20 train/validation-frozen subsampling replicates and average predictions; report between-replicate uncertainty. The matched S-latest prediction is repeated on the same patients.

4. **D2/T2 learned alternative:** a Deep Sets model over the two capped day sets and a two-step ordinal encoder, respectively, each with the same static inputs and no date/gap/count tokens. They can reveal nonlinear cross-marker and two-state interactions that penalized V2 loses. T2 must beat D2 and lose its gain when the two day embeddings are swapped; with only two days, it does not claim a rich trajectory.

5. **V-all/F-all/T-full exploratory ladder:** preserve the parent's all-observation summaries and learned model only as a process-sensitive contrast. Compare each with its observation-count-matched baseline and V2. Gain present only here is evidence for workup/intensity or exposure-count prediction, not biological trajectory.

This fixed-exposure design distinguishes the specific rival that more observed rows/days mechanically create more extrema, variance, or tokens. It cannot remove selection into having an earlier test or explain why either test was ordered. Therefore all results remain predictive and observational.

## Tumor burden and severity controls

[K1]'s AFP/size/margin score is a benchmark, not currently reproducible from named concepts alone. The examinations table provides dated report text but no images or validated structured tumor fields. Before any “beyond tumor burden” claim, a train-frozen parser must specify:

- latest eligible pre-cutoff report selected by `开始时间`;
- maximum lesion diameter in centimeters from explicit lesion-linked dimensions, multiplicity (single/multiple), and smooth versus irregular margin/capsule;
- modality from `检查`, with report identity by `检查号`;
- rejection of pathology, postoperative, MVI, or ambiguous multi-lesion contexts.

A blinded hepatobiliary/radiology review must sample at least 200 reports across years/modalities and all parser-positive categories. Require ≥95% leakage rejection; size agreement within 5 mm or 10% in ≥90%; and ≥90% agreement for multiplicity and margin. Report coverage and missingness by split/outcome. Until these pass, report-free S/V2/D2/T2 is primary, and conclusions must say “beyond latest routine labs and measured demographics,” not “beyond tumor burden.” If validated, add the same tumor fields to every arm and report the reduced AFP/size/margin benchmark.

Severity rivals are tested through latest liver reserve/inflammation/hematology values, demographics, service, and observation-process covariates. Association surviving adjustment is not mechanistic proof.

## Outcome parser and template falsification

Apply the exact grade regex only within HCC `检查所见`/`检查诊断` rows in the same patient/encounter as index resection. Require one unique grade. Primary pathology review samples 50 per grade plus every biopsy-only case and a stratified sample of the 534 lexical discordance flags across 2016–2020 and 2021. Review must verify HCC, resection specimen/index correspondence, grade, whether generic vascular-invasion fields refer to the same specimen/template section, and adequacy limits. Automated computation can check parser states; only blinded hepatopathology can resolve discordance.

Primary model results are repeated after excluding every lexical discordance flag. A material metric or calibration change, or <95% overall/<90% per grade-era parser agreement, makes outcome interpretation inconclusive. The 2021 stress set is reported separately and never pooled to rescue or reverse the 2020 primary conclusion.

## Estimands, analysis, and falsification

The primary contrast is V2 minus S-latest on identical 2020 patients, averaged over 20 locked subsampling replicates. Report paired AUROC, AUPRC, Brier, log loss, calibration intercept/slope, and decision net benefit at risks 0.20/0.30/0.40/0.50, with 2,000 patient bootstraps nesting the replicate average. Report 2019 validation and 2021 stress results, subgroup calibration when ≥20 events/cell, observation-count strata, and distribution of replicate effects.

Support requires 2020 V2 improvement of ≥0.02 AUROC and ≥0.01 Brier, both paired 95% intervals excluding zero, calibration slope 0.8–1.2, net-benefit gain at two adjacent thresholds without material harm elsewhere, no direction reversal in 2019, and a positive effect in at least 16/20 fixed replicates. It also requires V2 to improve over O-process, remain after discordance exclusion, and retain at least half its Brier gain after adding validated tumor burden if that parser passes.

A learned two-state claim additionally requires D2 or T2 to beat V2 in both AUROC and Brier with intervals excluding zero; an order-specific claim requires T2 to beat D2 and swapped-order T2 with ≥50% attenuation of its Brier gain.

Adverse evidence is precise exclusion of the V2 thresholds; gain only in V-all/F-all/T-full; O-process matching V2; instability across subsamples; disappearance after outcome-discordance exclusion or validated tumor burden; or reversal in 2019. These results park the biological-trajectory branch and may retain only an operational workup-intensity predictor.

Inconclusive evidence includes broad intervals, poor calibration, inadequate paired-label support after exact-label capping, failed tumor/pathology adjudication, or stable 2020 performance with major 2021 stress failure. The last indicates template dependence and blocks deployment but does not negate 2020 internal prediction.

Mandatory controls are outcome permutation, day −7 cutoff, latest-day-only input, report-free primary, exact-label-only processing, same-day median collapse, any-prior-recorded-treatment exclusion, 2014–2015 era stress, leave-one-training-year-out fits, feature-time leakage tests, and observation-only/value-masked controls.

## Exact read-only bindings

Snapshot: `3f97e661e1884c34c1e2cdbf74ba0cf6d6c8995853e85f1857c3d72b82ccf521`. Join encounter tables on (`患者主索引`, `就诊号`); link longitudinal history by `患者主索引`. Source files remain read-only; derived files stay in the workspace.

- `procedures`: `[private path]`; keys plus `手术`, `开始时间`, `结束时间`, `手术来源`. Index and recorded treatment exclusions.
- `encounters`: `[private path]`; keys plus `年龄`, `性别`, `就诊时间`, `入院时间`, `出院时间`, `就诊科室`. Demographics/service/clock audit.
- `labs`: `[private path]`; keys plus `检验`, `定性结果`, `定量结果`, `标本类型`, `检验时间`. Strict numeric exact-label values; no unit, platform, or reference-range columns.
- `examinations`: `[private path]`; keys plus `检查`, `检查所见`, `检查诊断`, `开始时间`, `机器型号`, `检查号`. Tumor-report validation only; no images.
- `medications`: `[private path]`; keys, medication/dose/unit/frequency, `开始时间`, `结束时间`, route/type. Prior systemic-treatment sensitivity; indication absent.
- `clinical_documents`: `[private path]`; keys and narrative fields. Adjudication only; no row time.
- `diagnoses`: `[private path]`; keys, `诊断名称`, `诊断类型`. Untimed audit only.

Mortality, recurrence, outside treatment/intent, assay units/platforms, pathology issue time, blocks/sampling protocol, and images are unavailable. Vitals, transfers, and front-page files contain identifiers only.

## Deliverable, alternatives, compute, and verification

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted S-latest, O-process, 20-replicate V2, D2/T2, and exploratory all-observation models with locked 2019/2020/2021 predictions; parser/adjudication manifests; paired metrics; and a `claims.json` linking each conclusion to computed outputs and the rules above. Confirmation is not required.

D2/T2 uses one allocated A100 plus 8 CPUs/64 GiB for an unverified 2–4 hours. This fits the 16-CPU/262-GiB/8-hour solver envelope.

A distant fixed-window slope was considered and rejected because no exact label had ≥20 early/late paired patients. The unrestricted V/F/T ladder is retained only as an exploratory process-sensitive contrast. GP/state-space models are deferred because two-day median support and missing units do not identify latent biology. Revisit a mechanistic trajectory study only with scheduled serial assays, stable units, validated imaging, and pathology sampling metadata.

The verifier can check source hashes/headers, joins, clocks, parser states, split isolation, one-value-per-label/day caps, fixed seeds, matched patients, nested bootstrap arithmetic, metrics, and whether conclusions obey supportive/adverse/inconclusive rules. It must reject claims of biology, mechanism, tumor-burden adjustment before parser validation, transport beyond explicitly graded cases, or clinical benefit. Clinical adjudication, sampling adequacy, and utility are not automatically verifiable.

## Frozen scientific design

# Can an all-hour excess-FiO2 signal survive phenotype and oxygen-record uncertainty without selecting on same-hour oxygenation?

## Status, scientific opening, and deliverable

This is a planned crossover of `candidate-cd573b08625c119f6e52a3d4` and `candidate-dd1326a6e221f73681ef2059`; no mortality association or model performance is reported. It preserves the former parent's pre-hour-24-standardized, all-hour exposure estimand and the latter parent's measurement-first phenotype/source-error design. It removes the latter parent's fatal same-hour adequacy filter: oxygenation observed at or after an FiO2 setting is a possible response, never a condition for that hour to enter the primary exposure.

ICU-ROX shows that an oxygen-target protocol can reduce oxygen exposure without significantly changing ventilator-free days in a broad ventilated ICU population [K1]. A mechanistic review distinguishes inspired hyperoxia from arterial hyperoxaemia and describes experimental oxygen–mechanical-stress synergy while emphasizing inconsistent clinical mortality evidence [K2]. LUNG SAFE shows incomplete, severity-dependent clinician recognition even when prospective Berlin-definition components were collected [K3]. The strongest supported claim is therefore limited: oxygen exposure is modifiable; inspired exposure and arterial oxygen are not interchangeable; and pulmonary-injury labels can be severity-dependent. These works do not establish oxygen toxicity in eICU, validate this pulmonary proxy, or validate recorded FiO2 as delivered airway FiO2.

The unresolved clinical hypothesis is:

**Among adult first ICU stays alive and still in ICU at hour 36, with a PaO2 80–120 mm Hg paired to FiO2 during hours 18–24, the pre-hour-24 acute-pulmonary-injury proxy modifies the association between mean all-hour excess FiO2 during hours 24–36 and seven-day post-hour-36 in-hospital death; a positive pulmonary interaction will remain distinguishable from phenotype/FiO2 error, evolving severity, clinician response, ventilation co-treatment, hospital practice, and observation processes.**

The primary estimand is descriptive: the pulmonary-minus-comparator difference in pre-hour-24-standardized seven-day death cumulative-incidence risk-difference slope per +0.10 in
`B_i=(1/12) sum_t (F_it-0.40)+` over all 12 exposure hours. Live hospital discharge competes. `F_it` is the true hour-level setting represented by an interval when uncertain. No same-hour SpO2, SaO2, or PaO2 determines whether an hour contributes. This is an exposure-response contrast among hour-36 survivors, not an identified treatment effect.

The new measurement hypothesis, tested first, is:

**Using blinded clinical labels, cross-source FiO2 pairs, and all-hour logical bounds, the simultaneous upper 95% bound on a pulmonary interaction producible by joint phenotype/FiO2 ascertainment alone is <1.5 absolute seven-day risk points per +0.10 excess FiO2, and the burden is measured precisely enough in both strata to resolve a clinically consequential 3-point interaction.**

Failure is informative: it means eICU cannot distinguish the proposed interaction from its measurement process under the frozen assumptions. It ends pulmonary-toxicity interpretation without changing the population, exposure hours, or outcome.

The required scientific deliverable is newly fitted/estimated output: a frozen cohort and 12-hour panel; phenotype review estimates; source-error and missing-hour burden intervals; transparent measurement/error envelopes; identical hospital folds; a calibrated ordered latent/sequential model; competing-risk interaction estimates; rival-prediction and falsification matrices; and a gate-governed supportive, adverse, or inconclusive conclusion. Completion never requires confirmation.

## Why this could change a clinical decision

A robust pulmonary-specific delayed signal would justify prospective phenotype validation and stratification in a future oxygen-titration trial. A precise adverse result would argue against enriching a trial with this eICU proxy. Broad all-hour bounds, source-dependent reversal, or failed phenotype validation would redirect resources toward device/chart validation rather than an oxygen-restriction trial. A signal explained by clinician response or ventilation would redirect the hypothesis toward treatment selection or combined ventilator management.

Leading and rival predictions are frozen before outcomes:

| Explanation | Distinguishing prediction |
|---|---|
| Delayed oxygen–mechanical-stress compatibility | After a pre-hour-24-standardized comparison, excess FiO2 precedes delayed deterioration; its lagged interaction with pressure/PEEP is stronger in validated injury; it survives source/hospital envelopes. |
| Evolving severity | Hypoxaemia, shock, or respiratory worsening precedes FiO2 escalation; pre-escalation deterioration predicts later burden; temporal representation removes the pulmonary pattern. |
| Clinician response | Treatment-head residuals and pre-decision state explain escalation; outcome association concentrates in settings strongly predicted from prior observed severity. |
| Ventilation co-treatment | Pressure/PEEP/tidal-volume/support changes travel with FiO2; ventilation burden, not oxygen lag, explains the transition or the oxygen interaction is not separable. |
| Observation practice | Burden or interaction follows chart presence, time since chart, source, entry delay, or hospital; downsampling/source balancing reproduces or reverses it. |
| Phenotype error | Review-supported injury crosses P0 strata differentially by severity/site; propagated label error can manufacture the interaction. |

Unmeasured intent, ambiguous simultaneous chart times, prior oxygen before hour 24, and unavailable delivered-airway measurements can leave rivals indistinguishable even after all models pass.

## Population, clocks, phenotype, outcome

Index `patient.patientunitstayid`. Include age >=18 (map `age='> 89'` to 90 for adjustment only), the first ICU stay in each `patienthealthsystemstayid` by lowest valid `unitvisitnumber` then `patientunitstayid`, and `unitdischargeoffset>2160`. Require alive/in ICU at minute 2160. Exclude impossible chronology, burns, documented extracorporeal support by minute 1440, and exact `carePlanGeneral.cplgroup='Care Limitation'`, `cplitemvalue='Comfort measures only'` by minute 1440. DNR, no-intubation, no-CPR, and EOL-discussion rows are retained as baseline indicators and sensitivities, not equated with comfort-only care.

Immutable boundaries:

- baseline and phenotype: ICU admission through minute 1440;
- anchor: last valid PaO2 80–120 in minutes 1080–1440, paired to closest valid FiO2 within ±60 minutes; equal-distance ties prefer preceding, then earlier FiO2;
- exposure: minute 1440 inclusive to 2160 exclusive, exactly 12 hourly bins;
- outcome origin: minute 2160;
- follow-up: `(2160,12240]`, seven days after hour 36.

P0 acute-pulmonary-injury proxy requires by minute 1440 both a frozen diagnosis/admission term (ARDS/acute respiratory distress, pneumonia, aspiration, pulmonary oedema, or acute respiratory failure) and anchor P/F <=300. Primary comparator has no frozen acute term, regardless of P/F. Term/PF>300 is discordant validation; no-term/PF>300 is a sparse sensitivity. The proxy is not Berlin ARDS.

Primary outcome is hospital death after minute 2160 through 12240 using `hospitaldischargestatus='Expired'` and `hospitaldischargeoffset`. Live hospital discharge in the interval is competing; still hospitalized at day seven is administrative censoring. Report Aalen–Johansen risks. Secondary ICU death and hour-36–72 respiratory deterioration are subordinate and require timestamp coverage. `actualventdays` is never a timestamped endpoint.

## Stage 1: measurement before association

### 1A. Outcome-blind census and clinician anchor

2. **Clinician-response head:** models latent FiO2 `F_t` from `S_t`, observed history, prior treatment, baseline P, and hierarchical hospital practice.
3. **Ventilation co-treatment head:** models support/PEEP/pressure/tidal-volume/rate changes jointly with FiO2. If order within a bin is ambiguous, treat them as a joint action; do not call one a confounder of the other.
4. **Observation head:** models whether/when FiO2 sources, ABG, saturation, ventilator settings, diagnoses, notes, and examinations appear, conditional on past observed state, action, and hospital.
5. **Response transition:** after action, predicts next-hour respiratory/hemodynamic state. Lagged excess FiO2, ventilation burden, and a prespecified oxygen × lagged-pressure/PEEP interaction enter here, never the pre-treatment state.
6. After hour 36, competing death/discharge heads use the inferred history.

Latent `F_t` emits respiratory-chart, lab, and respiratory-care values with source/hospital error. P1 clinician labels anchor pre-hour-24 latent pulmonary class. Outcome labels are withheld while treatment, source, observation, support-state, and next-hour physiology components are fitted. S1 must reproduce M0 observed-data contrasts on shared support and pass held-hospital calibration for FiO2 pairs, clinician labels, treatment density, observation hazards, support state, next-hour PaO2/SpO2, and event risk.

S1's primary scientific addition is decomposition, not predictive gain. Compare:

- FiO2 association before versus after representing clinician-response propensity;
- oxygen lag versus ventilation co-treatment and oxygen×mechanical-stress transition terms;
- complete-observation versus source-downsampled posterior predictions;
- outcome association beginning before escalation, 1–3 hours after, or later.

A secondary g-computation scenario caps `F_t` at 0.40 only when adequacy was documented strictly before the treatment decision; hypoxaemic and unknown hours remain observed. It is not the primary all-hour estimand and is called a model-based scenario under sequential exchangeability, consistency, positivity, ordering, and measurement assumptions—not a trial effect.

A structured Bayesian state-space model or constrained variational recurrent model is acceptable. Architecture is frozen by outcome-blind calibration, not AUROC. M1 cannot override M0 or rescue a failed gate.

## Baseline outcome analysis and matched evaluation

B0 is a cause-specific pooled logistic death/live-discharge model with restricted cubic spline for interval-valued all-hour burden, P1 pulmonary probability/stratum and interaction. Standardization uses only minute-1440-fixed variables: age, sex, ethnicity, admission source/type, unit type; hospital region/size/teaching and partial-pooling intercept; APACHE IV score/predicted mortality; anchor PaO2/FiO2/PF; baseline pH, PaCO2, lactate, renal/hepatic/haematologic measures; vasopressor/support status; pre-hour-24 PEEP/pressure/tidal-volume/rate; comorbidity/diagnostic groups; and treatment limitations. Report unadjusted and standardized Aalen–Johansen risks, hospital-cluster uncertainty, calibration, overlap, and exposure intervals.

A frozen attribution ladder adds hours 18–24 trends, then hour-24–36 severity/oxygenation, ventilation, and observation summaries. These are changed conditional contrasts, not total-effect repairs. Persistence does not prove toxicity; attenuation may reflect confounding control, mediation removal, measurement error, or collider conditioning.

All models use five folds grouped by `hospitalid`; `uniquepid` never crosses folds. Evaluate burden precision, calibration, Brier score/integrated calibration index, source agreement, treatment and observation calibration, physiology error, overlap/ESS, interaction interval, and error-only envelope. Small AUROC gain is irrelevant.

## Hard gates and falsification

Thresholds are frozen before outcomes and never relaxed:

1. Phase-II weighted P1 PPV and sensitivity each >=0.80 with simultaneous lower 95% bounds >=0.70; indeterminate <=15% overall and <=25% by documentation quartile. Simultaneous PPV/sensitivity differences across documentation quartiles/support classes <=0.15.
2. Paired-source median absolute FiO2 difference <=0.05, 90th percentile <=0.10, disagreement-probability difference by stratum/documentation quartile <=0.10; >=150 pairs per stratum from >=20 hospitals.
3. Report logical bounds for everyone. For association resolution, the validation-bounded median `B_i` width must be <=0.10 in each stratum and its 75th percentile <=0.15; no source family or five hospitals may provide >50% of weighted exposure information. Failure is an exposure-measurement result, not grounds to exclude sparse stays.
4. Both strata require >=40 seven-day deaths; generalized-propensity ESS >=100 per stratum and >=5% support in every prespecified decile.
5. M0 simultaneous upper 95% bound on maximum error-only interaction must be <1.5 risk points per +0.10. The observed clinically consequential interaction must remain distinguishable from zero and the error envelope. S1 must pass every held-hospital calibration gate and remain inside M0 measurement bounds.
6. Direction cannot be determined by five hospitals, event-versus-entry clock, one FiO2 source, or high-coverage sites.

Negative controls: hour-24–36 burden must not predict deterioration defined wholly in hours 12–18 after baseline adjustment; entry delay and LPM-O2 conditional on FiO2 must not reproduce the interaction; moving diagnosis cutoff from event to entry time must not create it. Report term-family removal, strict ARDS terms, P/F 200/300, invasive-support-only, source downsampling, lab-versus-respiratory FiO2, threshold 0.30/0.50/0.60, and high-coverage hospitals jointly. None may be promoted post hoc.

**Supportive:** all measurement/calibration/overlap gates pass; M0 and admissible S1 show a positive pulmonary interaction whose 95% lower bound exceeds the error envelope and includes approximately >=3 risk points per +0.10; FiO2 precedes delayed deterioration; ventilation and observation rivals do not reproduce it. This supports prospective validation/trial stratification, not causation.

**Adverse:** corrected estimates precisely exclude a 3-point interaction; the error envelope reproduces it; phenotype/source error is differential; temporal association begins before escalation; ventilation co-treatment explains it; or no pulmonary specificity remains. This argues against the proposed enrichment rationale.

**Inconclusive:** logical/validation bounds remain broad, review is unavailable, events/overlap/calibration fail, M0 and S1 disagree, or hospitals dominate. An imprecise null does not refute oxygen toxicity. Measurement failure is still a completed Stage-1 finding.

# Fixed-combined-eGFR profiles and commensurable broad first-code falsification

Status: prospective substantive child of candidate-16996354303179526dbd41f1. No P−/P0 association has been estimated. This child preserves the parent's age-40–69 population, fixed-combined-eGFR profiles, day-30 origin, common N17/N18-free risk set, 10-year competing-transition estimand D, profile-support and matching gates, censoring hard gate, uncertainty, and clinical limits. The change is confined to the strongest remaining interpretation threat: broad post-index first-code outcomes are redesigned so depletion of unseen codes, competing death, and different family risk subsets cannot masquerade as renal specificity.

## Opening, evidence, unresolved claim, and advance

The strongest inspected evidence supports only these bounded claims. Large eGFRcys-minus-eGFRcr differences are common in UK Biobank and have kidney and non-GFR predictors [K1]. In SPRINT, this difference tracked frailty and broad adverse outcomes, and the combined equation could lose prognostic information [K2]. Administrative AKI coding can be insensitive and subgroup-dependent relative to serum-creatinine KDIGO AKI [K3]. In the attached parent audit, recorded N17-first and N18-first also had different coding contexts: same-day principal-family confirmation was 12.0% versus 1.39%, and median nonrenal first-code counts in the prior 365 days were 3 versus 0. These are observed ascertainment differences; they do not establish a P−/P0 association or its cause.

Unresolved hypothesis: among supported UKB adults aged 40–69 in the common day-30 N17/N18-free state, P− (2021 combined eGFR G=90 and eGFRcys−eGFRcr=−15), versus P0 (G=90 and delta=0), has a larger adjusted 10-year relative-risk contrast for first recorded inpatient N17 than for first recorded inpatient N18, and that excess is greater than a commensurable contrast for generalized new nonrenal code emission after measured pre-index history is represented.

Let theta17=log RR10(N17-first; P−/P0), theta18=log RR10(N18-first; P−/P0), and D=theta17−theta18. D remains primary. The broad comparison's main contrast is thetaK=log RR10(reaching a profile-blinded K-th new nonrenal three-character code before death; P−/P0), standardized over exactly the primary renal cohort; QK=theta17−thetaK. The experiment distinguishes:

- renal-selective recorded transition information: theta17 and D are positive, while QK shows N17 is stronger than an adequately powered, incidence-commensurate broad first-code burden;
- generalized morbidity/first-code opportunity: measured baseline history explains D, or P− predicts the broad burden at least as strongly as N17 under both threshold and depletion-process analyses.

This is descriptive prognostic discrimination, not a causal effect of discordance. Neither adjustment nor QK identifies true GFR, renal reserve, biological AKI/CKD, contact opportunity, coding behavior, or mechanism. # Residual instability before ICU-to-ward transfer

## Objective and claim boundary

Run the frozen MIMIC-IV 3.1 experiment. Test whether, among adult ICU-to-general-ward transfers with the same measured endpoint state at ICU exit (t0), unusually worsening rather than improving recent measured-value history adds calibrated 48-hour ICU-return/death risk information and changes a fixed-capacity review list.

Existing evidence supports only bounded premises: longitudinal ICU-discharge models can outperform snapshot scores while operational factors and composite outcomes complicate interpretation [K1]; ICU-readmission studies are heterogeneous and often at risk of bias [K2]; and EHR observation patterns encode healthcare processes [K3]. The supplied outcome-blind audit established a reconstructible 49,157-transfer cohort and adequate trajectory coverage. None establishes the hypothesis.

The leading explanation is residual temporally ordered measured-value information. The principal rival is mathematical coupling/regression to the mean because endpoint state and direction share late observations, with treatment and observation processes as another rival. This is a predictive/measurement experiment, not a causal intervention study. Even supportive results cannot establish latent physiology, preventability, clinician intent, or benefit from delaying transfer or increasing monitoring.

## Private inputs and exact bindings

- /data/mimic-iv-3.1.zip, SHA-256 0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09.

Required archive members and fields:

Freeze the oxygen-device ordinal mapping using development data before evaluation.

## Population, timing, and outcomes

Select the first eligible transfer per [internal identifier], ordered by (t0, [internal identifier]), among patients aged at least 18 at ICU admission, ICU LOS at least 24 hours, alive at t0, and having an exact transfers.intime == icustays.outtime successor to one of: Medicine; Neurology; Med/Surg; Medicine/Cardiology; Transplant; Vascular; Med/Surg/GYN; Surgery/Trauma; Med/Surg/Trauma; Surgery; Cardiac Surgery; Medical/Surgical (Gynecology); Surgery/Pancreatic/Biliary/Bariatric; Cardiology; Thoracic Surgery; Oncology; Hematology/Oncology.

Expected cohort: 49,157 transfers in 40,014 subjects. The sorted [internal identifier]|[internal identifier]|[internal identifier]|t0 hash is 6ad3a42f647d239d5a164a0c4a0ca88834293ee03a55d836e20a16c929392502 using ISO timestamps, one LF-terminated record per line.

Use predictors only from [t0-24h,t0). For charted rows require charttime<t0 and storetime<t0; for interval events require window overlap and storetime<t0. The primary binary outcome is any later same-admission ICU intime or admissions.deathtime in (t0,t0+48h]. Preserve the raw return/death/no-event state and perform the adjudicated first-transition extension (ward-to-return, ward-to-death, or valid live discharge); retain unresolved and administratively discordant records. Expected raw composite events: 2,607. The sorted cohort-plus-y_rd hash is 69e531ca47d653593f7d236553e8d4cb6a4c338ce362727006c7cb36f466c154.

## Split and opening order

Create a deterministic subject-level pooled 60/20/20 development/validation/test split using seed string seed-20260923. In a restricted split builder, stratify subjects by (any qualifying R+D, dominant destination); resolve destination ties lexicographically, order subjects in each stratum by SHA-256(seed-20260923|[internal identifier]), then assign the first floor(0.60*n), next floor(0.20*n), and remainder. Write and hash the role-only split before model or outcome-responsive feature choices. Its required [internal identifier]|role LF-record SHA-256 is 9e6594c880cac8f2d5e218bfdd535431bd107f29e3a712fdc323ec289b88c576. No subject may cross roles. Evaluation labels remain closed until feature, nuisance, model, null, and seed choices are locked.

Also assign approximate eras from anchor_year_group shifted by t0.year-anchor_year: development if the entire interval is <=2013; validation if entirely 2014-2016; locked test if entirely 2017-2019; stress test if entirely >=2020; otherwise boundary-ambiguous. If a subject spans strict roles, retain only the latest strict role and mark earlier rows withheld. Fit on development, select/calibrate on validation, open 2017-2019 once, then open 2020-2022 separately. Expected strict counts: 17,215; 8,859; 6,435; 5,285. Boundary-ambiguous and withheld rows cannot establish transport.

## Features and models

Use six left-closed two-hour bins over [t0-12h,t0). Apply fixed plausibility checks; convert Fahrenheit to Celsius and percent FiO2 to fraction. For each domain compute a clinically oriented standardized abnormality margin, not a raw-unit average. Preserve missingness, freshness, observed-bin counts, distinct hours, store lag, and caregiver count.

E0 is a regularized endpoint-state model using final values/freshness/missingness for the six domains, GCS, ventilation/vasopressor/oxygen state, age, sex, ICU LOS, source, destination, latest service, transfer clock, and observation/process summaries. Fit multinomial return/death/no-event models in development, select regularization in subject-grouped folds, and calibrate only in validation. Set C=logit(p_E0(R+D)) using out-of-fold development predictions and frozen later-role predictions. E0-4 is identical except endpoint measurements are restricted to [t0-4h,t0).

For raw G, require at least two observed bins in each six-hour half in at least four of HR, BP, RR, SpO2, temperature, and oxygen support. For each eligible domain subtract the median standardized abnormality margin in [t0-12h,t0-6h) from [t0-6h,t0), then average domains; positive means worsening. Fit D1 = E0 + spline(G) + tensor-spline(C,G), retaining the multinomial target, grouped fitting, and calibration. Freeze development 30th/70th percentile communication cuts. Never tune thresholds or subgroups on outcomes.

Build nuisance Z from six endpoint margins, freshness/missingness, C, destination, service, ICU source, transfer clock, ICU LOS, per-half observation counts, distinct hours, store lag, caregiver count, and ventilation/vasopressor/oxygen start, stop, escalation, de-escalation, or no recorded change. Compare ridge additive and depth-3 histogram gradient boosting for m(Z)=E(G|Z) by grouped development RMSE only. Use out-of-fold development predictions and one frozen later-role fit. Define G_perp=(G-m_hat(Z))/development residual SD. R+D labels must not enter nuisance selection. In validation and each evaluation era, the balance gate requires absolute standardized slope on m_hat(Z)<0.05, absolute Spearman correlation with C<0.05, and no endpoint/process block explaining >1% additional residual variance. Fit D1-perp analogously.

For G_pre compare [t0-12h,t0-8h) with [t0-8h,t0-4h), requiring both bins per half and at least four domains. Fit D1-pre=E0-4+spline(G_pre)+tensor-spline(C-4,G_pre). Assert no chart row contributes to both G_pre and E0-4. Coverage below 70% in an evaluation role makes corroboration unavailable; null G-pre alone is not refutation.

The learned alternative L2-D is a fixed two-stream causal temporal convolutional network on the same grid and static E0 context, with five seeds, validation early stopping, and validation-only temperature scaling. The value stream has values/missingness; the process stream has observation/store-lag/caregiver/treatment signals. Fit full, value+static, process+static, and static-only heads. It can reveal nonlinear relapse, cross-domain lag, and opposing-domain patterns lost by scalar G. Select it over D1-perp only if calibrated and seed-stable, better in both locked late eras, and its value/full gain exceeds process-only and order-null heads. Otherwise prefer the transparent model.

## Endpoint-fixed order null and sensitivities

For each patient/domain, freeze the final observed bin and value. For exactly 200 seeds named order-null-000 through order-null-199, permute remaining observed abnormality-margin summaries only among that patient's remaining observed positions. For each seed, [internal identifier], and domain, initialize NumPy PCG64 from the first 16 hexadecimal characters of SHA-256(seed|[internal identifier]|domain); this makes permutations independent of row-processing order. Preserve value multiset, final value, missing positions, chart/store schedule, caregivers, process/treatment stream, outcomes, split, and era. Recompute G and refit nuisance and D1 pipelines using development/validation only for every seed. Never permute across patients or domains. Also reverse the five nonfinal positions exactly. Apply order-null-000 through order-null-019 to each learned value stream while holding its process stream fixed. Use learned training seeds l2-seed-0 through l2-seed-4.

Report the fraction of raw-G rows with >=4 domains having >=2 distinct nonfinal margins; row/era variance of G_perm; fraction unchanged under all permutations and reversal; and observed-minus-null interval widths. A positional movability count alone is insufficient. Degenerate permutations or intervals spanning material benefit and harm make order attribution inconclusive; L2-D cannot rescue it.

Report no-recorded-support-change and observation-stable sensitivities, plus active-treatment and observation-change strata. Stability requires equal observed-bin counts in both halves for every eligible domain and store-lag change within the development IQR.

## Metrics, uncertainty, and falsification

Use paired 2,000-replicate subject-cluster bootstraps. For each analysis/model/role/metric key, initialize NumPy PCG64 from the first 16 hexadecimal characters of SHA-256(bootstrap-20260923|analysis|model|role|metric), sample that role's unique subject IDs with replacement at the original subject count, and retain every row for each sampled subject. Reuse each paired replicate across models in the same analysis/role/metric comparison; resample eras independently. Report Brier score/gain versus E0, calibration, secondary discrimination, continuous C-by-direction contrast on the frozen 30/70 grid, and event capture/swaps at top 2%, 5%, and 10% review quotas. Include raw, adjudicated, pooled-test, locked-era, stress-era, quiet/stable, active/change, order-null, reversal, and model-head results with uncertainty.

A supportive result requires supportive raw D1; same-sign D1-perp interaction with 95% CI excluding zero in pooled test and both locked late eras; concordant adjudicated R+D; positive 95% intervals for observed-minus-median-null interaction and Brier gain; >=2 additional R+D events per 1,000 reviewed over null at a parent-supported quota without lower overall capture; attenuated/opposite reversal; and either concordant G-pre with interval excluding zero in pooled test or persistence in both quiet and observation-stable sensitivities. L2-D claims must exceed process-only and order-null heads.

A coupling/mean-reversion adverse result requires raw D1 support but reproduction by the order null: upper 95% bound of observed-minus-null Brier gain <0.002, interaction difference includes/favors zero, reversal does not attenuate/reverse, and upper capture advantage <2/1,000 at every quota. If D1-perp is materially null, attribute the raw pattern to unordered repeated values plus endpoint coupling under this design; do not rescue it with L2-D.

A treatment/measurement adverse result requires absence/reversal in quiet and stable sensitivities while process-only or active/change patterns reproduce ranking. It supports only a treatment/documentation-associated predictor. Endpoint sufficiency requires pooled and both late-era upper bounds excluding 0.002 Brier gain and 2 captures/1,000 at every quota. Otherwise report inconclusive, including failed balance, inadequate null variation, <70% coverage, unstable seeds, endpoint disagreement, calibration/support failure, or intervals spanning benefit and harm. Negative and inconclusive results are valid completions.

## Required deliverables

Write these files under /workspace/results/:

- manifest.json: schema residual-instability-v1; source/member/header checks; hashes; cohort/event/split/era counts; split hash; seeds; feature/model specifications; fit counts; code hashes; opening ledger; resources; and leakage assertions.
- predictions.csv.gz: one row per cohort transfer with [internal identifier],[internal identifier],[internal identifier],t0,pooled_role,era_role,y_rd,y_state,g,g_perp,g_pre,eligible_g,eligible_g_pre,quiet,observation_stable,administrative_discordance,p_e0,p_d1,p_d1_perp,p_d1_pre,p_l2_full,p_l2_value,p_l2_process,p_l2_static. Blank values are allowed only where prespecified eligibility makes them unavailable.
- metrics.csv: analysis,model,role,metric,estimate,ci_low,ci_high,n,events; include Brier/gain, calibration, interaction, and quota capture for every required comparison.
- interaction_grid.csv: analysis,model,role,c_quantile,direction_quantile,predicted_risk for the frozen development 30/70 endpoint-state and direction grid; metrics.csv interaction values must be the corresponding risk-scale difference-in-differences.
- bootstrap_metrics.csv.gz: all 2,000 replicate values as replicate,analysis,model,role,metric,value.
- null_metrics.csv.gz: every null as seed,model,role,metric,value, plus reversal rows with seed reversal.
- diagnostics.json: nuisance balance, G/G-pre coverage, nonoverlap, effective-permutation diagnostics, calibration, learned-seed stability, and adjudication diagnostics by role.
- conclusion.json: schema residual-instability-conclusion-v1; one primary_state from supportive, coupling_adverse, process_adverse, endpoint_sufficiency, inconclusive; claim_codes; criteria mapping every applicable rule to metric rows; limitations.
- conclusion.md: concise result narrative linked to computed files and uncertainty.
- code_manifest.json and executable analysis source under /workspace/results/code/. Hash every code file and identify the entry point; never copy source rows or note text.

The verifier recomputes cohort/outcome hashes, Brier scores, quota captures, bootstrap intervals, null contrasts, and permissible conclusion states from row-level artifacts. It rejects missing fits/uncertainty, canned summaries, stale hashes, nuisance outcome leakage, unsupported favorable claims, and overclaiming from adverse or inconclusive results. It cannot establish clinical meaning, novelty, mechanism, actionability, external transport, or intervention benefit.

## Key bibliography

[K1] Heo Y, Kim M, Han SS, et al. “AI-Driven Predictions of Readmission and Mortality for Improved Discharge Decisions in Critical Care: A Retrospective Study.” Diagnostics. 2026;16(6):874. https://doi.org/10.3390/diagnostics16060874

[K2] Ruppert MM, Loftus TJ, Small C, et al. “Predictive Modeling for Readmission to Intensive Care: A Systematic Review.” Critical Care Explorations. 2023;5(1):e0848. https://doi.org/10.1097/CCE.0000000000000848

[K3] Agniel D, Kohane IS, Weber GM. “Biases in electronic health record data due to processes within the healthcare system: retrospective observational study.” BMJ. 2018;361:k1479. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.k1479

# Residual instability before ICU-to-ward transfer: audited coupling-control support

Status: substantive feasibility child of `candidate-a55f6605efa134eb3b52755f`. The exact support audit reported here was outcome-blind. No post-transfer R+D label, outcome model, interaction, order-null metric, or clinical result was computed.

## What is known, what remains unresolved, and why it matters

The strongest evidence supports three bounded premises. Longitudinal ICU-discharge models can outperform a snapshot score, but operational factors, treatment limitation, and composite components remain unresolved [K1]. Across ICU-readmission studies, longitudinal predictors can improve performance, but populations, windows, outcomes, and risk of bias vary [K2]. Observation timing and frequency can be more predictive than measured values because EHR trajectories encode healthcare processes [K3]. The parent further established an exact 49,157-transfer MIMIC-IV cohort, 2,607 raw 48-hour ICU-return/death events, and a mathematical-coupling rival: endpoint severity and recent direction share late measurements.

This child establishes only computability. It exactly reproduces the frozen cohort and shows adequate pre-outcome support for temporally disjoint `G_pre` and endpoint-fixed order permutations in the full cohort and every reconstructible approximate-era role. It does not establish that direction predicts an outcome.

The unresolved hypothesis is unchanged: among ICU-to-general-ward transfers with the same measured endpoint state at `t0`, unusually worsening rather than improving recent measured-value history changes calibrated 48-hour ICU-return/death risk and fixed-capacity ranking, particularly when endpoint state and direction disagree. The leading bounded explanation is residual temporally ordered measured-value information. The strongest rival remains mathematical coupling/regression to the mean plus treatment- and observation-process dynamics. Resolution could determine whether ward/rapid-response review priority should depend on recent direction in addition to current state; it cannot show that review, delayed transfer, or ICU retention improves outcomes.

## Frozen design

Retain the parent without changing its hypothesis, population, temporal boundaries, estimands, outcomes, thresholds, analyses, or falsification criteria:

- first eligible adult ICU-to-one-of-17-frozen-general-ward transfers per hospitalization after ICU LOS at least 24 hours; `t0=icu/icustays.outtime` and exact `hosp/transfers.intime=t0`;
- predictors only in `[t0-24h,t0)`; chart rows require both `charttime<t0` and `storetime<t0`; interval treatment events require window overlap and `storetime<t0`;
- raw three-state 48-hour outcome, same-admission later ICU return or `admissions.deathtime` in `(t0,t0+48h]`, and the adjudicated first-transition R/D/valid-live-discharge extension;
- pooled seed-20260923 subject split, 2,000 subject-cluster bootstrap replicates, and subject-isolated approximate-era development, validation, locked 2017-2019 test, then separately opened 2020-2022 stress test;
- endpoint state `C=logit(p_E0(R+D))`;
- raw `G` over six two-hour bins in `[t0-12h,t0)`, requiring at least two observed bins per six-hour half in at least four of HR, BP, RR, SpO2, temperature, and oxygen support;
- outcome-blind `G_perp` residualization against endpoint, observation, context, and recorded treatment variables;
- `G_pre` from `[t0-12,-8)` versus `[t0-8,-4)` and `E0-4` restricted to `[t0-4,t0)`, with a half-open boundary proving no chart row enters both;
- 200 within-patient/domain endpoint-fixed order permutations plus reversal, preserving the final observed value, value multiset, missing positions, chart/store schedule, caregivers, process/treatment sequence, split, and era;
- transparent `E0/raw D1/D1-perp/D1-pre` models and the two-stream causal TCN `L2-D`, with full, value+static, process+static, and static-only heads.

The scientific deliverable remains newly fitted endpoint/direction models and two-stream alternatives, 200 refitted null pipelines, held-out predictions and uncertainty, and conclusion-rule-linked worklist/interaction/Brier outputs. This support audit is not that deliverable.

## Outcome-blind exact-cohort audit

The scan used MIMIC-IV 3.1 source rows but never constructed later ICU return, death after `t0`, the 48-hour composite, live discharge, notes, outcome-stratified cells, direction effects, or any outcome association. `admissions.deathtime` was read only for the frozen alive-at-`t0` inclusion rule. Numeric values were used only to enforce the fixed plausibility ranges before counting observed bins; device text was used only as nonempty exact support.

Cohort reconstruction found 94,444 ICU stays with an exact successor transfer, 53,001 broad eligible ICU-to-ward transfers, and exactly 49,157 first eligible transfers per hospitalization among 40,014 subjects. All frozen destination mappings and physical headers matched the frozen contract; 16 of the 17 allowed destination values were represented in the cohort.

Coverage uses six left-closed two-hour bins in `[t0-12h,t0)`:

| role | N | raw G eligible | G-pre eligible | G-pre + >=4 E0-4 domains | movable gate among raw-G |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| full pooled cohort | 49,157 | 43,600 (88.70%) | 41,208 (83.83%) | 40,600 (82.59%) | 43,600/43,600 (100%) |
| development | 17,215 | 15,609 (90.67%) | 14,953 (86.86%) | 14,716 (85.48%) | 100% |
| validation | 8,859 | 8,162 (92.13%) | 7,710 (87.03%) | 7,639 (86.23%) | 100% |
| locked 2017-2019 | 6,435 | 5,445 (84.62%) | 5,065 (78.71%) | 5,001 (77.72%) | 100% |
| stress 2020-2022 | 5,285 | 4,322 (81.78%) | 3,968 (75.08%) | 3,900 (73.79%) | 100% |

Thus `G_pre` exceeds the parent's frozen 70% gate in all reconstructible roles. The most adverse late role remains above the gate when oxygen is restricted to numeric flow/FiO2 and device text is ignored: 3,963/5,285 (74.99%). `E0-4` retains the parent's training imputation and missing flags, so the joint >=4-domain endpoint statistic is a conservative diagnostic, not a new exclusion or estimand.

The parent pooled 60/20/20 role assignment is not reconstructible from attached evidence: there is no subject-split artifact, its declared stratification uses qualifying outcomes and dominant destination, and the exact splitter/tie-breaking algorithm is unspecified. Inventing an assignment would violate this outcome-blind audit. Full-cohort pooled support is reported here; future execution must materialize the frozen assignment before opening evaluation outcomes and rerun this same audit by pooled role. Approximate-era roles were exactly reconstructible and match inherited counts, including 17,215/8,859/6,435/5,285 strict subject-isolated rows plus 10,323 boundary-ambiguous and 1,040 withheld earlier-role rows.

## Corrected meaning of the movable-bin gate

The measured positional gate passes for every raw-G-eligible row, but this is logically entailed by the frozen definitions: a raw-G-eligible domain has at least two observed bins in each three-bin half, hence at least four observed bins. Freezing its final observed bin necessarily leaves at least three movable nonfinal bins. Four raw-G domains therefore imply four domains meeting the movable-position rule.

This resolves attrition/computability, not attribution power. A row can have movable positions but identical nonfinal summaries, yielding little effective variation. Without changing eligibility or the hypothesis, the full extraction must report:

1. the fraction of raw-G rows with at least four domains having at least two distinct nonfinal abnormality-margin summaries;
2. per-row and per-era variance of recomputed `G_perm` across the 200 frozen seeds;
3. fraction unchanged under every permutation and under reversal;
4. observed-minus-null interval width for interaction, Brier gain, and quota capture.

These are null-informativeness diagnostics, not post-label selection gates. If permutations are degenerate or observed-minus-null intervals include material benefit and harm, order attribution is inconclusive. L2-D cannot rescue it.

## Prespecified continuation and fallback

Both original support gates pass, so proceed with the frozen experiment.

- Keep all windows, six domains, 70% thresholds, cohort, outcome, and opening order unchanged.
- Materialize and hash the pooled split before opening its outcomes; rerun coverage by pooled train/validation/test. If an evaluation role unexpectedly falls below 70% because its original assignment differs materially, the relevant claim is infeasible; do not resplit.
- Freeze the complete oxygen device ordinal dictionary in development. If exact mapping causes an evaluation-era `G_pre` coverage below 70%, G-pre corroboration is unavailable and supportive evidence must use the already-prespecified no-support-change plus observation-stable route.
- If exact-value permutation variation is inadequate, retain raw D1 and G-perp estimates but call order attribution inconclusive; do not borrow histories across patients, alter bins, or relax domains.
- G-pre null alone remains inconclusive. A supportive claim still requires the parent raw D1, transported D1-perp, positive observed-minus-null interaction/Brier/quota contrasts, endpoint agreement, and either G-pre or quiet/observation-stable corroboration.
- A null reproduced by endpoint-fixed permutations plus materially null G-perp supports the coupling/mean-reversion adverse interpretation. Process-only reproduction with loss in quiet/stable rows supports only a treatment/documentation-associated predictor.

Supportive results establish residual ordered measured-value information and consequential historical re-ranking only. Adverse results can reject the specified attribution. Inconclusive results warrant deferral. None establishes physiology, preventability, clinician intent, or intervention benefit.

## Baseline and learned alternative remain matched

The transparent baseline remains `D1-perp` alongside E0 and raw D1. It estimates the sign and size of unusual recent direction at matched endpoint state and exposes the exact `C×direction` contrast. Ridge versus depth-3 boosted nuisance regression is chosen only by subject-grouped development RMSE and residual-balance gates, never by R+D association.

The scientifically substantive alternative remains `L2-D`, the two-stream causal TCN over the same time grid and static E0 context. It can reveal nonlinear late relapse, cross-domain lag, and opposing-domain patterns that scalar G loses. It is selected only if calibrated and seed-stable, better than D1-perp in both locked late eras, and its value/full gain exceeds both process-only and endpoint-fixed order-null heads. Otherwise prefer the transparent model. A latent-state/domain-adversarial model remains deferred until independent physiologic, policy, transfer-intent, or external-site evidence can identify what it removes.

Measured audit cost was 1,817 seconds on 8 CPUs/64 GiB, no GPU. Future extraction and ridge/event analysis remain estimated at 8-16 CPUs/64-128 GiB for 4-6 hours including 200 null refits and bootstraps; five-seed L2-D remains one allocated A100 plus 8 CPUs/64 GiB for 3-6 hours. These fit the configured solver envelope; only the audit time is measured.

## Exact source contract

Read-only archive: `[private path]`, SHA-256 `0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09`.

Audited members and required columns:

- `icu/icustays` / `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/icustays.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],[internal identifier],first_careunit,last_careunit,intime,outtime,los`; `outtime=t0`;
- `hosp/transfers` / `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/transfers.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],transfer_id,eventtype,careunit,intime,outtime`; exact successor and destination;
- `hosp/admissions` / `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/admissions.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],admittime,dischtime,deathtime,admission_type,...,discharge_location,...,hospital_expire_flag`; alive-at-t0 and frozen endpoints;
- `hosp/patients` / `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/patients.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],gender,anchor_age,anchor_year,anchor_year_group,dod`; age and approximate-era roles;
- `icu/chartevents` / `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/chartevents.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],[internal identifier],caregiver_id,charttime,storetime,itemid,value,valuenum,valueuom,warning`; stay/item join, bins by charttime, strict storetime availability;
- `icu/d_items` / `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/d_items.csv.gz`: `itemid,label,abbreviation,linksto,category,unitname,param_type,lownormalvalue,highnormalvalue`; all selected labels matched;
- retained but not needed for this occupancy audit: `hosp/services`, `icu/inputevents`, and `icu/procedureevents` with the parent's exact joins/time fields for context and treatment transitions.

Frozen audit item IDs: HR 220045; SBP 220050/220179; MAP 220052/220181; RR 220210; SpO2 220277; temperature 223761/223762; oxygen flow 223834; FiO2 223835; device 226732. Retain the parent's GCS, code-status, ventilation, and vasopressor IDs for the full experiment. Notes remain endpoint adjudication only and never enter this audit or predictors.

Computationally checkable claims include headers/hashes, exact joins, cohort reproduction, pre-t0 availability, bins, role assignment, nonoverlap, support counts, invariant checks, fitting, permutations, uncertainty, and conclusion-rule linkage. Clinical meaning of device/treatment changes, physiology, intent, preventability, actionability, harms, and benefit require expert review or another study. External transport requires another institution; intervention benefit requires prospective or quasi-experimental evaluation.

## Exactly three inspected key references

[K1] Heo Y, Kim M, Han SS, et al. *AI-Driven Predictions of Readmission and Mortality for Improved Discharge Decisions in Critical Care: A Retrospective Study.* Diagnostics. 2026;16(6):874. doi:10.3390/diagnostics16060874.

[K2] Ruppert MM, Loftus TJ, Small C, et al. *Predictive Modeling for Readmission to Intensive Care: A Systematic Review.* Crit Care Explor. 2023;5(1):e0848. doi:10.1097/CCE.0000000000000848.

[K3] Agniel D, Kohane IS, Weber GM. *Biases in electronic health record data due to processes within the healthcare system: retrospective observational study.* BMJ. 2018;361:k1479. doi:10.1136/bmj.k1479.

The inherited excerpts and key-reference receipt were rechecked byte-for-byte and their claim mappings remain unchanged: K1 supports relevance while bounding operational/composite interpretation; K2 bounds longitudinal-model generalization; K3 motivates the healthcare-process rival. None establishes the hypothesis, coupling resolution, transport, physiology, or benefit.

# Recompute and interpret the frozen HCC 144-hour recovery diagnostic

## Objective

Reproduce the selected, already executed diagnostic from the four read-only HCC tables. Determine whether the 0–144-hour INR/total-bilirubin trajectory—especially bilirubin lag despite INR improvement—adds clinically meaningful, temporally transported prediction of discharge later than 240 hours beyond a POD5 snapshot.

This is a scoped numerical reproducibility task. You must newly construct the cohort, fit the models and controls, estimate uncertainty, and derive the interpretation from your computed outputs. The previously reported answer is not supplied as a solver artifact. Do not merely write expected aggregate numbers.

The hypothesis under test is prognostic, not causal: trajectory T1 should improve 2024–2025 prediction over snapshot B0 and show an adverse bilirubin-lag contrast. The strongest rival is that current POD5 state, operative burden, measurement practice, and calendar era explain any apparent trajectory signal. The endpoint is delayed recorded discharge. It is not PHLF, morbidity, mortality, survival, or discharge readiness.

## Evidence boundary and clinical relevance

Selected preoperative and operative factors have been associated with postoperative hospital stay after HCC resection [K1]. POD1 bilirubin plus clinical factors predicted adjudicated grade B/C post-hepatectomy liver failure after major hepatectomy [K2]. ISGLS PHLF requires concomitant INR and bilirubin abnormalities relative to local laboratory limits on or after POD5 and is graded by management consequences [K3]. None of these works establishes that the path to POD5 adds information about discharge delay.

At 144 hours, a stable trajectory association could motivate targeted review rather than indiscriminate testing. A precise adverse result would instead support retaining the simpler current-state model class for this recorded-discharge endpoint. Even a supportive result would not identify liver regeneration, cholestasis, PHLF, a complication, a treatment effect, or readiness for discharge.

## Exact private data bindings

All sources are ordinary CSV files (not archive members), mounted read-only. Write derived files only below `/workspace`.

| procedures | `/data/procedures.csv` | `[private path]` | `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `手术`, `开始时间`, `结束时间` |
| encounters | `/data/encounters.csv` | `[private path]` | `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `年龄`, `性别`, `就诊时间`, `入院时间`, `出院时间` |
| diagnoses | `/data/diagnoses.csv` | `[private path]` | `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `诊断名称`, `诊断类型` |
| labs | `/data/labs.csv` | `[private path]` | `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `检验`, `定量结果`, `检验时间` |

Join tables by the exact string pair `患者主索引 + 就诊号`; never coerce identifiers to numbers. Read UTF-8 with BOM handling. The labs file is about 2.2 GB, so stream selected columns in chunks. Do not emit direct identifiers, names, contact details, or exact source timestamps. The binding layer verifies the configured hashes; your analysis must also record the four expected hashes in `results.json` under `source_hashes`, although a second full 2.2 GB hash pass is optional.

## Frozen cohort and clocks

1. In procedures, require `手术` to contain both `肝` and `切除`. Exclude labels containing the regular expression `胆囊切除|肝移植|供肝|肝动脉|胰|胃|结肠|肾|肺`. Require a parseable `开始时间`.

3. Join its encounter. Require age at least 18, parseable admission and discharge, and T0 between admission and discharge inclusive.
4. Require discharge from 144 hours through 90 days after T0, T0 year 2013–2025, and a same-key diagnosis containing `肝细胞癌|原发性肝癌`.

Define:

- concordant recovery: both early-to-late changes < 0;
- bilirubin lag: INR change < 0 and bilirubin change >= 0;
- INR lag: INR change >= 0 and bilirubin change < 0;
- concordant non-recovery: both changes >= 0.

These quadrants are descriptive phenotypes, not diagnoses.

## Frozen models and fitting

Use deterministic seed 260924. Fit all transformations on train only.

**B0 snapshot baseline.** L2 logistic regression, C=1, maximum 3,000 iterations. Restricted cubic-style spline implementation is `SplineTransformer(n_knots=4, degree=3, include_bias=False)` for age, operation duration, late log INR, and late log bilirubin after median imputation with missing indicators; standardize those and all regular numeric terms. Regular terms are calendar year, late INR/bilirubin interaction, and late collection offsets. Include duration-missing, laparoscopic, major, and cirrhosis indicators and one-hot sex.

**B1 transparent trajectory model.** Elastic-net logistic regression using all B0 information plus early/middle log values and collection offsets, both interval changes, total changes, and discordance. Median-impute with indicators and standardize numeric inputs; one-hot sex. Select by uncalibrated 2022 log loss from C ∈ {0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0} × l1_ratio ∈ {0.2, 0.8}; use SAGA, maximum 3,000 iterations.

**T1 learned trajectory model.** Histogram gradient boosting on the same substantive inputs as B1. Median-impute numeric values with indicators and one-hot sex. Fix max depth 3, L2=1, no early stopping. Select by uncalibrated 2022 log loss from learning rate {0.03, 0.07}, minimum leaf {30, 80}, and iterations {150, 300}.

Fit each candidate model on 2013–2021 only. For each frozen fitted model, fit a logistic recalibrator on 2023 only: regress 2023 outcome on the logit of clipped raw probability (clip 1e-5 to 1−1e-5), then apply that intercept/slope to validation and test probabilities. The 2022 tuning subset must not fit recalibration.

Fit these frozen controls:

- temporal shuffle: jointly permute early/middle INR/bilirubin values and offsets within train-year × major × laparoscopic strata, preserve each patient's late state, recompute changes/discordance, and fit T1 with selected hyperparameters;
- timing-only: logistic model on age, duration, year, procedure indicators, sex, and all six INR/bilirubin collection offsets, without lab values;
- no-offset T1: selected T1 without any collection-offset features;
- ALT-history control: selected tree model on B0 plus ALT early/middle/late values, offsets, and changes, with missing-value indicators.

Use the same 2023-only recalibration procedure for every control.

## Estimates and uncertainty

On validation and locked test, report for every primary model and control: N, events, Brier score, log loss, AUROC, AUPRC, calibration intercept/slope, mean prediction, and event rate.

For B1, T1, temporal shuffle, timing-only, and ALT control, estimate paired differences from B0 in Brier and log loss with 2,000 patient bootstrap resamples of locked-test rows. Keep fitted and calibrated models frozen: this bootstrap quantifies test-sample uncertainty and deliberately does not include model-fitting uncertainty. Report percentile 95% intervals and disclose this limitation.

For the quadrant contrast, first restrict test patients to the train 1st–99th percentile range for both late log INR and late log bilirubin. Fit a train-only multinomial logistic model for quadrant using age, duration, year, late logs and interaction, major, laparoscopic, cirrhosis, and late collection offsets. Use generalized overlap weights: for a comparison of quadrant q against concordant recovery, assign the estimated probability of the other group. Report group N, effective N, weighted observed outcome difference, and the T1 predicted-risk difference with 2,000 patient bootstrap percentile intervals. This is adjusted descriptive separation, not a causal contrast.

Report B0 and T1 Brier scores and their difference within major/minor, cirrhosis/no-cirrhosis, laparoscopic/open, 2024, and 2025 strata. Small strata must be labeled unstable.

## Prespecified interpretation

Support the trajectory hypothesis only if all five gates pass on locked test:

1. B0 minus T1 Brier gain is at least 0.005 and the paired CI for T1−B0 is wholly below zero;
2. T1 calibration slope is 0.8–1.2 and absolute intercept <= 0.05;
3. bilirubin-lag versus concordant-recovery T1 risk difference is at least +0.03 and its CI is wholly above zero;
4. temporal shuffling removes at least half the favorable T1 Brier gain; and
5. T1−B0 direction is consistent in major/minor and cirrhosis/no-cirrhosis strata, allowing imprecision.

A result is **adverse to this exact prognostic phenotype** when adequate events and overlap permit a precise decision and the primary proper-score gain is below 0.005 or compatible with no gain, or when the bilirubin-lag interval excludes the prespecified clinically relevant +0.03 contrast. This adverse label takes precedence over inconclusive calibration when the primary proper-score comparison and lag contrast are already decisively adverse. A favorable AUROC alone cannot rescue failed proper-score/calibration gates. If T1 has no favorable gain, “fraction removed by shuffle” is undefined and cannot count as support.

Use **inconclusive** for failed computation, fewer than 200 test events, gross bilirubin scale discontinuity, inadequate overlap/effective N, or intervals broad enough to span clinically opposite bilirubin-lag effects. Calibration failure makes an otherwise favorable result inconclusive; it does not erase a separately precise adverse primary comparison. Never label the result supportive simply because one secondary metric improves, and never call a precise adverse result inconclusive merely because the favored hypothesis failed.

Whichever result you compute, distinguish:

- computationally checkable claims: cohort/split counts, leakage controls, model inputs, metrics, intervals, controls, subgroup directions, and whether gates pass;
- claims outside this experiment: biological recovery mechanism, PHLF, complication type, treatment benefit, mortality, discharge readiness, or external validity.

The latter require a laboratory unit/reference-limit dictionary, reliable operative extent, timestamped interventions and complications, death/disposition, clinical adjudication, and another external/prospective study. The local data do not supply these.

# Executed HCC 144-hour recovery diagnostic

Status: executed on the unchanged parent cohort and locked temporal split. Results are adverse to the prespecified trajectory hypothesis.

## Frozen question and evidence boundary

The evidence inspected before this analysis supports three limited facts: selected preoperative and operative factors have been associated with postoperative length of stay in HCC [K1]; POD1 bilirubin plus clinical factors predicted adjudicated grade B/C PHLF in a major-hepatectomy cohort [K2]; and ISGLS PHLF requires concomitant INR and bilirubin abnormalities on/after POD5 plus management-based grading [K3]. None establishes that the path to POD5 adds information about discharge delay.

The tested claim was that 0–144-hour INR/bilirubin trajectory—especially bilirubin lag despite INR improvement—would improve 2024–2025 prediction of discharge after 240 hours beyond a POD5 snapshot. The strongest rival was that current POD5 state, operative burden, measurement practice, and era explain the apparent signal. The endpoint remains delayed recorded discharge, not PHLF, morbidity, mortality, or discharge readiness.

## Data and execution

The parent’s population, T0, 48-hour windows, complete-case requirement, outcome, broad data-quality bounds, and thresholds were unchanged. Exact read-only bindings were:

- procedures: [private path]; 患者主索引, 就诊号, 手术, 开始时间, 结束时间.
- encounters: [private path]; 患者主索引, 就诊号, 年龄, 性别, 入院时间, 出院时间.
- diagnoses: [private path]; 患者主索引, 就诊号, 诊断名称.
- labs: [private path]; 患者主索引, 就诊号, 检验, 定量结果, 检验时间.

Joins used exact string 患者主索引 + 就诊号; first qualifying resection per patient defined T0. The reconstructed complete cohort exactly matched the frozen audit: train 2013–2021 N=6,975/events=1,851; validation 2022–2023 N=2,562/events=428; locked test 2024–2025 N=2,700/events=387. Patients were unique. Validation was divided before fitting: 2022 (N=1,025/events=212) tuned B1/T1; 2023 (N=1,537/events=216) fit logistic recalibration only. Test was evaluated after all choices and controls were frozen.

B0 was spline-penalized logistic regression on age, sex, operation duration/missingness, laparoscopic and coarse major-resection flags, cirrhosis, year, late measurement offsets, late log INR/bilirubin, and their interaction. B1 was elastic-net logistic regression on matched trajectory features; validation chose C=0.03 and l1_ratio=0.2. T1 was depth-3 histogram gradient boosting; validation chose learning rate 0.03, 150 iterations, minimum leaf 80, and L2=1. Controls were a timing-only model, T1 without offsets, within-train-year × major × laparoscopic early/middle temporal shuffle preserving late state, and B0 plus ALT history.

## Executed results

On locked test, B0 Brier was 0.11763 (log loss 0.39191; AUROC 0.650). T1 was worse: Brier 0.11857, paired difference T1−B0 +0.00094 (2,000-patient bootstrap 95% CI −0.00046 to +0.00231), log-loss difference +0.00393 (−0.00096 to +0.00861), and AUROC 0.645. T1 calibration slope was 1.342 and intercept 0.453, outside the prespecified 0.8–1.2 and ±0.05 bounds.

Transparent B1 was only trivially better in Brier: 0.11741, difference −0.00022 (95% CI −0.00180 to +0.00133), below the 0.005 threshold and compatible with no improvement. Its AUROC was 0.668, which is hypothesis-generating rank separation but does not rescue the failed proper-score/calibration criteria.

The train-weighted, late-state/severity-overlap bilirubin-lag contrast was +0.30 percentage points versus concordant recovery (95% CI −0.41 to +1.01; effective N 313 vs 710), far below the required +3 points. The weighted observed outcome difference was −0.19 points. These results are adverse to the proposed bilirubin-lag phenotype for this endpoint.

Controls did not reveal a hidden favorable interpretation:

- Temporal shuffle was worse than B0 by +0.00312 Brier (95% CI +0.00180 to +0.00446), showing that early/middle linkage contains some rank information, but T1 itself still did not beat B0; the required “half the gain removed” criterion is undefined because there was no positive T1 gain.
- Timing-only was worse than B0 by +0.00359 (95% CI +0.00149 to +0.00561), so timing alone did not explain a favorable trajectory gain.
- ALT history was worse than B0 by +0.00057 (95% CI −0.00128 to +0.00239), providing no evidence that nonspecific injury history adds a robust gain.
- T1 without measurement offsets remained worse than B0 (+0.00055 Brier), so offsets were not masking a useful trajectory result.
- T1−B0 directions were inconsistent across major/minor and cirrhosis strata; the coarse major flag had only 58 test patients and is not stable enough for a strong modern-era subgroup claim.

Annual outcome rates fell from 26.2% in 2021 to 20.7% in 2022, 14.1% in 2023, 15.9% in 2024, and 12.4% in 2025. Median late bilirubin remained about 19 across 2022–2025, while median late collection shifted from ~129 hours in 2024 to ~119 hours in 2025. Complete-trajectory coverage also rose from 31.0% in 2013 to 76.4% in 2025. This supports material discharge/measurement-era drift, not a gross bilirubin scale discontinuity.

## Interpretation and decision

The strongest computed claim is adverse: in this unchanged cohort, the prespecified learned INR/bilirubin trajectory did not improve locked-test proper scores or calibration over the POD5 snapshot, and bilirubin lag did not show the required adverse risk contrast. Current late state plus ordinary covariates should remain the preferred parsimonious model class for this recorded-discharge endpoint. The small B1 AUROC increase does not justify clinical use or a mechanistic label.

This result does not establish that biological recovery path never matters. It tests one routinely observed, complete-case, three-window representation against recorded discharge in one institution. The bootstrap resampled locked-test patients with frozen fitted/calibrated models; it did not refit the complete training/calibration pipeline, so its intervals omit model-fitting uncertainty. The first-versus-last value sensitivity was not fitted; all 12,237 primary complete cases had first values, making it feasible but unnecessary to overturn the decisive primary failure. Selection weighting and 336-hour outcome were not executed in this bounded diagnostic. These omissions narrow precision and generalizability but do not turn the failed prespecified primary gates into support.

The branch should be parked for this endpoint. Revisit only with adjudicated PHLF/complications, laboratory units/reference limits, reliable operative extent, timestamped interventions and disposition/death, preferably external validation. Those data could test liver-specific recovery rather than institutional discharge practice.

## Supportive, adverse, and inconclusive meanings

Supportive would have required all five frozen gates: Brier gain ≥0.005 with CI below zero, acceptable calibration, bilirubin-lag risk difference ≥3 points with CI above zero, ≥50% gain loss under shuffle, and consistent subgroup direction. None passed.

The executed result is adverse to this exact prognostic phenotype and model comparison. It is not proof of equivalence, absence of liver injury, or absence of PHLF. A future adjudicated study could reach a different conclusion.

An inconclusive label would have applied for inadequate events, gross scale drift, poor overlap, or intervals spanning clinically opposite bilirubin-lag effects. Events and weighted overlap were adequate, no gross bilirubin shift appeared, and the lag CI excluded the prespecified clinically relevant +3-point threshold; therefore “adverse” is more accurate than “inconclusive.”

## Exactly three inspected works

[K1] Li F, Ren Y, Fan J, Zhou J. *The predictive value of the preoperative albumin-to-fibrinogen ratio for postoperative hospital length of stay in liver cancer patients.* Cancer Med. 2023;12:20321–20331. doi:10.1002/cam4.6606. Full-text abstract/method passages inspected.

[K2] Baumgartner R, Engstrand J, Rajala P, et al. *Comparing the accuracy of prediction models to detect clinically relevant post-hepatectomy liver failure early after major hepatectomy.* Br J Surg. 2024;111:znad433. doi:10.1093/bjs/znad433. Full-text abstract/introduction/method/result passages inspected.

[K3] Rahbari NN, Garden OJ, Padbury R, et al. *Posthepatectomy liver failure: a definition and grading by the International Study Group of Liver Surgery (ISGLS).* Surgery. 2011;149:713–724. doi:10.1016/j.surg.2010.10.001. Abstract only inspected; full text unavailable through the frozen route.

Preserve P−: 85<=G<=95 and −18<=delta<=−12; P0: 85<=G<=95 and −3<=delta<=3. Require >=100/window in every sex×five-year-age stratum, both targets inside each observed-stratum convex hull, and the inherited local raw-assay nearest-neighbour gate, repeated after diagnosis and calendar-eligibility restrictions.

Preserve 1:1 matching without replacement, exact sex/five-year-age/assessment-year, |G difference|<=1.5, and 0.2 pooled-SD propensity-logit caliper using inherited baseline covariates, centre, continuous age, G and scalar baseline history. Reject if either group loses >50%, <1,000 pairs remain, or any prespecified covariate/G/history |SMD|>0.10. Matching is repeated in participant bootstraps.

Through S+10 calendar years classify N17-first, N18-first, same-day N17/N18 tie, death-first, death/renal tie, or event-free/censored. Preserve tie assignment/exclusion sensitivities. Participant eligibility requires S+10 years<=verified administrative end C. Observed maxima cannot establish C; absent export-linked participant-applicable provenance, clinical inference is inconclusive.

All adjustment/history features are strictly pre-index. Preserve the parent's scalar [index−5 years,index) history: log1p distinct nonrenal groups; counts in [−5,−2) and [−2,0); represented chapters; recency/none; principal-confirmation proportion/none; assessment year; and U only as a global-code QA bound.
