Preserve matched Aalen–Johansen corroboration and principal-position directional sensitivity. No post-index code state enters renal adjustment.

## Transparent broad baseline

Define V without markers/profile labels as all valid non-N17/N18 three-character groups present in paired 41270/41280. A post-S discovery is the first paired date of a group not seen by S. Multiple groups on a date count separately toward K but share a threshold-crossing date.

In the final eligible cohort's training split, blinded to markers/profiles, choose K from {1,3,5,10,15,20,30} minimizing absolute difference between pooled 10-year B_K CIF and pooled mean N17/N18 CIF; ties choose smaller K. The audit predicts K=30 but does not override this final protocol. Freeze K with no bootstrap/validation/test or post-association reselection.

B_K is first passage to the K-th new nonrenal group. Death before K competes; verified administrative end censors. Report global U as QA only. Commensurability requires >=95% in each profile window to have U>=K, >=200 B_K events/window, and held-out pooled B_K CIF between one-half and twice pooled mean renal CIF. No passing K is inconclusive.

Retain the parent's frozen respiratory, injury, ear/mastoid and skin families as context only over the full population. Family-free-at-S subsets remain sensitivity-only and cannot support/refute QK.

## Learned recording-process alternative

The baseline loses code composition, events after K, and whether threshold crossing reflects more recording dates or larger same-day bundles. Fit one alternative at matched specificity.

First learn outcome-blind baseline phenotypes from [index−5 years,index): sparse participant × (three-character group × recency bin [5,2), [2,0.5), [0.5,0) years × all-position/principal-confirmed channel) NMF. Training frequency threshold is 50. Fit ranks 8/16/32 and seeds 20260924–20260926 in training only; choose by validation Poisson deviance plus matched-component cosine stability >=0.80. Freeze loadings and top codes before naming components.

Then derive, while alive, two observable annual processes from paired 41270/41280:

1. discovery-day count: distinct dates with >=1 previously unseen nonrenal group;
2. bundle size: number of newly appearing groups on each discovery date.

Fit recurrent discovery-day intensity with a yearly piecewise-exponential or complementary-log-log baseline and a shared participant frailty with absorbing death. Conditional on a discovery day, fit zero-truncated negative-binomial bundle size. Both use baseline clinical covariates, scalar history, NMF scores and G/delta surface only. U is not a trial denominator. Post-S outcomes never enter renal models.

Jointly simulate standardized 10-year trajectories under P− and P0, preserving baseline histories. Report expected discovery days, conditional bundle size, total new groups, probability of K passage and death CIF. Compare scalar-only, scalar+NMF and scalar+NMF+frailty/process models.

Use the same frozen participant split. Fit on training, select rank/process complexity on validation, and report once on untouched test. Define V without markers/profile labels as all valid non-N17/N18 three-character groups present in paired 41270/41280. A post-S discovery is the first paired date of a group not seen by S. Multiple groups on a date count separately toward K but share a threshold-crossing date.

Freeze a 70/15/15 participant split before profile associations, seed 20260924, stratified only by sex and aggregate renal transition class. In the final eligible cohort's training split, blinded to markers/profiles, choose K from {1,3,5,10,15,20,30} minimizing absolute difference between pooled 10-year B_K CIF and pooled mean N17/N18 CIF; ties choose smaller K. The audit predicts K=30 but does not override this final protocol. Freeze K with no bootstrap/validation/test or post-association reselection.

B_K is first passage to the K-th new nonrenal group. Death before K competes; verified administrative end censors. Report global U as QA only. Commensurability requires >=95% in each profile window to have U>=K, >=200 B_K events/window, and held-out pooled B_K CIF between one-half and twice pooled mean renal CIF. No passing K is inconclusive.

Fit B_K with the identical Cox/CIF specification, population, S, horizon, death/tie handling, scalar history, profile standardization, bootstrap and matched pairs. Report thetaK and QK=theta17−thetaK with joint covariance. This aligns first-passage incidence and analysis; it does not make N17 and B_K biologically exchangeable.

Retain the parent's frozen respiratory, injury, ear/mastoid and skin families as context only over the full population. Family-free-at-S subsets remain sensitivity-only and cannot support/refute QK.

## Learned recording-process alternative

The baseline loses code composition, events after K, and whether threshold crossing reflects more recording dates or larger same-day bundles. Fit one alternative at matched specificity.

First learn outcome-blind baseline phenotypes from [index−5 years,index): sparse participant × (three-character group × recency bin [5,2), [2,0.5), [0.5,0) years × all-position/principal-confirmed channel) NMF. Training frequency threshold is 50. Fit ranks 8/16/32 and seeds 20260924–20260926 in training only; choose by validation Poisson deviance plus matched-component cosine stability >=0.80. Freeze loadings and top codes before naming components.

Then derive, while alive, two observable annual processes from paired 41270/41280:

1. discovery-day count: distinct dates with >=1 previously unseen nonrenal group;
2. bundle size: number of newly appearing groups on each discovery date.

Fit recurrent discovery-day intensity with a yearly piecewise-exponential or complementary-log-log baseline and a shared participant frailty with absorbing death. Conditional on a discovery day, fit zero-truncated negative-binomial bundle size. Both use baseline clinical covariates, scalar history, NMF scores and G/delta surface only. U is not a trial denominator. Post-S outcomes never enter renal models.

Jointly simulate standardized 10-year trajectories under P− and P0, preserving baseline histories. Report expected discovery days, conditional bundle size, total new groups, probability of K passage and death CIF. Compare scalar-only, scalar+NMF and scalar+NMF+frailty/process models.

Use the same frozen participant split. Fit on training, select rank/process complexity on validation, and report once on untouched test. Evaluate yearly day/count calibration, zero-count calibration, bundle quantiles/tails, death calibration slope/intercept, joint deviance, B_K Brier/calibration and seed stability. Carry process fitting/simulation and shared theta17/thetaK/QK through >=500 participant bootstraps. Retain the alternative only with acceptable held-out calibration, B_K Brier no worse than transparent baseline, and seed-stable profile contrasts.

This separates dates of new recording from same-day coding density, information the K-th endpoint loses. Without encounter IDs it cannot identify utilization, admission intensity, onset or mechanism. A transformer remains deferred because only first dates are available; revisit only if this model fails and a preregistered sequence model materially improves held-out process targets. A latent true-GFR model remains deferred without measured GFR/error data.

Approximate solver budget: vectorized parsing/checkpointing 0.5–1 hour (audit measured 410 seconds on 8 CPUs); Cox/matching/bootstrap 2–4 hours; NMF and joint process/bootstrap 2–4 hours; <=16 CPUs, <=262,144 MiB, <=8 hours. CPU-first is adequate. One allocated A100 is optional only after profiling; GPU use is neither necessary nor scientific merit.

## Falsification and interpretation

All interpretations require verified units/code semantics/C, support/matching/K/event gates, convergence, held-out process calibration, joint uncertainty, and no material tie/principal reversal.

Supportive for bounded recorded-N17 selectivity requires theta17 lower 95% bound >0, D lower bound >0, matched/principal directional agreement, QK lower bound >0, and agreement of calibrated recording-process simulation with the transparent B_K contrast. The pattern is strengthened if neither discovery-day nor bundle-size contrasts explain the N17 advantage. It warrants an external encounter/laboratory-adjudicated study only.

Adverse to selectivity/generalized-recording rival supported if thetaK lower bound >0 and QK upper bound <=0 in baseline and calibrated process analyses; or a stable NMF phenotype predicts N17, discovery days, bundle size, B_K and multiple families similarly with no precise N17 advantage. A bundle-only contrast is compatible with coding/admission intensity, not generalized incident disease. D upper bound<=0 is adverse to acute-versus-chronic selectivity; similar precise theta17/theta18 supports shared renal information. Both renal theta upper bounds<=0 are adverse to both profile claims.

Inconclusive includes unverified export completeness; no final-cohort K; profile support/matching/event failure; QK spanning clinically material alternatives; inadequate NMF stability/process calibration; <90% bootstrap convergence; death/CIF/cause-specific discordance; principal/tie reversal; or method disagreement without an identifiable calibrated recording pathway. An imprecise null does not refute the hypothesis. Do not rescue results by changing K, families, profiles, population, horizon, ranks or exclusions.

Biological AKI/CKD and coding sensitivity require record-level admissions, serial creatinine/cystatin C/albuminuria and clinical adjudication. Complete opportunity requires provider/nation/contact and export provenance. True filtration requires measured GFR/error data. Transportability and clinical benefit require external validation and prospective decision-impact/intervention study.

## Scientific deliverable and verifier boundary

A future solver must newly construct the final cohort/support; verify pairing/release; freeze V and K; construct pre-index scalar/NMF history; fit renal/B_K/family models; fit the discovery-day/bundle/death process; run matched/principal/tie analyses and joint bootstrap; and emit a rule-linked conclusion.

Required outputs: `run-manifest.json`, `censoring-provenance.json`, `field-audit.json`, `cohort-flow.csv`, `profile-support.json`, `matched-balance.csv`, `events-by-definition.json`, `code-universe.csv`, `k-selection.json`, `commensurability-audit.json`, `cox-results.json`, `broad-threshold-results.json`, `family-results.json`, `nmf-history-results.json`, `recording-process-results.json`, `transition-contrasts.json`, `conclusion.json`, and `report.md`.

The verifier can check source hashes/headers, joins/pairing, timestamps, V/K/split isolation, no post-index renal covariates, common population/clock/death handling, QA opportunity, calibration/convergence, bootstrap intervals and conclusion-rule consistency. It must accept correct supportive, adverse and inconclusive conclusions and reject unsupported favorable claims. It cannot establish export completeness, validate AKI/CKD, infer utilization/testing, adjudicate mechanism or prove clinical benefit.

## Exactly three inspected works

[K1] Chen DC et al. *Cystatin C- and Creatinine-based Estimated GFR Differences: Prevalence and Predictors in the UK Biobank.* Kidney Medicine. 2024;6:100796. doi:10.1016/j.xkme.2024.100796. Relevant full-text XML excerpt inspected.

[K2] Potok OA et al. *The Difference Between Cystatin C- and Creatinine-Based Estimated GFR and Associations With Frailty and Adverse Outcomes: A Cohort Analysis of SPRINT.* American Journal of Kidney Diseases. 2020;76:765–774. doi:10.1053/j.ajkd.2020.05.017. Relevant PMC full-text excerpt inspected.

[K3] Zhang J et al. *Validation of Administrative Coding and Clinical Notes for Hospital-Acquired Acute Kidney Injury in Adults.* AMIA Annual Symposium Proceedings. 2021:1234–1243. PMID:35308921; PMCID:PMC8861756. Relevant full-text sections inspected; US single-system performance is not transported to UKB.

{"result": {"text": "# Outcome-blind eICU excess-FiO2 identifiability audit

## Objective

Run a fresh, outcome-blind measurement study to determine whether the fixed all-hour eICU excess-FiO2 exposure can be identified precisely enough to justify a later mortality analysis. This is a prerequisite audit, not a mortality study. Do not read or model hospital death, live discharge, or post-hour-36 outcome fields.

External evidence supports only that oxygen exposure is modifiable [K1], hyperoxia–mechanical-stress interaction is biologically plausible but clinically uncertain [K2], and pulmonary/ARDS recognition is incomplete [K3]. None validates eICU FiO2 charting, the eICU pulmonary proxy, delivered-airway FiO2, or a mortality interaction.

The unresolved biological hypothesis, which this task does not test, is: among adult first ICU stays alive and in ICU at hour 36, with PaO2 80–120 mm Hg paired to FiO2 during hours 18–24, the pre-hour-24 acute-pulmonary-injury proxy modifies the association between mean all-hour excess FiO2 during hours 24–36 and seven-day post-hour-36 in-hospital death by 3 absolute risk points per +0.10 excess FiO2.

The tested measurement hypothesis is: before outcomes are used, respiratory-chart/lab FiO2 plus bounded carry-forward identify each stratum's 12-hour mean excess-FiO2 burden with median interval width <=0.10 and 75th-percentile width <=0.15. An ordered latent model, evaluated by hospital-held-out contiguous-block masking, must be calibrated and meet the same gate in both strata; it cannot override failure of the transparent envelope.

## Frozen population and time line

Use patientunitstayid as the ICU-stay index. All clinical tables join on that key; hospital would join by hospitalid; never join measurements by uniquepid.

1. Parse age, treating "> 89" as 90, and select age >=18.
2. Select the first ICU stay per patienthealthsystemstayid by the lowest valid unitvisitnumber, with patientunitstayid only as a deterministic tie-breaker. Exclude impossible chronology.
3. Require unitdischargeoffset >2160 minutes.
4. Exclude burns and ECMO documented at or before minute 1440 and exact "comfort measures only" before or at minute 1440. Publish exact case-insensitive term rules. Never select on oxygen-record completeness.
5. Find the last valid labname="paO2" value of 80–120 mm Hg in [1080,1440]. Pair to the nearest valid respiratory-chart or lab FiO2 within +/-60 minutes; ties prefer a preceding value, then the earlier event. Normalize [0.21,1.00] directly and [21,100] by division by 100.
6. Freeze phenotype at minute 1440. "injury" requires an ARDS/acute respiratory distress, pneumonia, aspiration, pulmonary oedema/edema, or acute respiratory failure diagnosis/admission term by 1440 plus anchor P/F <=300. "no_term" has none. Term with P/F >300 is discordant validation, excluded from the primary analysis.
7. Represent every primary stay in all 12 one-hour bins [1440,2160). No same-hour oxygenation may select an hour or stay. The eventual, untested outcome origin is minute 2160.

Reconcile the complete flow. Differences from prior descriptive checkpoints (90,296 adult first stays through hour 36; 85,428 after exclusions; 3,235 paired anchors; 1,348 injury; 1,693 no-term; 194 discordant) must be explained from row-level rules, not forced to match.

## Exact read-only inputs

Snapshot: 896e1fb70d4e2d1a59c9fd87c64735dcfaff476fe89543643c08b7df637a15ec. Inputs are ordinary gzip CSVs, not archive members.

- /data/eicu/patient.csv.gz, table patient: patientunitstayid, patienthealthsystemstayid, unitvisitnumber, hospitalid, age, unitdischargeoffset. Outcome/status columns are forbidden.
- /data/eicu/lab.csv.gz, table lab: patientunitstayid, labresultoffset, labresultrevisedoffset, labname, labresult, labresulttext, labmeasurenamesystem, labmeasurenameinterface.
- /data/eicu/respiratoryCharting.csv.gz, table respiratoryCharting: patientunitstayid, respchartoffset, respchartentryoffset, respcharttypecat, respchartvaluelabel, respchartvalue.
- /data/eicu/respiratoryCare.csv.gz, table respiratoryCare: patientunitstayid, respcarestatusoffset, ventstartoffset, ventendoffset, airwaytype, setapneafio2. setapneafio2 is excluded as exposure and retained only as a negative/source-failure control.
- /data/eicu/diagnosis.csv.gz, table diagnosis: patientunitstayid, diagnosisoffset, diagnosisstring, icd9code, diagnosispriority, activeupondischarge.
- /data/eicu/admissionDx.csv.gz, table admissionDx: patientunitstayid, admitdxenteredoffset, admitdxpath, admitdxname, admitdxtext.
- /data/eicu/carePlanGeneral.csv.gz, table carePlanGeneral: patientunitstayid, cplitemoffset, cplgroup, cplitemvalue.
- /data/eicu/treatment.csv.gz, table treatment: patientunitstayid, treatmentoffset, treatmentstring.

All four configured datasets remain mounted read-only under /data/hcc, /data/mimic, /data/eicu and /data/ukb, but cannot change this frozen design.

## Transparent baseline M0

For each bin, use median valid respiratory-chart FiO2 observed in-bin. If absent, carry the most recent prior respiratory-chart value only when the bin start is <=120 minutes after its event; never carry backward from the future. If unsupported, same-bin lab FiO2 may supply a validation-source point. Unsupported hours retain logical excess interval [0,0.60].

Hourly excess is max(F_it-0.40,0); B_i=(1/12) sum_t max(F_it-0.40,0).

Estimate respiratory-chart/lab disagreement from nearest pairs within 30 minutes, by hospital and phenotype. Propagate a declared empirical source-error interval and run sensitivity analyses. Agreement is not accuracy against delivered FiO2. Report entry delay and carry age. Never use missing=room-air, unlimited carry-forward, complete-case restriction, or apnea FiO2.

Use hospital-level bootstrap uncertainty for stratum medians, p75 values, disagreement and coverage; preserve the all-hour population.

## Ordered alternative

Fit an ordered latent FiO2 model on the same stays, hours, admissible sources and clocks. A finite-state HMM on 0.21–1.00 by 0.01, with empirical persistence and source-specific emissions, is acceptable; another explicit ordered model is allowed if documented.

Evaluate with hospital-held-out contiguous-block masking of observed respiratory-chart sequences. Compare against bounded last-observation/lab prediction on identical targets. Report MAE, interval coverage and uncertainty, interval width, performance by stratum and held-out hospital, and full-cohort latent burden widths. Masking validates chart reconstruction, not delivered FiO2. The alternative adds temporal persistence but cannot override failed M0 or justify never-charted states.

## Required deliverables

Create /workspace/analysis.py and these files under /workspace/results:

- summary.json: schema "eicu-fio2-identifiability-v1", seed, snapshot, outcomes_read=false, flow, source agreement, bootstrap uncertainty, transparent/latent stratum metrics, masking metrics, and structured conclusion.
- cohort_flow.csv: stage,n,rule.
- hourly_panel.csv.gz: patientunitstayid,hour,stratum,hospitalid,kind,source,source_offset,entry_delay_minutes,point,L,U.
- burden_intervals.csv.gz: patientunitstayid,stratum,hospitalid,transparent_L,transparent_U,transparent_width,latent_L,latent_U,latent_width.
- source_pairs.csv.gz: IDs, hospital, stratum, source, both offsets/values, absolute difference.
- masked_validation.csv.gz: masked block/stay/hospital/stratum, truth, baseline and latent predictions, latent lower/upper, fold.
- hospital_coverage.csv: hospital/stratum coverage and agreement.
- methods.json: exact terms, normalization, tie rules, intervals, model, split, bootstrap, software.
- report.md: concise report tied to computed files.

summary.json.conclusion must contain measurement_result in {supportive,adverse,inconclusive}; mortality_hypothesis_status exactly "not_tested"; mortality_analysis_performed=false; causal_recommendation=false; clinician_phenotype_gate_evaluable=false; reason_codes; evidence_files.

Supportive requires M0 median <=0.10 and p75 <=0.15 in both strata, agreement spanning >=20 hospitals, and a calibrated ordered alternative passing both strata while consistent with M0. It permits blinded phenotype review, not mortality claims. Adverse applies when transparent identification clearly fails; it defers mortality and does not refute oxygen toxicity. Inconclusive applies to threshold-adjacent estimates, inadequate hospitals, failed masking calibration, unstable bootstraps, or implementation uncertainty. Evaluation rewards gate-concordant interpretation, never confirmation.

## Clinical limits and compute

Two ICU clinicians plus adjudication are required to assess acute parenchymal injury, hydrostatic-only disease, support class and timing, blinded to hospital, proxy, exposure, post-hour-24 data and outcome. Computation cannot recover bilateral imaging, exclude hydrostatic oedema uniformly, verify delivered-airway FiO2, infer intent, establish oxidative injury, identify mortality interaction, or support oxygen targets. Those require device/chart validation, expert review, outcome follow-up and prospective evidence.

Prior bounded feasibility used 8 CPUs/64 GiB/188 seconds. Budget full bootstrap fitting for up to 16 CPUs, 128 GiB and 2–4 hours. No GPU is needed. Prior program and final results are not supplied.

## Key references

[K1] ICU-ROX Investigators and ANZICS Clinical Trials Group; Mackle D, Bellomo R, Bailey M, et al. "Conservative Oxygen Therapy during Mechanical Ventilation in the ICU." NEJM 2020;382:989–998. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1903297. Abstract only. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31613432/

[K2] Nadeau EE, Schwingshackl A, Sturgill JL, Waters CM. "Bench evidence, bedside uncertainty: hyperoxia, mechanical ventilation and lung injury." Eur Respir Rev 2026;35:260058. doi:10.1183/16000617.0058-2026. Version-of-record XML passages. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC13320619/fullTextXML

[K3] Bellani G, Laffey JG, Pham T, et al. "Epidemiology, Patterns of Care, and Mortality for Patients With Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome in Intensive Care Units in 50 Countries." JAMA 2016;315:788–800. doi:10.1001/jama.2016.0291. Abstract/metadata; supplement not inspected. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26903337/

- summary.transparent.injury and summary.transparent.no_term: n, median_width, p75_width, median_bootstrap_ci=[low,high], p75_bootstrap_ci=[low,high], gate_pass.

The last field is true only if every reported latent stay-level interval is nested within its transparent M0 interval (within numeric tolerance).

# Outcome-blind identifiability audit of the all-hour eICU excess-FiO2 crossover

## Status and scientific decision

This is a substantive child of `candidate-a64f6f96bc123cf5e54528a1`. It preserves the parent's target population, hour-24 phenotype landmark, hour-24–36 all-hour exposure, hour-36 outcome origin, seven-day competing-risk estimand, and 3 percentage-point interaction target. It reports a completed outcome-blind measurement experiment, not a mortality result.

The audit gives an adverse answer to the assigned feasibility question: under a transparent source-error plus logical-missingness model, the 12-hour excess-FiO2 burden is not identified precisely enough to resolve the prespecified interaction in the full fixed population. Therefore the mortality branch is deferred. Failure itself is the scientific result: eICU's chart streams can characterize oxygen-record observability and disagreement, but cannot presently support a pulmonary-specific mortality interpretation without unverifiable tightening assumptions and clinician adjudication.

## Evidence-supported claim, unresolved claim, and clinical importance

ICU-ROX established that an oxygen-target strategy can alter exposure without significantly changing ventilator-free days in a broad ventilated population [K1]. A mechanistic review supports biological plausibility for hyperoxia–mechanical-stress synergy while emphasizing inconsistent clinical mortality evidence [K2]. LUNG SAFE showed incomplete and severity-dependent clinician recognition of ARDS [K3]. Thus, the strongest external-evidence claim remains: oxygen exposure is modifiable; biological interaction with mechanical stress is plausible; and pulmonary labels are imperfect. None of the three works validates eICU FiO2, the eICU pulmonary proxy, or a mortality interaction.

The unresolved biological hypothesis remains the parent's:

**Among adult first ICU stays alive and in ICU at hour 36, with PaO2 80–120 mm Hg paired to FiO2 during hours 18–24, the pre-hour-24 acute-pulmonary-injury proxy modifies the association between mean all-hour excess FiO2 during hours 24–36 and seven-day post-hour-36 in-hospital death by a clinically consequential 3 absolute risk points per +0.10 excess FiO2.**

This child first tests the necessary measurement hypothesis:

**Before outcomes are used, respiratory-chart/lab FiO2 and bounded carry-forward identify each stratum's 12-hour mean excess-FiO2 burden with median width <=0.10 and 75th-percentile width <=0.15; an ordered latent model calibrated by masked-chart prediction must meet the same gate in both strata and cannot override failure of the transparent envelope.**

Answering this gate prevents a clinically seductive but unresolvable mortality association from consuming the evidence. Passing would justify phenotype adjudication and the mortality experiment. Failure redirects work to device/chart validation rather than oxygen-treatment inference.

## Fixed population, clocks, variables, and eventual outcome

The fixed design is unchanged. Index `patient.patientunitstayid`. Select age >=18, then the first ICU stay per `patienthealthsystemstayid` by valid lowest `unitvisitnumber`, then require `unitdischargeoffset>2160`. Exclude impossible chronology, burns, ECMO before minute 1440, and exact comfort-measures-only before minute 1440. The diagnostic implemented age, first-stay ordering, hour-36 presence, burn/ECMO/comfort exclusions; it found 90,296 adult first stays through hour 36 and 85,428 after these exclusions.

Anchor: last valid `lab.labname='paO2'` of 80–120 at minutes 1080–1440, paired to nearest valid FiO2 within +/-60 minutes, ties preceding then earlier. Respiratory-chart and lab FiO2 are admissible. `respiratoryCare.setapneafio2` is not: its field meaning is apnea FiO2 and its paired median absolute disagreement with respiratory charting was 0.50; it remains a negative/source-failure control.

Phenotype is frozen at minute 1440. P0 injury requires a diagnosis/admission term for ARDS/acute respiratory distress, pneumonia, aspiration, pulmonary oedema, or acute respiratory failure plus anchor P/F <=300. Primary comparator has no term. Term with P/F>300 is discordant validation, not primary analysis. The corrected audit found 3,235 anchored stays: 1,348 injury, 1,693 no-term, and 194 discordant.

Exposure is all 12 bins in [1440,2160). The target burden is
`B_i=(1/12) sum_t max(F_it-0.40,0)`.
No same-hour oxygenation selects an hour or stay. If the measurement gate eventually passes, outcome origin is minute 2160 and outcome is seven-day in-hospital death through minute 12,240 with live discharge competing and administrative censoring at day seven. No outcome or discharge status was read by this diagnostic.

## Exact data bindings

Read-only eICU snapshot: `896e1fb70d4e2d1a59c9fd87c64735dcfaff476fe89543643c08b7df637a15ec`. Files are ordinary gzip CSVs, no archive members, under `[private path]`. All clinical tables join on `patientunitstayid`; `hospital` joins on `hospitalid`; never join measurements on `uniquepid`.

- `patient.csv.gz`, table `patient`, catalog `datasets/eicu/table-ab037c09d7df9a3c.json`: `patientunitstayid`, `patienthealthsystemstayid`, `uniquepid`, `unitvisitnumber`, `hospitalid`, `age`, demographic/admission fields, `unitdischargeoffset/status`, and eventual `hospitaldischargeoffset/status`.
- `lab.csv.gz`, table `lab`, `table-79bdb33275339b1a.json`: `patientunitstayid`, event `labresultoffset`, revision `labresultrevisedoffset`, `labname`, `labresult`, `labresulttext`, measurement-system/interface. Required labels are `paO2` and `FiO2`; later analysis also uses PaCO2, pH, O2 Sat, PEEP, lactate, renal/hepatic/haematologic labs.
- `respiratoryCharting.csv.gz`, table `respiratoryCharting`, `table-339bf06c7eef27e0.json`: `patientunitstayid`, event `respchartoffset`, entry `respchartentryoffset`, `respcharttypecat`, `respchartvaluelabel`, `respchartvalue`. FiO2 labels contain FiO2/fraction of inspired oxygen; pressure, PEEP, tidal-volume, rate, saturation and device fields support later ordering.
- `respiratoryCare.csv.gz`, table `respiratoryCare`, `table-75bd08623beb504f.json`: `respcarestatusoffset`, `ventstartoffset`, `ventendoffset`, `airwaytype`, `setapneafio2`. The last field is excluded as an exposure source and retained only for the source-failure control.
- `diagnosis.csv.gz`, table `diagnosis`, `table-5d5ab99e8c359037.json`: `diagnosisoffset`, `diagnosisstring`, `icd9code`, priority/status.
- `admissionDx.csv.gz`, table `admissionDx`, `table-2e48e1043e7eaa89.json`: entry clock `admitdxenteredoffset`, `admitdxpath/name/text`.
- `carePlanGeneral.csv.gz`, table `carePlanGeneral`, `table-33b82ae7a5609587.json`: `cplitemoffset/group/value` for exact comfort-only exclusion.
- `treatment.csv.gz`, table `treatment`, `table-5461361964176606.json`: `treatmentoffset/string` for burn/ECMO flags.

The eventual outcome/adjustment tables from the parent remain available: `hospital`, `vitalPeriodic`, `note`, `physicalExam`, `apacheApsVar`, `apachePatientResult`, `apachePredVar`, `infusionDrug`, `carePlanEOL`, and `pastHistory`, with the same keys/clocks. They were not needed for this outcome-blind diagnostic. All four configured dataset trees remain directly accessible read-only; derived files are under `work/identifiability-gate/`.

## Transparent partial-identification baseline: completed M0 diagnostic

FiO2 normalization accepted 0.21–1.00 directly and 21–100 after division by 100. Within each hour, the median respiratory-chart value was primary. If absent, the most recent prior respiratory-chart value was carried forward only to a bin whose start was <=120 minutes later; future values were never carried backward. A same-bin lab FiO2 could supply a validation-source value when respiratory charting was unavailable. All other hours retained the logical excess interval [0,0.60].

Among the 1,348 injury stays, 5,325 of 16,176 hours (32.9%) were directly charted, 3,619 (22.4%) were supported by <=120-minute carry-forward, 402 (2.5%) by lab only, and 6,830 (42.2%) remained unsupported. Among 1,693 no-term stays, counts were 5,752/20,316 (28.3%), 3,563 (17.5%), 556 (2.7%), and 10,445 (51.4%). Median supported hours were 8 versus 6. Carry age had median 49 and 90th percentile 104 minutes.

Respiratory-chart/lab pairs within 30 minutes numbered 2,522. Median absolute difference was 0, 75th percentile 0, and 90th percentile 0.10. This is agreement, not accuracy against delivered FiO2. A conservative +/-0.10 source interval was propagated. Apnea-FiO2 produced 532 pairs with median difference 0.50 and was excluded.

The resulting transparent burden-width median/p75 was 0.283/0.517 in injury and 0.367/0.567 in no-term. Only 11.7% and 15.6% respectively had width <=0.10. Both prespecified stratum gates fail by large margins. Logical missingness, not sampling uncertainty, dominates.

## Ordered latent alternative: completed bounded comparison

The scientifically substantive alternative used the identical stays, 12 hours, respiratory-chart and lab measurements, source clocks, and no outcomes. It was a finite-state hidden Markov model over FiO2 0.21–1.00 in 0.01 steps. An empirical persistence transition kernel was fitted from consecutive observed hourly respiratory-chart medians. Source-specific emissions used respiratory-chart/lab pair residuals. It was tested by masking one directly charted hour in each stay with at least three direct hours (n=1,481) and predicting it from ordered surrounding observations.

The transparent last-observation/lab baseline was available for 1,022 masked hours and had MAE 0.0155. The latent model covered all masked hours, MAE 0.0172, and its nominal 90% intervals covered 90.7%; injury and comparator MAEs were 0.0157 and 0.0187. Thus the latent model adds broad coverage and uncertainty through ordering, but no precision improvement over simple carry-forward where the baseline is available.

Latent burden widths had median/p75 0.0567/0.1288 in injury, passing that stratum, but 0.0617/0.5608 in no-term, failing the p75 gate. The huge comparator tail corresponds to stays with little chart information; masked re-entry performance does not validate extrapolation to never-charted hours. Per the frozen hierarchy, latent assumptions cannot override the transparent M0 failure.

This comparison is substantive: M0 preserves honest ignorance but loses temporal persistence; the latent alternative uses persistence to recover charted states and quantifies when that information is insufficient. It shows that model complexity cannot solve structural absence in the comparator stratum.

## Gate interpretation and falsification

The measurement hypothesis is **adverse**, not merely statistically inconclusive:

- transparent median and p75 widths exceed 0.10/0.15 in both strata;
- the ordered alternative fails the comparator p75 gate;
- apnea-FiO2 is not a valid substitute;
- phenotype accuracy remains unmeasured without clinicians.

Consequently, the 3-point mortality interaction is not tested. It would be invalid to compute a mortality coefficient and call its wide or narrow conventional confidence interval biological evidence. The parent's proposed “maximum error-only risk interaction <1.5 points” cannot itself be evaluated outcome-blind: it requires outcomes plus explicit assumptions linking exposure/phenotype errors to risk. This child corrects that gate. The computable outcome-blind prerequisite is exposure identification at a +0.10 burden scale; it fails.

Supportive measurement result would have required both M0 stratum median widths <=0.10 and p75 <=0.15, adequate lab/respiratory agreement across >=20 hospitals, and an ordered model with calibrated held-out coverage that stayed inside M0. That would permit clinician phenotype review, then outcome modeling.

Adverse is the observed result: structural missingness makes M0 too broad and the latent alternative cannot pass both strata. This defers the biological/mortality branch and prioritizes device/chart validation. It does **not** refute oxygen toxicity or the 3-point interaction.

Inconclusive would mean estimates near thresholds, insufficient pairs/hospitals, failed masking calibration, or implementation uncertainty. Those do not describe the magnitude of the transparent failure here, although the exact anchor/cohort count differs from an inherited pilot because this audit applies first-stay ordering before the hour-36 criterion and excludes apnea-FiO2. The solver must publish a row-level flow reconciliation before any revival; no population change is authorized.

## Clinician adjudication and missing evidence

Two ICU clinicians plus adjudication remain essential to estimate whether pre-hour-24 eICU evidence supports acute parenchymal injury, hydrostatic-only disease, support class, and evidence timing. Review must be blinded to hospital, P0, exposure, post-hour-24 data, and outcome. It can validate consistency with available eICU evidence, not Berlin ARDS.

No automatic computation can recover bilateral imaging, exclude hydrostatic oedema uniformly, verify delivered airway FiO2, infer clinician intent, or establish oxidative injury. A future mortality study requires external device/chart validation or a design whose exposure is actually observed; causal oxygen-target recommendations require prospective evidence.

## Solver deliverables and resources

The next solver should deliver the completed measurement study, not a mortality estimate:

1. a row-level cohort-flow reconciliation against the inherited pilot, without changing the fixed rules;
2. a 12-hour source/age/entry-delay panel and hospital/stratum coverage matrix;
3. respiratory-chart/lab pair calibration by source age, support, stratum, and held-out hospital;
4. transparent logical and empirical-source burden intervals with the frozen gates;
5. the ordered latent model with hospital-held-out contiguous-block masking, calibration/coverage, and comparison to carry-forward;
6. the blinded clinician-review sampling frame and, if actual review is available, weighted confusion estimates;
7. a gate-concordant conclusion: measurement-only adverse unless all prerequisites pass.

Measured compute: final diagnostic used 8 CPUs, 64 GiB requested, 188 seconds; no GPU. Full hospital-bootstrap measurement fitting is estimated at 2–4 hours on 16 CPUs/128 GiB. A GPU is unnecessary for this finite-state model. Only if measurement and clinician gates later pass should the parent’s outcome model (16 CPUs, then at most one A100 for the ordered sequential alternative, within 8 hours) be reopened.

## Alternatives not chosen and revisit conditions

A complete-case or >=6-hour cohort was rejected because it changes the all-hour population through observation selection. Missing=0.21 and unlimited carry-forward were rejected. Same-hour oxygen adequacy conditioning remains rejected as post-treatment selection. A learned gradient-boosting re-entry model in existing support had worse error than carry-forward and optimistic missing-hour widths; this motivated the calibrated ordered model but does not justify imputation. A generic mortality RNN remains scientifically irrelevant.

Revisit the mortality branch only after an external delivered-FiO2 validation sample, dense device export, or a frozen redesign approved as a scientific child establishes both-stratum burden precision and clinician phenotype validity. A narrower high-coverage estimand could be proposed separately, but it is not this fixed all-hour target.

## Compact bibliography

[K1] ICU-ROX Investigators and ANZICS Clinical Trials Group; Mackle D, Bellomo R, Bailey M, et al. *Conservative Oxygen Therapy during Mechanical Ventilation in the ICU.* N Engl J Med. 2020;382:989–998. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1903297. Abstract-level record inspected.

[K2] Nadeau EE, Schwingshackl A, Sturgill JL, Waters CM. *Bench evidence, bedside uncertainty: hyperoxia, mechanical ventilation and lung injury.* Eur Respir Rev. 2026;35:260058. doi:10.1183/16000617.0058-2026. Version-of-record XML passages inspected.

[K3] Bellani G, Laffey JG, Pham T, et al.; LUNG SAFE Investigators and ESICM Trials Group. *Epidemiology, Patterns of Care, and Mortality for Patients With Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome in Intensive Care Units in 50 Countries.* JAMA. 2016;315:788–800. doi:10.1001/jama.2016.0291. Published abstract/metadata inspected; supplement not inspected.

# HCC MVI fixed-day history versus panel identity

## Objective

Execute the frozen, report-free experiment and determine whether one additional earlier observed preoperative laboratory day adds numeric predictive information about recorded M1/M2 microvascular invasion (MVI), beyond both the latest observed laboratory day and the identity of tests ordered on the two days.

This is an open-ended clinical research computation. Fit the models and report whatever the data show; a favorable result is not required. The superseded S-latest/V2 run was strongly adverse, but it is not an answer because it used 125 labels, unequal process covariates, and no O2-label rival. Treat 2020 as a prespecified but operationally unblinded test. Never tune after examining 2020 or 2021.

The strongest already-supported claims are bounded: a static AFP/tumor-size/margin score has shown discrimination for pathologic MVI [K1]; M0/M1/M2 are sampling-dependent histopathologic grades with adverse prognosis for M2 in one selected cohort [K2]; and routine-care measurement presence and timing can encode clinician behavior as well as health [K3]. The unresolved claim is whether fixed-day numeric history adds prediction in this snapshot after separating panel identity and observation process.

## Read-only inputs and exact schema

Snapshot: `3f97e661e1884c34c1e2cdbf74ba0cf6d6c8995853e85f1857c3d72b82ccf521`. Do not modify `/data`; write derived files only below `/workspace`.

| Table | Runtime path | Required columns | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| encounters | `/data/encounters.csv` | `患者主索引, 就诊号, 年龄, 性别, 就诊时间, 入院时间, 出院时间, 就诊科室` | eligibility, demographics, service, clocks |
| procedures | `/data/procedures.csv` | `患者主索引, 就诊号, 手术, 开始时间, 结束时间, 手术来源` | index and prior-treatment exclusion |
| labs | `/data/labs.csv` | `患者主索引, 就诊号, 检验, 定性结果, 定量结果, 标本类型, 检验时间` | preoperative features |
| pathology | `/data/pathology.csv` | `患者主索引, 就诊号, 病理, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 机器型号` | HCC/specimen eligibility and recorded outcome |
| examinations | `/data/examinations.csv` | `患者主索引, 就诊号, 检查, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 开始时间, 机器型号, 检查号` | optional adjudication; report-free primary |
| medications | `/data/medications.csv` | `患者主索引, 就诊号, 用药, 单次用药计量, 单次用药计量单位, 频次, 开始时间, 结束时间, 用药方式, 药品类型` | prior-treatment sensitivity; indication absent |
| clinical_documents | `/data/clinical_documents.csv` | encounter keys and narrative fields | untimed adjudication only |
| diagnoses | `/data/diagnoses.csv` | `患者主索引, 就诊号, 诊断名称, 诊断类型` | untimed adjudication only |

The clinical-document header contains `入院诊断` twice. Preserve both by position and document any mangling. Join encounter tables on `(患者主索引, 就诊号)` and longitudinal history by `患者主索引`. Pathology, diagnoses, clinical documents, post-cutoff medication, and post-cutoff examinations are never predictors. Lab units, reference ranges, assay platforms, pathology issue time, block/sampling metadata, images, mortality, recurrence, outside treatment, and treatment indication are unavailable.

## Frozen population, time origin, and outcome

1. Collapse exact duplicate procedure rows. Per patient, choose the earliest procedure whose `手术` contains both `肝` and `切除`. Exclude transplant/donor/retrieval, biopsy/puncture, drainage, abscess/cyst, and isolated cholecystectomy terms. Resolve same-time ties deterministically. Procedure start is time zero.
2. Include age ≥18 and index years 2014–2021.
3. Exclude recorded procedures containing embolization, intervention, ablation, radiofrequency, microwave, infusion, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or targeted-treatment terms on calendar days -180 through -1.
4. In same-encounter pathology, require HCC wording, exactly one distinct grade after `MVI提示风险分级:` (including full-width colon/bullet variants), and `手术标本`. Exclude the six training-era biopsy-only records.
5. Outcome is 1 for recorded M1/M2 and 0 for M0. Lexical contradictions with explicit microscopic vascular-invasion text are flags, not relabeling.
6. Parse `定量结果` strictly as finite numeric. Require `检验时间` strictly before procedure start and calendar day -90 through -1; exclude day 0 regardless of clock time. Use the median per patient/exact label/day. Require at least two eligible numeric lab days.
7. Split by index year: 2016–2018 train; 2019 validation; 2020 primary; 2021 template stress; 2014–2015 era sensitivity. Never pool 2021 with 2020. Reconcile train 1,918/835 events, validation 992/463, 2020 845/325, and 2021 520/185. Explain any mismatch; an unreconciled cohort is incomplete.

## Frozen sampling, models, and controls

Use seeds 1001–1020. The latest day is the maximum eligible day. For each patient/seed, choose one earlier day with the first eight SHA-256 bytes of `"{seed}|{患者主索引}"`, big-endian, modulo the sorted earlier days. Outcomes must not affect selection.

Freeze the top 100 exact labels observed in at least 100 training patients across eligible daily data, ranked by descending patient count then lexical order. Fit imputers, encoders, transforms, and penalties on train/2019 only. Scale numeric values by training median/IQR and clip at ±10 IQR; document a nonzero fallback for zero IQR. Never use 2020/2021 for selection.

Use L2 logistic regression. Use fixed `C={0.0001,0.0003,0.001,0.003,0.01,0.03,0.1}`, select by 2019 Brier (tie: higher AUROC, then smaller C), and freeze. For replicate-dependent arms choose one C by mean 2019 Brier across all 20 replicates.

Every arm receives age, sex, service, latest-day recency, total eligible distinct days, raw eligible row count before aggregation, and full eligible-day span.

- **S-latest:** shared covariates plus latest-day values and masks.
- **O2-label:** shared covariates and exact-label masks for identical selected earlier/latest panels, with all numeric values withheld.
- **V2:** shared covariates, identical panel masks, robust-scaled earlier/latest values, and differences only where the same label occurs on both days.

Use identical patients/days across arms. Do not call V2 a trajectory model or claim fixed analyte exposure. Average patient predictions across replicates.

C2 is secondary and restricted to patient-replicates with at least two common labels; hash-select exactly two and compare latest-only with earlier+latest values for those labels. Report support before fitting.

D2/T2 remain deferred from primary interpretation because the frozen prototype failed its stability gate. They may be exploratory only if a frozen 2019 gate is met: replicate-averaged learned arm beats V2 in AUROC and Brier, AUROC seed range ≤0.02, Brier range ≤0.005, beats label-only T2, and passes outcome permutation. An order claim also requires T2 > D2 and value-masked T2, with day swap and value-label reassignment each attenuating ≥50% of Brier gain.

Before modeling, flag a label if any 2016–2020 year has a >10-fold median ratio versus training or >5 training-IQR median shift. Report full and stable-label analyses. Unit harmonization cannot be claimed.

Also report pathology-discordance exclusion, observation-count strata, day -7 sensitivity, 2014–2015 era stress, annual drift, within-calendar-year outcome permutation, value-to-label reassignment, and earlier/latest day swap. Blinded hepatopathology review is not supplied: state whether performed. Outcome interpretation is inconclusive if agreement is <95% overall or <90% in any grade-era stratum.

## Evaluation and falsification

For 2019, 2020, and 2021 report AUROC, AUPRC, Brier, log loss, calibration intercept/slope, and net benefit at 0.20/0.30/0.40/0.50. Report V2 minus comparator AUROC and comparator minus V2 Brier for both comparators.

Use 2,000 paired patient bootstraps on replicate-averaged predictions, report percentile 95% intervals, every replicate effect, and positive-effect fractions. Disclose that bootstrap uncertainty does not include model refitting.

Support requires all frozen 2020 gates: V2 exceeds both comparators by ≥0.02 AUROC and ≥0.01 Brier gain; all paired intervals exclude zero; V2 calibration slope 0.8–1.2; net-benefit gain at two adjacent thresholds without material harm elsewhere; no 2019 direction reversal; positive Brier gain in ≥16/20 replicates for both comparisons; and direction persists after discordance and stable-label exclusions. This supports only fixed-day prediction and is hypothesis-generating because related 2020 outcomes were opened.

Adverse evidence includes precise exclusion of a threshold, O2 matching V2, worse calibration/net benefit, gain confined to drift-flagged labels or discordant outcomes, unstable replicates, or 2019 reversal. It parks numeric history while allowing a panel/workup predictor. Broad intervals, missing/failed adjudication, too few C2 events, incompatible sensitivities, or unresolved gates are inconclusive. Stable 2020 with 2021 failure indicates era dependence and blocks deployment.

## Required deliverables

Create `/workspace/submission/`:

- `analysis.py`: runnable source reading only `/data`.
- `study.json`: schema `hcc-mvi-fixed-day-v1`, status, source hashes, seeds, models, rules, operational-unblinding disclosure, bootstrap count, versions, and D2/T2 disposition.
- `cohort_flow.json`: exclusions and counts/events by split.
- `predictions.csv`: `subject_hash,split,year,variant,model,replicate,outcome,prediction`. Use one-way SHA-256 hashes, never raw IDs. Variants: `full,stable_labels,discordance_excluded`; models: `S-latest,O2-label,V2`; replicates 1001–1020.
- `metrics.csv`: `variant,split,model,n,events,auroc,auprc,brier,log_loss,calibration_intercept,calibration_slope,net_benefit_0.2,net_benefit_0.3,net_benefit_0.4,net_benefit_0.5`, from averaged predictions.
- `contrasts.csv`: `variant,split,comparison,metric,estimate,ci_low,ci_high,bootstrap_n`; comparisons `V2_vs_S-latest,V2_vs_O2-label`; metrics `delta_auroc,brier_gain`.
- `replicate_effects.csv`: `variant,split,comparison,replicate,delta_auroc,brier_gain`.
- `measurement_stability.csv`: label, annual counts/medians, training median/IQR, diagnostics, flag.
- `pathology_audit.json`: parser, discordance by grade/year, review status/agreement, unresolved needs.
- `c2_support.csv`: split/replicate eligible counts/events and clearly secondary metrics if fitted.
- `controls.json`: permutation, swaps/reassignment, day -7, era, strata, and drift results/status.
- `claims.json`: `primary_interpretation` (`supportive|adverse|inconclusive`), `claim_scope="prediction_within_snapshot"`, evidence row references, net-benefit judgment/rationale, precursor-not-primary and operational-unblinding disclosures, absence of model-refit uncertainty, and false booleans for mechanism, biological evolution, pathology truth, treatment benefit, deployment readiness, and transportability.

The verifier recomputes metrics/contrasts from predictions and checks structured interpretation gates. It cannot certify pathology truth, causal mechanism, assay equivalence, treatment benefit, novelty, or clinical utility.

## Key references

[K1] Xu J, Zhang Y-L, Yang M, et al. *Preoperative Prediction of Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Chinese Retrospective Multicenter Study Based on Global Meta-Analysis.* Cancer Medicine. 2026;15:e71749. doi:10.1002/cam4.71749. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC13122567/fullTextXML

[K2] Li Z, Xu L, Liu X, et al. *Comparisons of clinical patterns, short- and long-term prognostic outcomes in patients stratified by the severity of microvascular invasion after curative resection for hepatocellular carcinoma.* World Journal of Surgical Oncology. 2026;24:132. doi:10.1186/s12957-026-04229-2. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC13005532/fullTextXML

[K3] Sisk R, Lin L, Sperrin M, et al. *Informative presence and observation in routine health data: A review of methodology for clinical risk prediction.* Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association. 2021;28:155–166. doi:10.1093/jamia/ocaa242. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7810439/fullTextXML

# HCC MVI: fixed-day history separated from panel identity

Status: outcome-status child of candidate-32f98ddf1f9b6e8288bdb7d3. Its population, endpoint, time window, temporal split, matched S-latest/O2-label/V2 estimand, controls, thresholds, and interpretation rules are unchanged. After that design was frozen, a parallel worker completed the superseded parent's 2020/2021 S-latest-versus-V2 pipeline. Thus the statement that 2020/2021 outcomes were unopened was true at parent publication but is no longer true for the episode. The completed precursor is strongly adverse, but it is not the repaired primary computation because it lacks O2-label, uses a different 125-label vocabulary, and does not give all arms the same process covariates. The repaired analysis remains computable and prespecified relative to that late result, but 2020 is now described as a prespecified, operationally unblinded test; independent temporal or external confirmation is required for any positive claim.

## What is supported, what remains unresolved, and why it matters

The inspected evidence supports three bounded claims. A static AFP/tumor-size/margin score achieved C-statistics near 0.81 in two Chinese validation cohorts and MVI is confirmed pathologically [K1]. M0/M1/M2 have sampling-dependent histopathologic definitions, with adverse prognosis for M2 in one selected resection cohort [K2]. Routine-care test presence, timing, and intensity can encode health and clinician behavior and cannot automatically be called biology [K3]. None of these works establishes that an additional preoperative laboratory day predicts this database's recorded MVI grade beyond the latest available panel.

The unresolved repaired hypothesis is:

> Among explicitly graded, untreated, pathology-HCC first resections with at least two numeric preoperative laboratory days, does one additional earlier observed day improve 2020 prediction of recorded M1/M2 beyond the latest observed day after separating numeric-value information from exact-label panel identity and observation process?

This is clinically relevant because reproducible preoperative information could refine MVI-risk discussion and future study enrollment. It cannot establish treatment benefit, biological evolution, pathology adequacy, or transport beyond explicitly graded cases.

## Consequential audit result: the parent did not fix information exposure

The parent's one-value-per-label/day cap fixed duplicate rows but not panel size or analyte identity. On the frozen cohort, the new aggregate audit reproduced 1,918/835 train patients/events, 992/463 validation, 845/325 locked 2020, and 520/185 stress 2021 with at least two lab days.

Across 20 outcome-independent earlier-day draws, the locked 2020 earlier day contained a mean 67.6-69.7 exact labels, while the latest day contained 11.0. Mean shared labels were 4.47-5.42, but 67.7%-69.6% of patient-replicates had zero shared labels. In 2021, 75.6%-78.8% had zero shared labels. The distribution is strongly bimodal: in replicate 0 the 2020 shared-label quartiles were 0/0/2, even though the mean was 5.39. Thus V2/D2/T2 usually compare different panels rather than two measurements of the same analyte. An apparent gain can be caused by which tests were ordered on which day; “fixed information exposure,” “value evolution,” and “two-state trajectory” are unsupported labels for the primary estimand.

The latest day is also not literally a current snapshot. It is the maximum calendar day in [-90,-1] with at least one finite numeric result. In 2020 its median was day -2 (IQR -3 to -1; range -15 to -1). The correct boundary is: include lab timestamps strictly before index procedure start whose calendar-date difference is -90 through -1; exclude day 0 regardless of clock time. All models receive latest-day recency. Conclusions say “latest observed preoperative day,” not “current state.”

## Outcome/template and assay validity

The exact grade parser still yields 534 lexical discordance flags, not adjudicated errors. In the serial cohort the flag rate was 9.0% in 2016-2018, 2.4% in 2019, 2.8% in 2020, and 3.5% in 2021. Among all graded cases, M0 discordance fell from about 15.5% in 2016 to 4.2% in 2020; 2021 has the known grade-ascertainment discontinuity. These era patterns make 2020 the primary locked evaluation and 2021 a separate template stress set. Primary computation excludes flagged records only as a prespecified sensitivity; it cannot relabel them. Blinded hepatopathology review remains essential to verify specimen/index correspondence, grade, and template-section meaning. Failure of <95% overall or <90% per-grade-era agreement makes outcome interpretation inconclusive.

Labs provide exact label, qualitative result, quantitative result, specimen type, and timestamp, but no unit, reference range, or assay platform. Exact-label sparsity is not the main barrier: 100 labels each occurred in at least 100 training patients, and the top labels had broad 2019-2021 coverage. Numeric comparability is the barrier. The aggregate audit found an approximately 1,000-fold prealbumin median shift in 2020/2021 relative to training and other smaller shifts. This directly forbids biological-change claims and exposes temporal prediction to assay/unit discontinuity.

The primary pipeline therefore freezes train-only median/IQR transforms, clips at +/-10 IQR, and defines an outcome-blind measurement-stability manifest before fitting: exact labels with a >10-fold median ratio or >5 training-IQR median shift in any 2016-2020 calendar year are flagged. Report results both with the full train-supported vocabulary and after dropping flagged labels. The 2020 covariate distribution was inspected for the audit before the repaired design was frozen. Subsequently, a parallel worker opened 2020 outcomes for the superseded S-latest/V2 contrast; this is disclosed and the exact precursor outputs are attached. A conclusion is inconclusive if support depends on drift-flagged labels or reverses under the stability sensitivity. Unit harmonization itself requires laboratory metadata unavailable here.

## Frozen population, split, endpoint, and bindings

Preserve the parent's index: earliest qualifying procedure row whose `手术` contains 肝 and 切除, excluding transplant/donor, biopsy/puncture, drainage, abscess/cyst, and isolated cholecystectomy; collapse exact duplicates. Include age >=18, same-encounter pathology text supporting HCC, one unique grade after `MVI提示风险分级:`, surgical-specimen descriptor, no recorded procedure-defined locoregional/systemic treatment on days -180:-1, and at least two finite numeric lab days in -90:-1. Exclude the six biopsy-only training-era cases.

Outcome is recorded M1/M2 versus M0. Split: train 2016-2018; validation 2019; locked primary test 2020; template stress 2021. 2014-2015 is era sensitivity. The 2021 set is never pooled with 2020 to rescue or reverse the primary conclusion.

Read-only snapshot `3f97e661e1884c34c1e2cdbf74ba0cf6d6c8995853e85f1857c3d72b82ccf521`:

- `pathology`: `[private path]`; keys `患者主索引, 就诊号`; columns `病理, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 机器型号`; no timestamp. Outcome/parser/specimen audit only.
- `procedures`: `[private path]`; keys plus `手术, 开始时间, 结束时间, 手术来源`. Index and recorded-treatment exclusions.
- `encounters`: `[private path]`; keys plus `年龄, 性别, 就诊时间, 入院时间, 出院时间, 就诊科室`. Demographics, service, and clock checks.
- `labs`: `[private path]`; keys plus `检验, 定性结果, 定量结果, 标本类型, 检验时间`. Use finite strict numeric `定量结果`, exact `检验`, and same-label/day median. No unit/platform/reference-range columns.
- `examinations`: `[private path]`; keys plus `检查, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 开始时间, 机器型号, 检查号`. Report-free primary; tumor parser remains unvalidated.
- `medications`: `[private path]`; medication/dose/unit/frequency, start/end, route/type. Recorded prior-treatment sensitivity; indication absent.
- `clinical_documents` and `diagnoses` remain untimed adjudication sources, never predictive features.

Link encounter tables on (`患者主索引, 就诊号`) and longitudinal history by `患者主索引`. Pathology, documents, diagnoses, medication after cutoff, and examinations after cutoff are never model features. Mortality, recurrence, outside treatment, pathology issue time, block/sampling metadata, lab units/platforms, and images are unavailable.

## Revised matched comparison

This child replaces “fixed information” with a **fixed-day addition** and explicitly models panel identity.

For each of 20 frozen seeds, retain the latest eligible numeric day and sample one earlier eligible day uniformly by a deterministic patient/seed hash. Within exact label/day, use the median; retain one value per label/day. The vocabulary, transforms, penalties, architecture, epochs, early stopping, thresholds, and all repaired controls were frozen using train/2019 before the parallel 2020 precursor result became available. They must not be changed in response to that result.

1. **S-latest:** penalized logistic regression on latest-day values/masks, age, sex, service, latest-day recency, total preoperative distinct days, raw row count, and span. The operational covariates are shared by every arm.
2. **O2-label rival:** the identical two selected days and exact label/day masks, recency/process variables, demographics, and service, with all numeric values masked. This is the matched observation/panel-identity rival. A coarse count-only O-process remains descriptive.
3. **V2:** penalized logistic model on the identical selected panels, train-scaled numeric values, masks, and transparent earlier/latest/difference terms only where the same exact label occurs on both days. It tests additional numeric-value prediction beyond O2-label and S-latest; it is not a trajectory model.
4. **D2:** a label-value interaction encoder pooled within each day and averaged across the two days, plus the same static/process inputs. It can capture nonlinear cross-marker patterns but intentionally cannot use day order.
5. **T2:** the same day encoder followed by a two-step GRU in earlier-to-latest order. It can capture nonlinear dependence on panel/value order. Mandatory controls are T2 with all values zeroed, earlier/latest day swap, within-day value-to-label reassignment, and outcome permutation.
6. **C2 shared-label secondary:** for patient-replicates with at least two common exact labels across selected days, hash-select exactly two common labels and compare latest-only with earlier+latest values for those same labels. This is the only analysis that can speak to within-label ordered change, remains secondary because most patient-replicates have no shared label, and must report cohort/event counts before modeling.

The report-free analysis is primary. No claim “beyond tumor burden” is allowed unless the parent's blinded tumor-report parser gate passes and identical validated tumor variables are added to every arm.

## Validation prototype and learned-method decision

A bounded CPU prototype used one deterministic replicate, 1,918/835 train patients/events and 992/463 validation patients/events, a train-frozen 100-label vocabulary, identical two-day matrices, and three neural seeds. That prototype itself did not evaluate 2020 or 2021 outcomes; the later separate precursor execution did. Runtime was 134 seconds on 8 CPUs/64 GiB.

V2 validation AUROC/Brier/log loss were 0.630/0.239/0.675. D2 AUROC was 0.572-0.583 and Brier 0.244-0.245. T2 AUROC was 0.567-0.614 and Brier 0.242-0.246. Label-only T2 AUROC was 0.559-0.568; outcome permutation was 0.531. One T2 seed was highly sensitive to value-label reassignment, while other seeds were not. Validation was used for early stopping, so these are optimistic feasibility diagnostics, not scientific findings.

This adverse and unstable prototype selects V2 as the primary value model. D2/T2 are **deferred from locked primary interpretation**, not declared infeasible. The solver may fit the frozen three-seed learned models on all 20 replicates only if the already-frozen 2019 gate is met without using 2020/2021 results for selection: the replicate-averaged learned arm must beat V2 by both AUROC and Brier, have AUROC seed range <=0.02 and Brier range <=0.005, beat label-only T2, and pass outcome permutation. The current prototype fails that gate. If the solver retains D2/T2 for completeness, label them exploratory and do not let their 2020 result alter the primary V2 conclusion. Revisit a learned primary only with larger stable serial support or scheduled panels.

CPU is selected: the full matrices are about 3,000 fitting/validation patients, 100 labels, two days, and small networks; the measured multi-seed prototype took 134 seconds. Expected full 20-replicate V2/O2 plus bootstrap is 1-3 hours on 8-16 CPUs and <=64 GiB; optional D2/T2 is estimated 1-2 CPU hours from the prototype. GPU allocation is unnecessary for this scale, though it is available and not scientifically disallowed.

## Late precursor result and what it does—and does not—establish

After the repaired design was frozen, the parallel parent-specification run reconstructed the same 4,562-patient serial cohort and opened 845/325-event 2020 and 520/185-event 2021 outcomes. In 2020, its S-latest AUROC/Brier were 0.5003/0.2794 and V2 were 0.5070/0.3516. The paired V2-S AUROC difference was +0.0146 (95% CI -0.0353,+0.0618), Brier gain was -0.0721 (-0.0957,-0.0487), and zero of 20 replicates improved Brier. The parent-style V2 therefore fails the repaired study's required benefit over S-latest and is severely miscalibrated; this is strong adverse precursor evidence, not support.

It does not complete the repaired test. The run selected 125 labels by occurrence on the latest day, whereas the repaired prototype used a top-100 train-supported two-day vocabulary; its S and V2 arms shared age, recency, and distinct-day count but not all raw-count/span/service/process inputs; it omitted the identical-panel value-masked O2-label rival, train-frozen robust/IQR transform and drift-exclusion manifest, and C2 shared-label analysis. Those differences prevent attributing failure specifically to historical numeric values versus panel identity, assay drift, or mismatched covariates. They also forbid calling the repaired estimand prospectively locked after this episode.

The smallest consequential next check is therefore unchanged: run the already-frozen repaired S-latest/O2-label/V2 pipeline without post-result tuning. If repaired V2 remains worse than S-latest or fails calibration, the historical-value direction is parked regardless of O2. If V2 unexpectedly meets every frozen threshold against both comparators, the result is hypothesis-generating within this snapshot and requires independent temporal or external replication because related 2020 outcomes were already seen. O2 matching V2 would favor panel/workup identity over numeric history. Broad intervals or dependence on drift/discordance exclusions remain inconclusive.

## Evaluation, uncertainty, and falsification

Primary estimand: on identical 2020 patients and each frozen draw, V2 minus S-latest and V2 minus O2-label. This remains the prespecified repaired computation, but because a related 2020 contrast has been observed it is an operationally unblinded test, not a pristine lock. Average patient predictions across 20 replicates. Report AUROC, AUPRC, Brier, log loss, calibration intercept/slope, and net benefit at 0.20/0.30/0.40/0.50. Use 2,000 patient bootstraps that recompute metrics from replicate-averaged predictions; separately report all replicate effects and the fraction with positive gain. The bootstrap does not replace model-refit uncertainty, which must be disclosed. Report 2019, locked 2020, and separate 2021 stress; annual drift, discordance exclusion, stability-label exclusion, and observation-count strata.

Support within this snapshot for additional numeric history requires in 2020: V2 improves over both S-latest and O2-label by >=0.02 AUROC and >=0.01 Brier, both paired 95% intervals exclude zero; calibration slope 0.8-1.2; net-benefit gain at two adjacent thresholds without material harm elsewhere; no 2019 direction reversal; positive Brier effect in >=16/20 replicates; and persistence after pathology-discordance and measurement-stability exclusions. This supports fixed-day historical-value prediction only.

A learned nonlinear claim additionally requires the validation gate above and locked D2/T2 improvement over V2 in AUROC and Brier with paired intervals excluding zero. An order-specific value claim requires T2 > D2 and > value-masked T2; day swap must attenuate >=50% of its Brier gain; value-label reassignment must attenuate >=50%; and label-only swap cannot explain the effect. Only C2 can support a limited within-label order claim, with adequate counts and the same gates.

Adverse evidence is precise exclusion of the V2 thresholds; O2-label matching V2; gain confined to drift-flagged labels or discordant outcomes; instability across replicates; reversal in 2019; or failure of calibration/net benefit. This parks the historical-value claim while allowing a panel/workup predictor. Learned-model validation failure, already observed in the prototype, defers D2/T2 without refuting V2.

Inconclusive evidence includes broad intervals, failed pathology adjudication, too few C2 events, poor calibration, major 2021-only failure, or incompatible results between full and measurement-stable vocabularies. Stable 2020 performance with 2021 failure indicates template/assay-era dependence and blocks deployment but does not erase the bounded 2020 association.

Mandatory checks: source hashes/headers, cohort reconciliation, strictly pre-index timestamps, day-0 exclusion, fixed seeds, train-only vocabulary/transforms, patient split isolation, one value per label/day, outcome permutation, O2-label, value-label reassignment, day swap, day -7 sensitivity, discordance exclusion, assay-drift manifest, 2014-2015 era stress, and claims linked to computed outputs.

## Scientific deliverable and claim boundary

Completion requires newly fitted, specification-identical S-latest, O2-label, and 20-replicate V2; frozen patient-level predictions for 2019/2020/2021; aggregate replicate and bootstrap metrics; calibration and decision curves; pathology/measurement manifests; C2 support counts; and `claims.json` mapping every interpretation to an output and rule. D2/T2 completion is conditional on the validation gate and otherwise recorded as a justified deferral.

The verifier can check computation, bindings, clocks, split isolation, sampling, masks, transforms, controls, metrics, and whether conclusions obey support/adverse/inconclusive rules. It cannot establish pathology truth, specimen adequacy, assay equivalence, tumor burden, clinical utility, mechanism, or treatment benefit. Those require expert adjudication, missing metadata, external validation, or another study.

## Exactly three key references

[K1] Xu J, Zhang Y-L, Yang M, et al. Preoperative Prediction of Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Chinese Retrospective Multicenter Study Based on Global Meta-Analysis. Cancer Medicine. 2026;15:e71749. doi:10.1002/cam4.71749.

[K2] Li Z, Xu L, Liu X, et al. Comparisons of clinical patterns, short- and long-term prognostic outcomes in patients stratified by the severity of microvascular invasion after curative resection for hepatocellular carcinoma. World Journal of Surgical Oncology. 2026;24:132. doi:10.1186/s12957-026-04229-2.

[K3] Sisk R, Lin L, Sperrin M, et al. Informative presence and observation in routine health data: A review of methodology for clinical risk prediction. Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association. 2021;28:155-166. doi:10.1093/jamia/ocaa242.
