`capacity(c-1) discharge end < I(c) start < V(c) end < IX(c) start < IX(c) end < capacity(c) charge start < capacity(c) discharge end`.

At LV (end V), Q only through c-1, I/V at c, cycle 1–5 anchors, and diagnostics through c-1 are available. At LD (IX start), D(c)=IX_start(c)-V_end(c) becomes available. At LX (IX end), IX-minus-V becomes available. Q[c] and later capacities are outcomes and must never be predictors or preprocessing inputs.

## Outcomes

For ten consecutive capacities q0…q9, define positive fade rate
`g(q) = -median over j<k of (q[k]-q[j])/(k-j)`.

At origin c:
`g_pre=g(Q[c-10:c-1])`, `g_near=g(Q[c:c+9])`, `g_late=g(Q[c+10:c+19])`;
`A_near=g_near-g_pre`, `A_late=g_late-g_pre`;
`M=(A_near+A_late)/2`, `C=A_late-A_near`;
`P=sign(M)*max(0,abs(M)-abs(C)/2)`.

Jointly fit M and C. Derive P, A_near, and A_late; do not fit or count the algebraically dependent original triple as independent hypotheses. Also compute washout `W=g(Q[c+5:c+19])-g_pre`, OLS-slope and median-adjacent-loss variants, leave-one-capacity-out ranges, Q/Q0 and ox/red=1 variants, and L10/L20 endpoint comparators.

## Predictors and models

For scalar D and the 120-component X=IX−V spectrum, define per cell:
`S_z=median(z[1],...,z[5])`, `P_z(c)=z(c-1)-S_z`, and `U_z(c)=z(c)-z(c-1)`.
Require reconstruction error <=1e-9 s for D and <=1e-12 ohm for X.

History B contains c, log(1+c), numeric and one-hot temperature, Q0, Q[c-1], Q[c-1]/Q0, Q[c-10:c-1]/Q0, nine first differences, five- and ten-cycle OLS slopes and their difference, ten-cycle quadratic coefficient and residual SD, and temperature interactions with age/level/slope. At LV add current V, dI=V-I, S_D, P_D, S_X, and P_X.

Fit these matched rungs within each family:

- A1: all LV variables, no current update.
- AD: A1 + U_D.
- AX: A1 + U_X.
- ADX: A1 + U_D + U_X.

ADX versus A1 is primary. AD and AX are simultaneous attribution contrasts. ADX-only support means combined acquisition information and cannot identify a modality.

The deterministic baseline extrapolates the pre-window slope over 20 cycles and predicts M=C=P=0.

The auditable model is weighted multi-output ridge for (M,C), with predictors and outcomes standardized using outer-training cells only. Tune alpha in {0.01,0.1,1,10,100} and age-spline df in {3,5,7} by inner leave-one-cell-out family-balanced score. Run both the full spectra and fixed frequencies 17.79613 and 2.16054 Hz.

The substantive functional alternative predicts the 20-vector residual trajectory
`R_h=Q[c+h]-{Q[c-1]-(h+1)g_pre}`.
Represent training trajectories in a fixed six-degree-of-freedom cubic B-spline basis. Use training-only weighted PCA separately for V,dI,S_X,P_X,U_X (99% variance, cap chosen from {10,20}), then RBF Nystroem plus multi-output ridge. Tune gamma in {0.5,1,2} times inverse median squared training distance, landmarks {128,256}, ridge alpha above, and roughness {0,0.1,1,10}; seed 20260923. Reconstruct trajectories and derive M,C,P,W. This can distinguish an early excursion, stable slope shift, and bend; it is not a mechanistic state-space decomposition. Compare rungs only within the same family.

A local-linear state-space model is deferred because process and observation noise are not separately measured. A neural sequence model is deferred because there are only eight mature specimens. Equivalent-circuit fitting is deferred pending a validated topology and identifiability evidence.

## Splits, fitting, and uncertainty

Use eight outer leave-one-mature-cell-out folds. The held cell supplies prediction-time measurements only and no outcomes to scaling, bases, PCA, landmarks, tuning, calibration, or feature selection. Inner selection is leave-one-training-cell-out. Weight by inverse cell count and inverse represented-family cell count, renormalized to training-row count.

Report origin-, cell-, and temperature-family-level MAE, RMSE, bias for M,C,P,A_near,A_late; integrated trajectory MAE; and nominal 90% interval coverage, width, and interval score. Primary aggregation averages origins within cell, cells within temperature family, then the three families.

Use all 256 mature-core paired cell sign assignments and 10,000 fixed-seed hierarchical cell bootstraps. Construct a simultaneous 95% max-deviation band over scalar-ridge AD, AX, and ADX versus A1 contrasts for P and C. Give functional ADX-versus-A1 P/C contrasts a simultaneous two-outcome band. Report every cell contrast and family direction; do not present coarse p-values as population proof.

Run the frozen anchor, lag, timing, representation, duplicate-spectrum, family-holdout, whole-cell-within-family update permutation, Q[c] oracle, identity, censoring, target-jackknife, washout, and age-stratum controls. Never permute origins independently.

## Required outputs

Write all files directly under `/workspace`:

- `results.json`: contract version `1.0`; source hashes; population counts; outcome definitions; model/split settings; computed primary metrics and bands; sensitivity directions; deterministic outcome labels; claims; and evidence limitations.
- `predictions.csv`: every mature origin × model family × rung, with cell, family, cycle, outer fold, true/predicted M,C,P,A_near,A_late, interval bounds, sample weight, and selected hyperparameters.
- `trajectory_predictions.csv`: every mature origin × functional rung × h=0…19, with true and predicted residual trajectory.
- `contrasts.csv`: overall, cell, and temperature-family AD/AX/ADX-versus-A1 contrasts for P and C, including estimate and simultaneous lower/upper percent-gain bounds.
- `uncertainty_draws.csv`: the 256 sign assignments and 10,000 hierarchical bootstrap draws with seed and draw type.
- `manifest.json`: immutable input hashes, archive members/table IDs/columns, software versions, split membership, preprocessing and tuning selections, feature provenance, and checks that Q[c:] never entered predictors.

See [output-contract.md](output-contract.md) for exact mechanical schema. Preserve all unfavorable and inconclusive outputs; do not omit failed models or cells.

## Falsification and interpretation

The 10% relevance and 5% no-value margins are design choices.

A mature P-support claim requires scalar ADX family-balanced MAE gain >=10%, its simultaneous lower bound >0, functional ADX improvement in the same direction, no washout reversal, improvement in at least two temperature families with none below −10%, interval coverage 0.80–1.00, and no reversal in OLS, Q/Q0, or jackknife-stable analyses. Apply the analogous rule to C. D-only or X-only attribution requires the corresponding simultaneous side contrast to pass; otherwise use combined-acquisition language.

If gains occur only before cycle 50, label them early-only and do not claim mature prognosis. L10/L20-only gain is endpoint-only. Label no useful mature trajectory information only when both P and C ADX upper bounds are <=5% in both model families, calibration is acceptable, and no family gains >10%. Label adverse only when relevant simultaneous upper bounds are <=0 without sensitivity reversal. The global hypothesis is falsified as posed when ADX upper bounds are <10% for both P and C in both matched families. Otherwise, intervals crossing 0 or 10%, family conflict, scalar/functional disagreement, poor calibration, washout/slope reversal, unstable targets, early/mature conflict, identity dependence, or inadequate specimens is inconclusive.

Negative M or C does not itself falsify predictability. The verifier rewards correct computation and warranted interpretation, never a favorable answer. It checks arithmetic and declared gates but cannot scientifically adjudicate headerless semantics, disputed identities, mechanism, causality, practical margins, or external transfer.

The expected full workload is CPU-oriented: up to 16 CPUs, 64 GiB, zero GPUs, and seven hours. GPU use is allowed but provides no presumed merit. Readiness probes only source layout, counts, imports, outcome algebra, and a tiny two-fold fit; readiness is not a solved experiment.

# Zhang2020 recovery-aware trajectory experiment: can current diagnostic updates forecast a stable rate shift rather than early-life settling?

## Scientific decision and unresolved hypothesis

The selected parent correctly moved beyond a single future capacity endpoint, but its three claim-gating outcomes are not three independent scientific quantities:

`A_late = A_near + A_shape`.

It also pooled markedly different age support. Two retained cells have only 6 and 8 H20 origins, all near the beginning of life, whereas seven cells contribute observations beyond cycle 150. A new read-only stress audit shows that the median mean post-versus-pre rate shift is -0.00109 mAh/cycle over all 1,974 H20 origins but -0.10706 mAh/cycle on the only ten-cell common support, cycles 10–15. This is direct evidence of strong early trajectory nonstationarity; it is not evidence of a degradation mechanism. The exact data can describe whether an observed change lasts for 20 cycles, but without replicated capacity measurements or protocol interventions they cannot distinguish measurement fluctuation, reversible capacity recovery, and a physical early-life process.

The confirmatory question is therefore narrower and falsifiable:

> Among cells with complete mature common-age origins at cycles 50–99, do the current within-cell update in the observed V-to-IX transition clock and/or the current IX-minus-V impedance update improve held-cell forecasts of (i) a same-direction rate shift present in both future ten-cycle windows or (ii) a near-to-late bend, beyond an identically fitted model of the cell's own pre-origin trajectory?

The strongest claim currently supported is only that the exact Zhang2020 archive contains the required chronological measurements, that the proposed outcomes vary, and that early and pooled supports differ substantially. No current-update prediction has been fitted. The unresolved claim is conditional, specimen-transferable prognostic information. It is not a claim that the cohort generally accelerates, that an observed recovery is electrochemical rather than measurement-related, that the clock is a discharge duration, or that either update identifies a microscopic mechanism.

A positive mature-core result could justify collecting the current diagnostic acquisition when a stable 20-cycle trajectory change is operationally relevant. An early-only result would instead support prediction of this archive's early settling behavior and cannot be relabeled as mature degradation prognosis.

## Executed stress audit and consequential repairs

The inherited audit, `parents/candidate-62e7203ef376f91f401e72fe/support-0-zhang_rate_shape_audit.py` and its JSON output, established the exact H10/H20 risks and source chronology. - the algebraic residual `A_late-A_near-A_shape` is at floating-point zero (maximum (5.55	imes10^{-17}) mAh/cycle);
- `A_near` and `A_late` correlate 0.6555 across repeated origins, whereas the nonredundant mean-shift and bend coordinates correlate 0.2577;

- the median leave-one-capacity-out range of each ten-point Theil-Sen slope is 0.0111–0.0114 mAh/cycle, roughly half the 0.0191–0.0243 mAh/cycle IQRs of the original rate-change targets;

These results warrant three repairs: replace the redundant triple by two coordinates and one derived persistence score; make an age-balanced mature core the confirmatory population; and compare current-update versus no-current-update rungs within both scalar and functional model families.

## Frozen specimens, temporal populations, and chronology

The conservative physical-cell keys remain exactly:

`25C01, 25C04, 25C05, 25C06, 25C07, 25C08, 35C01, 35C02, 45C01, 45C02`.

For every origin `c`, preserve:

`capacity(c-1) discharge end < I(c) start < V(c) end < IX(c) start < IX(c) end < capacity(c) charge start < capacity(c) discharge end`.

```
h_L = (-1,  0, 1) / sqrt(2)
```

- **S (simple persistence):** `yhat_C=b_C*x_C`; `yhat_D=b_D*x_D`.

```
L_C,mi = ||y_Ci-yhat_C,mi||²
L_D,mi = ||y_Di-yhat_D,mi||_F²

G_D,S   = 1-E_D,S/E_D,P
```

```
T_C   = G_C
T_D   = max(G_D,S, G_D,R)
T_any = max(T_C,T_D)
p_any = #{a:T_any,a >= T_any,observed}/432
p_C   = #{a:T_any,a >= T_C,observed}/432
```

# Proposal: where does row-order-invariant Oxford longitudinal identity reside?

## Scientific question, hypothesis, and advance

For the 11 Oxford NCR18650BD specimens with paired beginning-of-life (BoL) and ordinal middle-of-life (MoL) real-impedance measurements at nominal 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC, is any reproducible longitudinal identity in the unordered empirical `ReZ_Ohm` distributions:

1. carried only by the quantile profile common to all three SOCs;
2. still present in orthogonal SOC-differential quantile contrasts after that common profile is removed;
3. shared by both components; or
4. absent or too unstable to distinguish?

This is a substantive child of `candidate-ac6512cd6c91927f19f0d56d`. The parent repairs unsupported source-row/frequency alignment by independently sorting every specimen-stage-SOC table, but its primary representation is only the two-dimensional SOC-contrast profile. It therefore cannot tell whether failure after projection means no longitudinal identity or whether identity was concentrated in the discarded SOC-common profile. Conversely, differential support is scientifically stronger than unseparated support because a stage-wide or cell-wide common shift cannot create it. The child changes the estimand and conclusion space: it makes the discarded common profile an explicit outcome, compares it with the orthogonal differential profile under identical folds and relinkings, and controls selection across the two components.

The primary hypothesis is **SOC-differential distributional identity**: after fold-local removal of documented protocol and blockwise normalization, correctly linked BoL SOC-differential quantile profiles reduce held-specimen MoL directional loss by at least 10% versus protocol-only prediction, survive familywise calibration against all common/differential models over all 432 admissible within-protocol relinkings, and are broad and tail-robust.

The mutually interpretable component hypothesis is **SOC-common distributional identity**, evaluated by the same margin, held specimens, relinkings, uncertainty, and robustness gates. “Common-carried” requires common support and differential adversity; common support alone is not enough. A raw-ohm companion asks whether the same attribution holds when magnitude is retained, but cannot rescue a failed primary scale-free claim.

## Supported evidence and unresolved claim

The inspected Oxford README supports 12 NCA/graphite NCR18650BD 3 Ah cells, a 24 degC chamber setpoint, four schedule/rate groups, and EIS at supplied BoL and MoL checkpoints and 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC. It reports 100 mA peak-to-peak excitation from 5 kHz to 10 mHz at six points per decade. The configured EIS ZIP has complete paired coverage for 11 of those Group 1-4 cells.

Native export job `job-caee1e9fb0738c866b29bb5f` requested the exact 66 containers and completed in 11.97 s. The strongest evidence-supported claim is therefore that a complete 11-cell, 66-table, 2,310-row `ReZ_Ohm` array exists and can be transformed exactly invariantly to arbitrary within-table row permutations. The archive and README do not establish per-row frequency, acquisition order, row spacing, equal frequency coverage across tables, repeatability, or a shared physical-age definition of MoL.

A separate low-dimensional conformal fit did not improve on scalar differential persistence. - Group 2, C/4, one cycling day plus five calendar days: `G2_C3,G2_C4,G2_C8`;

`group,cell_id,specimen_key,stage,SOC_label_pct,source_row_index,ReZ_Ohm,channel2_raw,cycling_rate_C,cycling_block_days,calendar_block_days,periodicity_class`.

Require 66 canonical tables, 2,310 rows, 11 specimen keys, two stages, three SOC tables per specimen-stage, and 35 values per table. The source table key is `(group,cell_id,stage,SOC_label_pct)`. Never join BoL to MoL on `source_row_index`. After independent tablewise sorting, `quantile_rank=1..35` is a derived empirical-rank coordinate only.

SOC is supplied nominal metadata, not independently validated physical SOC, coulomb-counted SOC, or a BMS estimate. Current sign, charge return, capacity normalization, equilibration, measurement order, repeat spectra, exact frequency support, and log-frequency weights are unavailable.

## Orthogonal row-order-invariant representation

For specimen `i`, stage `t`, SOC `s`, define the equal-mass empirical measure

`mu_its = (1/35) sum_j delta[ReZ_Ohm_itsj]`.

Sort independently within every table. Let `q_its,k` be order statistic `k`, `p_k=(k-0.5)/35`, and let `Q_it` be the 3-by-35 matrix in SOC order 20, 50, 80 and increasing empirical rank. Define the orthonormal Helmert matrix by rows

`u=(1,1,1)/sqrt(3)`, `h_L=(-1,0,1)/sqrt(2)`, and `h_Q=(1,-2,1)/sqrt(6)`.

The exact decomposition is:

- SOC-common profile: `C_it = u Q_it`, shape 1-by-35;
- SOC-differential profile: `D_it = H Q_it`, shape 2-by-35, where `H` has rows `h_L,h_Q`;
- reconstruction: `Q_it = u' C_it + H' D_it`;
- energy identity: `||Q_it||_F^2 = ||C_it||_F^2 + ||D_it||_F^2`.

`C/sqrt(3)` is the equal-SOC average empirical quantile function. `D` contains monotonic-across-SOC and curvature-across-SOC contrasts at equal empirical ranks. It is not itself an impedance spectrum or a pair of probability quantile functions.

Arbitrary independent permutations of the 35 source rows leave `Q,C,D`, predictions, and losses unchanged. Adding the same profile to all three SOC rows changes only `C`; `D` is exactly unchanged. Orthogonal re-expression of the two contrast axes preserves scalar/Frobenius results and transforms the learned rotation covariantly. These properties are unit-tested. The representation is not invariant to changed frequency coverage, unequal inclusion weights, SOC-specific calibration, or nonlinear measurement distortion.

## Specimen-held-out protocol adjustment

Use 11 leave-one-specimen-out outer folds. Code `r=+1/-1` for C/2/C/4, `p=+1/-1` for short/long periodicity, and include `rp`. In every fold and separately for BoL/MoL and `C/D`, standardize nonconstant nuisance columns on training specimens and fit multi-output ridge with an unpenalized intercept and fixed `alpha=1`. Subtract the training fit from training profiles and the training-derived prediction from the held profile. These terms adjust documented protocol; they are not causal effects.

Held MoL enters only its outcome and loss. A fold is unstable if a required training or held residual norm is at most 1% of the corresponding training median unadjusted norm. Any primary-fold failure makes the affected component inconclusive. Repeat 0.5% and 2% gates as sensitivities.

Transport fits give each of four documented groups equal total weight; cells divide their group's weight. Require at least six independent within-group specimen contrasts in every outer training set, finite denominators, model rank as specified, and condition number at most `1e8`.

## Primary scale-free experiment: matched P, S, and R

Normalize common and differential nuisance residuals separately within each specimen-stage:

`x_C=C_BoL,res/||C_BoL,res||`, `y_C=C_MoL,res/||C_MoL,res||`,

`x_D=D_BoL,res/||D_BoL,res||_F`, `y_D=D_MoL,res/||D_MoL,res||_F`.

This equalizes the two scientific blocks without treating 35 ranks or two contrast rows as independent specimens. It removes each block's magnitude but not its empirical-quantile direction.

Fit the following nested competitors on exactly the same training specimens, inputs, and outcomes:

- **P, protocol only:** predict zero residual in both blocks; held losses are exactly one.
- **S, simple orthogonal persistence:** `yhat_C=b_C x_C`; `yhat_D=b_D x_D`. It estimates one scalar per prespecified orthogonal block and directly tests whether common and differential directions persist.
- **R, learned orthogonal transport:** `yhat_C=b_C x_C`; `yhat_D=b_D x_D+c Jx_D`, where `J=[[0,-1],[1,0]]` acts on the two SOC-contrast rows. Report differential amplitude `a_D=sqrt(b_D^2+c^2)` and angle `theta=atan2(c,b_D)`.

S is the simple linked baseline; R is the scientifically substantive alternative on the same targets and folds. R adds only a coherent rotation between linear and curvature SOC dependence. It can reveal redistribution that scalar persistence loses, but it cannot exploit arbitrary rank-specific coefficients or let the common profile masquerade as a differential signal. Select `W_D` as S or R by larger observed differential gain, choosing S on a tie. No selection occurs for the common component because S and R share the same common prediction.

For held cell `i`, use

`L_C,mi=||y_Ci-yhat_C,mi||^2`, `L_D,mi=||y_Di-yhat_D,mi||_F^2`.

Let `E` be the unweighted mean over the 11 held cells and define

`G_C=1-E_C,S/E_C,P`, `G_D,S=1-E_D,S/E_D,P`, `G_D,R=1-E_D,R/E_D,P`, and `Delta_rot=1-E_D,R/E_D,S`.

Also report the block-balanced joint loss `E_joint,m=(E_C,m+E_D,m)/2`, all held predictions and losses, group-specific gains, fold coefficients, norm gates, and reconstructed centered three-SOC predictions `H' Dhat`. The common and differential component gains, not the joint average, determine attribution.

## Raw-ohm companion

Repeat P/S/R on unnormalized nuisance residuals. Within each outer fold, divide common and differential coordinate losses by their respective training-MoL residual mean square, so the two blocks are reportable on comparable fold-local scales without using held outcomes. Fit coefficients on raw residuals with the same equal-group weights. Report unscaled RMSE in ohms as well.

This companion distinguishes persistence of magnitude-bearing empirical distributions from scale-free profile direction. It has its own 432-allocation familywise calibration and uncertainty, but is secondary and non-rescuing: raw support with primary adversity warrants only an amplitude-sensitive association vulnerable to cell/fixture/contact persistence. Primary support with raw adversity means relative distributional geometry persists without material absolute prediction.

## All 432 relinkings, multiplicity, and hierarchy

Enumerate exactly `2! * 3! * 3! * 3! = 432` allocations, including identity. Within each documented group, assign each recipient one donor's complete BoL bundle: all three SOC tables and all 35 values. Keep recipient protocol and MoL fixed. Rerun sorting, nuisance fits, normalization or raw scaling, all 11 outer folds, coefficient fitting, winner selection, and gates. P must remain invariant. Never permute SOCs, ranks, or rows separately.

For the primary track define for every allocation

`T_C=G_C`, `T_D=max(G_D,S,G_D,R)`, and `T_any=max(T_C,T_D)`.

The omnibus exact conditional tail fraction is `p_any=#{T_any,a >= T_any,obs}/432`. Componentwise familywise fractions are `p_C=#{T_any,a >= T_C,obs}/432` and `p_D=#{T_any,a >= T_D,obs}/432`. Thus component claims account simultaneously for choosing common versus differential and S versus R. First require `p_any<=0.05`; then adjudicate components using `p_C` and `p_D`. Test `Delta_rot` only if differential identity is already supportive, using its exact upper-tail fraction across the same allocations. This closed hierarchy prevents rotation or a secondary raw result from manufacturing primary identity. Run an independent analogous max family for raw-ohm results and label it secondary.

These fractions are exact for the enumerated conditional no-linkage reference set under unverified within-group exchangeability. They are not treatment-randomization p-values or population probabilities.

## Uncertainty, breadth, deletion, and tail sensitivity

Using `numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(20260923))`, draw 10,000 group-stratified specimen resamples of sizes 2/3/3/3. Apply common resample multiplicities to the frozen outer-loss tuples for P/S/R and report percentile stability intervals for every component and joint gain. Refit full-data `b_C,b_D,c` in each resample and report intervals and fit failures. These are observed-cell weighting-stability summaries, not population confidence intervals.

Delete each specimen in turn and rerun the complete observed-linkage outer pipeline, winner selection, and raw companion. Report the 11 aggregate component gains and coefficient paths. Deleted-set relinking fractions are diagnostics, not required.

Tail sensitivity is scientifically central because an empirical Wasserstein geometry gives every order statistic equal mass while the acquisition frequency and weighting semantics are unavailable. Freeze these analyses:

1. full 35 ranks is primary;
2. trim the lowest and highest one order statistic from every table (33 ranks);
3. trim the lowest and highest three from every table (29 ranks);
4. replace the 35 ranks by seven prespecified consecutive five-rank means;
5. winsorize ranks 1-3 and 33-35 to ranks 4 and 32, respectively;
6. report loss-reduction numerators separately for lower ranks 1-6, center 7-29, and upper ranks 30-35, with no rank treated as an independent replicate.

Rerun all 432 relinkings for items 2-5. A full-rank signal that disappears or reverses under trimming/winsorization is classified tail-dependent and inconclusive for a broad distributional fingerprint, not discarded as an outlier result. A center-adverse but tail-supportive pattern may motivate a separately registered tail study; it does not satisfy this proposal.

Other frozen sensitivities are nuisance ridge `alpha in {0.1,10}`, additive nuisance `[r,p]`, equal-cell transport weighting, residual gates 0.5% and 2%, independent positive BoL/MoL multipliers in `{0.1,10}`, an alternate orthonormal basis for the differential plane, and at least 1,000 seeded independent source-row shuffles. The primary directional result must be invariant to stage multipliers and row shuffles to numerical tolerance; raw gains must be equivariant to a common positive unit change and row-invariant. The parent's SOC-differential-only result is reproduced as a correspondence check but cannot rescue this joint multiplicity-controlled analysis.

## Frozen decision rules

The 10% gain is a prespecified dataset-scale materiality threshold, not validated engineering utility. Report 5% and 20% thresholds descriptively without changing classification.

A component (`C` common or selected `D` differential) is **supportive** only if:

- `p_any<=0.05`, its familywise `p_component<=0.05`, and observed gain is at least 0.10;
- its 95% stratified stability lower bound is above zero;
- it beats P in at least 9/11 held specimens;
- every specimen-deletion aggregate gain is positive and at least 9/11 deletion gains are at least 0.10;
- no protocol-group gain is at or below -0.10;
- all norm, rank, denominator, and conditioning gates pass;
- trim-one, trim-three, seven-bin, and winsorized analyses retain gain at least 0.10, positive stability, no adverse group, and no sign reversal; and
- nuisance, weighting, row-shuffle, scale, and basis checks do not reverse the conclusion.

A component is **adverse for the 10% margin** only if its observed selected gain is below 0.10, stability upper bound is below 0.10, familywise tail fraction exceeds 0.05, the selected model beats P in at most 7/11 cells, no group has stable multiplicity-compatible 0.10 gain, all validity gates pass, and no registered row-invariant sensitivity is supportive. Every other valid pattern is **inconclusive**, including exactly 8/11 improved cells, tail dependence, deletion dependence, margin-spanning stability, group opposition, relinking/stability disagreement, or failed identifiability gates.

The primary conclusion is assigned deterministically:

- **common-carried:** common supportive and differential adverse;
- **differential-survives:** differential supportive and common adverse;
- **shared:** both supportive;
- **absent at the registered margin:** both adverse;
- **unstable/inconclusive:** every other combination, with failed gates named.

“Differential-survives” and “shared” warrant the narrow statement that a correctly linked BoL SOC-differential empirical-quantile direction predicts ordinal-MoL differential direction beyond documented protocol in these specimens. “Common-carried” warrants only the analogous statement about the across-SOC average quantile direction and explicitly says the SOC-specific evidence is adverse. Rotation is supportive only if R is selected, `Delta_rot>=0.10`, its gated exact tail fraction is at most 0.05, R beats S in at least 9/11 cells and every deletion aggregate, and the stability interval for `c` excludes zero with one sign across deletions. `theta` remains an electrical distribution descriptor, not a mechanism.

Apply the same component rules to the raw companion but label outcomes `raw-common`, `raw-differential`, `raw-shared`, `raw-absent`, or `raw-inconclusive`. They qualify rather than change the primary result.

Support does not prove a shared frequency grid, electrochemical mechanism, causal path dependence, or transfer to other cells. Adversity does not reject a frequency-localized fingerprint because sorting deliberately discards frequency identity.

## Method alternatives and selection record

P is the no-linkage baseline. S is the simplest scientifically adequate linked model: one scalar for the common profile and one for the complete differential plane. R is matched to the same inputs, folds, outcomes, weights, and losses and adds only coherent rotation between prespecified linear- and curvature-SOC axes. R could reveal longitudinal redistribution among SOC contrasts that S necessarily loses. The bounded screen did not show a predictive advantage for rotation, so R is retained for falsification rather than presumed superior.

The full 35-rank quantile representation is selected because it preserves all admitted `ReZ_Ohm` distribution information and has canonical one-dimensional equal-mass transport geometry. Seven rank bins lose within-bin shape but provide a lower-variance comparator. Trimming and winsorization are mandatory because the preliminary gain changed materially at the tails.

A full 3-by-3 learned cross-mode map was considered. It could let BoL common variation predict MoL differential variation, but that would undermine the attribution question by allowing common mode to masquerade as differential survival and is too flexible for seven within-group specimen contrasts. Revisit it only after the direct component claims are resolved or with a larger cohort. Arbitrary 70-by-70 maps, kernels, and neural encoders are deferred because 11 specimens cannot distinguish their extra predictive flexibility from specimen idiosyncrasy; a larger external cohort or reproducible residual nonlinearity would justify reconsideration. Equivalent-circuit, DRT, and frequency-localized alternatives require authoritative frequency and complex-impedance semantics not present in the admitted tables. CPU is selected for these tiny linear fits; GPU availability is irrelevant, not a scientific merit judgment.

## Deliverable and compute budget

Completion requires newly fitting all 11 outer folds for primary and raw P/S/R; all 432 joint whole-BoL-bundle relinkings for the primary, raw, trim-one, trim-three, seven-bin, and winsorized analyses; 10,000 stratified stability resamples and coefficient refits; 11 specimen deletions; every registered nuisance, weighting, gate, scale, basis, and row-shuffle check; and the deterministic attribution trace.

Required outputs are:

- source/audit: `source_audit.json`, `member_manifest.csv`, `duplicate_audit.json`, `normalized_eis.parquet`;
- representation: `empirical_quantiles.parquet`, `orthogonal_profiles.parquet`, `orthogonality_audit.json`, `row_permutation_audit.json`;
- primary: `directional_outer_predictions.parquet`, `directional_outer_losses.csv`, `directional_fits.csv`, `directional_relinkings.parquet`;
- raw: `raw_outer_predictions.parquet`, `raw_outer_losses.csv`, `raw_fits.csv`, `raw_relinkings.parquet`;
- robustness: `stability.parquet`, `coefficient_stability.parquet`, `deletion_metrics.csv`, `tail_metrics.csv`, `sensitivity_metrics.csv`;
- synthesis: `metrics.json` and `conclusion.json`, including sentence-to-field provenance and every failed gate.

Use 8 CPUs, 32 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, deterministic BLAS/thread settings, and allocation-level parallelism. The native export measured 11.97 s; bounded Python formulations with all 432 allocations measured under 20 s per track in discovery. The complete nested sensitivity/resampling workload is estimated at 60-150 CPU minutes and fits the 7,200-second reference-execution and 28,800-second solver envelopes when parallelized and checkpointed every 36 allocations. These measurements establish feasibility only; they are not completion of the future experiment.

## Verification and evidence boundaries

The verifier can recompute source hashes, member/internal-variable selection, duplicate equality, counts, independent sorting, orthogonal reconstruction and energy identities, absence of source-row joins, specimen splits, nuisance residualization, P/S/R fits, losses, all 432 relinkings, max-family fractions, stability summaries, deletions, tail analyses, invariance tests, and the deterministic conclusion. It must accept supportive, adverse, or inconclusive outcomes when the computed gates warrant them and reject correct calculations paired with unsupported interpretation.

Scientific adjudication remains necessary for equal weighting of the 35 acquired values, whether frequency coverage was identical, within-group exchangeability, the 10% materiality margin, SOC accuracy/equilibration, and MoL comparability. Stronger frequency-resolved, fixture-separated, mechanistic, causal, population, or deployment claims require authoritative per-row frequency and complex-impedance fields, acquisition order and repeat spectra, contact/fixture controls, common-horizon capacity or throughput records, assignment provenance, expert review, and an independent prospective cohort.

## Inspected provenance

Inspected on 2026-09-23: `datasets/README.md`; the Oxford dataset guide, metadata, full catalog entry, source ZIP member inventory, and full acquisition README; `binding-template.json`; `inputs.json`; research-ambition and method/compute guidance; expert-seed availability; assigned parent `candidate-ac6512cd6c91927f19f0d56d`; native export job `job-caee1e9fb0738c866b29bb5f`; and bounded common/differential formulation calculations. Raj et al. (2020) full paper and supplementary methods were not acquired and are not claimed read.

# Li2025 partial-discharge early-stop experiment

## Objective

Conduct the complete, newly fitted investigation frozen below. Test, without assuming a favorable answer, whether information available during the first part of a fresh Li2025 0.1C discharge improves a strictly prospective two-RPT forecast for a wholly held specimen and retains most of the information in the completed curve.

The unresolved hypothesis is:

> For a completely held Li2025 specimen in one of the five represented protocol families, fresh innovation observed by q/Ci0 = 0.30 contains practically important information about measured state two RPTs later beyond resolved history and expected sibling progression, and retains most of the gain of a fair completed-curve oracle.

The existing audit supports only feasibility: all 511 curves, all 275 nominal capacity forecast origins, and all 107 nominal resistance origins reach q/Ci0 = 0.30 and causal 3.90 V. No endpoint model has yet been fitted. You must fit the models, quantify uncertainty, run the controls, and derive the verdict. A negative or inconclusive result is a valid completion.

This is an observational, protocol-conditional diagnostic association study. “Causal” below describes one-sided filtering and the acquisition clock, not a causal treatment effect.

## Inputs and exact binding

Use only these read-only runtime inputs for the analysis:

- `/data/d740a0fd11-li-full.zip`, SHA-256 `51e37532a759e1a3bed1f05dd17b682eca0eb38c132c37481c534baf4526e42c`, 835,141,024 bytes, 3,993 members.
- `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`, SHA-256 `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`.

All configured sources remain mounted, but no other dataset is part of the estimand. Do not modify anything under `/data`.

The catalog contains 1,801 Li2025 table records: 511 discharge, 249 charge, and 40 extracted-summary tables. Use only the 511 discharge and 40 summary members.

Summary-member pattern:

`SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/{short} - cell {cell} ({10|25|40}degC) - Extracted Data.csv`

Representative catalog table `datasets/Li2025/table-92783194d5d74ccc.json` binds:

`SimSave/InputData/Expt 1 - Si-based Degradation/Expt 1 - cell A (10degC) - Extracted Data.csv`

Required summary columns, after stripping header whitespace, are:

`""` (integer RPT), `Ageing Sets`, `Ageing Cycles`, `Age set start date`, `Age set end date`, `RPT start date`, `Days of degradation`, `Age set average temperature (degC)`, `Charge Throughput (A.h)`, `Energy Throughput (W.h)`, `C/10 Capacity (mA.h)`, `C/2 Capacity (mA.h)`, `0.1s Resistance (Ohms)`, `Mean_R (Ohms)`, `R_80to48_SOC (Ohms)`, and `R_100SOC (Ohms)`.

Discharge-member pattern:

`SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/0.1C Voltage Curves/cell {cell}/{short} - cell {cell} - RPT{rpt} - 0.1C discharge data.csv`

Representative catalog table `datasets/Li2025/table-48e85d15b6c70efa.json` binds:

`SimSave/InputData/Expt 1 - Si-based Degradation/0.1C Voltage Curves/cell A/Expt 1 - cell A - RPT0 - 0.1C discharge data.csv`

Required discharge columns are `Time (s)`, `Voltage (V)`, `Current (mA)`, `Charge (mA.h)`, and `Temperature (degC)`.

Join one-to-one on exact experiment directory, cell letter, and integer RPT parsed independently from each member and summary. The specimen key is `experiment directory|cell letter`; a cell letter alone is not unique. Treat E1–E5 as five fixed opaque protocol-family strata, not mechanisms or independent cohorts. Parse `RPT start date` day-first. Require unique increasing dates and consecutive RPT indices.

Retain finite discharge rows with -550 <= current <= -450 mA, preserving the negative sign. Subtract the first retained time and charge values. Require monotone time and acquired charge and verify charge against the trapezoidal integral of -current over time divided by 3600. Abort on source hash, catalog/member count, schema, key, chronology, sign, unit, monotonicity, or uniqueness failure. `Charge (mA.h)` is a phase-local coulomb counter, not independent SOC truth.

## Population, clocks, and labels

There are 40 specimens and 511 joined RPT states dated 2020-06-26 through 2021-07-22. RPT0 curves establish previously resolved Ci0 and are never scored.

At each RPT t >= 1, the q-boundary decision clock is the first acquired-charge sample at or above b*Ci0, linearly interpolated to the exact boundary. The primary b is 0.30. The fixed-voltage clock is the first row where a trailing causal mean of the latest 101 voltage rows is at or below the threshold; use an expanding trailing mean for the first 100 rows. Centered smoothing is prohibited.

Primary labels are future absolute measured state:

- capacity: YC_it = C_i,t+2 / C_i0, where C is measured `C/10 Capacity (mA.h)`;
- resistance: YR_it = log(R_i,t+2 / R_i0), where R is finite positive scheduled `Mean_R (Ohms)`.

The paired nominal score sets must contain exactly 275 capacity and 107 resistance origins. They require at least six earlier same-family eligible training rows from at least four other specimens. The conservative sets enforce the originally written 12-row rule and must contain exactly 240 capacity and 67 resistance origins; E4 resistance is absent there. Whenever fewer than 12 training rows or fewer than two inner-validation specimens are available, use the frozen one-component/default-penalty fit. Every supportive claim must pass on both sets.

Secondary comparability labels are (C_i,t+2-C_it)/C_i0 and log(R_i,t+2/R_it). Current C_it and R_it may be used only after prediction to construct labels, never by a partial model.

For every scored row, remove the complete held specimen from fitting, scaling, expected-prefix construction, registration, components, and tuning. A supervised training row is eligible only when it is in the same family and its t+2 target date is strictly earlier than the held row’s RPT-t date; exclude same-day targets. Inner folds repeat both specimen and target-resolution boundaries. Repeated RPT rows are not independent specimens.

At the partial decision clock, current-RPT inputs are limited to observed-prefix elapsed time, voltage, signed current, phase-local charge, temperature, known specimen/family/RPT identity, nominal temperature, RPT start date, and previously resolved RPT0 capacity. Summary histories end at t-1. Prohibit current C/10 capacity, every resistance field, completed active span, end voltage, full duration, any t+1/t+2 field, and current cumulative cycles/days/throughput.

## Frozen representations

For q30, use first online downward crossings of causal-smoothed 4.05, 4.00, 3.95, and 3.90 V, expressed as q/Ci0. Append q/Ci0 = 0 and 0.30, construct a monotone piecewise-linear warp to equally spaced canonical knots, evaluate voltage at 61 canonical coordinates, and remove fixed-voltage knot values before fitting. Add prefix elapsed time, final voltage, median and variation of signed current and temperature, charge-integral discrepancy, and voltage/noise QA flags. Do not normalize by the current curve’s completed span.

For v39, stop at the first causal-smoothed 3.90 V crossing. Include q/Ci0 at the landmarks and total q/Ci0 to 3.90 V, with the analogous registered inverse path. q30 fixes charge and permits endpoint voltage to vary; v39 fixes voltage and permits acquired charge/time to vary.

For both clocks, form the no-new-current expected prefix from that held specimen’s t-1 curve plus family-specific one-RPT prefix increments from other specimens whose increment endpoint date is strictly earlier than the row’s decision date. Retain static RPT0 shape and the t-1 prefix. Fit expected maps, affine corrections, warps, scaling, residualization, FPCA, and tuning on eligible training data only. Fresh innovations equal observed minus expected prefix.

Repeat primary extraction with trailing windows 1, 101, and 501. Fit q10/q20/q40 and v4.0/v3.8 as multiplicity-adjusted secondary acquisition-curve boundaries.

The fair full-curve oracle sees complete t curve and final span, but not current summary capacity or resistance. Preserve primary, shifted-dense, sparse-landmark, smoothing, and unregistered-own-span registrations. The completed-RPT oracle adds current completed span and summary state, is operationally unavailable at the early clock, and can never support an early-stop claim.

## Matched models and controls

Use identical endpoint rows, folds, row weights, and target scales:

- P0: last resolved specimen outcome/state, falling back to earlier-resolved family/temperature and family medians.
- B: ridge plus fixed cubic splines on history through t-1: prior normalized capacities and changes/slopes, prior finite resistance and staleness, RPT, nominal temperature, calendar ordinal, prior cumulative cycles/days/charge/energy, backward exposure increments, prior interval temperature, and missing-history indicators.
- H: B plus the no-new-current expected prefix.
- S30/S39: H plus structured fresh landmark shifts, interval signed/absolute area and RMS, interval slopes and derivative extrema, endpoint voltage or charge-to-threshold, elapsed time, current, and temperature. Select ridge penalties in safe inner folds.
- F30/F39: H plus full fresh phase displacement and registered-amplitude innovation. Residualize each channel against B using training data, reduce channels separately to 1–6 training-only FPCA components, and fit a rank-bounded PLS/ridge correction to H residuals.
- O-full: corresponding structured and functional complete-curve models under every frozen registration.
- O-RPT: O-full plus current completed span and summary state.

F is primary because it retains distributed correlated deformation; S is the matched lower-variance, interpretable alternative. If only F improves or S and F signs disagree, evidence is not robust.

Run dimension-matched same-family/RPT/date sibling-swap prefixes, held-specimen lagged prefix, within-specimen time permutation, and target-trajectory shuffle controls. Run an acquisition-only elapsed-time/current/temperature control without voltage morphology.

## Metrics and uncertainty

Average absolute error first over RPTs within specimen, then specimens within family, then equally over the five fixed families. Also report RMSE, reconstructed absolute-state error, calibration coverage and width, row/training counts, per-family effects, and capacity on resistance-complete rows.

For boundary b, independently compute:

- prognostic gain Gb = 1 - M_F(b)/M_H;
- excess loss Db = (M_F(b)-M_O)/M_H;
- when M_H-M_O > 0, retained gain rho_b = (M_H-M_F(b))/(M_H-M_O), without clipping.

Use 10,000 paired trajectory bootstrap replicates resampling specimens within each fixed family and a family-RPT-stage block bootstrap. Use the wider interval for interpretation. These intervals condition on the five families and do not describe a family superpopulation. Use max-statistic bootstrap adjustment over nested secondary boundaries.

## Deterministic interpretation

Support partial prognostic information for an endpoint only when all conditions hold:

1. F30 has point G30 >= 0.10 and 95% lower bound > 0 on nominal and conservative sets.
2. F39 has point gain >= 0.10 and lower bound > 0; S30 and S39 agree in sign; windows 1/101/501 do not reverse the result.
3. At least four of five family effects are positive, no family worsens by more than 5%, and every leave-one-specimen-out aggregate contrast is positive.
4. F30/F39 beat B, H, P0, acquisition-only, sibling-swap, lag, permutation, and target-shuffle controls.
5. No prohibited field enters a partial artifact.

Support early-stop sufficiency only after that gate, and only when the upper 95% bound of D30 is below 0.05 under every full registration and rho30 >= 0.80 whenever O-full gains at least 0.05 over H. Capacity-only or resistance-only conclusions are allowed. A joint monitoring claim requires both endpoints.

An upper 95% bound for G30 below 0.10 is adverse evidence against a practically important prefix effect. An upper bound <= 0 supports no detectable benefit or harm. If O-full improves but partial models do not, conclude that detectable information lies in the later/lower-voltage segment or completed span. If partial models improve but fail equivalence, conclude useful but insufficient. If neither partial nor full oracle improves, conclude no detectable fresh-morphology benefit over history at this resolution. Fixed-charge/fixed-voltage disagreement is coordinate-sensitive. Threshold overlap, S/F disagreement, retained placebo signal, unstable family influence, poor calibration, nominal/conservative disagreement, or resistance-definition conflict is inconclusive.

Do not describe voltage morphology as an ageing mechanism. Do not claim that interruption is safe, identify LLI/LAM/plating/SEI, infer causality, or transport beyond the five same-lineage families.

# Can the first 30% of a low-rate discharge replace waiting for the completed diagnostic curve?

## Scientific decision and substantive advance

The parent asks whether a newly completed Li2025 0.1C discharge curve contains specimen-specific information about measured capacity and resistance two RPTs later, and whether that information is robust to phase/amplitude registration. It does not answer the acquisition decision because its predictors use the completed curve, its final charge span, and contemporaneous summary capacity. A useful association discovered only after an eight-hour discharge may not justify retaining the full test.

This child tests the prospective hypothesis:

> For a completely held Li2025 specimen in an already represented experimental family, the fresh innovation observed by the time discharge reaches (q/C_{i0}=0.30) contains practically important two-RPT prognostic information beyond all resolved history and expected sibling progression, and retains most of the information available from the completed curve.

The primary stop is fixed before seeing any current curve: 30% of that specimen's already resolved RPT0 C/10 capacity. A causal 3.90 V stop is a prespecified acquisition-coordinate check. Nested 10%, 20%, 40%, 4.00 V, and 3.80 V stops estimate an information-versus-time curve but cannot replace the primary test. The experiment distinguishes three decisions: whether a prefix has any prognostic value, whether it is sufficient to stop early, and whether useful information appears only in the lower-voltage remainder.

This is a substantive change in information time, not a smaller reproduction of the parent. The prefix models are forbidden from using contemporaneous completed capacity, resistance, final span, end voltage, full duration, or own-span normalization. A favorable result could justify a roughly three-hour diagnostic read rather than waiting for the full discharge in these protocols. It would not show that interrupting the physical RPT is safe, because recharge, downstream test order, and subsequent cell conditioning are not recorded as interventions.

## Evidence supported now and unresolved claim

The strongest supported claim is feasibility. A managed two-CPU audit read every one of 511 bound discharge curves. Every curve, all 275 nominal parent capacity rows, and all 107 nominal parent resistance rows reach each prespecified stop. On capacity/resistance rows respectively:

| Online stop | Available | Median elapsed hours | 95th-percentile hours | Median fraction of eventual span |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (q/C_{i0}=0.10) | 275/275; 107/107 | 0.971; 0.971 | 0.979; 0.979 | .115; .117 |
| (q/C_{i0}=0.20) | 275/275; 107/107 | 1.943; 1.943 | 1.958; 1.957 | .230; .233 |
| **(q/C_{i0}=0.30)** | **275/275; 107/107** | **2.914; 2.914** | **2.936; 2.935** | **.345; .350** |
| (q/C_{i0}=0.40) | 275/275; 107/107 | 3.885; 3.885 | 3.915; 3.914 | .460; .466 |
| causal 4.00 V | 275/275; 107/107 | 1.641; 1.601 | 1.796; 1.785 | .195; .195 |
| **causal 3.90 V** | **275/275; 107/107** | **2.480; 2.443** | **2.655; 2.612** | **.294; .294** |
| causal 3.80 V | 275/275; 107/107 | 3.456; 3.427 | 3.611; 3.580 | .407; .408 |

The completed curve lasts a median 8.447 h on capacity rows and 8.354 h on resistance rows. The primary stop therefore precedes completion by about 5.53 and 5.44 h at the median. Across all 511 curves, it ends at median 3.858 V (range 3.531–3.881 V); every causal 3.90 V crossing occurs by (q/C_{i0}=0.2823). Full span ranges from 0.44945 to 1.00000 (C_{i0}), so all fixed-charge stops are observed, although 40% approaches the shortest curve's end.

These numbers establish availability and burden only. No endpoint model has been fitted. The unresolved claims are whether the prefix improves a strict held-specimen forecast, whether a structured and a learned representation agree, whether the improvement survives fixed-charge versus fixed-voltage stopping, and whether it is statistically equivalent to a completed-curve oracle.

## Specimens, clocks, and outcomes

The specimen key is exact `experiment directory|cell letter`; a letter alone is not unique. E1–E5 are fixed opaque protocol-family strata, not mechanism labels or independent cohorts. The archive has 40 specimens, 511 RPT states, and RPT dates from 2020-06-26 through 2021-07-22.

At RPT (tge1), the decision clock is the first sample satisfying the frozen online stop. The q/C0 stop is permitted because the specimen's measured RPT0 C/10 capacity was resolved before t; it is not prospective at RPT0, and those 40 baseline curves are never scored. The voltage stop is the first point at which a trailing causal mean of the most recent 101 voltage rows is at or below the threshold. An expanding trailing mean is used for the first 100 rows. Centered smoothing is prohibited.

To make the forecast meaningful before current RPT completion, primary outcomes are future absolute state:

- capacity: (Y^C_{it}=C_{i,t+2}/C_{i0}), where C is measured `C/10 Capacity (mA.h)`;
- resistance: (Y^R_{it}=log(R_{i,t+2}/R_{i0})), where R is finite positive scheduled `Mean_R (Ohms)`.

The nominal score sets are frozen to the parent's 275 capacity and 107 resistance rows, so the acquisition comparison is paired. The parent's original changes, ((C_{i,t+2}-C_{it})/C_{i0}) and (log(R_{i,t+2}/R_{it})), are secondary comparability outcomes. Current (C_{it}) and (R_{it}) may be used only after prediction to construct these labels; they never enter a partial model.

A source re-audit found that the reported 275/107 counts correspond exactly to requiring at least six earlier same-family training rows from at least four other specimens, each with target date strictly before the held row's index date. The parent's prose says 12 rows; enforcing that written rule yields 240 capacity and 67 resistance rows and removes E4 resistance. This child preserves the reported nominal sets, uses a frozen one-component/default-penalty fit whenever fewer than 12 rows or two inner validation specimens are available, and requires every supportive claim to agree on the conservative 240/67 subset. Both sets and the discrepancy are machine-reported.

For each scored row, the complete held specimen is absent from fitting, scaling, expected-trajectory construction, registration, components, and tuning. Supervised fitting uses only other same-family rows whose t+2 target date is strictly earlier than the held row's RPT-t date; same-day resolved targets are excluded. Inner folds repeat specimen and target-resolution boundaries. Repeated RPT rows are not independent specimens.

## Exact read-only binding and required fields

The source is:

- `[private path]`
- runtime `/data/d740a0fd11-li-full.zip`
- SHA-256 `51e37532a759e1a3bed1f05dd17b682eca0eb38c132c37481c534baf4526e42c`
- 835,141,024 bytes and 3,993 archive members.

The catalog is:

- `[private path]`
- runtime `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`
- SHA-256 `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`.

Its 1,801 Li2025 table records contain exactly 511 discharge, 249 charge, and 40 extracted-summary tables. The experiment uses the 511 discharge and 40 summary tables only.

Summary members follow
`SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/{short} - cell {cell} ({10|25|40}degC) - Extracted Data.csv`.
Representative catalog table `datasets/Li2025/table-92783194d5d74ccc.json` binds the E1-cell-A member and columns `""` (integer RPT), `Ageing Sets`, `Ageing Cycles`, `Age set start date`, `Age set end date`, `RPT start date`, `Days of degradation`, `Age set average temperature (degC)`, `Charge Throughput (A.h)`, `Energy Throughput (W.h)`, `C/10 Capacity (mA.h)`, `C/2 Capacity (mA.h)`, `0.1s Resistance (Ohms)`, `Mean_R (Ohms)`, `R_80to48_SOC (Ohms)`, and `R_100SOC (Ohms)`.

Discharge members follow
`SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/0.1C Voltage Curves/cell {cell}/{short} - cell {cell} - RPT{rpt} - 0.1C discharge data.csv`.
Representative catalog table `datasets/Li2025/table-48e85d15b6c70efa.json` binds E1-cell-A-RPT0 and columns `Time (s)`, `Voltage (V)`, `Current (mA)`, `Charge (mA.h)`, and `Temperature (degC)`.

Join one-to-one on exact experiment directory, cell, and integer RPT parsed independently from member and summary. Parse `RPT start date` day-first and require unique increasing dates and consecutive RPT indices. Retain finite discharge rows with (-550le Ile-450) mA, preserve the negative current sign, set elapsed time and acquired charge to their value minus the first retained value, and verify charge against (-int I,dt/3600). Abort on source hash, member, schema, key, chronology, sign, monotonic-time/charge, unit, or uniqueness failure. `Charge (mA.h)` is a phase-local coulomb counter, not independent SOC ground truth.

At the decision clock, allowed current-RPT inputs are only the observed prefix's elapsed time, voltage, current, charge, temperature, known specimen/family/RPT identity, nominal temperature, RPT start date, and previously resolved RPT0 capacity. Summary histories end at t-1. Current `C/10 Capacity`, all resistance fields, completed active span, end voltage, full duration, and any t+1/t+2 field are prohibited. Current cumulative cycles/days/throughput are also excluded because their availability relative to the within-RPT curve clock is not independently timestamped.

## Frozen partial representations

The primary q30 prefix ends at the first acquired-charge sample at or above (0.30C_{i0}), with linear interpolation to the exact boundary. It is represented without current-span normalization:

1. **Upper-curve phase:** first online downward crossings of causal-smoothed 4.05, 4.00, 3.95, and 3.90 V, expressed as q/C0. The full audit establishes that 3.90 V is reached by q/C0=.2823 in every curve.
2. **Registered amplitude:** append q/C0=0 and .30 to those ordered landmarks, form the monotone piecewise-linear warp to equally spaced canonical knots, evaluate voltage at 61 canonical coordinates, and remove fixed-voltage knot values before fitting.
3. **Acquisition scalars:** prefix elapsed time, final observed voltage, median and variation of signed current and temperature, charge-integral discrepancy, and voltage/noise QA flags.

The v39 representation stops at the first causal-smoothed 3.90 V crossing. Its phase includes q/C0 at the same landmarks and total q/C0-to-3.90 V; amplitude uses the analogous registered inverse path. Thus fixed-charge and fixed-voltage stopping preserve different information by design: q30 fixes charge and lets endpoint voltage vary, while v39 fixes voltage and lets acquired charge/time vary.

For both, construct the no-new-current expected prefix from the held specimen's t-1 curve plus family-specific one-RPT prefix increments from other specimens whose increment endpoint date is strictly before the row's decision date. Static RPT0 shape and the t-1 prefix are retained. All expected maps, affine corrections, warps, scaling, residualization, FPCA, and tuning are training-only. Fresh phase and amplitude innovations are observed prefix minus expected prefix. Repeat extraction with causal windows 1 and 501 as sensitivity; no future sample is used.

The full-curve oracle preserves the parent's primary, shifted-dense, and sparse landmark registrations, smoothing sensitivity, and unregistered own-span comparator. It uses the same history baseline and held-row rules but may see the complete t curve and final span. It may not see current summary capacity or resistance. A separately labeled completed-RPT oracle adds those summaries and is never used to support an early-stop claim.

## Comparable models

All models use identical endpoint rows, folds, row weights, and target scales.

- **P0:** last resolved outcome/state for the specimen, then earlier-resolved family/temperature and family medians.
- **B:** ridge plus fixed cubic splines on only history resolved through t-1: prior normalized capacities and changes/slopes, prior finite resistances and staleness, RPT, nominal temperature, calendar ordinal, prior cumulative cycles/days/charge/energy, backward exposure increments, prior interval temperature, and missing-history indicators.
- **H:** B plus the no-new-current expected prefix. This retains static curve identity and expected family progression without observing the current prefix.
- **S30/S39:** H plus structured fresh innovations: landmark shifts, interval signed/absolute area and RMS, interval slopes and derivative extrema, endpoint voltage or charge-to-threshold, elapsed time, current, and temperature. Ridge penalties are selected in safe inner folds.
- **F30/F39:** H plus full fresh phase displacement and registered-amplitude innovation. Each channel is residualized against B in training data, reduced separately to 1–6 training-only FPCA components, and entered through rank-bounded PLS/ridge correction to H residuals.
- **O-full:** the corresponding full-curve structured and functional models under all parent registrations; this is the fair information oracle.
- **O-RPT:** O-full plus current completed span and summary state; this is an unavailable operational upper benchmark.

F is primary because it retains distributed, correlated prefix deformation that S discards. S is the equally timed, lower-variance and interpretable alternative. If only F improves, or their signs disagree, evidence is not considered robust. q10/q20/q40 and v4.0/v3.8 repeat S and F to estimate acquisition curves; they are secondary and multiplicity-adjusted.

Dimension-matched negative controls are same-family/RPT/date sibling-swap prefixes, the held specimen's lagged prefix substituted for the current prefix, within-specimen time permutations, and target-trajectory shuffles. An acquisition-only control uses elapsed time/current/temperature without voltage morphology. These determine whether gains reflect specimen-specific voltage information rather than chronology, donor identity, duration, or model flexibility.

## Metrics, uncertainty, and falsification

Average absolute error first across RPTs within specimen, then specimens within family, then equally across the five fixed families. Report MAE, RMSE, reconstructed absolute-state error, calibration coverage/width, row and training counts, per-family effects, and capacity results restricted to resistance-complete rows.

For boundary b, define prognostic gain (G_b=1-M_F(b)/M_H), and excess loss against the fair full oracle (D_b=[M_F(b)-M_O]/M_H). When (M_H-M_O>0), also report retained gain (
ho_b=[M_H-M_F(b)]/[M_H-M_O]), without clipping values outside [0,1]. Use 10,000 paired trajectory bootstraps resampling specimens within fixed family and a family-RPT-stage block bootstrap; interpretation uses the wider interval. Families are fixed, so intervals do not describe a family superpopulation. Control false discovery across the nested secondary boundaries by max-statistic bootstrap.

Support **partial prognostic information** for an endpoint only if:

1. F30 has point (G_{30}ge0.10) and its 95% lower bound exceeds zero on both the nominal and conservative row sets;
2. F39 also has point gain at least .10 with lower bound above zero, S30 and S39 agree in sign, and causal windows 1/101/501 do not reverse the result;
3. at least four of five family effects are positive, no family worsens by more than 5%, and every leave-one-specimen-out aggregate contrast stays positive;
4. F30/F39 beat B, H, P0, acquisition-only, sibling-swap, lag, permutation, and target-shuffle controls; and
5. no prohibited current/full field enters any partial artifact.

Support **early-stop sufficiency** only after that gate and only if the upper 95% bound of (D_{30}) is below .05 under every full registration and (
ho_{30}ge.80) when the full oracle has at least a .05 gain. Capacity-only and resistance-only conclusions are allowed; a joint monitoring claim requires both endpoints.

Adverse evidence against a practically important prefix effect is a 95% upper bound for G30 below .10; an upper bound at or below zero supports no detectable benefit or harm. If O-full improves but F30/F39 do not, conclude that information lies in the later/lower-voltage segment or completed span. If prefixes improve but fail equivalence, conclude that early information is useful but insufficient to replace completion. If neither prefix nor oracle improves, conclude that fresh curve morphology has no detectable benefit over history at this resolution. Fixed-charge/fixed-voltage disagreement means acquisition-coordinate-sensitive evidence. Interval overlap with thresholds, structured/functional disagreement, placebo retention, unstable family influence, poor calibration, nominal/conservative-set disagreement, or resistance-definition conflict is inconclusive.

No result may be described as an ageing mechanism. Phase and amplitude remain registration-dependent electrical summaries. An automatic verifier must accept supportive, adverse, endpoint-specific, full-only, useful-but-insufficient, coordinate-sensitive, and inconclusive outcomes.

## Deliverable, compute, and evidence limits

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted, strictly clocked held-specimen predictions for H, S30/S39, F30/F39, nested boundaries, and both oracles, plus paired uncertainty and a deterministic rule-derived verdict. Completion requires `source_audit.json`, `source_manifest.csv`, `row_gate_audit.json`, `forecast_rows.parquet`, `folds.csv`, `prefix_boundaries.parquet`, `acquisition_burden.csv`, `expected_prefixes.parquet`, `prefix_innovations.parquet`, `registration_artifacts/`, `predictions.parquet`, `metrics.json`, `oracle_comparison.json`, `negative_controls.json`, `uncertainty.parquet`, `influence.csv`, `model_artifacts/`, `environment.json`, `verdict.json`, and `report.md`. Every narrative conclusion must cite computed fields.

The solver budget is 8 CPU cores, 32 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, and 7,200 seconds, within the configured 16-CPU, 262,144-MiB, 28,800-second envelope. The full-source audit took 123.28 s on two managed CPUs and 8 GiB; this establishes extraction feasibility, not model results. The low-rank nested fits and bootstraps are CPU-suitable.

The verifier can recompute source hashes, catalog/member/schema counts, joins, clocks, stops, burden, prohibited-field lists, folds, transformations, predictions, losses, bootstrap intervals, controls, and rule-to-verdict mapping. It should explicitly reject a numerically correct submission that claims early sufficiency without oracle equivalence, claims a mechanism from voltage morphology, or interprets an interval-crossing result as support.

It cannot establish that an interrupted RPT leaves subsequent cell state unchanged, that voltage features identify LLI, LAM, plating, SEI, or another microscopic mechanism, or that the result transports beyond these five fixed same-lineage families. Those stronger conclusions require a randomized interrupted-versus-completed RPT experiment, electrochemical expert review, independent half-cell/post-mortem evidence, and an external cohort. Li/Kirkaldy share source lineage and are not independent validation. No unavailable paper text or supplementary methods are claimed inspected.

Test whether the current state-IX acquisition adds held-cell information about a persistent change or bend in measured discharge-capacity fade. The unresolved hypothesis is that the joint current update in the observed V-to-IX acquisition clock and IX-minus-V impedance contrast improves prediction of either persistence P or bend C beyond every observation available before those updates, in both a direct scalar ridge and a functional residual-trajectory ridge. The direct family fits each rung to standardized (M,C). The functional family fits each rung to six residual-trajectory coefficients and reconstructs 20 capacities. Select alpha separately by branch and outer fold with inner leave-one-training-cell-out predictions scored with equal cell weight. No held-cell outcome may affect selection. Functional fits reveal whether scalar gain is a stable shift/bend or only local trajectory displacement.

## Evaluation, uncertainty, and claims

Use leave-one-cell-out outer evaluation and equal total training weight per cell. For outcome Y, model m, comparator n compute per-cell `delta_i=MAE_i(n,Y)-MAE_i(m,Y)`. Publish equal-cell mean, ordered eight-vector, median, range, positive count, and eight leave-one-cell-out means. Also publish three family means and family-balanced mean, never as a substitute for cell vectors.

Publish 95% studentized t7 intervals, all 256 cell-level sign assignments, and leave-one-cell jackknife. For the four primary mature ADX-vs-A1 contrasts (P/C, direct/functional), publish one simultaneous 95% max-|t| band based on the conservative empirical 0.95 quantile of maximum absolute studentized statistics over null-centered sign-flipped cell vectors, with critical value and all 256 maxima. Origin-level SEs, random-origin splits, and origin bootstrap inference are prohibited.

The relevance screen is 10% relative improvement plus raw margins M=0.0025, C=0.0032, P=0.0011 mAh/cycle; rerun 5%, 15%, 20%. These are not utility thresholds.

For each P or C, `supportive` requires:

1. ADX beats A1 in direct and functional families by >=10% relative improvement, and both simultaneous lower bounds exceed zero.
2. Each ADX separately improves over P0, SQ, and FQ on identical held rows.
3. Both matched raw improvements exceed the outcome margin; >=6/8 cell deltas are positive in each family; no LOCO mean changes sign; no family mean is below the negative margin.
4. Direct and functional directions agree; trajectories reproduce P/C rather than endpoint-only displacement; P does not reverse under washout W.
5. No-refit c=100–119 matched improvement is positive in each family, >=5/8 cells improve, and no family mean is below the negative margin.

D-only or X-only language additionally requires corresponding AD-vs-A1 or AX-vs-A1 secondary simultaneous support. Otherwise identify only combined update information.

Labels: `supportive` only if every gate passes; `history_only` when SQ/FQ/A1 beats P0 but updates remain below relevance; `persistence_null` when P0 remains best and updates fail A1; `adverse` only when ADX is worse than A1 and every null with simultaneous upper bounds below zero and no sensitivity reversal; global `falsified_at_margin` only when for both P/C and both families the simultaneous upper bounds exclude the relative and/or absolute relevance boundary; otherwise `inconclusive`. Family reversal, one-cell control, method disagreement, sensitivity reversal, too few positive cells, interval crossing, or mature/forward conflict is inconclusive or narrows scope. Negative average M/C is not adverse evidence.

## Outputs under /workspace

- `predictions.csv`: one row per stratum/cell/cycle/outcome for M,C,P,W, observed value, and P0/SQ/FQ plus direct/functional Q,A1,AD,AX,ADX predictions; include held cell, alpha, fit-band ID.
- `trajectories.csv`: one row per stratum/cell/cycle/horizon 0–19 with observed Q, P0, FQ, and all five functional reconstructions.
- `split_manifest.json`: all outer/inner folds, exact cells/cycles, weights, selected alphas, transform/PCA fit identities/component counts, and proof age-forward rows reuse mature fits.
- `provenance.json`: exact source hashes, members, table IDs, fields/units/sign, frequency hash, software, Q extraction, chronology ledger, target indices, D/X reconstruction maxima, elapsed/peak memory, and output hashes.
- `results.json`: `schema_version="zhang-mature-update-v1"`; counts; all cell/family/LOCO vectors; MAEs; t7/sign/max-|t| results; null results; early/attrition/sensitivity results; gate booleans linked to supporting numbers; per-outcome/overall labels; limitations.

All files must agree. Preserve adverse/inconclusive outputs. Summary tolerance is 1e-9; raw-capacity target tolerance 1e-7.

Automatic checks cover schemas, raw targets, splits, chronology summaries, errors, uncertainty arithmetic, and label gates. They cannot adjudicate headerless semantics, what physical operation D represents, 25C02/03 identity, repeatability, practical margins, causality, mechanism, safety, or external validity. Those need data-owner/electrochemical review, protocol/replicate evidence, independent specimens/interventions, and utility study.

Budget: 16 CPUs, 64 GiB, zero GPUs, eight hours. Record actual use.
