# Zhang2020 mature trajectory updates against frozen endogenous-history nulls

## Decision, evidence boundary, and falsifiable question

This crossover retains the mature, age-balanced trajectory question from
`candidate-fe2b794ebdba23fc56e7f016` and the explicit capacity-history nulls from
`candidate-f8813852f5325b3853f2a32d`. It changes the inferential target and method
gate in three consequential ways.

First, the independent evaluation unit is the physical cell. The 400 overlapping
origins are useful prediction occasions, not 400 replicates. Second, equal-cell
paired error improvement is primary because the eight-cell mature cohort contains
four 25 C cells but only two 35 C and two 45 C cells, and no deployment mixture over
temperature families has been specified. Family-balanced error, every cell contrast,
and every family mean remain mandatory sensitivities. Third, current-update
attribution is always made within a matched model family; comparison with the best
capacity-history forecast is a separate operational-dominance requirement.

The unresolved hypothesis is:

> In eight cells with complete origins at cycles 50–99, the joint current update in
> the observed V-to-IX transition clock and IX-minus-V impedance contrast contains
> held-cell information about either a same-direction 20-cycle fade-rate shift or a
> near-to-late bend that is absent from all observations available before those
> updates. That information must improve both a direct scalar ridge and a functional
> residual-trajectory ridge relative to their matched no-update rungs and to each
> frozen capacity-history null, and must retain direction when the same models are
> carried without refitting to cycles 100–119.

The strongest evidence presently supports only feasibility and the need for this
test. The exact archive supplies the required chronology and 50 mature origins for
each of eight cells. A new capacity-only audit found that the learned null advantage
reported on all ages does not transfer to the mature core: persistence had lower
equal-cell MAE than either learned history model for all three outcomes. No EIS
predictor has been fitted and no current-update benefit is claimed.

This matters because a diagnostic acquisition is scientifically informative only if
its current change adds out-of-cell trajectory information beyond endogenous capacity
history. It also prevents strong early-life nonstationarity from being renamed mature
degradation prognosis. Even a positive result would concern measured cycler capacity
under this protocol, not a microscopic aging mechanism, safety, or a general battery
population.

Zhang et al. (2020), DOI `10.1038/s41467-020-15235-7`, was inspected from full-text
XML (source ID
`33086e0650f9774d98a2853f7973f0a88c4e8c045703abb09e08fa21aadabf79`,
SHA-256 `ef60f78e673d5bc5c93aecf68520f4b018343f2d4465b56acb0ca6be71ac0144`).
It supports the 12-cell, multi-temperature, multi-state EIS setting and EIS-based
capacity/RUL prediction. It does not establish this prospective current-update
hypothesis, the mature-age restriction, the null ranking, or a mechanism.

## Executed mature-null audit

`zhang_mature_null_audit.py` (SHA-256
`a29aed42b776718f01b0a7740e86ba8d8b4df7be7113d8fa176c5ba7d3644f0d`)
read the capacity ZIP and performed nested leave-one-cell-out fits.
`zhang_mature_null_audit.json` (SHA-256
`92fc249fc9165ce2144cd60ab5a5a15325d9146b63f22ce6983ad0e0ddabd4ec`)
contains all cell/family results. The managed four-CPU job completed in 15.9 s.
This is a design diagnostic, not an EIS result.

On 400 origins at c=50–99 (50 per cell), with equal total fitting weight per cell:

| predictor | M MAE | C MAE | P MAE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| local-linear persistence P0 | 0.02443 | 0.03171 | 0.01044 |
| direct scalar history SQ | 0.03817 | 0.04171 | 0.02116 |
| functional residual history FQ | 0.03919 | 0.04183 | 0.02179 |

All values are mAh/cycle. FQ improved over P0 in only one of eight cells for each
outcome. For FQ-minus-P0 paired error differences, adjacent-origin lag-1 correlations
ranged from 0.51–0.95 for M, 0.31–0.94 for C, and 0.39–0.95 for P. Naive origin-level
standard errors were 3.4–4.3 times smaller than cell-level standard errors. This
directly demonstrates the pseudo-replication risk.

Family-balanced fitting/evaluation did not rescue the learned null: P0 versus FQ MAE
was 0.01830 versus 0.02692 for M, 0.02308 versus 0.02968 for C, and 0.00823 versus
0.01546 for P. Family balancing also changed the apparent scale because each 35 C or
45 C cell receives twice the evaluation weight of each 25 C cell. In the equal-cell
analysis, 25C07 alone had P0 M MAE 0.12720 while the other seven cells ranged
0.00207–0.01675. A single family-balanced mean hides this heterogeneity.

A strict age-forward diagnostic fit models only on c=50–99 in the other seven cells
and evaluated c=100–119 in the held cell (160 origins, 20 per cell). P0 again beat FQ
in equal-cell MAE: 0.03943 versus 0.05629 for M, 0.01665 versus 0.03472 for C, and
0.03288 versus 0.04392 for P. FQ improved only one cell for M and P and none for C;
25C07 nevertheless showed a large opposing M/P benefit. Thus neither the pooled
all-age history advantage nor a global null ranking is portable to mature ages.
P0, SQ, and FQ must all remain frozen comparators and their eight paired contrasts
must remain visible.

The audit did not test EIS, prove P0 optimal, quantify instrument noise, or establish
a population effect. It used one deliberately compact implementation of the
predeclared scalar and functional nulls. Its role is to prevent deletion of an
unfavorable simple baseline and to freeze the inferential unit.

## Specimens, clocks, and temporal populations

The confirmatory physical cells are exactly:

`25C01, 25C05, 25C06, 25C07, 35C01, 35C02, 45C01, 45C02`.

Each contributes c=50,…,99 with Q[c-10:c+19] and complete I/V/IX at c: exactly 400
origins, 50 per cell. The temperature-family counts are 4/2/2, not eight independent
temperature experiments.

Cells 25C04 and 25C08 remain valid physical identities but have no mature origin;
they enter only the early c=10–15 ten-cell common-support analysis. Tokens 25C02 and
25C03 remain excluded before fitting because their capacity filenames conflict with
acquisition-clock continuity; alternative mappings are identity sensitivities only.

For every origin preserve the acquisition order:

`capacity(c-1) discharge end < I(c) start < V(c) end < IX(c) start <
IX(c) end < capacity(c) charge start < capacity(c) discharge end`.

The prediction landmarks are LV at V(c) end, LD at IX(c) start, and LX at IX(c) end.
Q[c] and all later capacities are outcomes. The primary comparison is at LX on
identical rows. An LD D-only analysis is secondary and cannot be compared as though it
had the same acquisition burden as LX.

Temporal analyses are frozen as:

- confirmatory mature cell transfer: train/tune on seven cells and test the eighth,
  all at c=50–99;
- prespecified within-archive age-forward transport: use each mature-trained outer
  model without refitting and test its held cell at c=100–119, exactly 20 origins per
  cell;
- descriptive early common support: c=10–15, six origins in each of all ten accepted
  identities;
- exploratory attrition strata: c=120–149 and c>=150, reported cell by cell with no
  balanced-transfer claim.

Passing c=50–99 but failing c=100–119 restricts any result to the mature fitting band.
Passing both supports only within-archive age-forward transport to c=119. It does not
establish lifetime extrapolation or transfer to another cohort.

## Outcomes

For ten consecutive measured discharge capacities q define positive Theil-Sen fade

`g(q) = -median_{j<k} (q[k]-q[j])/(k-j)`.

At each origin:

- `g_pre=g(Q[c-10:c-1])`;
- `g_near=g(Q[c:c+9])`;
- `g_late=g(Q[c+10:c+19])`;
- `M=((g_near-g_pre)+(g_late-g_pre))/2`;
- `C=(g_late-g_pre)-(g_near-g_pre)=g_late-g_near`;
- `P=sign(M) max(0, |M|-|C|/2)`.

M and C are the nonredundant fitted coordinates. P is derived and equals the smaller
signed post/pre shift when both future windows have the same sign, otherwise zero.
Recover `A_near=M-C/2` and `A_late=M+C/2`; do not count them as independent
hypotheses. The two scientific outcomes are P (persistence) and C (bend); M and the
recovered rates are mandatory diagnostics.

Robustness outcomes are OLS and median-adjacent slopes, Q/Q0, leave-one-capacity-out
target ranges, and the washout shift
`W=g(Q[c+5:c+19])-g_pre`. Endpoint losses L10/L20 are comparators only.
Single protocol-defined capacity traces cannot distinguish reversible recovery,
cycler fluctuation, and physical degradation.

For token T, archive members are `EIS data/EIS_state_I_T.txt`,
`EIS data/EIS_state_V_T.txt`, `EIS data/EIS_state_IX_T.txt`, and
`Capacity data/Data_Capacity_T.txt`.

use. Each spectrum must have 60 finite unique frequencies on the descending
20,004.453-to-0.01999 Hz grid, compact-array SHA-256
`651b878c886a5deb40c50a612343b25bbd45ff97c5919d49a76419517d54d226`.
Preserve ohms and the stored negative-imaginary sign.

time/s, cycle, ox/red, Capacity/mA.h. The six-field 25C04/06/07/08 rows insert
Ewe/V and I/mA before the final capacity field. Q is the maximum finite positive
final-field value on ox/red=0; verify negative current where available. Q is measured
cycler discharge capacity, not charge return, SOC, a BMS estimate, a fitted state, or
a mechanism label. No SOC anchor is available.

## Predictors and matched methods

For scalar `D=IX_start-V_end` and 120-component
`X=(Re_IX-Re_V, (-Im)_IX-(-Im)_V)`, define componentwise:

- `S_z[i]=median(z[i,1],...,z[i,5])`;
- `P_z[i,c]=z[i,c-1]-S_z[i]`;
- `U_z[i,c]=z[i,c]-z[i,c-1]`.

Require reconstruction error at most 1e-9 s for D and 1e-12 ohm for X. D is an
observed acquisition-clock interval, not a known discharge duration. X is a
state contrast, not a latent degradation state.

The future-safe capacity block BQ contains c, log(1+c), fixed temperature numeric
and one-hot terms, Q0, Q[c-1], Q[c-1]/Q0, Q[c-10:c-1]/Q0, nine first differences,
five- and ten-cycle slopes and their difference, a ten-cycle quadratic coefficient
and residual SD, and prespecified temperature-by-age/level/slope interactions.
All transformations are fit on outer-training cells only.

At LX use identical feature rungs in both model families:

- Q: BQ only;
- A1: BQ + I(c), V(c), V(c)-I(c), S_D, P_D, S_X, P_X, but no U_D or U_X;
- AD: A1 + U_D;
- AX: A1 + U_X;
- ADX: A1 + U_D + U_X.

Each spectral block is standardized and reduced by weighted training-only PCA
retaining 99% variance with a hard cap of 10 components. The inherited two-frequency
17.79613/2.16054 Hz representation is a sensitivity, not a separate route to support.

Three frozen comparators answer different questions:

1. P0 is the auditable local-linear persistence forecast
   `Qhat[c+h]=Q[c-1]-(h+1)g_pre`, hence M=C=P=0.
2. SQ is weighted ridge from BQ directly to standardized joint (M,C), with P derived.
3. FQ predicts the residual trajectory
   `R_h=Q[c+h]-Qhat_P0[c+h]`, h=0,…,19, in a fixed six-degree-of-freedom cubic
   B-spline basis, then reconstructs Q and derives M,C,P.

The direct scalar family fits Q/A1/AD/AX/ADX to joint (M,C). The functional family
fits the same five rungs to the same six residual-trajectory coefficients. Both use
the same rows, predictors, PCA blocks, outer/inner folds, weights, and ridge alpha
grid {0.01,0.1,1,10,100}. The direct model preserves outcome-specific rate
coordinates; the functional alternative reveals whether any apparent gain is a
localized excursion, stable shift, or future bend that two scalars lose.

The prior PCA/RBF-Nystroem branch is deferred. With seven training specimens per
outer fold, its gamma, landmark, rank, and roughness choices add method-family
degrees of freedom without demonstrated necessity. Revisit it only if the frozen
linear functional residuals show reproducible nonlinear structure across held cells.
Neural and state-space models are deferred pending materially more specimens or
replicated capacity measurements. Equivalent-circuit inference requires a validated
topology and cannot establish microscopic truth here.

## Splits, weighting, and inference

Primary fitting gives each training cell equal total weight; origins within a cell
share that weight. Outer evaluation is leave-one-mature-cell-out. Inner model
selection is leave-one-training-cell-out and scores held cells equally. No held-cell
outcome enters scaling, PCA, basis fitting, hyperparameter choice, calibration, or
feature selection.

For each outcome Y, model m, and comparator n, first calculate within each cell:

`delta_i(n,m,Y)=MAE_i(n,Y)-MAE_i(m,Y)`.

The primary estimand is the equal-cell mean of the eight deltas. Always publish the
ordered eight-vector, median, range, number positive, and leave-one-cell-out means.
Also publish family means and the family-balanced mean. Family weighting is a
sensitivity because no target deployment mixture was supplied; it is not allowed to
replace the cell vector.

Use all 256 cell-level sign assignments as a symmetry-based randomization sensitivity,
a studentized t7 interval, and a leave-one-cell jackknife. Use one simultaneous
max-|t| band for the four primary joint-update contrasts (P and C in scalar and
functional families). These procedures describe uncertainty among the eight observed
cells; they do not turn the sample into a population probability. Origin-level
standard errors, random origin splits, and bootstrapping origins as independent are
prohibited.

Partial pooling is not claim-gating. With only three fixed temperature families and
two cells in each hotter family, between-family and within-family variance components
are weakly identified and prior-sensitive. An optional hierarchical sensitivity may
shrink cell deltas toward family means, but must show prior sensitivity and raw
deltas beside posterior summaries. It cannot rescue a failed paired-cell gate or
support a temperature trend. Additional independently prepared cells per family and
batch metadata are required for that inference.

A finite distribution-free 90% cell-block prediction interval is not available from
seven outer-training specimens. Prediction residual quantiles and coverage may be
reported descriptively, but coverage is not a support gate.

## Relevance and claim gates

The 10% relative margin is a prespecified screening threshold, not an instrument,
economic, or safety threshold. Because P0 error is very small in some temperature
families, every result must also report raw mAh/cycle improvement. Frozen audit-scale
absolute reference margins are 0.0025 mAh/cycle for M, 0.0032 for C, and 0.0011 for
P (approximately 10% of mature equal-cell P0 MAE, rounded upward). Sensitivities use
5%, 15%, and 20%. Practical acquisition value requires measurement-repeatability and
cost evidence not present here.

A joint current-update claim for P or C requires all of:

1. ADX beats A1 within the scalar family and within the functional family: each
   equal-cell point improvement is at least 10% and the simultaneous lower bound is
   above zero.
2. Each ADX prediction beats P0, SQ, and FQ on the same held rows. These are separate
   paired contrasts, not a synthetic winner selected per origin or family.
3. The raw improvement exceeds the outcome's absolute reference margin, at least
   six of eight cell deltas are positive, no leave-one-cell-out mean changes sign,
   and no temperature-family mean is below the negative absolute margin.
4. Scalar and functional predictions agree on direction; reconstructed functional
   trajectories show the claimed persistence or bend rather than only an endpoint
   displacement. P support cannot reverse for washout W.
5. The c=100–119 no-refit age-forward mean is positive, at least five of eight cell
   deltas are positive, and no family mean is below the negative margin. Failure
   here narrows a positive mature result to c=50–99.

D-only or X-only language additionally requires the corresponding AD or AX side
contrast to pass its simultaneous secondary family. Joint-only success means combined
update information; it cannot identify a modality.

- **Supportive:** all applicable gates pass. This supports within-archive,
  held-cell prediction of an operationally defined measured-capacity trajectory
  feature.
- **History-only:** SQ, FQ, or A1 beats P0 but current-update intervals remain below
  relevance.
- **Persistence-null:** P0 remains best and updates do not pass the matched A1 gate.
- **Adverse:** ADX is worse than A1 and every null, with simultaneous upper bounds
  below zero and no sensitivity reversal.
- **Falsified at the chosen margin:** for both P and C, the simultaneous upper bound
  on ADX-versus-A1 improvement is below 10% or below the absolute margin in both
  model families. The global disjunction is then rejected for this mature cohort.
- **Inconclusive:** intervals cross zero or the margin; fewer than six cells improve;
  a family reverses; one cell controls the mean; scalar and functional results
  disagree; washout/target definitions reverse; or c=100–119 conflicts.

A negative average M or C is not adverse evidence: prediction, not sign, is tested.
All null, adverse, and inconclusive outputs are retained.

## Deliverable and verification

Completion requires newly fitted held-cell predictions for P0, SQ, FQ and every
scalar/functional Q/A1/AD/AX/ADX rung; reconstructed 20-cycle trajectories; exact
cell and family contrast vectors; mature and no-refit age-forward outputs; all target,
representation, chronology, identity, washout, and slope-definition sensitivities;
and a machine-readable claim-to-output map.

Required provenance includes immutable source/catalog/software manifests; archive
members, table IDs, fields, units, signs, frequency grid, Q extraction, clock ledger,
all c-10:c+19 indices, split/weight/PCA/basis/tuning manifests, every prediction, and
all uncertainty draws. Readiness must reproduce the 400 mature and 160 age-forward
origins, chronology, S/P/U reconstruction, and a two-fold smoke fit. Readiness is not
a solved scientific objective.

An automatic verifier can recompute parsing, joins, features, targets, fits, paired
errors, null comparisons, uncertainty summaries, and whether a textual conclusion
matches the gates. It must reject row-level inference, omission of an unfavorable
null, family-balanced-only reporting, cross-family model comparison presented as
update attribution, Q[c] leakage, or a mature/age-forward claim unsupported by its
stratum.

Automation cannot establish headerless field semantics, the physical operations
inside D, the identity of 25C02/03, measurement repeatability, a practically adequate
margin, causality, mechanism, safety value, or transfer beyond these cells. Those need
data-owner/electrochemical review, repeated capacity measurements, protocol logs,
independent compatible specimens, interventions, and utility evidence.

The solver envelope is 16 CPUs, 64 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, and at most 8 hours. The
capacity-only audit used four CPUs and 16 GiB allocation and completed in 15.9 s.
The full estimate is unmeasured. These compact ridge/spline fits do not justify GPU
use.

## Selection record

Retained from the mature-core parent: the c=50–99 eight-cell core, nonredundant
(M,C) coordinates, derived P, washout/jackknife checks, exact bindings and chronology,
and non-mechanistic limits.

Retained from the null-envelope parent: P0/SQ/FQ, capacity-history challenge, and the
principle that current diagnostics must beat a useful endogenous forecast.

Changed: equal-cell paired improvement is primary; family-balanced MAE is a sensitivity;
all eight cell contrasts are mandatory; c=100–119 is an exact no-refit age-forward
test; nulls are compared separately rather than collapsed into an aggregate winner;
the scalar and functional methods share one linear ridge/PCA specification; and
partial pooling is non-gating because 4/2/2 cells cannot identify temperature
variance reliably.

The frozen assignment misspelled the second parent as
`candidate-f8813852f5325b385e3f2a32d`; the catalogued parent used here is
`candidate-f8813852f5325b3853f2a32d`.

# Proposal: is row-order-invariant Oxford identity affine, or does residual distributional shape persist?

## Question, hypothesis, and substantive advance

For the 11 Oxford NCR18650BD specimens with paired beginning-of-life (BoL) and ordinal middle-of-life (MoL) measurements at nominal 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC, does longitudinal information in each table's unordered empirical `ReZ_Ohm` distribution reside in:

1. its location;
2. its scale;
3. residual distributional shape after exact removal of location and positive scale;
4. more than one of these factors; or
5. none of these factors at the registered resolution?

This is a substantive child of `candidate-b9a943aec6ce2243cf6af8b1`. That parent exactly separates SOC-common from SOC-differential empirical-quantile profiles, but both blocks can still be driven by stable table offsets or spreads. Its whole-block normalization does not remove each SOC table's own location and scale, and its raw companion deliberately retains them. Therefore neither a common nor a differential result identifies whether higher-order distributional shape is needed.

The primary hypotheses are three separately falsifiable direct-persistence claims: correctly linked BoL location, log-scale, or standardized residual shape reduces matched held-specimen MoL factor loss by at least 10% beyond exact-protocol peers. A joint exact relinking family controls selection among all three factors and the scalar versus structured transport models. “Shape survives” requires support after tablewise location and scale have been removed and under robust tail/scale definitions.

The advance is not a new frequency interpretation. It is an exact, row-order-invariant empirical-distribution factorization that distinguishes affine information from higher-order distributional shape. This matters because location persistence is particularly compatible with stable series/contact offsets, while shape persistence would rule out a purely positive affine tablewise explanation. Even shape support would remain an electrical-distribution association, not a cell-intrinsic fingerprint or an ageing mechanism.

## Evidence-supported and unresolved claims

The inspected source README supports 12 NCA/graphite NCR18650BD 3 Ah cells, a 24 °C chamber setpoint, four schedule/rate groups, and EIS at supplied BoL and MoL checkpoints and nominal 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC. It reports 100 mA peak-to-peak excitation from 5 kHz to 10 mHz at six points per decade. The configured ZIP has complete paired coverage for 11 Group 1–4 cells.

Registered native export job `job-caee1e9fb0738c866b29bb5f` requested the exact 66 containers and completed in 11.97 s. Its manifest has 74 table objects, including exactly 66 canonical container/internal-name matches. Every canonical table has 35 rows and columns exactly `ReZ_Ohm,N_A`; all canonical `ReZ_Ohm` values are finite. Known repeated internal copies in G2_C3 and G3_C11 are byte-identical after export. Conversion verifies numeric availability and round trip, not scientific field semantics.

A bounded factorization audit found canonical ReZ values from 0.04013411 to 0.11474854 source-labeled Ω, RMS table spreads from 0.00457155 to 0.02277180, and IQRs from 0.00675364 to 0.03545878; hence every primary and robust scale is positive. A deliberately incomplete 11-fold/all-432 formulation screen gave best full-rank gains of -12.4% for location, -3.9% for log-scale, and -0.7% for shape; the joint relinking tail fraction was 0.889. Trimming or winsorizing did not make any factor positive in that screen. These unfavorable observations establish nondegeneracy and motivate a result-neutral experiment; they are not the proposed study's result because registered uncertainty, influence, robustness, and conclusion logic were not run.

The strongest supported claim is only that 66 finite unordered 35-value ReZ tables can be exactly and stably factorized. The unresolved claim is whether their true BoL–MoL specimen links contain direct held-specimen information in location, scale, or affine-invariant shape beyond exact protocol. Raj et al. (2020) full text and supplementary methods were not inspected here; no frequency, mechanism, or paper-result claim is borrowed from them.

## Exact location–scale–shape factorization

For specimen `i`, stage `t`, SOC `s`, let `q[i,t,s,1] <= ... <= q[i,t,s,35]` be the independently sorted ReZ values. Define:

```text
m[i,t,s] = mean_k(q[i,t,s,k])
r[i,t,s] = sqrt(mean_k((q[i,t,s,k] - m[i,t,s])^2))
z[i,t,s,k] = (q[i,t,s,k] - m[i,t,s]) / r[i,t,s]
a[i,t,s] = log(r[i,t,s])
```

Require `r[i,t,s] > 1e-6` source-labeled Ω and finite `a,z`. Then:

```text
q[i,t,s,k] = m[i,t,s] + exp(a[i,t,s]) * z[i,t,s,k]
mean_k(z[i,t,s,k]) = 0
mean_k(z[i,t,s,k]^2) = 1
```

These constraints make the decomposition unique. Stack SOCs in order 20,50,80 to obtain location vector `L[i,t]` in R^3, log-scale vector `R[i,t]` in R^3, and residual-shape matrix `Z[i,t]` in R^(3x35).

Arbitrary source-row permutations leave all factors unchanged. For any tablewise transformation `q* = alpha + beta*q`, `beta > 0`, `Z* = Z`, while `m* = alpha + beta*m` and `a* = a + log(beta)`. Thus a shape result cannot be generated by a purely positive affine change within each table. It can still reflect nonlinear calibration, differing row inclusion/weights, fixture behavior, or other non-cell effects.

This is an invertible factorization of each empirical distribution, not an additive partition of predictive gain. The experiment tests direct same-factor persistence and forbids cross-factor prediction. Therefore all-factor adversity does not exclude, for example, BoL scale predicting MoL shape; such cross-factor transport is not identifiable with only six within-group contrast degrees of freedom per outer fold.

## Leakage-safe matched models

Run 11 leave-one-specimen-out outer folds. All held MoL factors are outcomes only. For each factor `B in {L,R,Z}`, stage, and protocol group, compute training-only exact-group means. Subtract them from training and held factors. The held no-linkage baseline is the training MoL mean of its exact protocol group.

A singleton group in an outer training set supplies the held baseline when applicable but contributes zero centered slope information. Every outer fold must have exactly `sum_g(n[g,train]-1) = 6` within-group contrast degrees of freedom and at least three slope-contributing groups.

Within each fold and factor, divide BoL and MoL residuals by separate training-only RMS values `tau_XB,tau_YB`, computed with equal total weight per slope-contributing group, equal cell weight within group, and equal coordinate weight within a specimen. Require each `tau` above 1% of the corresponding median uncentered training norm; repeat 0.5% and 2% as gate sensitivities. This scaling is for numerical comparability and never uses the held outcome.

Fit on the same normalized residuals:

- **P, exact-protocol peer:** predict zero residual.
- **S, scalar persistence:** `yhat_B = b_B*x_B`. This one-parameter baseline asks whether the complete factor persists radially.
- **H, two-gain SOC-structured transport:** let `u=(1,1,1)/sqrt(3)`, `P_C=u*u^T`, and `P_D=I-P_C`. Fit `yhat_B=b_BC*P_C*x_B+b_BD*P_D*x_B`. For `L,R`, project the three-vector; for `Z`, left-multiply its three SOC rows. H adds one coefficient and can reveal whether persistence differs between across-SOC-common and SOC-differential modes, information S necessarily loses.

Use unpenalized weighted least squares. No hyperparameter, basis, tail policy, or block is chosen from held outcomes. All centering, scales, denominators, coefficients, and predictions are recomputed inside each outer fold and every relinking. Require finite denominators, both H subspaces to contain at least 5% of training predictor energy in every fold, design condition number at most `1e8`, and finite predictions. If H fails, S remains computable but H-specific interpretation is inconclusive.

For held specimen `i`, define mean squared normalized coordinate loss `L[B,m,i]`, treating the whole factor as one specimen outcome. Aggregate the 11 held cells equally and define `G[B,m] = 1 - mean_i(L[B,m,i])/mean_i(L[B,P,i])`, for `m in {S,H}`.

Report source-unit location RMSE, log-scale RMSE plus multiplicative error `exp(RMSE)`, shape RMS, every held prediction/loss, fold coefficient, group gain, and common/differential subloss. Select `W_B` as the larger observed S/H gain, S on a tie, only for concise attribution. Selection is protected by the exact maximum statistic below; fixed S and H results remain reported.

H-specific SOC-mode heterogeneity is a separate gated claim: `Delta_B = 1 - mean(L[B,H])/mean(L[B,S])`. It requires H to beat S materially and does not substitute for factor identity.

## Joint calibration over all 432 relinkings

Enumerate exactly `2! * 3! * 3! * 3! = 432` within-protocol allocations, identity included. Each allocation assigns a donor's complete BoL bundle—three SOC tables and all 35 values—to one recipient. Keep recipient protocol, MoL, stage and SOC labels fixed. Rerun sorting, factorization, fold means/scales, all P/S/H fits, winner designation, and gates. Never relink ranks, SOC tables, or factors separately. P must be invariant.

For allocation `c`, define `T_B[c]=max(G[B,S,c],G[B,H,c])` and `T_max[c]=max_B(T_B[c])` across `B in {L,R,Z}`. The omnibus exact conditional fraction is `p_any = #{c:T_max[c] >= T_max[observed]}/432`. The family-wise component fraction is `p_B = #{c:T_max[c] >= T_B[observed]}/432`.

Thus location, scale, shape, and S/H selection are calibrated jointly. After factor support only, assess structured transport with `p_delta,B = #{c:max_B'(Delta_B'[c]) >= Delta_B[observed]}/432`. These are exact for the enumerated conditional reference set under unverified within-group exchangeability, not treatment-randomization or population p-values.

## Small-n uncertainty, influence, and robustness

Using `numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(20260923))`, generate 10,000 group-stratified Bayesian-bootstrap draws over the frozen 11 outer-fold loss tuples, fixing each observed group's total weight at (n_g/11). Report percentile stability intervals for every fixed model gain, each fixed-winner gain, S/H contrast, and held-cell win fraction. These summarize dependence on the observed cells; overlapping folds preclude a population-confidence interpretation.

Report fixed-prediction omission of each held cell, all four group gains, and full-data coefficient refits after deleting each specimen. A deletion that leaves a singleton group contributes no slope contrast; do not manufacture a prediction for an absent protocol peer. Factor support requires breadth and low influence, while H-specific submode interpretation additionally requires coefficient signs not to reverse across valid deletions.

All-35 equal-mass mean/RMS factorization is primary. Freeze and rerun all 432 allocations for:

1. trim rank 1 and 35, then refactorize 33 values;
2. trim ranks 1–3 and 33–35, then refactorize 29;
3. winsorize ranks 1–3 to rank 4 and 33–35 to rank 32;
4. replace each consecutive five-rank block by its mean, yielding seven equal-mass bins;
5. center-weight ranks by `w_k proportional to p_k*(1-p_k)`, `p_k=(k-0.5)/35`, using weighted means, RMS, shape constraints, and shape loss;
6. use robust `m_R=q_18`, `r_R=(q_26+q_27-q_9-q_10)/2`, and `z_R=(q-m_R)/r_R`, with positive-IQR gate;
7. use raw RMS scale rather than log RMS, with fold-local unit scaling.

For the primary shape winner, also report loss-reduction numerators for lower ranks 1–6, center 7–29, and upper ranks 30–35. These are coordinates of one specimen, not independent tests. Tail-only benefit or center reversal makes broad-shape attribution inconclusive.

Additional invariance checks are at least 1,000 independent seeded source-row permutations; independent positive BoL/MoL unit multipliers in ({0.1,10}); stage/SOC-common additive offsets; alternate orthonormal bases within the SOC-differential plane; equal-cell rather than equal-contributing-group fit weights; and RMS gates 0.5%/2%. Shape outputs must be invariant to arbitrary positive tablewise affine transformations to numerical tolerance. Sensitivities may narrow support or force inconclusiveness but cannot rescue a failed primary.

## Frozen falsification and interpretation

The 10% gain is a dataset-scale materiality convention, not validated engineering utility. Report 5% and 20% descriptively.

A factor is **supportive** only if:

- `p_any <= 0.05`, `p_B <= 0.05`, and fixed selected gain is at least 0.10;
- the fixed-winner 95% stability lower bound is above zero;
- it beats P in at least 9/11 held specimens;
- every held-loss omission retains positive gain and at least 9/11 retain gain at least 0.10;
- no group gain is at or below -0.10;
- all source, spread, RMS, denominator, rank, conditioning, and invariance gates pass;
- trim-one, trim-three, winsor, seven-bin, center-weighted, and robust factorization retain positive gain, with trim-three and robust gain at least 0.10;
- no registered weighting or scale check reverses the conclusion; and
- for shape, the center-rank numerator is positive and neither tail sector is at or below -0.10.

A factor is **adverse for the 10% direct-persistence claim** only if selected gain is below 0.10, its stability upper bound is below 0.10, (p_B>0.05), the winner beats P in at most 7/11 cells, no group has multiplicity-compatible 0.10 support, all validity gates pass, and no registered sensitivity is supportive. Every other valid pattern—including exactly 8/11 wins, tail dependence, one-cell/group dependence, margin-spanning stability, relinking disagreement, or failed subspace gates—is inconclusive.

Classify the factorization deterministically:

- **affine-only:** location and/or scale supportive, shape adverse;
- **shape-only:** shape supportive, both location and scale adverse;
- **distributed:** shape and at least one affine factor supportive;
- **no direct factor persistence at the margin:** all three adverse;
- **unstable/inconclusive:** every other combination.

Within “affine-only,” say location-only, scale-only, or location-and-scale exactly as computed. Do not call all-factor adversity absence of every possible identity because cross-factor and frequency-resolved mappings were not tested.

H-specific SOC-mode heterogeneity is supportive only if its factor is supportive, H is the fixed winner, `Delta_B >= 0.10`, `p_delta,B <= 0.05`, H beats S in at least 9/11 cells and every held-loss omission, and the relevant common/differential coefficient contrast has one direction across valid deletions and registered sensitivities.

Support for location warrants only persistent empirical-distribution centers and is especially vulnerable to fixture/contact offsets. Scale support warrants persistent empirical spreads, not frequency bandwidth. Shape support warrants only that standardized unordered ReZ value distributions carry direct BoL-to-ordinal-MoL association beyond exact protocol and cannot be explained by positive tablewise affine transformations alone. None proves a frequency grid, transfer function, electrochemical mechanism, LLI/LAM, SEI growth, plating, causal path dependence, common age, fixture independence, or external transfer.

## Deliverable, alternatives, resources, and verification

Completion requires newly fitting all 11 outer folds for P/S/H in all three factors; all 432 whole-bundle relinkings for the primary and seven robustness definitions; 10,000 stability draws; held-loss omissions and coefficient deletions; invariance checks; and the deterministic attribution trace. Conversion or readiness is not scientific completion.

Required outputs:

- source: `source_audit.json`, `member_manifest.csv`, `duplicate_audit.json`, `normalized_eis.parquet`;
- factors: `empirical_quantiles.parquet`, `location_scale_shape.parquet`, `factorization_audit.json`, `affine_invariance_audit.json`;
- fits: `outer_predictions.parquet`, `outer_losses.csv`, `transport_coefficients.csv`, `all_432_relinkings.parquet`;
- robustness: `stability_gains.parquet`, `held_influence.csv`, `coefficient_deletions.csv`, `tail_sector_metrics.csv`, `sensitivity_metrics.csv`;
- synthesis: `metrics.json` and `conclusion.json` with sentence-to-field provenance and every failed gate.

P is the no-linkage baseline. S is the simple one-gain persistence model. H is the scientifically substantive low-capacity alternative on identical inputs, folds, and outcomes; it adds only one coefficient and reveals common-versus-SOC-differential persistence that S averages away. Unrestricted cross-factor maps, SOC-specific rank maps, kernels, and neural encoders are deferred because six within-group contrast degrees of freedom per fold cannot adjudicate them. Revisit cross-factor transport or richer models only with a substantially larger independent cohort. Frequency-localized, DRT, and equivalent-circuit models require authoritative frequency and complex-impedance fields. Repeat-remount/fixture controls are specifically required to distinguish cell from measurement-chain persistence.

Use 8 CPUs, 16 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, deterministic BLAS/thread settings, and allocation-level parallelism with checkpoints every 36 allocations. Native export measured 11.97 s. The bounded single-process Python screen of the primary 432 allocations took 10.2 s; the full registered workload is estimated at 10–30 CPU minutes and fits the configured 16-CPU, 262,144-MiB, 28,800-s solver envelope and 7,200-s reference limit. GPU use adds no scientific value for sorting and tiny least-squares fits.

The verifier can recompute hashes, canonical table selection, duplicate equality, factor identities, row/affine invariance, specimen splits, group means, fold-local scales, coefficients, losses, all relinkings, stability summaries, robustness variants, and the deterministic conclusion. It must accept supportive, adverse, or inconclusive outcomes when computed gates warrant them, and reject correct calculations paired with unsupported frequency, mechanism, causality, fixture-independence, population, or deployment claims. Equal empirical mass, within-group exchangeability, nominal-SOC validity, the 10% margin, MoL comparability, and scientific importance require expert adjudication or additional evidence.

## Exact location–scale–shape factorization

For specimen `i`, stage `t`, SOC `s`, let `q[i,t,s,1] <= ... <= q[i,t,s,35]` be the independently sorted ReZ values. Define:

```text
m[i,t,s] = mean_k(q[i,t,s,k])
r[i,t,s] = sqrt(mean_k((q[i,t,s,k] - m[i,t,s])^2))
z[i,t,s,k] = (q[i,t,s,k] - m[i,t,s]) / r[i,t,s]
a[i,t,s] = log(r[i,t,s])
```

Require `r[i,t,s] > 1e-6` source-labeled Ω and finite `a,z`. Then:

```text
q[i,t,s,k] = m[i,t,s] + exp(a[i,t,s]) * z[i,t,s,k]
mean_k(z[i,t,s,k]) = 0
mean_k(z[i,t,s,k]^2) = 1
```

These constraints make the decomposition unique. Stack SOCs in order 20,50,80 to obtain location vector `L[i,t]` in R^3, log-scale vector `R[i,t]` in R^3, and residual-shape matrix `Z[i,t]` in R^(3x35).

Arbitrary source-row permutations leave all factors unchanged. For any tablewise transformation `q* = alpha + beta*q`, `beta > 0`, `Z* = Z`, while `m* = alpha + beta*m` and `a* = a + log(beta)`. Thus a shape result cannot be generated by a purely positive affine change within each table. It can still reflect nonlinear calibration, differing row inclusion/weights, fixture behavior, or other non-cell effects.

This is an invertible factorization of each empirical distribution, not an additive partition of predictive gain. The experiment tests direct same-factor persistence and forbids cross-factor prediction. Therefore all-factor adversity does not exclude, for example, BoL scale predicting MoL shape; such cross-factor transport is not identifiable with only six within-group contrast degrees of freedom per outer fold.

## Leakage-safe matched models

Run 11 leave-one-specimen-out outer folds. All held MoL factors are outcomes only. For each factor `B in {L,R,Z}`, stage, and protocol group, compute training-only exact-group means. Subtract them from training and held factors. The held no-linkage baseline is the training MoL mean of its exact protocol group.

A singleton group in an outer training set supplies the held baseline when applicable but contributes zero centered slope information. Every outer fold must have exactly `sum_g(n[g,train]-1) = 6` within-group contrast degrees of freedom and at least three slope-contributing groups.

Within each fold and factor, divide BoL and MoL residuals by separate training-only RMS values `tau_XB,tau_YB`, computed with equal total weight per slope-contributing group, equal cell weight within group, and equal coordinate weight within a specimen. Require each `tau` above 1% of the corresponding median uncentered training norm; repeat 0.5% and 2% as gate sensitivities. This scaling is for numerical comparability and never uses the held outcome.

Fit on the same normalized residuals:

- **P, exact-protocol peer:** predict zero residual.
- **S, scalar persistence:** `yhat_B = b_B*x_B`. This one-parameter baseline asks whether the complete factor persists radially.
- **H, two-gain SOC-structured transport:** let `u=(1,1,1)/sqrt(3)`, `P_C=u*u^T`, and `P_D=I-P_C`. Fit `yhat_B=b_BC*P_C*x_B+b_BD*P_D*x_B`. For `L,R`, project the three-vector; for `Z`, left-multiply its three SOC rows. H adds one coefficient and can reveal whether persistence differs between across-SOC-common and SOC-differential modes, information S necessarily loses.

Use unpenalized weighted least squares. No hyperparameter, basis, tail policy, or block is chosen from held outcomes. All centering, scales, denominators, coefficients, and predictions are recomputed inside each outer fold and every relinking. Require finite denominators, both H subspaces to contain at least 5% of training predictor energy in every fold, design condition number at most `1e8`, and finite predictions. If H fails, S remains computable but H-specific interpretation is inconclusive.

For held specimen `i`, define mean squared normalized coordinate loss `L[B,m,i]`, treating the whole factor as one specimen outcome. Aggregate the 11 held cells equally and define `G[B,m] = 1 - mean_i(L[B,m,i])/mean_i(L[B,P,i])`, for `m in {S,H}`.

Report source-unit location RMSE, log-scale RMSE plus multiplicative error `exp(RMSE)`, shape RMS, every held prediction/loss, fold coefficient, group gain, and common/differential subloss. Select `W_B` as the larger observed S/H gain, S on a tie, only for concise attribution. Selection is protected by the exact maximum statistic below; fixed S and H results remain reported.

H-specific SOC-mode heterogeneity is a separate gated claim: `Delta_B = 1 - mean(L[B,H])/mean(L[B,S])`. It requires H to beat S materially and does not substitute for factor identity.

## Joint calibration over all 432 relinkings

Enumerate exactly `2! * 3! * 3! * 3! = 432` within-protocol allocations, identity included. Each allocation assigns a donor's complete BoL bundle—three SOC tables and all 35 values—to one recipient. Keep recipient protocol, MoL, stage and SOC labels fixed. Rerun sorting, factorization, fold means/scales, all P/S/H fits, winner designation, and gates. Never relink ranks, SOC tables, or factors separately. P must be invariant.

For allocation `c`, define `T_B[c]=max(G[B,S,c],G[B,H,c])` and `T_max[c]=max_B(T_B[c])` across `B in {L,R,Z}`. The omnibus exact conditional fraction is `p_any = #{c:T_max[c] >= T_max[observed]}/432`. The family-wise component fraction is `p_B = #{c:T_max[c] >= T_B[observed]}/432`.

Thus location, scale, shape, and S/H selection are calibrated jointly. After factor support only, assess structured transport with `p_delta,B = #{c:max_B'(Delta_B'[c]) >= Delta_B[observed]}/432`. These are exact for the enumerated conditional reference set under unverified within-group exchangeability, not treatment-randomization or population p-values.

## Small-n uncertainty, influence, and robustness

Using `numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(20260923))`, generate 10,000 group-stratified Bayesian-bootstrap draws over the frozen 11 outer-fold loss tuples, fixing each observed group's total weight at (n_g/11). Report percentile stability intervals for every fixed model gain, each fixed-winner gain, S/H contrast, and held-cell win fraction. These summarize dependence on the observed cells; overlapping folds preclude a population-confidence interpretation.

Report fixed-prediction omission of each held cell, all four group gains, and full-data coefficient refits after deleting each specimen. A deletion that leaves a singleton group contributes no slope contrast; do not manufacture a prediction for an absent protocol peer. Factor support requires breadth and low influence, while H-specific submode interpretation additionally requires coefficient signs not to reverse across valid deletions.

All-35 equal-mass mean/RMS factorization is primary. Freeze and rerun all 432 allocations for:

1. trim rank 1 and 35, then refactorize 33 values;
2. trim ranks 1–3 and 33–35, then refactorize 29;
3. winsorize ranks 1–3 to rank 4 and 33–35 to rank 32;
4. replace each consecutive five-rank block by its mean, yielding seven equal-mass bins;
5. center-weight ranks by `w_k proportional to p_k*(1-p_k)`, `p_k=(k-0.5)/35`, using weighted means, RMS, shape constraints, and shape loss;
6. use robust `m_R=q_18`, `r_R=(q_26+q_27-q_9-q_10)/2`, and `z_R=(q-m_R)/r_R`, with positive-IQR gate;
7. use raw RMS scale rather than log RMS, with fold-local unit scaling.

For the primary shape winner, also report loss-reduction numerators for lower ranks 1–6, center 7–29, and upper ranks 30–35. These are coordinates of one specimen, not independent tests. Tail-only benefit or center reversal makes broad-shape attribution inconclusive.

Additional invariance checks are at least 1,000 independent seeded source-row permutations; independent positive BoL/MoL unit multipliers in ({0.1,10}); stage/SOC-common additive offsets; alternate orthonormal bases within the SOC-differential plane; equal-cell rather than equal-contributing-group fit weights; and RMS gates 0.5%/2%. Shape outputs must be invariant to arbitrary positive tablewise affine transformations to numerical tolerance. Sensitivities may narrow support or force inconclusiveness but cannot rescue a failed primary.

## Frozen falsification and interpretation

The 10% gain is a dataset-scale materiality convention, not validated engineering utility. Report 5% and 20% descriptively.

A factor is **supportive** only if:

- `p_any <= 0.05`, `p_B <= 0.05`, and fixed selected gain is at least 0.10;
- the fixed-winner 95% stability lower bound is above zero;
- it beats P in at least 9/11 held specimens;
- every held-loss omission retains positive gain and at least 9/11 retain gain at least 0.10;
- no group gain is at or below -0.10;
- all source, spread, RMS, denominator, rank, conditioning, and invariance gates pass;
- trim-one, trim-three, winsor, seven-bin, center-weighted, and robust factorization retain positive gain, with trim-three and robust gain at least 0.10;
- no registered weighting or scale check reverses the conclusion; and
- for shape, the center-rank numerator is positive and neither tail sector is at or below -0.10.

A factor is **adverse for the 10% direct-persistence claim** only if selected gain is below 0.10, its stability upper bound is below 0.10, (p_B>0.05), the winner beats P in at most 7/11 cells, no group has multiplicity-compatible 0.10 support, all validity gates pass, and no registered sensitivity is supportive. Every other valid pattern—including exactly 8/11 wins, tail dependence, one-cell/group dependence, margin-spanning stability, relinking disagreement, or failed subspace gates—is inconclusive.

Classify the factorization deterministically:

- **affine-only:** location and/or scale supportive, shape adverse;
- **shape-only:** shape supportive, both location and scale adverse;
- **distributed:** shape and at least one affine factor supportive;
- **no direct factor persistence at the margin:** all three adverse;
- **unstable/inconclusive:** every other combination.

Within “affine-only,” say location-only, scale-only, or location-and-scale exactly as computed. Do not call all-factor adversity absence of every possible identity because cross-factor and frequency-resolved mappings were not tested.

H-specific SOC-mode heterogeneity is supportive only if its factor is supportive, H is the fixed winner, `Delta_B >= 0.10`, `p_delta,B <= 0.05`, H beats S in at least 9/11 cells and every held-loss omission, and the relevant common/differential coefficient contrast has one direction across valid deletions and registered sensitivities.

Support for location warrants only persistent empirical-distribution centers and is especially vulnerable to fixture/contact offsets. Scale support warrants persistent empirical spreads, not frequency bandwidth. Shape support warrants only that standardized unordered ReZ value distributions carry direct BoL-to-ordinal-MoL association beyond exact protocol and cannot be explained by positive tablewise affine transformations alone. None proves a frequency grid, transfer function, electrochemical mechanism, LLI/LAM, SEI growth, plating, causal path dependence, common age, fixture independence, or external transfer.

## Deliverable, alternatives, resources, and verification

Completion requires newly fitting all 11 outer folds for P/S/H in all three factors; all 432 whole-bundle relinkings for the primary and seven robustness definitions; 10,000 stability draws; held-loss omissions and coefficient deletions; invariance checks; and the deterministic attribution trace. Conversion or readiness is not scientific completion.

- factors: `empirical_quantiles.parquet`, `location_scale_shape.parquet`, `factorization_audit.json`, `affine_invariance_audit.json`;

P is the no-linkage baseline. S is the simple one-gain persistence model. H is the scientifically substantive low-capacity alternative on identical inputs, folds, and outcomes; it adds only one coefficient and reveals common-versus-SOC-differential persistence that S averages away. Unrestricted cross-factor maps, SOC-specific rank maps, kernels, and neural encoders are deferred because six within-group contrast degrees of freedom per fold cannot adjudicate them. Revisit cross-factor transport or richer models only with a substantially larger independent cohort. GPU use adds no scientific value for sorting and tiny least-squares fits.

It must accept supportive, adverse, or inconclusive outcomes when computed gates warrant them, and reject correct calculations paired with unsupported frequency, mechanism, causality, fixture-independence, population, or deployment claims. - `G_R=1-CRPS_R(H-div)/CRPS_R(U-meta)`
- `G_ES=1-EnergyScore_W(H-div)/EnergyScore_W(U-meta)`
- `Delta_LPD=(LPD_H-div-LPD_U-meta)/K`
- condition-balanced point RMSE and `G_total=1-RMSE_H/RMSE_B`, `G_shape=1-RMSE_H/RMSE_M`, and H-peer versus B-own `G_zero` on the 601 zero-peer cases.

Also report model-wise NLL/LPD, energy score, CRPS(R), 50/80/90 coverage, calibration error, radial/marginal widths, predicted-scale/error rank association and all 44 condition effects, plus the frozen strata. Use 10,000 paired whole-condition bootstrap draws and simultaneous one-sided 95% max-root bounds for `G_R-0.05`, `G_ES-0.05` and `Delta_LPD`; resample conditions for coverage. These summarize finite-cohort stability, not a random-condition population.

Define J-gate high dispersion by the outer-training 75th percentile of filtered h. Report gain over H-peer in that stratum and overall noninferiority.

## Mandatory controls

Execute metadata containment; target-replicate/order and zero/one/two restrictions; >22-day staleness removal and one-bin-lag analyses; 5,000 deterministic matched false-peer trajectory assignments; metadata-matched whole-trajectory D/C/J permutation; inherited point-sentinel ablations/nulls; K=8/16 and original geometry; spline, SOC/frequency deletion, raw amplitude/phase reconstruction, normalization, visit/bin, duplicate/origin, 23–27 °C, temperature/OCV and noise sensitivities; and 1,804 versus labeled 1,926 analysis. Preserve failures and match failures.

Leak canaries must reject equality at cutoff, incomplete peer visits, future target residuals/features, full-cohort or held-condition preprocessing, and future peer records. Repeated visits, peers, SOCs, frequencies and rows are not independent cells.

## Decision rules

Reliability is **supportive** only when simultaneous lower bounds exceed 5% for both G_R and G_ES and zero for Delta_LPD; 90% radial coverage is 85–95%; H-div mean 90% width is ≤110% of U-meta; true-peer gains exceed the 95th percentile of both nulls; dispersion ranks realized error positively; at least 36 conditions survive required controls; and no required condition deletion, replicate, class, lag, SOC/frequency, correction or representation check reverses direction.

It is **adverse** if simultaneous upper bounds are below 2% for both proper-score gains, H-div worsens either proper score, U-meta captures the gain, scale association is nonpositive, or true peers are null-like. If benefit is confined to the 601 current-pair cases with upper bounds below 2% in zero/one-peer strata, reject general longitudinal reliability and report at most short-lag reliability. Otherwise it is **inconclusive**, including intervals crossing margins, width-only calibration, score disagreement, fewer than 36 surviving conditions, unstable fitting/matching, deterioration outside 85–95% coverage, or a result driven by one restricted stratum.

Adaptive pooling is supportive only in addition to reliability support when the simultaneous lower bound on high-dispersion point-RMSE gain exceeds 5%, the upper bound on overall worsening is below 2%, nulls are beaten and direction survives controls. It is adverse if high-dispersion upper bound is below 2% or overall RMSE worsens by more than 2%; otherwise inconclusive.

The point sentinel is supportive only when lower bounds exceed 10% for G_total and 5% for both G_shape and G_zero, with shared-linear/false-peer and robustness success. It is adverse if total upper bound is below 5%, shape upper bound below 2%, H-peer is worse, true peers are null-like, or benefit is confined to same-bin peers while G_zero upper bound is below 2%; otherwise inconclusive. Report the three conclusions separately. A monitoring recommendation requires both supportive point sentinel and supportive reliability. Reliability support with adverse point accuracy means only that divergence diagnoses forecast failure.

## Required deliverables

Produce these nonempty files under `/workspace`:

`source_manifest.csv, frequency_map.csv, spectrum_audit.json, duplicate_provenance.csv, visits.parquet, forecast_examples.parquet, availability_audit.json, peer_pair_histories.parquet, reliability_features.parquet, folds.json, shape_transform.json, pca_loadings.parquet, model_spec.json, fitted_hyperparameters.json, forecast_provenance.parquet, point_predictions.parquet, predictive_distributions.parquet, dispersion_states.parquet, metrics.json, uncertainty.json, condition_effects.csv, false_peer_null.parquet, shape_null.parquet, sensitivities.csv, conclusions.json, result_bundle.json`.

`result_bundle.json` is the compact verification ledger and must contain:

- `study`: source/catalog hashes, counts (228,44,132,774,2322,1804), same-bin counts [601,602,601], dimensions 180 and K=12, and strict-cutoff flag.
- `models`: all nine model names and booleans for newly fitted, LOCO predictions, cross-fitted residuals, center lock, containment and required controls.
- `metrics`: primitive score/RMSE values plus reported gains and intervals. Gains must recompute exactly from primitives.
- `diagnostics`: 90% coverage, width ratio, rank association, surviving controls, null/control booleans and J-gate/point adverse flags.
- `decisions`: exactly `supportive`, `adverse` or `inconclusive` for reliability, adaptive pooling and point sentinel, derived from the rules above.
- `claims`: a list using only the finite-cohort claim scope above; `reserved_claims` must list mechanism, capacity, safety, causality, condition-population variability and external transport as not established.
- `provenance`: seeds, software versions, weighting, bootstrap count 10000, fold membership and links to detailed artifacts.

The verifier checks files, counts/schema declarations, score arithmetic, model containment/center locks, strict chronology declarations, decision-rule consistency and prohibited overclaims. It accepts scientifically appropriate supportive, adverse and inconclusive conclusions. It cannot automatically establish source-field semantics, electrochemical origin, causal mechanism, margin adequacy or external validity.

## Resources and completion

Use up to 16 CPUs, 96 GiB RAM, zero GPUs and 28,800 seconds. Checkpoint after extraction, cohort/folds, each point model, cross-fitted residuals, each uncertainty model, nulls and sensitivities. CPU is adequate for these low-rank state-space fits. If execution is incomplete, report incompleteness; do not change the population, cutoffs, estimand, outcomes, margins or controls. Readiness checks only packaging, imports, hashes/headers and tiny arithmetic canaries; it does not solve this objective or certify scientific truth.
